searchDocs.title: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
Steps​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Confirm the placement Model exists.ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name> must already exist — this is required for placement itself and is the same model used by Stash/Move. Author the Tool template.Create (or confirm) a Tool in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name>. Create the PlaceableTools folder under ReplicatedStorage if it does not exist yet.Set the attribute PlaceableName = "<Name>" on the Tool root (string attribute, exact match).The Tool must have a Handle BasePart. Author its scripts and behaviour as you would any other placeable tool. If PlaceableTools/<Name> is missing, both buttons fail silently server-side — no model is destroyed and no item is lost, but the buttons do nothing. Add the buttons to the GUI.Inside the GUI that the placeable's ProximityPrompt opens, add two ImageButton instances: one named exactly MoveButton, one named exactly StashButton. They can be placed at any depth in the GUI's descendant hierarchy. To make them invisible but still clickable, set both ImageTransparency = 1 and BackgroundTransparency = 1 on each button. If either button is missing, PlaceableActions.bind will log a warning at runtime. Bind and unbind in the controller.In the controller script that opens and closes the placeable GUI, call PlaceableActions.bind when the GUI opens and binding:Unbind() when it closes: local PlaceableActions = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.PlaceableActions) -- When the GUI opens for a specific placed Model: local binding = PlaceableActions.bind(placedModel, guiRoot) -- When the GUI closes (or the controller cleans up): binding:Unbind() placedModel is the Model instance in workspace.PlacedObjects. guiRoot is the root GUI instance opened by the ProximityPrompt (the ancestor that contains MoveButton and StashButton). If you use a Janitor for the GUI lifecycle, track the binding with it: cleaner:Add(binding, "Unbind") (Optional) Configure sound IDs.In src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau (or the equivalent config for your placeable system), set PlacementConfig.Sounds.Stash and PlacementConfig.Sounds.Move to the desired rbxassetid:// strings. Leave as "" to disable sound playback for that action. See Add a Sound if the asset ID does not yet exist in SoundConfig. (Optional) Tune cooldown and poof duration.In PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions: Cooldown — minimum seconds between successive Stash/Move requests per player (default 0.4).PoofDuration — how long the shrink-and-disappear visual plays (seconds).

searchDocs.title: Server-side guarantees​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Per-player cooldown gates spam.The target must be a direct child of workspace.PlacedObjects and carry a non-empty PlaceableName attribute (set automatically by PlacementServer at place-time).An atomic claim ensures two players cannot double-grant the same Tool simultaneously.No distance check — the ProximityPrompt enforces proximity at GUI-open time.  On success, every client receives a BroadcastPlaceablePoof packet and renders a transient shrinking clone at the model's position, parented to workspace.PlaceablePoofs and destroyed when the animation completes.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Enable Stash / Move on a Placeable
searchDocs.content: Place the item in Studio via the normal placement flow.Walk up to it so the ProximityPrompt activates and the GUI opens.Click StashButton — confirm the model disappears with the poof effect and the Tool appears in your Backpack.Place it again, open the GUI, click MoveButton — confirm the model disappears and the Tool is immediately equipped.Check the Output window for any PlaceableActions warnings about missing buttons or a missing Tool template.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Set up the premium subscription. BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID gates the entire Premium row. While it's "" (the pre-launch default), premium is never granted and the subscription APIs (GetUserSubscriptionStatusAsync, PromptSubscriptionPurchase) are skipped entirely — safe to ship pre-launch without spamming errors. In the Creator Dashboard, go to Monetization → Subscriptions and create the subscription first (price, billing period, display copy).Paste its id (format EXP-XXXXXXXXXX) into BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID.Keep the value identical in every place of the universe — BattlePassManager runs place-agnostic (lobby and gameplay both resolve premium status live), so a mismatch would make premium appear/disappear across a teleport. Edit the tier track. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/BattlePassConfig.luau. The base Tiers[level] table (level = 1..MAX_LEVEL) is generated in a loop; edit an individual tier after generation, or edit the loop itself for a track-wide change: -- Bump a single regular tier's Free reward after the fact: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[7].Free = { Type = "Coins", Amount = 300 } -- Or add a one-off Item reward on a non-milestone tier: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[20].Premium = { Type = "Item", ItemId = "SomeAccessoryId" } A Reward is { Type = "Coins", Amount: number } or { Type = "Item", ItemId: string }. An empty ItemId = "" is a placeholder milestone slot — see Gotchas. Milestone tiers (15, 30, 45, 60 in the shipped default) pay a chunkier Free coin bonus plus a Premium Item slot; regular tiers pay Coins on both rows. Add a SeasonOverrides entry for one month (optional). To swap in a different reward for one specific season only (e.g. a themed accessory for this month's milestone) without touching the evergreen base Tiers, add an entry to BattlePassConfig.SeasonOverrides, keyed by season index (year*12 + month-1, i.e. BattlePassState.seasonIndex), then by tier level: -- Override tier 30's Premium reward for a specific season (e.g. July 2026 = 2026*12+6 = 24318). BattlePassConfig.SeasonOverrides[24318] = { [30] = { Premium = { Type = "Item", ItemId = "JulyAccessory" } }, } Any row present in SeasonOverrides[seasonIndex][level] shadows the base Tiers[level] entry for that row, for that one season only — an override that only sets Premium leaves Free on the base table for that tier. BattlePassState.tierReward resolves the override before falling back to Tiers, and both the server (grant) and client (display) call the same function, so they can never disagree. Fill milestone ItemIds. Every milestone tier ships with an empty Premium Item slot (ItemId = "") as a placeholder. Before launch, replace each with a real asset id: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[15].Premium = { Type = "Item", ItemId = "AccessoryAssetId15" } See Gotchas — an unfilled slot silently grants nothing and still marks itself claimed. Tune ExpPerLevel against quest BPExp. BattlePassConfig.ExpPerLevel (a flat number, or a { [level]: number } table for a curve) sets the cumulative EXP cost per tier. The only EXP source is Reward.BPExp on quests (fed via Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted — see Battle Pass — EXP earning), so a full clear's reachability is entirely a function of how much BPExp the Season quests (and other BPExp sources such as the jump drive arrival reward) pay out over a month. Daily/Weekly board quests pay no BPExp: Flat default: ExpPerLevel = 1000, MAX_LEVEL = 60 → 60,000 total EXP for a full clear.The shipped Scope = "Season" quests pay 3000 BPExp each (SeasonJunk/SeasonKills/SeasonDistance/SeasonBiomeJumps = 12,000 for the month).To make a full clear reachable in a month: estimate the BPExp a reasonably active player earns per day from non-quest sources, multiply by ~30, add the Season total, and set ExpPerLevel (or the per-level table) so the running total lands near or under that number. Raise Season quest BPExp values instead of lowering ExpPerLevel if you want the quests to feel more rewarding rather than the track to feel shorter.A { [level]: number } table lets early tiers cost less (fast early momentum) and late tiers cost more (a grind at the top) — BattlePassState.levelFromExp/progress handle either shape transparently. Add Scope = "Season" quests (optional). Season quests are the dedicated battle pass EXP feed — the whole set is active for the entire month (no rotation/shuffle, unlike Daily/Weekly). Add an entry to QuestConfig.Quests in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/QuestConfig.luau: SeasonCrafting = { Scope = "Season", Category = "Personal", Metric = QuestConfig.Metrics.JunkCollected, Target = 2000, DisplayName = "Season Scrapper", Description = "Collect 2,000 junk this season", Reward = { Coins = 0, Exp = 0, BPExp = 3000 } }, Metric must be one of QuestConfig.Metrics, same as any other quest — see Tune Quests — Add a quest for wiring a brand-new metric. The shipped Season quests pay Coins = 0, Exp = 0 and only BPExp — Season quests exist purely to move the battle pass track, not the coin/XP economy — but this isn't enforced; a Season quest can also pay coins/exp if you want it to. No Counts entry applies to Scope = "Season" — every Season quest in the pool is always active, so add exactly as many as you want visible this month.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled.Confirm BattlePassClient.GetProgress() returns level 0, Exp 0 on a fresh profile, and BattlePassClient.GetTiers() reflects your edited Tiers/SeasonOverrides.Complete a quest carrying BPExp and confirm BattlePassClient.Changed fires with the level/progress advancing accordingly.Call BattlePassClient.Claim(); confirm BattlePassClient.GetClaimableSummary() returns (0, 0, 0) immediately after (idempotent — a second claim finds nothing outstanding).If testing Premium: set a real SUBSCRIPTION_ID, subscribe as a test account, and confirm BattlePassClient.IsPremium() flips to true and a retroactive sweep grants every reached Premium tier for the season.If you changed SeasonOverrides, confirm the override actually landed on the current season index (BattlePassState.seasonIndex(os.time())) — an override keyed to the wrong season silently never applies.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved data BattlePassConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerBattlePass") must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places — it's the shared ProfileStore key that lets session-locking hand off cleanly across the teleport boundary. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile: all season progress and claimed flags become unreachable. Only do this intentionally, and change it in both places together.  An empty ItemId slot grants nothing — and is still marked claimed A milestone Item reward left at ItemId = "" is a placeholder. Granting it fires no Signals.OnBattlePassItemGranted (there's nothing to hand off to an inventory system) but the claimed flag is still set, so the player never sees that tier offered again — even after you later fill in a real ItemId. Fill every milestone slot before launch, not after.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Choose a starter perk. A perk with UnlockCost, UnlockLevel, and UnlockPointCost all 0 is a free "starter" — PerkManager.seedStarters auto-unlocks it for every player on load and after every respec of its pool. Today the two starters are IronConstitution (Personal) and ScavengersEye (Party) — one per pool, so a brand-new player always has a perk to upgrade in each pool. Starters still pay upgrade coins. IronConstitution = { Category = "Personal", DisplayName = "Iron Constitution", Order = 1, Description = "+{1} max health", MaxLevel = 10, Buffs = { { Key = "HPBonus", PerLevel = 0.04 } }, UnlockCost = 0, UnlockLevel = 0, UnlockPointCost = 0, UpgradeCoinStep = 100 }, -- starter To make a different perk a starter, set its UnlockCost, UnlockLevel, and UnlockPointCost to 0. Make sure at least one perk per pool stays a 0/0/0 starter. A starter cannot be Hidden (a boot self-check asserts this). Set a perk's level gate and costs. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luau and edit the entry: MarathonLungs = { Category = "Personal", DisplayName = "Marathon Lungs", Order = 2, Description = "+{1} max stamina, −{2} sprint drain", MaxLevel = 6, Buffs = { { Key = "MaxStaminaBonus", PerLevel = 0.05 }, { Key = "SprintDrainReduction", PerLevel = 0.03 } }, UnlockCost = 250, UnlockLevel = 2, UnlockPointCost = 1, UpgradeCoinStep = 100 }, UnlockLevel — minimum player XP level (LEVEL_REQUIRED below this).Upgrade gates follow from UnlockLevel: the max level needs UnlockLevel + PerkConfig.UPGRADE_GATE_SPAN (35), see Perks — Upgrade gates.UnlockCost — coins deducted once via CoinManager.DeductCoins at unlock, and recorded in the CoinsSpent ledger.UnlockPointCost — points from the perk's own pool, spent once at unlock (NO_POINTS when the pool can't pay).UpgradeCoinStep — each later level n costs UpgradeCoinStep × n coins plus 1 point. All checks are enforced server-side by PerkState.canUnlock (order: unknown → hidden → already unlocked → level → points → coins). Unlock is one-time; upgrades are paid per level. UnlockCost buys access. Each level after that costs 1 point plus rising coins (see Perks — Point and coin economy). UnlockPointCost competes with upgrades for the same pool, so a high point cost delays a player's first levels in other perks. Respec refunds come from the ledger. PerkManager.Respec (a pool) and RespecPerk (one perk) refund exactly CoinsSpent[perkId] — every coin the player paid on that perk — via CoinManager.RefundCoins (not scaled by Pocket Change). A coin-price re-tune therefore never changes what an existing player gets back. A starter refunds its upgrade coins, loses its levels, and stays unlocked. Unlock points always come back in full, because points are derived.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled.Open the Perk menu (P). Confirm both starters (Iron Constitution, Scavenger's Eye) show unlocked, locked perks show their coin + point price, and the six hidden perks never appear.Unlock Marathon Lungs (250 coins + 1 point), then upgrade it to level 1 (100 coins) and level 2 (200 coins; needs player Lv 9, the upgrade gate). The button reads UPGRADE · 300 before level 3 and NEED COINS when short.Try to unlock a perk while under-leveled, out of points, or under-funded and confirm the request is rejected with no coin deduction.Reset the perk and confirm: the level clears, the perk re-locks, exactly 550 coins (250 + 100 + 200) come back, and the points return. Changing UpgradeCoinStep in Studio before the reset does not change the 550.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing UnlockPointCost re-prices perks players already own Points are derived: spent reads the current UnlockPointCost of every unlocked perk. Raising a perk's point cost from 1 to 3 takes 2 more points from every player who already unlocked it — their available points can drop to 0. Lowering it gives points back. Coins do not have this problem (the ledger records what was paid); points do. Tune point costs before launch, or pair a raise with a Respec announcement.  Changing STORE_NAME wipes all saved perk + unlock data PerkConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerPerks") is the ProfileStore key for PerkLevels, Unlocked and CoinsSpent. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile — equivalent to wiping all perk progress, unlocks and the refund ledger. Only do this intentionally.  Schema migrations run once per profile migrateAndSeed has two version-guarded steps: schema 1 (one-time wipe) and schema 2 (Perk Rework: bank the v1 unlock coins in PendingLegacyRefund, wipe, pay the refund once the coin profile loads). PerkManager only bumps PerkSchemaVersion forward; editing it back down does not replay cleanly. A future perk-id change that strands old ids needs a new guarded step (schema 3) with its own frozen refund table.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Change a perk's numeric values. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luau and adjust the entry: IronConstitution = { Category = "Personal", DisplayName = "Iron Constitution", Order = 1, Description = "+{1} max health", MaxLevel = 10, -- ← cap Buffs = { { Key = "HPBonus", PerLevel = 0.04 } }, -- ← buff per level (0.04 = 4%) UnlockCost = 0, UnlockLevel = 0, UnlockPointCost = 0, UpgradeCoinStep = 100 }, -- ← level n costs 100 × n coins PerLevel is a fraction (not percent) unless the buff's Format says otherwise. The buff folder attribute is PerLevel * level, so a change here propagates automatically — no code change needed. Format only changes the GUI text: "percent" (default), "count", "total" (1 + value, used by Wide Net), "seconds". Change upgrade prices. UpgradeCoinStep sets the coin price of each level: level n costs UpgradeCoinStep × n coins plus 1 point. The catalog uses 100 for perks unlocked at level 0–9, 200 for 10–19, and 350 for 20+. A price change never changes refunds: respec returns exactly what each player paid, read from the CoinsSpent ledger (see Coin ledger). Add a new perk — declare it in PerkConfig.Perks. Pick a unique id, a Category ("Personal" or "Party"), Order (display order within the tab), DisplayName, Description with {1}, {2} … placeholders (one per buff), MaxLevel, one or more Buffs entries with unique keys, the unlock fields, and UpgradeCoinStep. Set Hidden = true if its consumer does not exist yet: the perk is then not listed and cannot be unlocked (PERK_UNAVAILABLE). Wire a consumer. Read the value through PerkBuffRead — never with a new inline folder lookup: Personal: PerkBuffRead.Personal(player, "MyKey")Party: PerkBuffRead.Party("MyKey") Apply it with the shared math: bonuses value * (1 + b), reductions PerkBuffRead.Reduce(value, b) (never below 10% of base), material costs PerkBuffRead.ReduceCost(cost, b) (rounded up), duration speed-ups duration / (1 + b). Read it fresh each time it is needed so a mid-run change applies live. Server checks read the server's own copy; a client read is for prediction and visuals only. Understand the point economy before tuning it. Each XP level grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point — no separate point storage.Available points = playerLevel - spent, where spent = perk levels + UnlockPointCost of unlocked perks in that pool.You cannot tune the point grant rate without changing PerkState.available and PerkManager.replicate in tandem. There is intentionally no config for it. Know what respec does. Players can respec a pool or one perk from the GUI. The server clears the levels, re-locks non-starter perks, and refunds every coin in CoinsSpent for them via CoinManager.RefundCoins (exact, not scaled by Pocket Change's CoinGainBonus). Points return automatically. Change a shop perk's numbers. Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ShopPerkConfig.luau. A shop perk has a fixed Value per buff (no levels). Its Description is hand-written, so change the number in the text too. Example: Gold Rush pays the JunkCoinsT4 / JunkCoinsT5 Buff values, and its Description repeats them. Timers and counters (SALVAGE_DRONE_SECONDS, OVERCLOCK_EVERY, …) are constants at the top of the file; their Descriptions repeat them as well.

The Output shows no assert failure from PerkState or PerkBuffRead (Studio-only self-checks).Open the perk panel (P).Upgrade a perk and confirm: The level counter increments and the coins drop by UpgradeCoinStep × level.In Explorer, ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId> shows the updated attribute(s).The downstream consumer reflects the change (e.g. Humanoid MaxHealth for Iron Constitution). Reset the perk and confirm levels reset, points return, and the refund equals everything paid on it.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Add or change a board quest. Daily/Weekly quests live in Quest List.xlsx (sheet Quests, outside the repo). Edit the sheet, then regenerate the pool from the repo root: python tools/gen_quest_pool.py "../Quest List.xlsx" src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/QuestPool.luau The script needs 100 rows, 25 per Scope × Category, with unique names. Ids are Q + the sheet's # (Q001).Target is read from the task text: the number before "minutes", else the first number, else 1.Metric decides whether the quest is offered. A quest is offered only when its Metric is a key of QuestConfig.Metrics. To make a new metric live, add the key to QuestConfig.Metrics, then report it from src/ServerScriptService/QuestSourcesLoader.server.luau with QuestManager.ReportProgress(actor, metricKey, amount) (has an actor — credits Personal + fans out to Party) or QuestManager.ReportPartyProgress(metricKey, amount) (ownerless world event — Party only). See Quests — Sources. Tune rewards and mileage in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/QuestBoardConfig.luau: Rewards[scope][category] = { Coins, Exp } — every quest of that period × category pays this on claim (× the Contract Bonus locked at completion). Coins go through CoinManager.AddCoins(player, coins, "Quest:"..questId), so the Fortune perk's CoinGainBonus also applies (see Economy).Mileage[scope] — 5 checkpoints { Coins, Exp, Boxes? }. Checkpoint k needs k claimed quests of that period. Keep Boxes on the last one.PerkBox — LengthWeights (box length odds by how many lengths a perk has; an expiring perk's lengths are its ShopPerkConfig Variants), ConsumableCopies per consumable, SuperRareChance (the super rares are the BoxOnly perks in ShopPerkConfig). Tune offers and slots in QuestBoardConfig: OFFER_SIZE, BASE_SLOTS, MAX_EXTRA, FREE_REFRESHES. Changes apply to each player's next reset; boards already built keep their offers. Products and passes. Create the Developer Products (refresh, 4 temporary slots) and the 6 slot passes in the Creator Dashboard, then paste their ids into QuestBoardConfig.Products / Passes. 0 = not on sale (the GUI hides the button). Prices are read from Roblox, never from config. Season quests (battle pass feed) stay in QuestConfig.Quests with Scope = "Season". See Tune Battle Pass. Shift reset boundaries. Resets happen at local midnight, where "local" is set by QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset — a fixed offset in seconds from UTC (pre-launch default -5 * 3600 = US Eastern). This is the one knob to change to re-timezone the whole system; set it to 0 for pure UTC. It does not follow daylight saving. QuestConfig.DailyResetOffset (= -ResetTimezoneOffset) and QuestConfig.WeeklyResetOffset (= 345600 - ResetTimezoneOffset; the 4-day base aligns week starts to Monday since the Unix epoch was a Thursday) are derived from it. A change applies on each player's next ensureCurrent check. Changing a boundary mid-period can fire the reset earlier or later than players expect, so prefer a maintenance window (see Disruption). The value must stay identical in both places (it's the same shared file).

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join the Lobby in Studio with API Services enabled and open the Quest Terminal.Confirm each bucket offers only quests whose metric is live, and that a small bucket shows fewer than 5 offers.Accept a quest, join the Game Instance, trigger its source (collect junk, defeat a tagged enemy, wait through a distance tick, jump) and confirm its progress advances in the tracker.Return to the Lobby and claim it: coins and EXP are granted once, the mileage track gains 1 point, and a second claim fails with ALREADY_CLAIMED (code 5).

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved quest data QuestConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerQuests") must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places — it's the shared ProfileStore key that lets QuestManager's session locking hand off cleanly across the teleport boundary. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile.  Removing a quest id strands an active quest A board quest id that leaves QuestPool while a player holds it in a slot can never progress or pay. Keep ids stable (they come from the sheet's #), and remove or renumber quests only at a reset you control.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Change a node's cost or duration.Open src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ResearchConfig.luau and edit the Levels table on the node: Shield_Alpha = { DisplayName = "Shield α", Branch = "TrainShield", Tier = 1, Column = 0.5, Prereqs = nil, MaxLevel = 1, Effects = { { Type = "StatBuff", Key = "MaxHP", PerLevel = 50 } }, Levels = { [1] = { Cost = { Metal = 25 }, Duration = 30 } }, -- ← cost / time }, Cost is a { [material]: number } map spent from the server-wide Material Pool — only Wood and Metal are valid (any other key makes MaterialPool.Spend refuse the enqueue, and the GUI only draws Metal and Wood costs). Duration is in seconds of research while fuel is available — see step 2. Both values take effect for any job enqueued after the change; jobs already queued or active keep the cost/duration they were enqueued with. Every node ships at MaxLevel = 1, so only Levels[1] exists. Changing an Effects entry's PerLevel (for StatBuff) or DrainPerLevel (for FuelEfficiency) changes the buff granted — see step 5 for the effect shapes. ResearchEffectsDispatcher recomputes buffs from every node's Effects list on every level-up, and the detail panel's EFFECT row updates from the same number. Review the fuel and pause behavior before retuning it. Bench fuel has no cap: players can store as much as the pool's Energy pays for.FUEL_BURN_RATE (default 1.0/sec) — how fast fuel burns while a job is active. Raising this makes jobs pause more often; consider raising FUEL_PER_POINT with it.FUEL_PER_POINT (default 2) — bench fuel per pool Energy point.HOLD_TICK (default 0.1 s) and REFUEL_POINTS_PER_TICK (default 1) — how fast holding the REFUEL button grows the preview (10 Energy/s at the defaults). Nothing is spent until the player lets go; the server then spends only the points needed. While any player holds, the burn and the job timer stop for everyone.MAX_HOLD_POINTS (default 255) — a hold pays by itself at this much Energy, or after the time that takes (25.5 s at the defaults) when a small pool stops the charge first. Keep it at or below 255: ReqResearchRefuel carries the points as a NumberU8.HOLD_TIMEOUT (default 30 s) — a holder whose release never arrives (crash, lost packet) stops freezing the bench after this long. Keep it above MAX_HOLD_POINTS / REFUEL_POINTS_PER_TICK × HOLD_TICK so a real hold never times out. A job's elapsed only advances while fuel is available (ResearchState.advance clamps effectiveDt = min(dt, fuel / burnRate)), so each fuel point at the defaults buys one second of research. Change the queue depth.QUEUE_MAX (default 3) caps how many jobs can wait behind the active one (ResearchState.validateEnqueue rejects with QUEUE_FULL beyond this). The GUI has three slot cards (QueueButton1..3 under QueueContainer.Slots). To raise it, duplicate a slot in Studio and name it QueueButton4; the controller warns at load if a slot is missing. Change the cancel refund fraction.ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION (default 0.5) is the fraction of the active job's cost refunded when it is cancelled — queued jobs always refund at 1.0. The in-progress box reads "50% BACK" from this value (or "FULL BACK" while the Lab Insurance perk is active). This does not affect the cascade behavior (see Research Bench — Cascade-cancel). Add a node. One config entry; no Studio work. TechTreeGuiController clones a card from Templates.CardTemplate for every node of the open branch and draws its lines from Prereqs. Pick a free slot: Branch (an Id from ResearchConfig.Branches), Tier (row, 1 = top, at most ResearchConfig.MAX_TIER = 5, the rows the tree canvas fits) and Column (0 left, 0.5 centre, 1 right). A centred node must be alone in its row. Prereqs must be in the same branch and a higher row. A line from a prereq more than one row up runs straight down the prereq's column, so every slot it passes must stay empty (Ranged_SniperRifle → Ranged_EnergyFirearms keeps tier 4 column 1 empty). Give it Unlocks = { "..." } (one detail-panel row per string) for an unlock-flag node, or an Effects list for a buff node. A new StatBuff key also needs a ResearchConfig.EffectLabels entry. Example — "Reinforced Hull" below Shield δ: Shield_ReinforcedHull = { DisplayName = "Reinforced Hull", Branch = "TrainShield", Tier = 5, Column = 0.5, Prereqs = { "Shield_Delta" }, MaxLevel = 1, Effects = { { Type = "StatBuff", Key = "MaxHP", PerLevel = 75 } }, Levels = { [1] = { Cost = { Metal = 320, Wood = 60 }, Duration = 240 } }, }, Effect shapes (a node can list more than one, see Shield_Efficiency/Shield_Delta): { Type = "StatBuff", Key = <attributeName>, PerLevel = <number> } — ResearchEffectsDispatcher sums PerLevel * level across every node sharing the Key into that attribute on ReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs. Publishing a key with no consumer is safe but be deliberate about it.{ Type = "FuelEfficiency", DrainPerLevel = <number, 0 < n < 1> } — multiplies into ResearchBuffs.FuelEfficiency as DrainPerLevel ^ level. TrainFuelManager already reads it.Any other Type warns and no-ops in ResearchEffectsDispatcher.nil — an unlock-flag node. At level 1, ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> is written; wire a Workbench recipe's RequiresNode to that id (see Workbench Crafting). Optional Gamepass id: the card gets a gold rail and ticket, and the detail panel shows a "Game pass" chip. Reload in Studio: ResearchConfig.validate() warns on an unknown branch or prereq, a bad Tier/Column, two nodes in one slot, a line through a card, a prereq cycle, a node with neither Unlocks nor Effects, an effect with no dispatcher handler, or a buff key with no label. Add a branch. Add { Id, DisplayName, Icon } to ResearchConfig.Branches (list order = tab order; Icon is a key of ResearchConfig.Icons), then give nodes that Branch. The tab list scrolls when the tabs outgrow it. Change an icon. Upload the PNG (white on transparent for line icons; the controller tints them) and paste rbxassetid://<id> into ResearchConfig.Icons under its key.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Join in Studio with API Services enabled, walk to the placed bench under workspace.PlacedObjects.Open the tree (TechPromptPart prompt), pick the branch tab, and check the new card sits where Tier/Column say, with its lines.Select a cheap node and press RESEARCH. Confirm materials are deducted at once, the in-progress box shows the job, and the card's stroke pulses.Let fuel run to 0 and confirm the bar stops, the running card reads PAUSED and the fuel hint reads "RESEARCH PAUSED". Hold REFUEL with Energy in the pool: the job box reads REFUELING and its timer stops. Release, and confirm one payment and the job resumes.Cancel the active job from the in-progress box — it refunds at ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION. Queue a job and cancel it from its slot — full refund.Let a StatBuff node complete and confirm the attribute in ReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs updates and the card turns green, or an unlock-flag node and confirm ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> appears.For a Gamepass node, confirm enqueue is rejected with GAMEPASS_REQUIRED while not owned.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the shredder config.All shredder constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ShredderConfig.luau. Tune hold duration.The required hold scales linearly between one junk item and MAX_JUNK_COUNT items: Field	Default	EffectMIN_HOLD_DURATION	0.3 s	Hold time required for exactly 1 junk item MAX_HOLD_DURATION	3.5 s	Hold time required when carrying MAX_JUNK_COUNT or more items MAX_JUNK_COUNT	10	Junk count at which duration is fully capped at MAX_HOLD_DURATION Increase MAX_HOLD_DURATION to make large batches feel weightier. Keep MIN_HOLD_DURATION above the sum of normal round-trip latency to avoid the server rejecting fast single-item shreds. Tune arc animation (client-side cosmetic). Field	Default	EffectARC_HEIGHT_BOOST	5 studs	Extra Y added to the arc midpoint — controls arc peak height ARC_DURATION	0.55 s	Travel time per cosmetic piece from spawn to landing LANDING_SCATTER_RADIUS	1.5 studs	Random spread around LandingPoint Piece count, stagger, rest time, and the fly-to-HUD leg live in MaterialHudConfig — see Material Pool. Handle anti-exploit tolerances with care.These fields directly affect server-side rejection rates. Tighten them only after validating against real network conditions: Field	Default	Risk of over-tighteningINTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE	5 studs	Added on top of INTERACT_DISTANCE (10 studs) server-side to cover positional desync. Reducing below 3 will cause false rejections on high-latency clients. HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE	0.5 s	Subtracted from required hold when server validates timing. Setting below 0.3 will reject legitimate completions on 150ms+ RTT connections. PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN	1.0 s	Minimum gap between consecutive successful shreds per player. Do not set below 0.5 s. Adjust material yield.Material types produced by a shred are determined by JunkConfig.MaterialRules in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luau: MaterialRules = { Metal = {"Metal"}, Wood = {"Wood"}, Energy = {"Energy"}, } The shredder credits only Wood and Metal: ShredderServer.computeYield counts those two. MaterialPool also holds Energy, but Energy is credited on grab, never shredded. A new shreddable material needs computeYield and the MaterialPool whitelist extended, plus a HUD row (MaterialPoolClient.Materials); a CraftingMaterials template is optional (without one its fly effect skips straight to 2D). Verify Studio asset setup before testing.The shredder system requires the following to be in place in the live place: Each workbench Model in Workspace must be tagged Workbench (CollectionService).Each workbench Model must have its PrimaryPart set.Each workbench should contain a child Model named TrajectoryPoints (field: TRAJECTORY_MODEL_NAME) with two invisible, anchored, non-collidable BasePart children: SpawnPoint (field: SPAWN_POINT_NAME) and LandingPoint (field: LANDING_POINT_NAME). Tag this model with PlacementIgnore. If missing, the pool is still credited and the effect starts at the workbench pivot.ReplicatedStorage should contain a Folder named CraftingMaterials (field: MATERIALS_FOLDER) with Tool templates Wood and Metal, each with a BasePart child named Handle. Clients clone the Handle for the cosmetic arc; without it the effect skips straight to the 2D fly.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Run a solo session, carry a mix of junk counts (1 item, 5 items, 10 items), and hold the shredder interaction. Confirm hold durations roughly match the linear interpolation between MIN_HOLD_DURATION and MAX_HOLD_DURATION. Watch the arc land near LandingPoint, then the pieces fly into the Materials HUD, and confirm the HUD total rises by the yield.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the stamina config.All tunable constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/StaminaConfig.luau. This file is shared between client and server, so one edit propagates to both sides. Adjust core stamina values. Field	Default	EffectMaxStamina	100	Pool ceiling StaminaDrain	10	Units drained per second while sprinting StaminaRegen	15	Units regenerated per second when not sprinting RegenDelay	1.4	Seconds after sprint ends before regen starts Adjust sprint feel. Field	Default	EffectWalkSpeed	16	Base walk speed (studs/s) SprintSpeed	24	Speed while sprinting DefaultFOV	70	Camera FOV at walk SprintFOV	85	Camera FOV during sprint FOV transitions are animated by SprintController; changing the values here is enough — no animation code changes needed. See Change Sprint Behavior for keybind and state-machine edits. Adjust sprint keybinds (if needed).The SprintBinds array accepts any mix of Enum.KeyCode and Enum.UserInputType values: SprintBinds = { Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonB }, Add or replace entries. Both SprintController and StaminaManager read from the same config array. Validate client feel and server authority.SprintController (client) predicts drain and regen locally. StaminaManager (server) is the source of truth and corrects the client via packets. After saving, test in a live Studio session: sprint until exhausted, confirm drain/regen rates match the new values, and confirm the server correction does not cause jarring snaps.

searchDocs.title: Verify​
searchDocs.content: Sprint until stamina is depleted, release sprint, and confirm the regen delay then regen rate match the new config values. Check the Output window for any StaminaManager sync errors.

searchDocs.title: Steps​
searchDocs.content: Open the placement config.Visual and icon settings live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau. Replace icon asset IDs.The Icons table holds one entry per toolbar button: Icons = { GridOn = "rbxassetid://118749020984103", GridOff = "rbxassetid://132920215751528", GhostUnlocked = "rbxassetid://132512888685903", GhostLocked = "rbxassetid://128344634676430", Place = "rbxassetid://104931706363823", Blocked = "rbxassetid://111228091742290", } Replace the rbxassetid://... value for any icon you want to update. Upload the new image in Studio's Asset Manager first to get a valid asset ID. The key names (GridOn, GridOff, GhostUnlocked, GhostLocked, Place, Blocked) must remain unchanged — BuildModeGuiController looks them up by key. The ROTATE and CANCEL icons are static and set on the Icon ImageLabels in Studio. Icons must be white so ImageColor3 can tint them. Adjust ghost appearance. Field	Default	EffectVisualGhostTransparency	0.45	Opacity of main model parts during ghost preview CollisionBoxGhostTransparency	0.65	Opacity of the CollisionBox part during preview OtherGhostVisualTransparency	0.60	Opacity of other parts in other players' ghosts ShowCollisionBox	false	Set true to make CollisionBox visible during preview (debug aid) ColorValid	Color3.fromRGB(100, 210, 255)	Tint when placement is valid ColorInvalid	Color3.fromRGB(255, 80, 80)	Tint when placement is blocked ColorTweenTime	0.12 s	Duration of color transition between valid/invalid states Adjust ghost movement responsiveness. Field	Default	EffectFreeModeLerpSpeed	20	How quickly the ghost follows the cursor in free mode RotationLerpSpeed	15	How quickly the ghost rotates when the player rotates the item GhostUpdateHz	20	Raycast update rate (Hz) — lower values reduce CPU cost but feel less smooth Adjust the grid overlay. Field	Default	EffectGridTextureId	"rbxassetid://6372755229"	Decal texture applied to build area surfaces during grid mode GridTransparency	0.35	Opacity of the grid overlay (0 = opaque, 1 = invisible) Keep the button-to-signal mapping consistent.src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/BuildModeGuiController.client.luau wires each toolbar button to a Signals event. If you add a new button (e.g. a new toggle), you must: Add the new icon key to PlacementConfig.Icons.Create a corresponding Signals entry in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau if the button drives new behavior.Wire the button in BuildModeGuiController to fire/subscribe to that signal.Update the signals map (and the networking map if the signal crosses the client/server boundary). Do not add raw RemoteEvent calls from BuildModeGuiController — all cross-boundary communication must go through Packets. Keep the mobile layout.The GUI tree and sizes are described in Placement → Mobile build GUI. Its palette constants (LINE, ACCENT, GOOD, BAD, DEEP, MUTED) live at the top of BuildModeGuiController. Add a HUD that should hide while building to its HIDDEN_WHILE_BUILDING list. Test mobile input parity.Build mode must be fully operable without a keyboard. In a Studio mobile emulation session (or on device): Confirm all toolbar buttons are reachable and tap targets are large enough.Confirm grid/free toggle and rotation controls work via touch.Confirm pinch zooms the top-down camera, and that jump, sprint, fuel and health bars hide while building and come back after.Confirm the ghost follows touch drag correctly. Test desktop input parity.In a standard Studio session: Confirm keyboard shortcuts for grid toggle and rotation still fire correctly after any icon or signal changes.Confirm the cursor-following ghost is smooth at the configured GhostUpdateHz.

Hover over a valid and an invalid surface and confirm the ghost color transitions. Check the Output window for any missing-asset warnings from BuildModeGuiController.

searchDocs.title: Notes​
searchDocs.content: We do not re-document third-party libraries. Only heavily-modified in-tree dependencies (Packets, MotionMaster, Signals) have their own documentation pages.The TweenPlus TweenPreallocations attribute must be re-set in Studio after everywally install. Details are on the Toolchain page.Janitor usage patterns — one Janitor per scope, Cleanup vs Destroy, keyed collections — are covered on Janitor Patterns.

searchDocs.title: Core rule: one Janitor per lifecycle scope​
searchDocs.content: Each distinct lifecycle gets exactly one Janitor. When that lifecycle ends, call:Cleanup or :Destroy on it (see below for which to use).  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Janitor = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Janitor) local janitor = Janitor.new() -- Track a signal connection (cleaned up by calling :Disconnect) janitor:Add(inst.Event:Connect(fn), "Disconnect") -- Track an Instance (cleaned up by calling :Destroy) janitor:Add(part, "Destroy") -- Tear down and reuse (leaves the Janitor alive for the next cycle) janitor:Cleanup() -- Tear down and discard (the Janitor itself is gone afterward) janitor:Destroy()

searchDocs.title: Cleanup vs Destroy​
searchDocs.content: Method	When to use	Typical example:Cleanup()	The Janitor is module-level and reused across respawns or re-equips.	characterJanitor, backpackJanitor — cleaned on every CharacterAdded, then refilled. :Destroy()	The Janitor is created per-entry and discarded when the entry is removed.	WorkbenchEntry.Cleaner, engine/lever entry janitors.  Using :Destroy on a reused janitor silently breaks the next cycle because the object becomes unusable. Using :Cleanup on a per-entry janitor leaks the janitor table itself. Match the method to the ownership model.

searchDocs.title: Keyed-collection pattern​
searchDocs.content: When managing a dynamic set of entries (workbenches, junk pickups, registered engines, etc.), give each entry its own Janitor stored under a predictable key:  -- Type annotation (Luau) type Entry = { model: Model, cleaner: Janitor.Janitor, } local registry: { [string]: Entry } = {} local function register(id: string, model: Model) local entry: Entry = { model = model, cleaner = Janitor.new(), } entry.cleaner:Add(model, "Destroy") entry.cleaner:Add(model.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child) -- ... end), "Disconnect") registry[id] = entry end local function unregister(id: string) local entry = registry[id] if entry then entry.cleaner:Destroy() -- per-entry → Destroy registry[id] = nil end end   The pattern guarantees that removing an entry also disconnects every signal and destroys every instance that entry owns, with no possibility of leaking a handle.

searchDocs.title: Singleton exception​
searchDocs.content: Top-level controller connections that live for the full session do not need a Janitor. If the connection is created once at script root and never torn down (for example, Players.LocalPlayer.CharacterAdded at the top of a client controller), wrapping it in a Janitor adds overhead with no benefit.  Only use a Janitor when the scope can end before the script does.

searchDocs.title: Why a PlayerAdded push is unreliable​
searchDocs.content: Packet (the vendored networking library) connects the underlyingRemoteEvent at module-require time and dispatches every incoming payload into a plain Signal with no backlog. That connection is almost always live well before the script that actually cares has connected its own handler — every client script that requires Packets at the top of the file opens the door before anything downstream is listening. Anything the server sends in that window is dispatched into a signal with no subscribers and is gone. There is no retry, and no way for a late subscriber to ask for the current value.  Players.PlayerAdded compounds this: it is not guaranteed to fire for the first player in a server, who may already be in Players when the server script runs. A manager that only connects the event — never also iteratingPlayers:GetPlayers() — can miss that player's join entirely.  Put together: a one-shot PlayerAdded → FireClient push can be dropped by either the player already being present, or the client not yet listening, and the sender has no idea it happened.

searchDocs.title: The mechanism​
searchDocs.content: JoinSync inverts the direction. The client, not the server, decides when it is ready:  ClientReadyController.client.luau fires Packets.ClientReady (client → server, zero payload) exactly once, after game.Loaded plus a task.defer— giving every other StarterPlayerScript a chance to finish connecting.JoinSync.Initialize() (called once, from JoinSyncLoader.server.luau) handles that packet by running every registered sender for that player, each isolated in its own task.spawn + xpcall so one erroring sender can't starve the rest.JoinSync.Register(name, sender) also serves any player who is alreadyready at the moment of registration. This is what makes registration order and script-load timing irrelevant — a manager whose Initialize() runs late still reaches everyone.A per-player ready flag (cleared on PlayerRemoving) means a repeatedClientReady is a no-op, so a client can't make the server replay every system's snapshot in a loop.  name must be unique per system — it exists only to label the warning if that sender's send errors, or to catch a double-registration (skipped, with a warning, rather than double-sending).

searchDocs.title: The rules​
searchDocs.content: Follow these when adding any new server-authoritative readout that a client needs on join:  Register a JoinSync sender; never connect PlayerAdded to push a snapshot. PlayerAdded fires too early relative to the client's own readiness, and can miss the first player outright. JoinSync fires exactly when the client says it's listening.Read state at send time, inside the sender; never capture it at registration. Register is called once, at server startup, long before any player exists. A sender is a closure that reads live state (an upvalue, a table lookup) each time it runs — it must never close over a value snapshotted at registration, or every player will be served whatever the state happened to be at boot.Server-side record creation stays on PlayerAdded; only the send moves. If a manager's PlayerAdded handler both creates a per-player record and pushes it, keep the record creation where it is — gameplay code may read that record before the client is ready — and move only theFireClient call into a JoinSync.Register sender. That handler still needs the usual Players:GetPlayers() bootstrap loop alongside itsPlayerAdded connection, so a player already present when the server script runs still gets a record.Never invent a client-side default for a server-authoritative value.Render a placeholder ("—", a neutral colour, a zero-width bar — whatever fits the widget) until the real snapshot arrives, and snap directly to the first real value instead of easing from a guess. A guessed default is worse than no data: it looks like an answer.Never seed an extrapolation baseline from a client-read clock.workspace:GetServerTimeNow() is the client's own converging estimate of server time; read early in the client's life (module load, script start) it has not converged yet. Extrapolate only from a serverTime the server itself stamped onto the snapshot it sent.  Rule 4 and rule 5 are what actually fixed the reported bug — JoinSync alone makes the send reliable, but the old fallback snapshots (seeded from config defaults, timestamped from an unconverged client clock) were what turned an occasional dropped packet into a HUD that always swept 100% → 0% on join. SeeTrainFuelGuiController and TrainShieldGuiController for the placeholder pattern, and TrainStateCache for the shared extrapolation helper that returns nil until a real snapshot lands.

searchDocs.title: Worked example​
searchDocs.content: TrainFuelManager.Initialize() registers its join-time sender instead of connecting Players.PlayerAdded:  -- The client send waits until the client is listening; see JoinSync. JoinSync.Register("TrainFuel", function(player: Player) Packets.TrainStateSync:FireClient(player, fuelAtLastEvent, currentRate, isBraked, isStalled, lastEventTime) end)   fuelAtLastEvent, currentRate, isBraked, isStalled, and lastEventTimeare all upvalues read fresh every time the closure runs (rule 2) — a player who joins mid-round gets the fuel level as of their join, not whatever it was when the server booted.  MaterialPool follows the same pattern: it registers "MaterialPool" at module load and sends MaterialPoolUpdate with the live Wood/Metal totals and zero gain, so the joining client's HUD snaps to the real totals with no fly-to-HUD effect. It deliberately broadcasts (:Fire) instead of:FireClient: the Packet library flushes the broadcast buffer before per-player buffers each frame, so a FireClient snapshot could arrive aftera same-frame Add broadcast and leave the joiner on stale totals. For the other clients a zero-gain update is a harmless re-render. SeeMaterial Pool.

searchDocs.title: The two deliberate exclusions​
searchDocs.content: Not every server-authoritative system needs a JoinSync sender. Two managers were deliberately left out of this conversion:  AmmoManager pushes nothing at join. Ammo pools start empty, and an empty pool is the correct initial state — there is nothing to snapshot.AmmoPoolSync only fires on award, consume, or equip, none of which need a join-time replay.ArmorManager replicates through an attribute folder, not a packet.Attributes are ordinary replicated Instance state — readable by the client at any time, including before it has connected anything. There is no connect-after-the-fact race to guard against, so JoinSync would add nothing.  If a future system's join state is provably always correct with no send at all (like AmmoManager), or replicates through Instance/attribute state rather than a packet (like ArmorManager), it does not need a JoinSyncsender either. Everything else that pushes a one-shot snapshot to a joining player does.

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Play(target, goals, config)​
searchDocs.content: Fire-and-forget shorthand. Creates a TweenObject, calls :Play(), and returns it.  MotionMaster.Play(frame, { BackgroundTransparency = 0 }, { Duration = 0.3, Model = "EaseOutQuad" })

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Create(target, goals, config)​
searchDocs.content: Returns a TweenObject for manual lifecycle control. Does not start playback.  local tween = MotionMaster.Create(label, { TextTransparency = 1 }, { Duration = 0.5 }) tween:Play()   TweenObject methods​  Method	Description:Play()	Start or restart from current elapsed position. :Pause()	Pause; preserves elapsed time. :Resume()	Resume a paused tween. :Cancel()	Pause and reset to the start value. :Reverse()	Flip direction mid-playback; elapsed time mirrors continuously. :Scrub(alpha)	Jump to a normalized position [0, 1] without playback. :Destroy()	Disconnect all connections and release memory. :OnStep(cb)	Register cb(alpha, dt) — fires every frame. Chainable. :OnComplete(cb)	Register cb() — fires when the tween finishes. Chainable. :OnDestroy(cb)	Register cb() — fires on :Destroy(). Chainable.

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Spring(target, prop, config)​
searchDocs.content: Creates and starts a SpringDriver that follows a dynamically updated endpoint. Supports number and Vector3 properties only.  local driver = MotionMaster.Spring(frame, "Position", { Omega = 18, Zeta = 1.0 }) driver:SetTarget(newPosition) -- update the goal at any time   SpringDriver config fields: Omega (natural frequency), Zeta (damping ratio),MaxSubsteps, FixedDt. searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Sequence(config)​
searchDocs.content: Chain or parallelize TweenObjects. Returns a Sequence.  local seq = MotionMaster.Sequence() -- serial (default) seq:Add(tweenA) seq:Add(tweenB, 0.1) -- 0.1 s gap before tweenB seq:Play() local par = MotionMaster.Sequence({ Parallel = true }) -- all at once par:Add(tweenC) par:Add(tweenD) par:OnComplete(function() print("all done") end) par:Play()   Sequence methods: :Add(tweenObj, delay?), :Play(), :OnComplete(cb), :Destroy().

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.SplineMove(target, controlPoints, config)​
searchDocs.content: Moves target (a BasePart) along an arc-length-reparameterized Catmull-Rom spline.controlPoints is an array of BasePart instances or Vector3 values (minimum 2).  local tween = MotionMaster.SplineMove(cart, { p0, p1, p2, p3 }, { Duration = 4, Model = "EaseInOutCubic", ConstantSpeed = true, -- default true for SplineMove }) tween:Play()   Returns a TweenObject (same lifecycle methods as above).

searchDocs.title: Formula​
searchDocs.content: f = min(ViewportSize.X / 1920, ViewportSize.Y / 1080) f < 1: MinTextSize = MaxTextSize = round(AuthoredMax * f) -- forced size f >= 1: MaxTextSize = round(AuthoredMax * f), MinTextSize = round(AuthoredMin * f) ScrollBarThickness = round(Authored * f)   Text-size limits are capped at 100: the engine clamps UITextSizeConstraintlimits and TextScaled text at 100 px. On 4K (f = 2), text authored above 50 px at 1080p stops at 100 px.

searchDocs.title: Authoring rule​
searchDocs.content: Tag the ScreenGui ResponsiveScale (Studio Tags panel).Use TextScaled + UITextSizeConstraint on every text. Set MaxTextSizeto the size the text has at 1920×1080 (device emulator) — not higher, or the forced size overflows on phones.Lay out in Scale; lock root containers with UIAspectRatioConstraint.GUIs built with a fit UIScale (TechTreeGui, JumpDriveGui,PartyVoteGui, PerkMenuGui) use fixed TextSize and are not tagged.

searchDocs.title: Behaviour​
searchDocs.content: Only tagged ScreenGuis under the local PlayerGui; NovaChat and Satchel constraints are never touched.Authored values are stored once as Authored<Property> attributes, so rescales never compound and runtime clones carry them.Rescales on Camera.ViewportSize changes (one pass per frame) and rebinds when Workspace.CurrentCamera changes; respawned ScreenGuis are rebound.Do not write MinTextSize/MaxTextSize from other scripts at runtime — change the Authored* attribute instead.

searchDocs.title: Formula​
searchDocs.content: From the SliceScale formula devforum thread(post 5: SliceScale = ViewportSize.Y / 2700, i.e. 0.4 at 1080p), generalised to any designed value:  live SliceScale = designed SliceScale * (ViewportSize.Y / 1080)

searchDocs.title: Authoring rule​
searchDocs.content: Set SliceScale in Studio while the viewport is 1080 px tall (e.g. the 1920×1080 device emulator). That value is captured as the designed value the first time the image appears in PlayerGui.

searchDocs.title: Behaviour​
searchDocs.content: Covers every ImageLabel / ImageButton with ScaleType = Slice under the local PlayerGui, including respawned ScreenGuis and runtime-built UI (e.g. Satchel's slot selector). Set ScaleType before parenting so the image is picked up.Rescales on Camera.ViewportSize changes (debounced to one pass per frame) and rebinds when Workspace.CurrentCamera changes.Scales by height only; width is ignored.Do not write SliceScale from other scripts at runtime — the scaler will overwrite it with the captured designed value on the next resize.

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ArmorController.client.luau	One-line bootstrap: calls ArmorClient.Init() once on join Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ArmorClient.luau	GUI-agnostic read model: ArmorView descriptors, Equip/Recharge commands, Changed signal Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ArmorResultCodes.luau	Frozen result-code enum returned by equip/recharge Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ArmorManager.luau	Owns the PlayerArmor_v2 profile (Owned, Equipped); Absorb, Grant, Equip, Recharge, OwnsAtFullPool Server	src/ServerScriptService/ArmorService.server.luau	Bootstraps ArmorManager.Initialize(); handles ReqEquipArmor/ReqRechargeArmor, gated on a valid bench and proximity Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/WorkbenchStation.luau	IsValidStation/IsPlayerNear — shared bench validity + proximity checks, also used by WorkbenchService Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ArmorConfig.luau	The five-kind Kinds catalog, MaxReductionCap, RESERVE_PER_POINT, STORE_NAME Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/WorkbenchConfig.luau	Five CraftArmor* recipes, each gated by RequiresNode  Packets: ArmorStateSync, ReqEquipArmor, ReqRechargeArmor — see Networking MapSignals: none — armor state travels only over ArmorStateSync; HealthManager calls ArmorManager.Absorb directly rather than through a signal

searchDocs.title: The two types​
searchDocs.content: Every armor kind — Ballistic or Energy — is defined entirely by ArmorConfig.Kinds[kindId] (Type, Tier, BaseReduction, Pool, RequiresNode) plus one persisted number: pool remaining. ArmorManager.Absorb drains that number by whatever damage the hit actually absorbed, identically for both types. The only branch is what happens when the pool reaches zero:  Ballistic — the set is destroyed: owned[kindId] is cleared and, if it was worn, Equipped is cleared too. The player is unarmored until they craft another.Energy — the kind stays in Owned and stays Equipped. Absorb returns the full incoming amount unmitigated (pool <= 0 short-circuits before any reduction), so a drained Energy set simply does nothing until ArmorManager.Recharge refills it.

searchDocs.title: The catalog​
searchDocs.content: ArmorConfig.Kinds is the entire catalog — five kinds, no separate tier ladder (Tiers no longer exists; Tier on a kind is a display badge only):  Kind id	Type	Tier	Reduction	Pool	Research nodeLight	Ballistic	1	0.10	250	Armor_Light MedBallistic	Ballistic	2	0.20	500	Armor_MedBallistic MedEnergy	Energy	2	0.14	700	Armor_MedEnergy HeavyBallistic	Ballistic	3	0.30	900	Armor_HeavyBallistic HeavyEnergy	Energy	3	0.22	1200	Armor_HeavyEnergy  By design, the Energy kind at a given tier always reduces less than its Ballistic counterpart (0.14 vs 0.20 at tier 2; 0.22 vs 0.30 at tier 3) — a refillable reserve trades raw mitigation for never being permanently destroyed. Light has no tier-1 Energy counterpart. Reduction, pool size, type and tier are all derived from this table at read time, so retuning a kind here applies retroactively to every player already holding it.

searchDocs.title: Crafting​
searchDocs.content: Each kind has a matching recipe in WorkbenchConfig.Recipes (CraftArmorLight, CraftArmorMedBallistic, CraftArmorMedEnergy, CraftArmorHeavyBallistic, CraftArmorHeavyEnergy), each with Output = { Kind = "Armor", ArmorKind = "<id>" } and its own RequiresNode gate matching the table above. WorkbenchService's craft handler checks CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(player, output) before consuming materials; for an Armor output that calls ArmorManager.OwnsAtFullPool, so crafting a kind already at full pool is refused up front and costs nothing. Crafting a kind that is owned but damaged (or destroyed, for a Ballistic kind) instead calls ArmorManager.Grant, which refills it to full — recrafting is how a set is repaired. Grant also auto-equips the kind if the player has nothing worn, so a player's first craft is immediately useful without a separate equip step.

searchDocs.title: Mitigation​
searchDocs.content: HealthManager.ApplyDamage is the single damage sink for every attack category (Bullet/AOE/environment/NPC). Its internal applyDamageInternal reads the player's ArmorEfficiency perk bonus and calls ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, efficiency) on every hit — no caching, so crafting, equipping or recharging armor takes effect on the very next hit. Absorb computes reduction = clamp(kind.BaseReduction * (1 + efficiency), 0, ArmorConfig.MaxReductionCap) for whichever kind is equipped, exactly as the armor-efficiency perk (now Plated) already worked before this system existed (see Perks — Armor damage mitigation), then drains the pool by min(amount * reduction, pool). A hit never absorbs more than the pool has left, so the overflow of the hit that breaks a Ballistic set still reaches health in the same call. With nothing equipped, or an Energy kind at zero pool, Absorb returns the full amount and health takes it all.

searchDocs.title: Equipping and recharging​
searchDocs.content: Both Equip and Recharge are workbench actions — ReqEquipArmor and ReqRechargeArmor — handled by ArmorService, which validates the target with WorkbenchStation.IsValidStation and WorkbenchStation.IsPlayerNear (the same checks WorkbenchService uses for crafting) before delegating to ArmorManager. Client input is never trusted: both the bench and the distance are re-derived from server-owned state on every request.  ArmorManager.Recharge(player, kindId, fraction) refills fraction (0..1, how far the workbench hold got) of the reserve the pool Energy can reach: with maxAdd = min(Pool − reserve, Energy × perPoint), a partial hold (fraction < 1) buys whole Energy points only — want = floor(maxAdd × fraction / perPoint) × perPoint, so a short tap never pays a full point for a sliver of reserve — while a full hold takes floor(maxAdd) and may spend one last partial point to top off. It is spent via MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", want, perPoint) — only the points needed, never past the Pool cap. A share that adds nothing returns (true, 0, NONE) without spending. ArmorService trusts the fraction but clamps it to 0..1 (NaN counts as 0): a forged value only skips the hold wait, because the Energy cost scales with the share. It draws on the same material pool Energy the train burns for fuel (mirroring TrainFuelManager.handleRefuel), and needs no serialization: the path is synchronous with no yield point, so two in-flight requests can't interleave.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: ArmorClient is a GUI-free read model, structured like PerkClient/QuestClient: it caches the ArmorStateSync snapshot, exposes IsReady/GetArmors/GetEquipped queries returning ArmorView descriptors, carries the Equip/Recharge request/response calls — both are declared with Packet:Response(...), so calling them on the client yields until the server answers and returns (ok, code) and (ok, reserveAdded, code) respectively; Recharge(bench, kindId, fraction) carries the hold fraction (no optimistic prediction — the server owns ownership and pools) — and fires Changed on every snapshot update. ArmorController.client.luau is the one-line bootstrap that calls ArmorClient.Init() once on join.  The player-facing surface is the Workbench GUI's armory page (ArmoryContainer, reached by the Recharge tab), driven by WorkbenchGuiController. The page is gated on owning at least one armor: with none, the tab, a swipe, gamepad or scroll wheel all bounce back to the workbench page with a "You must wear or craft an armor to access Recharge." toast. The gate checks owned, not worn, because this page is the only place to equip — an unworn owned set (e.g. after a worn Ballistic set broke) must stay reachable. If the last armor breaks while the page is showing, or a reopen lands on it, it silently returns to the workbench page.  Inventory (LeftContainer.ScrollingFrame, titled YOUR ARMOR) — one card per owned kind, cloned from ExampleItem, in ArmorClient.GetArmors() order, with a mint WORN tag on the worn kind. Tapping one selects it (amber stroke; the rest use the line color). With nothing selected (or the selected Ballistic set broke) the selection falls back to the worn kind, then the first owned.Detail (ActionContainer) — uppercased name, a type tag (ENERGY mint / BALLISTIC amber), then a WORN tag for the worn kind or the EquipButton (EQUIP, sends ReqEquipArmor) for any other. Three stat boxes: DAMAGE CUT (base reduction), RECHARGE (YES mint for Energy, NO rust for Ballistic) and ENERGY (pool Energy). Icons borrow the kind's CraftArmor* recipe icon, since ArmorConfig carries no art.Reserve — ReserveTitle reads ARMOR ENERGY for an Energy kind and DURABILITY for a Ballistic kind; ReserveBar.FillBar and ArmorValuePercent show the selected kind's PoolFraction.Recharge — ChargeButton exists only for Energy kinds (Visible = false for Ballistic). It is disabled with the reason in its label when the reserve is full (RESERVE FULL) or the pool has no Energy (NO ENERGY IN STOCK). Holding it (label RECHARGING…) eases the fill toward the level the pool Energy can reach over RECHARGE_HOLD_TIME, and the percent counts up every frame with it. The hold ends on release (anywhere on screen), when the time runs out, on close, or on a tab or armor switch. Every end keeps what was filled: the fill stays where it stopped (the tween is paused, never cancelled — Cancel restores the start value) and ArmorClient.Recharge(bench, id, fraction) sends the share reached. Until the reply lands, repaints leave the fill and percent alone, so nothing snaps back.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Equipping a depleted Energy kind is allowed ArmorManager.Equip does not check the pool — wearing an Energy kind at zero reserve succeeds and returns Codes.NONE. It is worn and worthless until recharged; this is the intended failure mode, not a bug.  A catalog rename or removal drops the profile's copy, not just the display If a kind id is renamed or deleted from ArmorConfig.Kinds, ArmorManager drops it from Owned (and clears Equipped if it was worn) the next time that player's profile loads — silently, with no refund. Renaming a shipped kind id is effectively deleting it for every player who owns it.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Armor Weave (ArmorRechargeBonus): ArmorManager.Recharge refills RESERVE_PER_POINT / Reduce(1, bonus) per Energy point; WorkbenchGuiController shortens the hold to Reduce(RECHARGE_HOLD_TIME, bonus) and previews the same reach.

searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant H as HealthManager (Server) participant A as ArmorManager (Server) participant S as ArmorService (Server) participant C as ArmorClient (Client) Note over H: HealthManager.ApplyDamage(amount, type, ...) H->>A: ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, efficiency) A->>A: reduction = clamp(kind.BaseReduction * (1+efficiency), 0, MaxReductionCap) A->>A: absorbed = min(amount * reduction, pool); pool -= absorbed alt Ballistic pool reaches 0 A->>A: owned[kindId] = nil; Equipped cleared if worn else Energy pool reaches 0 A->>A: kind stays owned + equipped, protects nothing end A->>C: ArmorStateSync:FireClient(owned, equipped) A-->>H: return amount - absorbed H->>H: record.Health -= (amount - absorbed) Note over C,S: EQUIP / RECHARGE (at a Workbench) C->>S: ReqEquipArmor(bench, kindId) / ReqRechargeArmor(bench, kindId, fraction) S->>S: WorkbenchStation.IsValidStation + IsPlayerNear S->>A: ArmorManager.Equip / ArmorManager.Recharge A->>C: ArmorStateSync:FireClient(owned, equipped) A-->>S: (ok, code) / (ok, energyAdded, code) S-->>C: (ok, code) / (ok, energyAdded, code)

searchDocs.title: Season math​
searchDocs.content: The season index is a calendar-month index, not a rolling 30-day window: BattlePassState.seasonIndex(now) = year*12 + (month-1), computed in the timezone defined by BattlePassConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset (a fixed seconds-from-UTC offset, pre-launch default US Eastern -5*3600, mirroring QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset). Being a fixed offset, month boundaries do not track daylight saving.  BattlePassState.seasonIndex(now: number): number BattlePassState.seasonExpiresAt(now: number): number -- unix ts of the 1st of next month   The underlying day math (daysFromCivil) is a pure-integer proleptic-Gregorian calculation (Howard Hinnant's algorithm), so client and server always agree without relying on os.date's host timezone handling. seasonExpiresAt is sent to the client so it can drive a countdown without any client-side date math. The server re-checks online players for a rollover — and refreshes cached premium status — every BattlePassConfig.ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS (default 60s).  The quest system's Season scope (see Quests — Season quests) uses this exact same seasonIndex as its period key, so a battle pass season and its season-long quests always start and end together.

searchDocs.title: EXP earning​
searchDocs.content: There is no gameplay source that awards battle pass EXP directly. Instead, BattlePassManager subscribes to Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted — fired by QuestManager when a Season quest pays (on completion, or by the Season rollover sweep) — and reads the optional Reward.BPExp field off the quest's reward table:  Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted:Connect(function(player, reward) if reward and reward.BPExp then BattlePassManager.AddExp(player, reward.BPExp, "Quest") end end)   Any quest can feed the pass just by adding a BPExp number to its Reward table — no new signal or wiring per quest. The shipped pool leans on this for its dedicated Scope = "Season" quests: three quests (SeasonJunk, SeasonKills, SeasonDistance), the whole set active for the entire month, each paying 0 coins/exp but 3000 BPExp. Daily/Weekly board quests pay coins + EXP only and do not feed the pass (quest board spec, 2026-10-15).

searchDocs.title: Tier track and bulk claim​
searchDocs.content: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[level] (level = 1..MAX_LEVEL, MAX_LEVEL = 60) is a { Free: Reward?, Premium: Reward? } pair. A Reward is either { Type = "Coins", Amount } or { Type = "Item", ItemId } (an empty ItemId = "" marks a milestone slot not filled in yet).  Tier kind	Free row	Premium rowRegular	Coins = 100 + (level-1)*10	Coins = 150 + (level-1)*15 Milestone (15/30/45/60)	Chunkier 500-coin bonus	Empty accessory Item slot (to be filled)  BattlePassConfig.SeasonOverrides[seasonIndex][level] sparsely shadows the base Tiers entry for one specific season only (e.g. swap in a different accessory for one month while keeping the rest of the track the same):  BattlePassState.tierReward(level: number, row: "Free" | "Premium", seasonIndex: number): BattlePassConfig.Reward?   tierReward resolves the override first, falling back to the base table, and is used identically by the server (grant) and client (display) so the two can never disagree.  Level is derived, never stored:  BattlePassState.levelFromExp(exp: number): number BattlePassState.progress(exp: number): (level: number, expIntoLevel: number, expForNextLevel: number)   levelFromExp walks MAX_LEVEL down to 1 and returns the highest level whose cumulative EXP threshold (BattlePassConfig.ExpPerLevel — a flat per-level number or a { [level]: number } table) is met; progress additionally returns the two extra values for a progress bar (both 0 once level >= MAX_LEVEL).  There is only one claim entry point:  function BattlePassManager.ClaimBattlePass(player: Player): (boolean, number, number, number, number)   Packets.ReqClaimBattlePass (no payload) invokes it, and it bulk-banks every unlocked-but-unclaimed reward across both rows in one call — there's no per-tier claim. Premium-row rewards are only granted while the player is currently premium. Claimed flags (ClaimedFree[level] / ClaimedPremium[level]) are set before the grant executes (the same idempotent-guard pattern as QuestManager.ClaimQuest), so a re-entrant call finds nothing outstanding and returns NOTHING_TO_CLAIM rather than double-paying. Returns (ok, reasonCode, freeCount, premiumCount, coinsGranted); counts/coins are 0 on any failure. Result codes (BattlePassResultCodes): OK = 0, NO_PROFILE = 1, NOTHING_TO_CLAIM = 2.

searchDocs.title: Premium (subscriptions)​
searchDocs.content: Premium is never persisted — it's live-resolved from MarketplaceService:GetUserSubscriptionStatusAsync(player, SUBSCRIPTION_ID) and cached in-memory per session (premiumCache, keyed by Player). The cache is (re)populated at three points:  Trigger	WhyJoin	Before the first sweep/replicate MarketplaceService.PromptSubscriptionPurchaseFinished	The prompt closing doesn't guarantee a successful purchase, so status is always re-resolved rather than assumed Periodic rollover tick	Bounds staleness to ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS  resolvePremium yields (a web call), so it only ever runs from spawned contexts — never from the synchronous AddExp/ClaimBattlePass paths, which read the cache. On a false→true transition (a fresh subscribe), onPurchaseFinished retroactively runs a sweep granting the Premium row for every tier already reached this season, so buying mid-season immediately feels rewarding instead of only affecting future tiers. Packets.ReqPromptPremium (no payload, server-initiated) calls MarketplaceService:PromptSubscriptionPurchase — the prompt must originate server-side.  While BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID = "" (the pre-launch default), premium is never granted and the subscription APIs are skipped entirely — resolvePremium short-circuits to false and ReqPromptPremium returns false without calling MarketplaceService, so pre-launch never spams errors for a subscription that doesn't exist yet.

searchDocs.title: Rollover and auto-grant sweep​
searchDocs.content: ensureCurrent (called at the top of AddExp and ClaimBattlePass, on join, and on the rollover tick) compares the profile's stored SeasonIndex against BattlePassState.seasonIndex(os.time()). On a mismatch it first auto-grants every reached-but-unclaimed tier from the old season (Free always; Premium only if the player is currently premium) via the same sweep helper the manual claim uses — nothing earned is lost just because a player never opened a claim UI before the month rolled. It then resets Exp = 0, ClaimedFree = {}, ClaimedPremium = {}, and advances SeasonIndex to the current value. Coins and items already granted by the sweep persist wherever they live (the coin wallet, a future inventory) — only the pass's own tier/EXP bookkeeping resets.

searchDocs.title: Item seam​
searchDocs.content: Item-type rewards fire Signals.OnBattlePassItemGranted(player, itemId) — a seam with no consumer this cycle, reserved for a future inventory/accessory system. Milestone tiers ship with an empty Premium Item slot (ItemId = ""); granting one is a no-op (no signal fires) and logs a one-time warning (warnedEmptyItem, a module-level flag) reminding a developer to fill BattlePassConfig with a real asset before launch. The claimed flag is still set even for an empty slot, so it's marked claimed and never re-offered.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: BattlePassClient is a GUI-agnostic read-model, same shape as QuestClient/PerkClient. It caches the authoritative BattlePassStateSync snapshot and derives per-tier views using the same BattlePassState.tierReward the server grants from:  export type TierView = { Level: number, FreeReward: BattlePassConfig.Reward?, PremiumReward: BattlePassConfig.Reward?, IsUnlocked: boolean, IsFreeClaimed: boolean, IsPremiumClaimed: boolean, }   Exposes GetProgress (level, expIntoLevel, expForNextLevel), GetLevel, IsPremium, GetSeasonExpiresAt, GetTiers (all 60, in order), GetClaimableSummary (a preview of what a Claim() would bank right now — counts + coin total, without actually claiming), and fire-and-forget Claim() / PromptPremium() commands. A Changed signal fires on every snapshot update. No GUI ships this cycle — a future screen requires BattlePassClient and subscribes to Changed.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved battle pass data BattlePassConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerBattlePass") must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places — it's the shared ProfileStore key that lets session-locking hand off cleanly across the teleport boundary. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile: all season progress and claimed flags become unreachable.  An empty ItemId slot grants nothing — and is still marked claimed A milestone Item reward with ItemId = "" is a placeholder. Granting it fires no OnBattlePassItemGranted signal (nothing to grant) but still flips the claimed flag, so the player never sees it offered again even after you fill in a real ItemId later — fill milestone slots before launch.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Season Surge (BPExpBonus): BattlePassManager.AddExp scales BP EXP × (1 + bonus), rounded down, at least 1.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant QM as QuestManager (server) participant BPM as BattlePassManager (server) participant Client as BattlePassClient (owning client) Note over QM: Season quest completes (or Season rollover sweep) QM->>QM: pay() — CoinManager.AddCoins, XPManager.AddXP QM->>BPM: Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted:Fire(player, quest.Reward) alt reward.BPExp present BPM->>BPM: AddExp(player, reward.BPExp) — ensureCurrent() first BPM->>BPM: profile.Data.Exp += amount alt derived level rose BPM->>BPM: Signals.OnBattlePassLevelUp:Fire(player, newLevel) end BPM->>Client: BattlePassStateSync (season, exp, level, progress, claimed, premium, expiresAt) end Note over Client,BPM: bulk CLAIM Client->>BPM: ReqClaimBattlePass() BPM->>BPM: ensureCurrent(); sweep(1..level) — Free always, Premium if isPremium BPM->>BPM: claimed flags set BEFORE grant (idempotent guard) BPM-->>Client: (ok, reasonCode, freeCount, premiumCount, coinsGranted) BPM->>Client: BattlePassStateSync (reconciled snapshot)

searchDocs.content: Config module: BattlePassConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/BattlePassConfig.luauPlaybook: Tune Battle PassQuestConfig.Quests[id].Reward.BPExp (optional) is how a quest feeds the pass; Scope = "Season" quests are the dedicated monthly source — see Tune Quests.  Field	EffectSTORE_NAME	ProfileStore key — change this only if you intentionally want to wipe all saved battle pass progress. SUBSCRIPTION_ID	The Roblox subscription id whose active status unlocks Premium. Empty ("") disables premium entirely and skips the subscription APIs. ResetTimezoneOffset	Fixed seconds-from-UTC offset the calendar-month boundary is measured in (mirrors QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset). No DST tracking. MAX_LEVEL	Top tier of the track (60). ExpPerLevel	BP EXP required per level — a flat number or a { [level]: number } table. ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS	How often the live server tick re-checks online players for a season rollover and refreshes cached premium status. Tiers[level].Free / .Premium	Base reward per tier per row. SeasonOverrides[seasonIndex][level]	Sparse per-season tier reward shadowing, keyed by BattlePassState.seasonIndex.
