Player hitscan against enemies is lag-compensated (see Weapons); enemy fire at players is not.

searchDocs.title: The EnemyBrain director​
searchDocs.content: EnemyBrain is a single module-level loop, not one script per enemy. EnemyBrain.Init() connects one RunService.Heartbeat listener and accumulates dt until TICK_INTERVAL (1 / TICK_HZ, TICK_HZ = 10) has elapsed, then calls tick() once. Every registered enemy is iterated in that single tick — there are no per-enemy RunService connections, task.spawn loops, or while true do task.wait() end patterns. This keeps the cost of N enemies roughly linear and avoids N independent scheduler entries.  Each registered enemy is a Record (an in-memory table, not an Instance) keyed by its Model in a module-level records dictionary:  type Record = { model: Model, humanoid: Humanoid, root: BasePart, profile: Profile, -- EnemyCombatConfig.Profile cleaner: Janitor.Janitor, target: Player?, -- movement waypoints: { PathWaypoint }, waypointIndex: number, pathGoal: Vector3?, nextRepathAt: number, -- firing fireState: "Idle" | "Bursting" | "Cooldown", shotsLeft: number, nextShotAt: number, nextBurstAt: number, telegraphUntil: number?, }   Every tick, for every record that is still alive and rooted, EnemyBrain:  Reacquires a target if the current one is missing or dead — nearestPlayer scans Players:GetPlayers() for the closest player with a living Humanoid and a HumanoidRootPart. Targeting is pure distance; there is no aggro persistence, threat table, or line-of-sight requirement to pick a target (LOS only gates firing, see below).Steps movement (stepMovement) — independent of firing.Steps firing (stepFiringRanged) — independent of movement.  This is the two-concern (move ‖ fire) model: an enemy can be walking toward the player and shooting at the same time (run-and-gun), because neither step blocks or depends on the other completing first within the tick.  Movement and path-compute budgeting​  stepMovement holds the enemy still (Humanoid:MoveTo(currentPosition)) once it is within profile.CloseDistance (default 30) of the target — this "comfort band" makes ranged enemies stop closing once they're inside a distance they consider safe to shoot from, rather than walking into point-blank range. Outside that band, it paths toward the target's HumanoidRootPart position.  Paths are computed via PathfindingService:CreatePath/ComputeAsync, but not on every tick for every enemy. A shared pathBudget of PATH_BUDGET_PER_TICK (1) ComputeAsync calls is allocated per tick and decremented as enemies consume it — with a 10 Hz tick this caps fresh pathfinding compute at ~10 calls/sec total across all enemies, naturally staggering large waves instead of bursting 40 simultaneous ComputeAsync calls in one frame. An enemy only requests a new path when it has none yet, REPATH_INTERVAL (1.0s) has elapsed since its last compute, or the target has drifted more than REPATH_THRESHOLD (8 studs) from the path's original goal — most ticks for most enemies do no path computation at all, they just step along existing waypoints (WAYPOINT_REACHED = 3 studs advances to the next one). If ComputeAsync fails or the budget is exhausted, the enemy falls back to beelining straight at the goal with Humanoid:MoveTo — pathfinding failure is non-fatal, it just degrades to dumb-walk.  Ranged firing: the burst/cooldown state machine​  stepFiringRanged drives a three-state machine per enemy: "Idle" → "Bursting" → "Cooldown" → back to "Idle".  No target, out of range, or no line of sight: firing is suspended and movement keeps closing/repositioning. Critically, if the enemy was mid-burst ("Bursting") when any of these interruptions occurs, its state is reset to "Idle" rather than left to resume later: if rec.fireState == "Bursting" then rec.fireState = "Idle" end This reset exists specifically so that re-engagement always rolls a brand-new burst (startBurst) instead of resuming a stale partial burst whose nextShotAt/shotsLeft may be long expired or, for a sniper, whose Telegraph window has already elapsed. Without the reset, a player could duck behind cover for a moment to skip past a sniper's aim-telegraph and pop back out already inside the weapon's nextShotAt window — defeating the reaction-window fairness the telegraph exists to provide. The fix applies identically to the out-of-range case (LOS-break and range-break share the same reasoning) so the dodge counter-play stays consistent regardless of why the enemy lost its shot. "Cooldown": holds fire until now >= nextBurstAt, then transitions to "Idle". "Idle": immediately calls startBurst, which rolls shotsLeft between BurstMin/BurstMax, sets fireState = "Bursting", and sets nextShotAt = now + Telegraph (0 for non-snipers). For a sniper (Telegraph > 0), this delay before the first shot is the player's reaction window — telegraphUntil is exposed on the record so a future client-side "enemy is aiming at you" cue could read it, though nothing currently renders it. "Bursting": once now >= nextShotAt and shotsLeft > 0, fires one shot (fireOneShot — routes to EnemyWeapon.Lob or EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile depending on profile.FireMode), decrements shotsLeft, and schedules the next shot at now + ShotInterval. When shotsLeft reaches 0, transitions to "Cooldown" and rolls the next burst's start time.  Line of sight is checked every tick a ranged enemy considers firing (hasLineOfSight): a raycast from the muzzle origin to the target's root, excluding the shooter's own model, treats a hit against the target's own character as clear (not blocked) and anything else solid as blocked. This stops enemies shooting through walls; it is a fairness check, not a cover-seeking AI — enemies make no attempt to flank around an obstruction, they simply hold fire and let stepMovement keep closing the distance.  Fairness rationale​  No ammo, ever. Enemies have no magazine or reload — the only throttle on rate of fire is the burst/cooldown rhythm in EnemyCombatConfig. This is a deliberate simplification versus the player's ammo system (Weapons); the challenge lever is burst size and cooldown length, not resource starvation.No hitscan. EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile always launches a travelling FastCast2 projectile at a finite ProjectileSpeed; damage applies on Hit after real flight time elapses, so a player who strafes out of the bullet's path after it's fired takes no damage, exactly like dodging a player-fired bullet.No target leading. Both FireProjectile and Lob aim at the target's current position (targetPos) at the moment of firing, never a predicted future position. Combined with finite projectile speed and Spread (an aim-error cone in degrees, via WeaponValidation.applySpread), this makes every ranged archetype dodgeable by lateral movement, not just by breaking LOS.Sniper telegraph as a reaction window. PirateSniper's Telegraph = 0.6 inserts a fixed delay between entering "Bursting" and the first (and only) shot, giving the player six-tenths of a second of visible aim-up before the highest single-hit damage in the game (Damage = 40) fires. The reset-on-interrupt fix above ensures this window cannot be bypassed by ducking LOS or range right before the shot and popping back — the telegraph always re-applies on re-engagement.

searchDocs.title: EnemyWeapon​
searchDocs.content: EnemyWeapon is the enemy attack action — it owns no timing or ammo state (that's EnemyBrain's job) and instead reuses the exact same player damage layer end to end:  EnemyWeapon.MuzzleOrigin(model, profile) — returns the world position fire should originate from. If the rig has a descendant Attachment named "Muzzle" (an authored weapon model), its WorldPosition is used. Otherwise it falls back to the root part's CFrame offset by profile.MuzzleOffset (default (0, 1.5, -1)) — an art-less first pass that still produces a sensible shoulder-height, slightly forward origin.EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile(model, profile, origin, targetPos) — fires one travelling bullet through a dedicated module-level FastCast2.new() caster (bulletCaster, separate from the player gun caster in WeaponServer, but wired the same way: LengthChanged steps an optional cosmetic part, Hit resolves the struck model via WeaponValidation.resolveHumanoidModel and applies damage via CombatService.ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, damage, "Bullet", enemyModel)). Fires Packets.WeaponFired on both a real hit and a miss-timeout backstop (task.delay guarded by a data.fired flag so a real hit and the timeout can never both resolve), so the tracer always renders even when nothing is struck. The optional cosmetic bullet comes from ServerProjectile.spawnRocket(profile.Weapon, ...) — nil-safe; if no WeaponAssets/<Weapon> template exists, fire still works, just without a visible bullet model.EnemyWeapon.Lob(model, profile, origin, targetPos) — reuses the player grenade path: ServerProjectile.spawnThrowable(weapon, origin, unit, speed, "Bounce", { model }) for a server-replicated physics throw, biased upward (+ Vector3.yAxis * 0.5) so it arcs rather than fires flat. After profile.FuseTime, detonates via CombatService.ApplyAOE and fires Packets.ExplosionAt, then destroys the charge instance. In every case the attacker argument passed to CombatService is the enemy Model, not a Player — CombatService/Factions already supports a non-Player attacker (the Faction of a Model is resolved by its EnemyNPC/FriendlyNPC CollectionService tag), so no changes were needed to the damage router itself to support enemies attacking players. Factions.canDamage("Enemy", "Player") is true by default; the reverse and same-faction pairs are not, which is what prevents enemies from ever damaging each other or friendly NPCs by the same mechanism that prevents player-on-player damage. See Weapons → CombatService and Architecture → Backbone for the faction model itself.

searchDocs.title: EnemyCombatConfig profiles​
searchDocs.content: EnemyCombatConfig holds one Profile per archetype name, keyed identically to the archetype names used in EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes. An archetype with no entry here stays passive — EnemyBrain.Register looks up EnemyCombatConfig.GetProfile(archetypeName) and simply returns without arming the enemy if it's nil. This is the only "is this archetype armed" check in the system — see Studio setup below for the common mistake this invites.  export type FireMode = "Projectile" | "Lob" export type Profile = { Weapon: string, -- FX/sound key (WeaponFx) + WeaponAssets cosmetic name Damage: number, -- Ranged FireMode: FireMode?, -- "Projectile" | "Lob" ProjectileSpeed: number?, -- studs/s; finite + dodgeable Spread: number?, -- aim-error cone (degrees) Range: number?, -- max distance the enemy will fire from CloseDistance: number?, -- pathfind until generously inside Range, then hold MuzzleOffset: Vector3?, -- HRP-relative origin until a "Muzzle" attachment exists -- Burst rhythm (no ammo) ShotInterval: number?, BurstMin: number?, BurstMax: number?, BurstCooldownMin: number?, BurstCooldownMax: number?, Telegraph: number?, -- sniper: seconds aiming before the shot -- Lob-only AOERadius: number?, FuseTime: number?, -- Optional animation asset ids (server rig) FireAnimId: string?, }   EnemyCombatConfig.FindByWeapon(weaponName) linear-scans Profiles for a matching Weapon key — used by WeaponFx to resolve enemy weapon FX by name, the mirror of how it resolves player weapons via WeaponConfig.  Shipped archetypes​  Archetype	Weapon (FX key)	Damage	Fire mode	Projectile speed	Spread	Range / Close	Burst (shots)	Shot interval	Cooldown	TelegraphPirateGruntSMG	EnemySMG	6	Projectile	140	5°	80 / 35	2–5	0.10s	1.2–2.5s	— PiratePistoleer	EnemyPistol	8	Projectile	150	3°	60 / 30	3–5	0.18s	1.5–3.0s	— PirateSniper	EnemySniper	40	Projectile	320	1°	200 / 120	1–1	0s	3.0–4.5s	0.6s PirateGrenadier	EnemyGrenade	50 (AOE r16)	Lob	60	—	90 / 50	1–1	—	3.5–5.0s	—  PirateGrenadier's FuseTime is 2.0s; MuzzleOffset for all archetypes is (0, 1.5, -1) except PirateGrenadier's (0, 2, -1). These archetype names are combat profiles only — they still need a corresponding entry in EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes to ever be spawned in the first place (see Studio setup).

searchDocs.title: WeaponFx bridge and the widened WeaponFired packet​
searchDocs.content: Player weapon FX (impact/explosion sounds) are looked up by weapon name in WeaponConfig. Enemy weapons are a different name (EnemySMG, not SMG) living in a different config module, so a single client FX controller needs a single resolver that checks both. WeaponFx.resolve(weaponName) checks WeaponConfig[weaponName] first, then falls back to EnemyCombatConfig.FindByWeapon(weaponName), returning { ImpactSound?, ExplodeSound? } either way (or an empty table if neither matches). WeaponEffectsController.client.luau calls this for WeaponFired/ExplosionAt instead of indexing WeaponConfig directly — this is the only client-side change needed to render enemy weapon FX through the existing tracer/spark/explosion rendering code.  This works because the WeaponFired packet's shooter field was widened from Player to Instance so it can carry either a Player (player guns) or an enemy Model (EnemyWeapon fire):  local WeaponFired = Packet( "WeaponFired", Packet.Instance :: Instance, -- shooter (Player or enemy Model) Packet.String, -- weaponName Packet.Vector3F32, -- origin (muzzle) Packet.Vector3F32, -- endpoint (hit position or max-range point) Packet.Boolean8 -- isHit )   WeaponEffectsController ignores WeaponFired only when shooter == player (the local player's own gun already drew its own tracer client-side); an enemy Model shooter is never equal to a Player instance, so enemy shots always render for every client, including the player they're aimed at. See the WeaponFired row in the Networking Map for the full packet contract.

searchDocs.title: Lifecycle and cleanup​
searchDocs.content: EnemyBrain.Register(model, archetypeName) is idempotent (returns immediately if the model is already registered) and requires the model to have both a Humanoid (via FindFirstChildOfClass) and a root part (PrimaryPart or HumanoidRootPart) — if either is missing, registration silently no-ops and the enemy stays unarmed. On success, one Janitor is created per record (cleaner) and two connections are added to it, both tagged "Disconnect":  humanoid.Died → EnemyBrain.Unregister(model)model.AncestryChanged (fires when parent becomes nil) → EnemyBrain.Unregister(model)  EnemyBrain.Unregister(model) removes the record from the module-level records table and calls cleaner:Destroy(). This covers both lifecycle exits an enemy can take: dying (Humanoid.Died) and being despawned without dying (wave Despawn/Destroy, or any other code that removes the model from the DataModel — see EnemySpawner → WaveHandle lifecycle). There is no Destroy/Cleanup distinction here (unlike some other Janitor-owning modules in this codebase) because an unregistered enemy record has no further use — the Janitor is always fully torn down.  Within tick() itself, a record whose root.Parent is falsy or whose humanoid.Health <= 0 is skipped for that tick (continue) rather than acted on — the actual removal from records happens asynchronously via the Died/AncestryChanged connections above, so there's a brief window (within the same frame) where a dead enemy's record can still exist but is simply not ticked.

searchDocs.title: Edge cases​
searchDocs.content: Case	BehaviorNo target found (no living, rooted player)	stepMovement halts the enemy in place (MoveTo(currentPosition)); stepFiringRanged resets fireState to "Idle" so the next valid target starts a fresh burst. Target dies or leaves mid-burst	Next tick's targetRoot lookup fails, rec.target is re-acquired via nearestPlayer (or left nil if no one is left), and a stale "Bursting" state is abandoned the same way as the out-of-range/LOS-blocked cases. Target goes out of Range mid-burst	Firing is suspended; a "Bursting" state resets to "Idle" (see the telegraph-reset fix); movement keeps closing. Line of sight blocked mid-burst	Same reset-to-"Idle" behavior as out-of-range; the enemy holds fire and lets movement reposition rather than trying to flank. Friendly fire (enemy vs. enemy, enemy vs. friendly NPC)	Physically impossible by design — CombatService.ApplyToModel gates every hit through Factions.canDamage, and Enemy -> Enemy / Enemy -> Friendly are not in the allow table. Wave despawn while enemies are armed	EnemyWave's Despawn/Destroy removes the enemy Model from the DataModel, which fires model.AncestryChanged with a nil parent, which calls EnemyBrain.Unregister — the brain record and its Janitor are torn down in the same tick the model is destroyed, with no dangling references. Archetype has no EnemyCombatConfig profile	EnemyBrain.Register returns early; the enemy spawns and is fully visible/collidable but never moves toward or fires at players. Enemy model missing Humanoid or root part	EnemyBrain.Register returns early without warning (mirrors EnemySpawner's existing tolerance for placeholder/incomplete rigs during early development).

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: EnemyAssets rig requirements​  An enemy Model in ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/ needs the same minimum viable rig that EnemySpawner already requires for spawning at all: a Humanoid and a PrimaryPart or HumanoidRootPart. EnemyBrain.Register re-checks both of these independently and silently skips arming the enemy if either is missing — so a rig that spawns fine but never moves or fires is almost always missing one of these two parts.  Optional Muzzle attachment​  For a visually accurate origin, add an Attachment named exactly Muzzle anywhere in the rig's descendant hierarchy (typically welded to a held weapon model's barrel tip). EnemyWeapon.MuzzleOrigin finds it via model:FindFirstChild("Muzzle", true) (a recursive search) and fires from its WorldPosition. Without one, fire still works — it falls back to the root part's CFrame offset by the profile's MuzzleOffset, a perfectly playable art-less placeholder. Add the attachment (and a welded weapon model, and optional FireAnimId) whenever art is ready; no code changes are needed either way.  Arming an archetype: the two-registry relationship​  This is the most common setup mistake, so it's worth stating explicitly: an archetype needs entries in BOTH registries to be a functioning armed enemy.  EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes[name] — required for the archetype to spawn at all (Model name, Health, WalkSpeed, DefaultRadius, optional Faction). See Enemy Spawner → Tuning.EnemyCombatConfig.Profiles[name] — required for the spawned enemy to be armed (move toward and fire at players). Keyed by the same archetype name as above.  An archetype with only #1 spawns, walks nowhere on its own, and never fires — useful for cosmetic/decorative NPCs or placeholder testing before combat tuning is ready. An archetype with only #2 (a profile with no matching spawner entry) is simply dead config — EnemySpawner.placeAt is the only call site for EnemyBrain.Register, so a profile with no way to spawn the archetype never gets used. There is no validation or warning today if these two registries drift out of sync (e.g. renaming an archetype in one but not the other) — check both tables by hand when adding or renaming an archetype.  Verifying combat in Studio​  No additional Studio-side wiring is required beyond the two config entries above and the rig requirements — EnemyBrain.Init() is called once automatically by EnemyCombatSystemLoader.server.luau at server start, the same pattern as EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau calling EnemySpawner.Init(). Spawn a wave with an archetype that has both registry entries and the enemy should path toward the nearest player and open fire once in range.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Telegraph and burst values are tuned by feel, not measured ProjectileSpeed, Spread, Telegraph, and the burst/cooldown ranges directly control how dodgeable and how punishing each archetype is. There is no automated test for "is this fair" — these are Studio-playtest-and-adjust knobs, the same as PATH_BUDGET_PER_TICK/REPATH_INTERVAL/REPATH_THRESHOLD/TICK_HZ at the top of EnemyBrain.luau. Adjust archetype values in EnemyCombatConfig directly; avoid touching EnemyBrain's tick/path constants unless movement itself feels laggy or pathfinding spikes with large waves.  Cosmetic bullet/throwable templates are optional, not required EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile's cosmetic bullet (ServerProjectile.spawnRocket) and EnemyWeapon.Lob's throwable charge (ServerProjectile.spawnThrowable) both look up a template by profile.Weapon in ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets. If the named template doesn't exist yet, both functions are nil-safe — the shot/lob still fires, damages, and broadcasts its FX packet; it just has no visible travelling model. Add WeaponAssets/EnemySMG (etc.) whenever art is ready; this is a drop-in, no code change.  Re-engagement always restarts the burst from scratch By design (see the telegraph-reset fix), an enemy that loses LOS or range mid-burst does not "remember" how many shots it had left — it goes back to "Idle" and rolls an entirely new BurstMin–BurstMax count next time it can see and reach the target. This is intentional fairness behavior, not a bug: do not "fix" it by trying to persist shotsLeft/nextShotAt across an interruption, as that would let a player skip past a sniper's telegraph window by breaking LOS for a single frame.

searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant B as EnemyBrain (10 Hz tick) participant W as EnemyWeapon participant FC as FastCast2 (bulletCaster) participant CS as CombatService participant Fx as WeaponEffectsController (all clients) Note over B: tick(): reacquire target -> stepMovement -> stepFiringRanged B->>B: stepFiringRanged: fireState machine (Idle -> Bursting -> Cooldown) B->>B: hasLineOfSight? in Range? else reset "Bursting" -> "Idle" B->>W: fireOneShot -> EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile(model, profile, origin, targetPos) W->>FC: cast bullet at ProjectileSpeed (+ Spread) FC-->>W: LengthChanged (steps optional cosmetic part) FC-->>W: Hit(target) OR miss-timeout backstop W->>CS: CombatService.ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, Damage, "Bullet", enemyModel) CS->>CS: Factions.canDamage("Enemy","Player") gate CS->>CS: HealthManager.ApplyDamage (armor mitigation) W->>Fx: Packets.WeaponFired(shooter=enemyModel, weaponName, origin, endpoint, isHit) Fx->>Fx: WeaponFx.resolve(weaponName) -> WeaponConfig or EnemyCombatConfig.FindByWeapon Fx->>Fx: render tracer + impact FX (shooter is never == local Player, so always renders)

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleServer	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EventOrchestrator.luau	Odometer loop, per-channel state machines, weighted roll + pity, handler registry Server	src/ServerScriptService/EventSystemLoader.server.luau	Bootstrap — registers handlers, calls EventOrchestrator.Init() Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/Events/PirateAttackEvent.luau	Handler stub; wires to EnemySpawner.SpawnWave Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/Events/VoidSwarmEvent.luau	Void channel: rolls a void enemy pack from the biome table and spawns it via VoidEnemyService (Void Enemies) Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/Events/OutpostEvent.luau	Handler stub; side-attribute marker for a fixed window Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EventConfig.luau	Cruise speed, tick interval, per-channel roll tables/cadence, per-event parameters, master enable switch  Packets: none — the orchestrator never touches networking; each handler owns its own client communicationSignals: OnGameEventStarted, OnGameEventEnded — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Master switch​
searchDocs.content: EventConfig.Enabled gates the entire system — while false, EventOrchestrator.Init() registers nothing, builds no channels, and never starts the odometer loop; the orchestrator stays fully dormant. It is true. Each channel also has its own Enabled field: a channel with Enabled = false is never built or validated. Encounter is off until Pirate Attack and Outpost are finished (see TODO.md); Void is on.

searchDocs.title: The virtual odometer​
searchDocs.content: The train has no physical speed/odometer of its own — TrainFuelManager only tracks Running/Braked/Stalled state. EventOrchestrator owns its own distance counter: a task.spawn loop ticks every EventConfig.TickInterval seconds (0.25s by default — ample precision for event cadence and cheaper than a per-frame Heartbeat). While running is true it accumulates EventConfig.CruiseSpeed * dt into the odometer, then ticks every channel. running is driven by Signals.SetTrainState (fired by TrainFuelManager on every brake/stall flip) — accumulation pauses on brake, stall, and the pre-game freeze. Signals.SetTrainStarted(true) (first un-brake of a round) calls EventOrchestrator.Reset(), zeroing the odometer and returning every channel to Idle, including force-finishing any handler that's currently Active via its finish().

searchDocs.title: Channel model​
searchDocs.content: Channels run fully independently, each with its own roll table, cadence, and state:  Encounter (off: Enabled = false) — PirateAttack and Outpost share this channel and are mutually exclusive (only one can be active at a time).Void — VoidSwarm only. Rolls every 600 studs; the handler's CanTrigger stays closed until a weapon is researched or the first jump, then applies the current biome's chance. See Void Enemies — Spawning.  Each channel is a state machine: Idle → Active → Cooldown → Idle.  Phase	BehaviorIdle	Every RollInterval boundary crossed since the last tick rolls the weighted table once (a long pause/lag spike doesn't skip rolls). A real pick moves the channel to Active. Active	The chosen handler's Start(ctx, finish) is running. A MaxActiveDistance watchdog (if > 0) force-finishes a handler that never calls finish(). Other channels keep rolling independently. Cooldown	After finish(), the channel stays quiet until PostEventDelay odometer studs have passed, then returns to Idle with lastRollAt reset to the current odometer (the next roll is a full RollInterval away, not immediate).

searchDocs.title: Weighted roll + pity​
searchDocs.content: Each channel's Table is a list of RollEntrys — either a real event ({ Event = "PirateAttack", Weight = 50 }) or the no-op entry ({ Nothing = true, Weight = 20 }). On each roll:  Build the eligible candidate set: real entries are excluded if their handler's optional CanTrigger(ctx) returns false (or no handler is registered for that Id); the Nothing entry is excluded outright when pity is forcing a real event.Pick one candidate by weight (Random:NextNumber(0, total) against cumulative weight).If the pick is Nothing (or nothing was eligible), emptyRollStreak increments and the channel stays Idle.If the pick is a real event, emptyRollStreak resets to 0 and the channel activates that event's handler.  Pity: once emptyRollStreak >= PityRolls, the next roll excludes the Nothing entry, forcing a real event. This bounds the maximum distance a channel can go without a real event to roughly (PityRolls + 1) * RollInterval studs.

searchDocs.title: EventHandler interface​
searchDocs.content: export type EventContext = { odometer: number, -- current odometer value at roll/activation time rng: Random, -- orchestrator-owned Random instance channel: string, -- the channel name this activation belongs to janitor: Janitor.Janitor, -- per-activation Janitor; destroyed automatically on finish() } export type EventHandler = { Id: string, -- unique; must match an EventConfig table entry Channel: string, -- which channel this handler is registered under CanTrigger: ((ctx: EventContext) -> boolean)?, -- optional eligibility guard, checked at roll time Start: (ctx: EventContext, finish: () -> ()) -> (), -- begin the event; call finish() exactly once when done }   Handlers register via EventOrchestrator.RegisterHandler(handler) (call before Init(), from the system loader). A duplicate Id is ignored with a warn. Start runs inside a pcall; a throwing handler is logged and the channel is force-finished into Cooldown so one bad event can't wedge the channel. finish is guarded by a per-activation nonce — late or duplicate calls (e.g. a watchdog firing after the handler already finished normally) are no-ops. ctx.janitor is destroyed automatically the moment finish() resolves, so handlers should hang connections/instances/cleanup off it rather than tearing down manually. A load-time validation pass (validate() in Init) warns if a config table references an Id with no registered handler, or a handler's Channel doesn't match the channel it's listed under (or targets an unknown channel) — these are warnings, not hard errors, matching the EnemySpawnerConfig missing-model convention.

searchDocs.title: Public API​
searchDocs.content: EventOrchestrator.RegisterHandler(handler: EventHandler)   Registers a handler module. Call before Init() (from the system loader).  EventOrchestrator.Init()   Builds channel state from EventConfig.Channels, runs the validation pass, subscribes to Signals.SetTrainState / Signals.SetTrainStarted, and starts the odometer loop. No-ops entirely while EventConfig.Enabled is false; skips channels whose Enabled is false. Idempotent otherwise — a second call warns and is ignored.  EventOrchestrator.Reset()   Zeroes the odometer, force-finishes any Active channel (via its handler's finish), and returns every channel to Idle with lastRollAt reseeded from StartGrace. Called automatically on Signals.SetTrainStarted(true).  EventOrchestrator.GetState()   Returns a snapshot (odometer, running, per-channel phase/lastRollAt/emptyRollStreak/activeId/cooldownUntil) for debugging/inspection.

searchDocs.title: The two event handlers (stubs)​
searchDocs.content: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/Events/ holds one module per event, each implementing EventHandler. Both are intentionally thin — full behavior is deferred to later, per-event specs:  PirateAttackEvent (Channel = "Encounter") — calls EnemySpawner.SpawnWave with the group/wave composition from EventConfig.Events.PirateAttack, hangs the returned WaveHandle off ctx.janitor (so a force-finish despawns survivors), and calls finish when WaveHandle.OnCleared fires. It also sets the replicated workspace attribute PirateAttackActive = true on start; its janitor sets it back to false on every end path (wave cleared, watchdog, reset, jump pause) — Free Runner reads it. This is the one handler with "real" wiring; wave difficulty/rewards are a later spec.OutpostEvent (Channel = "Encounter") — picks a side via ctx.rng, sets a workspace attribute (ActiveOutpostSide), and calls finish after a fixed distance window approximated as time at CruiseSpeed (a handler has no direct access to the live odometer tick). Approach telegraph, stop-by prompt, and outpost contents are a later spec.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Channel switches A channel with Enabled = false never rolls (Encounter is off). If an event "isn't firing" in a playtest, check its channel's Enabled, then the master EventConfig.Enabled.  Reset force-finishes Active handlers, not Cooldown EventOrchestrator.Reset() only calls activeFinish() for a channel currently in the Active phase. A channel in Cooldown is simply snapped back to Idle — there's no handler running to finish. A round reset mid-cooldown discards the cooldown window rather than honoring it.  OutpostEvent's window is time-based, not distance-based Because a handler doesn't have direct access to the live odometer tick, OutpostEvent approximates its Window (studs) as Window / EventConfig.CruiseSpeed seconds and uses task.delay. If the train brakes or stalls during the window, the outpost still ends on the original wall-clock timer rather than pausing with the odometer. Called out as a stub limitation in the handler's own doc comment.  Channels are independent; "Encounter" exclusivity is per-channel, not global PirateAttack and Outpost cannot overlap because they share the Encounter channel. A future event on its own channel could roll and activate while an Encounter event is Active; one needing true global exclusivity would need an explicit cross-channel guard (e.g. a CanTrigger that inspects another channel's state).  Biome change is now a player-initiated Jump Drive action, not a random orchestrator event — see Jump Drive.

searchDocs.title: Future directions​
searchDocs.content: See the design spec's "Out of scope" section: full Pirate-attack behavior (wave composition/difficulty/rewards), full Outpost behavior (approach telegraph, stop-by prompt, contents, departure), any client HUD/banner, and persistence of event history across sessions.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Fuel as TrainFuelManager participant Orc as EventOrchestrator participant H as EventHandler (e.g. PirateAttackEvent) Fuel->>Orc: Signals.SetTrainStarted(true) Orc->>Orc: Reset() - zero odometer, all channels Idle Fuel->>Orc: Signals.SetTrainState(isRunning) Orc->>Orc: running = isRunning loop every TickInterval while running Orc->>Orc: odometer += CruiseSpeed * dt Orc->>Orc: tickChannel() per channel alt Idle, RollInterval boundary crossed Orc->>Orc: weightedPick() - CanTrigger filter, pity check alt real event picked Orc->>Orc: activate() - phase=Active Orc->>H: Signals.OnGameEventStarted(eventId); Start(ctx, finish) else Nothing / no eligible candidate Orc->>Orc: emptyRollStreak += 1 end else Active, MaxActiveDistance exceeded Orc->>H: force-call finish() (watchdog), warn end end H->>Orc: finish() Orc->>Orc: ctx.janitor:Destroy(); phase=Cooldown; cooldownUntil = odometer + PostEventDelay Orc->>Orc: Signals.OnGameEventEnded(eventId)

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: EventConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EventConfig.luau  Field	Scope	EffectEnabled	global	Master on/off switch. false disables the orchestrator entirely (no registration, no loop). Enabled	per channel	false = channel never built (no rolls). Omitted = on. CruiseSpeed	global	Virtual odometer rate in studs/sec, accumulated only while the train is running. TickInterval	global	Seconds between odometer-loop ticks (task.wait cadence). Weight	per roll-table entry	Relative chance this entry (event or Nothing) is picked on a roll. RollInterval	per channel	Odometer studs between roll attempts on this channel. PostEventDelay	per channel	Quiet studs after an event's finish() before the channel resumes rolling. PityRolls	per channel	Consecutive empty rolls before the Nothing entry is excluded, forcing a real event. StartGrace	per channel	Odometer offset before the channel's first roll (keeps players from being ambushed the instant the train starts moving). MaxActiveDistance	per channel	Watchdog: if an Active handler hasn't called finish() within this many odometer studs, the orchestrator force-finishes it with a warn. 0 disables the watchdog.  Current channel values for Encounter and the per-event parameter tables (EventConfig.Events.PirateAttack / .Outpost) live directly in the config module — see it for exact numbers, since those are expected to be tuned independently of this page.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPack/Grabhook/GrabHook.client.luau	Tool activation, spherecast aim, force-field highlight, grapple animation orchestration, sound scheduling Server	src/ServerScriptService/JunkService.server.luau	Validates claim/finalize requests (see Junk) Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/GrabHookVisuals.luau	Beam creation and projectile / observer animation loops Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/GrabHookConfig.luau	All physics, visuals, and sound timing constants  Packets: none directly — claims/finalizes flow through Packets.ReqJunkClaim / ReqJunkClaimBatch / ReqJunkFinalize, fired by JunkController on behalf of the GrabHook (see Junk and Networking Map)Signals: TryClaimJunk, TryClaimJunkBatch, TryFinalizeJunk, RequestShootingCamera, RequestReticleScale — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Aiming​
searchDocs.content: GrabHook.client.luau runs entirely as a LocalScript inside the Grabhook Tool under StarterPack. On equip, mouse.TargetFilter is set to the PlacedObjects folder so placed items don't occlude aim, and Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true) puts CameraController into aim mode. Every RenderStepped frame while equipped, GetAimedJunk(rootPart) performs a Spherecast from the handle's Attachment.WorldPosition toward mouse.Hit.Position — radius Physics.HitboxRadius (2 studs), max distance Physics.MaxDistance (150 studs), gated to within 90° of the character's forward vector. The junk ID is resolved by invoking GetJunkIdFromPart via BindableCore (registered by JunkController).  A force-field highlight (ReplicatedStorage/ForceField template cloned to workspace) tracks the currently aimed junk part on every RenderStepped tick; if aim is found it calls ShowForceField(junkPart, junkId), and a 0.08-second grace window prevents flickering (HideForceField) when the spherecast briefly misses.

searchDocs.title: Firing​
searchDocs.content: On tool.Activated, if no earlier cast is still reeling in (canShoot), the client fires Signals.TryClaimJunk(id, hitPoint) (handled by JunkController), increments fireToken to version all pending callbacks, then calls FireGrappleAndAttach(targetPart, hitPoint, junkId, token):  Creates an Attachment on the junk part ("HookAttachment").Calls GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam(handleAtt, junkAtt, targetPart).Calls GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile, a three-phase animation: Flight (junkAtt.WorldPosition lerps toward the junk at Physics.Speed = 200 studs/s, beam curves oscillate with Amplitude=12, Frequency=40, Decay=4), Latch (a single transition frame, curves flattened to 0), Retract (targetPart.Position lerps back to the handle at Physics.RetractSpeed = 50 studs/s).On retract complete, fires Signals.TryFinalizeJunk(id) (handled by JunkController).  SoundManager.PlaySFXAt("GrabHookFire") plays a shot replicated to all clients; SoundManager.PlayLooped("GrabHookLoop") schedules a fade-in/out loop. When retraction completes, the collector hears the 2D MaterialCollect cue (the same cue the Materials HUD plays), so Wood/Metal pickups are as audible as Energy. The loop sound is scheduled with a LoopStartDelay (0.15 s) fade-in and a timed fade-out matched to the total hook animation duration.

searchDocs.title: Unequipping​
searchDocs.content: On unequip, fireToken is incremented (invalidating all pending task.delay callbacks), loopHandle:Destroy() runs, and Signals.RequestShootingCamera(false) returns CameraController to its normal mode.

searchDocs.title: Wide Net perk (multi-catch)​
searchDocs.content: The WideNet perk (see Perks) raises hook capacity beyond 1. netCapacity() reads NetCapacityBonus client-side through PerkBuffRead.Personal: capacity = 1 + NetCapacityBonus. At capacity 1 (no perk levels) the tool is byte-for-byte identical to the base single-hook path (GetAimedJunk + Signals.TryClaimJunk). At capacity ≥ 2:  Aim — GetAimedJunks(rootPart, capacity) replaces the single spherecast with workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox at GrabHookConfig.Physics.NetHitboxRadius (4 studs) along the aim line, returning up to capacity NetTargets ({ id, part, hitPos }) sorted by distance.Fire — one tool.Activated still means one cast (the next cast waits for the last beam), one GrabHookFire sound, and one loop sound, but drives a beam per target. Claim ids are batched through Signals.TryClaimJunkBatch:Fire(ids) (consumed by JunkController, which invokes Packets.ReqJunkClaimBatch) instead of the per-junk TryClaimJunk. Finalize remains per-junk (Signals.TryFinalizeJunk / ReqJunkFinalize) once each beam's retraction completes.Server clamp — JunkService.ClaimJunkBatchForPlayer never trusts the client's capacity or positions: it re-reads NetCapacityBonus from the published buff folder, clamps to GrabHookConfig.Physics.NetMaxTargets (5, hard cap), and reconstructs each junk's position from the junk odometer (SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer)) before reserving it.Reticle — on equip, if netCapacity() >= 2, fires Signals.RequestReticleScale(CameraConfig.NetReticleScale) (1.6×) so CameraController enlarges the aim reticle; otherwise fires RequestReticleScale(1). Unequip always fires RequestReticleScale(1) unconditionally, so the reticle never gets stuck enlarged.Highlighting — the force-field highlight loop shows one force field per currently-aimed NetTarget instead of a single one when capacity ≥ 2.Reel slowdown — a fuller net reels slower: the reel speed is multiplied by PerkBuffRead.NetReelFactor(caught) = max(0.1, 1 − 0.10 × (caught − 1)). The client uses the aimed count; the server uses the count it accepted when it times BeginJunkRetract.

searchDocs.title: Shared visuals​
searchDocs.content: GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam(att0, att1, parent) instantiates a Beam and copies all properties from GrabHookConfig.Visuals onto it. AnimateProjectile(beam, startAtt, targetPart, hitPos, onCleanup, retractSpeed?) (reel speed with perks applied; defaults to Physics.RetractSpeed) runs the three-phase RenderStepped loop (Flight / Latch / Retract), aborts if targetPart leaves workspace (e.g. pool reclaim), and calls onCleanup when retraction completes or on abort. AnimateObserver(beam, startAtt) is a simpler decay loop for other players watching the retraction animation, started by JunkController on BeginJunkRetract.

searchDocs.title: Server-side validation​
searchDocs.content: ReqJunkClaim reconstructs junk world position from SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer), checks player distance against MaxDistance × (1 + HookRangeBonus) + 15 studs, rejects the claim while the player still has a pull in flight (reserved, not collected, before its reel-in end), and reserves the junk. There is no time cooldown: the next cast is allowed as soon as the pulled junk lands. ReqJunkFinalize checks reservation ownership and the reservation deadline (reel-in time + 5 s), marks the junk collected, broadcasts JunkCollected, and gives the corresponding tool to player.Backpack. See Junk for the full server-side claim/finalize detail.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Server proximity check uses a latency slack of 15 studs The claim check compares the player's position against the reconstructed junk position with GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15. The extra 15 studs compensates for network latency. Increasing MaxDistance without adjusting the slack (or vice versa) can allow or block claims unexpectedly.  Shift-lock / aim camera interplay. Equipping the GrabHook fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true) to enter aim mode. Unequipping fires (false) to exit. If you add another system that also drives RequestShootingCamera, ensure the signals do not conflict (last writer wins).mouse.TargetFilter = PlacedObjects prevents placed items from blocking the aim raycast. If new workspace folders are added for collidable world geometry that should also be ignored, add them to the filter.fireToken versioning. Incrementing fireToken on unequip cancels all pending task.delay callbacks (sound fade-out, finalize). Never skip the token check inside scheduled callbacks or sounds will play on the next hook cycle.Force-field template must exist. GrabHook.client uses ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForceField") at startup. If the template is missing, the script will yield indefinitely.Beam and attachment cleanup. AnimateProjectile destroys both the Beam and the HookAttachment on cleanup. If you add more attachments or constraints to the junk part during a hook cycle, extend the CleanupJunkModel function in JunkController to remove them on pool return.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Wide Net (permanent, HookAimBonus 0.05/level): GrabHook.client scales HitboxRadius and NetHitboxRadius × (1 + HookAimBonus). Client only: the server checks reach distance, and REACH_SLACK covers the wider cast.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant G as GrabHook (client) participant Cam as CameraController participant JC as JunkController participant S as JunkService (server) P->>G: Equip GrabHook tool G->>Cam: RequestShootingCamera(true) loop RenderStepped while equipped G->>G: GetAimedJunk - Spherecast toward mouse.Hit alt junk found G->>G: ShowForceField(junkPart, junkId) else aim lost > 0.08s G->>G: HideForceField end end P->>G: tool.Activated (no cast in flight) G->>JC: Signals.TryClaimJunk(id, hitPoint) JC->>S: ReqJunkClaim S->>JC: BeginJunkRetract (broadcast) G->>G: FireGrappleAndAttach: Flight -> Latch -> Retract G->>JC: Signals.TryFinalizeJunk(id) JC->>S: ReqJunkFinalize S->>JC: JunkCollected (broadcast) P->>G: Unequip tool G->>Cam: RequestShootingCamera(false)

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: GrabHookConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/GrabHookConfig.luauSee also Junk — Adjust Junk Flow for the claim/collection side of the loop.Perks: ReelSpeedBonus (reel speed ×(1+b), Wide Net ×NetReelFactor), HookRangeBonus (reach ×(1+b)), NetCapacityBonus (net size). The client (GrabHook.client) and the server (JunkService) apply the same PerkBuffRead math. The reel bonus now also drives GrabHookVisuals and the server BeginJunkRetract time (before the Perk Rework it changed only the loop-sound timing).  Physics  Field	Default	EffectPhysics.MaxDistance	150 studs	Maximum hook range; also used as server proximity threshold base Physics.HitboxRadius	2 studs	Spherecast radius for junk detection Physics.NetHitboxRadius	4 studs	Box-cast radius used instead of HitboxRadius when the Wide Net perk is active (capacity ≥ 2) Physics.NetMaxTargets	5	Server hard cap on batch-claim size, independent of the perk's own MaxLevel clamp Physics.Speed	200 studs/s	Hook projectile travel speed (Flight phase) Physics.RetractSpeed	50 studs/s	Junk retraction speed (Retract phase) Physics.Amplitude	12	Starting beam curve amplitude Physics.Frequency	40	Beam oscillation frequency Physics.Decay	4	Rate at which rope curvature decays during flight  Visuals  Field	Default	EffectVisuals.Width0 / Width1	0.5	Beam start/end width Visuals.Segments	20	Beam segment count (affects curve smoothness) Visuals.TextureSpeed	-1	Negative value scrolls texture toward the hook tip Visuals.LightInfluence	1	Beam responds fully to scene lighting  Sound timing  Field	Default	EffectSounds.LoopStartDelay	0.15 s	Delay before loop sound starts playing Sounds.LoopFadeInDuration	0.2 s	Loop sound fade-in time Sounds.LoopFadeOutDuration	0.25 s	Loop sound fade-out time

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/HealthController.client.luau	Minimal bridge: HealthStateSync → Signals.OnHealthValueChanged Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/HealthManager.luau	Authoritative health record, regen heartbeat, ApplyDamage, HealPlayer Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ArmorManager.luau	Owns crafted armor; Absorb is the mitigation seam HealthManager calls at the damage sink Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/HealthConfig.luau	HPMultiplier (scales every HP amount), MaxHealth, regen rate/delay, regen kill-switch Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ArmorConfig.luau	The five-kind armor catalog, reduction cap — see Armor  Packets: HealthStateSync — see Networking MapSignals: OnHealthValueChanged — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Server: authoritative record and regen heartbeat​
searchDocs.content: HealthManager is bootstrapped by HealthSystemLoader.server.luau via HealthManager.Initialize(). It maintains a HealthRecord per player (Health, LastDamageTime, LastSyncTime, LastSyncedHealth), created on PlayerAdded and deleted on PlayerRemoving — no stale data persists across sessions. CharacterAdded unconditionally resets record.Health to MaxHealth and mirrors it to humanoid.MaxHealth/humanoid.Health.  The regen heartbeat runs on RunService.Heartbeat, capped at MAX_HEALTH_STEP_DT = 0.1 seconds per step to prevent delta-time spikes from applying burst healing. While eligible (alive, not full, past RegenDelay since last damage), it adds HealthRegen * HPMultiplier * dt to the record each step. Syncs are batched: regen fires HealthStateSync at most every HEALTH_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 seconds, or immediately when health reaches full.

searchDocs.title: Damage and armor mitigation​
searchDocs.content: HealthManager.ApplyDamage validates AttackType/AOEVariant, clamps the amount to [0, MaxHealth / HPMultiplier] (amounts arrive at 100-HP scale), then applies armor mitigation, then scales what is left by HPMultiplier before subtracting from the record:  amount = ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, efficiency) amount *= HPMultiplier -- armor works at 100-HP scale, so its pools keep their meaning record.Health -= amount record.LastDamageTime = os.clock() humanoid.Health = record.Health -- HealthStateSync:FireClient(player, record.Health)   applyDamageInternal reads PerkBuffs/<UserId>.ArmorEfficiency (the Plated perk) and calls ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, efficiency) on every hit — Absorb is the mitigation seam: it looks up the player's equipped kind, computes clamp(kind.BaseReduction * (1 + efficiency), 0, ArmorConfig.MaxReductionCap), drains the kind's pool by the amount absorbed, and returns what's left to subtract from health. Crafting, equipping, recharging or respeccing the perk all take effect on the next hit; with nothing equipped, or an Energy kind at zero pool, Absorb returns the full amount unmitigated. The old ReplicatedStorage/ArmorState folder and its ArmorBaseReduction attribute no longer exist — mitigation is a direct function call, not a published attribute. See Armor for the two armor types and Perks for the cap rationale and the attacker-bonus-then-armor multiplication order. HealthManager.HealPlayer is the mirror path: record.Health = min(MaxHealth, record.Health + amount * HPMultiplier), mirrored and synced the same way. It ignores a dead player, so a heal never revives.

searchDocs.title: Temporary shields​
searchDocs.content: Each health record holds Shields: source name → list of entries { amount, expiresAt }, at 100-HP scale (pure math in ShieldMath). HealthManager.AddShield(player, source, amount, seconds, maxStacks) adds an entry (the one ending first drops past maxStacks). In ApplyDamage the order is: Shock Absorber → shields (Plating, then Scrap, then Spawn; inside a source the entry that expires first drains first; expired entries take nothing) → armor → × HPMultiplier → health. A hit a shield takes in full still sets LastDamageTime (regen delay, Recharge Plating) and still syncs. The Heartbeat prunes ended entries for every live player, even with RegenEnabled = false, and re-syncs when the total changes. A respawn clears all shields.  HealthStateSync(health, shield) carries the live shield total × HPMultiplier. HealthStaminaGuiController draws it as the mint ShieldCells row under the health cells (10 cells, fill = shield ÷ max health, capped at full) and adds +N to the health value; the row is hidden while the shield is 0.  CombatService is the only caller of ApplyDamage for weapon and NPC-collision damage — see Weapons → CombatService for the routing logic.

searchDocs.title: Client bridge​
searchDocs.content: HealthController.client.luau listens to Packets.HealthStateSync.OnClientEvent and re-fires Signals.OnHealthValueChanged with the received health value. It owns no state. HealthStaminaGuiController (not part of this system) consumes OnHealthValueChanged to draw the HUD: 10 health cells, a damage chip that holds the old HP for 0.35 s then eases down, and a red pulse at 25 % health or less.

searchDocs.title: Dev command​
searchDocs.content: /hurt (aliases /damage, /dmg) in the chat command bar damages the caller for 10% of their own max health, for exercising the HUD and the damage pipeline. It is registered client-side in NovaChat's Commands.client.luau and handled by DevCommandsService.server.luau, which gates it on place owner / group rank 250+ and ignores unauthorised callers. It routes through HealthManager.ApplyDamage, so armour reduction applies — the health actually lost is less than 10% whenever the player has armour.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: HUD instance names are load-bearing HealthStaminaGui is a fixed tree: MainContainer → Content → Gauge → Labels / Well / Values, with HealthCells, ShieldCells and StaminaCells each holding Cell1…Cell10 (Fill, plus Ghost on health cells). The controller looks every one up by name at load and sets each cell's Fill X scale to clamp(value / max × 10 − (i − 1), 0, 1). Renaming any of them in Studio breaks the HUD. The full tree is in the controller's doc-comment.  Non-CombatService damage bypasses HealthManager Any damage source that writes directly to Humanoid.Health — such as default Roblox fall damage or unrouted hazards — bypasses HealthManager's internal record, causing the HUD to show a stale value and skipping armor mitigation. Before shipping such a source, either disable it or listen to Humanoid.HealthChanged and reconcile the record.  One-way mirror: HealthManager writes record.Health → humanoid.Health but never reads back from the Humanoid. Any external write to humanoid.Health is invisible to the manager until a HealthStateSync event corrects the client. Keep all health mutations going through HealthManager.ApplyDamage or HealthManager.HealPlayer.  HP scale: every HP amount passed to ApplyDamage / HealPlayer and every HP number in configs (enemy damage, healing, the lifesteal cap) is at 100-HP scale. To raise player health, change HealthConfig.HPMultiplier, never each damage source. SetHealth / GetHealth / GetMaxHealth are absolute (/hurt divides the multiplier back out).  Roblox default regen is off: an empty Script StarterCharacterScripts.Health (from src/StarterPlayer/StarterCharacterScripts/Health.server.luau) replaces Roblox's built-in regen script, which raised Humanoid.Health behind the record.  Character respawn resets health: CharacterAdded unconditionally resets record.Health to MaxHealth. Characters no longer respawn by themselves in the Game Instance: ReviveService turns off CharacterAutoLoads and respawns a player only on a paid or ad revive (see Paid Revive). If a partial-health respawn mechanic is ever needed, this reset must be conditional.  Sync rate: HealthStateSync is sent at most every 0.1 seconds during regen, but every ApplyDamage call forces an immediate sync — avoid calling it in tight per-frame loops.  Coverage is bounded by the chokepoint: damage that bypasses HealthManager.ApplyDamage also bypasses armor mitigation.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Shock Absorber (AOEResist): AOE hits are reduced (PerkBuffRead.Reduce) before armor.Quick Recovery (RegenDelayReductionPct): cuts a percent of the regen delay left after Field Medic's seconds; the delay stays at least 1 s.Vampire Rounds (Lifesteal 0.03): CombatService heals the attacker by 3% of the NPC health a player's hit actually removed (any weapon), at most ShopPerkConfig.LIFESTEAL_MAX_PER_SECOND (2) per second, through HealthManager.HealPlayer.Rally Banner (RallyRegenBonus 0.20, party): regen rate ×(1 + RegenBonus + rally) while another live player is within ShopPerkConfig.RALLY_RADIUS (20 studs) — PerkBuffRead.Rally.Recharge Plating (PlatingShieldHP 15): after ShopPerkConfig.PLATING_RECHARGE_DELAY (8 s) without a hit, the Heartbeat refills the Plating shield to 15 (no timeout). It drains before Scrap Shield. A respawn refills it at once.Fresh Start (SpawnShieldPct 0.30): on CharacterAdded, after the shield reset, HealthManager adds one Spawn shield worth 30% of max health (MaxHealth ÷ HPMultiplier at 100-HP scale, so it follows HPMultiplier) for ShopPerkConfig.FRESH_START_SECONDS (90 s). It drains last, after Plating and Scrap. The first spawn of a run can come before the perk buffs publish, so that spawn can miss the shield.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant S as HealthManager (Server) participant H as Humanoid participant C as HealthController (Client) Note over S: PlayerAdded -> create HealthRecord{Health=MaxHealth} Note over S: CharacterAdded -> reset Health to MaxHealth S->>H: humanoid.MaxHealth / humanoid.Health = record.Health S->>C: HealthStateSync:FireClient(player, health) C->>C: Signals.OnHealthValueChanged:Fire(health) loop RunService.Heartbeat (server) alt regen eligible (alive, not full, past RegenDelay) S->>S: record.Health += HealthRegen * dt S->>H: humanoid.Health = record.Health opt periodic sync (0.1s) or full S->>C: HealthStateSync:FireClient end end end Note over S: HealthManager.ApplyDamage(amount, type, ...) S->>S: record.LastDamageTime = os.clock() S->>S: amount = ShieldMath.absorb(Shields, amount) (Plating, Scrap, Spawn) opt shields took the whole hit S->>C: HealthStateSync:FireClient (return early) end S->>S: amount = ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, ArmorEfficiency) S->>S: record.Health -= amount S->>H: humanoid.Health = record.Health S->>C: HealthStateSync:FireClient Note over S: HealthManager.HealPlayer(amount) S->>S: record.Health = min(MaxHealth, record.Health + amount) S->>H: humanoid.Health = record.Health S->>C: HealthStateSync:FireClient

See Perks. searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleServer	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/JumpDriveManager.luau	Authority: charge gauge, deposit handling, vote, phase state machine, biome seam, arrival rewards Server	src/ServerScriptService/JumpDriveSystemLoader.server.luau	Bootstrap — calls JumpDriveManager.Initialize() Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/JumpDriveGuiController.client.luau	Bench panel JumpDriveGui (hold-to-charge JumpButton, UNKNOWN SIGNAL threat card, destination picker or ERROR card, vote row, named roster); feeds the generic PartyVoteGui banner (SharedModules/Gui/PartyVoteGui.luau) Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/JumpTransitionController.client.luau	Laser, black hole motion, speed lines, camera shake + FOV, SFX — owns one Janitor per jump Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JumpDriveConfig.luau	Bench tags/prompt names, charge values, phase durations, biome registry, arrival rewards, VFX tuning Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/JumpDriveResultCodes.luau	Deposit/vote/jump rejection codes  Packets: JumpStateSync, ReqDepositJumpCharge, ReqStartJumpVote, ReqCastJumpVote, ReqPickJumpDestination — see Networking MapSignals: OnJumpPhaseChanged — see Signals MapJoin-time delivery: via JoinSync on ClientReady, not Players.PlayerAdded — see Join-Sync Snapshot Handshake  The bench is the PowerCore model, which is also the train engine (it carries both JumpDriveBench and TrainEngine; see Train Fuel). It has two prompts: Refuel (ProxPromptPart, key E, hold) and Jump Drive (JumpPromptPart, key F). The keys differ because Exclusivity = OnePerButton shows only one prompt per key. It has no DepositPromptPart: players charge the drive by holding the JumpButton in the panel.

searchDocs.title: The charge gauge​
searchDocs.content: A single scalar 0..JumpDriveConfig.MAX_CHARGE, server-authoritative and global (one drive for the whole train, not per player). It does not decay. Players hold the panel's JumpButton; the client fires ReqDepositJumpCharge(bench)every HOLD_TICK (0.1 s). Each call spends at most DEPOSIT_PER_TICK (2) pool Energy points via MaterialPool.SpendUpTo, only what is needed to fill, so a full drive takes 5 s of holding. JumpDriveConfig.CHARGE_PER_POINT (1) is charge per Energy point, so a full drive costs 100 points. Range is checked against JumpPromptPart. The server refuses one player's calls closer thanMIN_DEPOSIT_INTERVAL (TOO_FAST). An isDepositing guard still serializes deposits.

searchDocs.title: Phase machine​
searchDocs.content: JumpDriveManager owns a single server-side phase. Every advance is guarded by a generation nonce, so a scheduled callback left over from a previous jump can never advance a later one (the same pattern TrainFuelManager.reschedule()uses).  stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Idle Idle --> Ready: gauge reaches MAX_CHARGE Ready --> Voting: a player starts a jump vote Voting --> Ready: vetoed, or expires with no > yes Voting --> Engulf: vote passes (charge consumed) Engulf --> InWormhole: EngulfDuration elapsed InWormhole --> Exit: biome ready AND MinWormholeHold elapsed InWormhole --> Exit: MaxWormholeHold watchdog fires Exit --> Idle: ExitDuration elapsed, rewards granted   Phase	MeaningIdle	Gauge not full; deposits accepted Ready	Gauge full; a vote can be opened Voting	Vote open, countdown running (VoteDuration) Engulf	Laser, black hole grows ahead of the train, glides in and stops centred on it (EngulfDuration) InWormhole	Held while the destination biome prepares (MinWormholeHold..MaxWormholeHold) Exit	Black hole speeds past the train back and shrinks (ExitDuration)  EngulfDuration, MinWormholeHold and ExitDuration are built fromJumpDriveConfig.Transition, the same table the client show reads, so each motion fills its phase exactly (see Client presentation).  The whole state — phase, gauge, and ballots — travels in one JumpStateSyncbroadcast rather than three, so a client can never render a phase and a gauge from two different moments. phaseEndsAt is a workspace:GetServerTimeNow()deadline; clients extrapolate their own countdown against it (the same prediction pattern TrainStateSync uses for the fuel bar), so there's no per-frame server traffic. InWormhole broadcasts phaseEndsAt = 0, meaningindefinite — hold the current visual state until the next broadcast; clients must treat 0 as "no known end," never as "already expired." Joining players get the current snapshot via a JoinSync sender ("JumpDrive"), run once the client announces readiness with ClientReady — not from Players.PlayerAdded, which is unreliable (seeJoin-Sync Snapshot Handshake). JumpDriveGuiControllerneeds no client-side cache for this: phaseEndsAt is always a server-supplied absolute timestamp, and countdownText() already renders "--" when it is unset, so a dropped or delayed snapshot just leaves the countdown honestly blank rather than wrong.

searchDocs.title: The vote​
searchDocs.content: Opening a vote (ReqStartJumpVote) requires standing at the bench and phaseReady; the opener is recorded as an automatic yes. Casting a ballot (ReqCastJumpVote) has no proximity check — see "Why the vote banner is pushed, not bench-gated" below — and may be changed freely while the countdown runs. Players.PlayerRemoving drops a leaver's ballot so they can't hold a decision hostage. Down players do not vote: a down sender's start returnsNOT_READY and a cast NO_VOTE_ACTIVE, Signals.OnPlayerDownChanged drops a ballot when its player goes down, and "present" counts only living players (ReviveState.LivingCount). See Paid Revive.  The opener's userId travels in JumpStateSync as initiator (0 outsideVoting), so the client can hide the pushed banner from the player who started the vote.  Every accepted ballot change and destination pick broadcasts JumpStateSync to all players, so the server refuses one player's picks and ballot changes closer than REQUEST_COOLDOWN (0.25 s) apart with TOO_FAST (silent on the client). A looping client can then cause at most four broadcasts a second.  Resolution is a pure function so it can be exercised in isolation (JumpDriveManager._resolveVoteForTest exposes it for a Studio command-bar check):  resolveVote(yes, no) -> yes > 0 and no <= yes   It passes if at least one player approved and the objectors do not outnumber them; abstaining (AFK, loading, never walked to the bench) is neutral and can never deadlock a jump. The countdown also resolves early — as soon as every present player has voted, or as soon as no remaining ballot could change the outcome — so a decided vote doesn't sit on screen for the rest of the 60 seconds.  Why the vote banner is pushed, not bench-gated​  Abstaining is neutral in resolveVote. If casting a ballot required standing at the bench, everyone who never walked over would abstain — over a 60-second window mid-combat, that's most of the party. The vote would then resolve on the initiator's lone yes every time: no > yes is nearly impossible to reach with a single voter, so the veto would exist in the resolution rule and never fire in practice. Pushing a non-modal banner to every player the momentVoting starts (JumpDriveGuiController) is what makes the vote a vote — opening it still requires the bench; casting a ballot in response to the pushed banner does not. The banner must not capture input (no ModalEnabled, nothing over the crosshair) so a player under attack can keep fighting and vote with one click when they choose to.

searchDocs.title: Destination​
searchDocs.content: CurrentBiome starts at START_BIOME. With the Biome Selector researched (BIOME_SELECTOR_NODE, gamepass-gated in ResearchConfig), a player at the bench picks the next biome with ReqPickJumpDestination while Idle orReady. The pick is stored as picked and sent in the destination field until a vote opens; chooseDestination (pure, _chooseDestinationForTest) then locks it in, or rolls at random when there is no valid pick or no research. A failed vote keeps the pick; arrival clears it.

searchDocs.title: Cross-system state during a jump​
searchDocs.content: Signals.OnJumpPhaseChanged(phase: string) is the single broadcast point for suspending world activity. JumpDriveConfig.IsJumpActive(phase) is true forEngulf/InWormhole/Exit (not Voting — the train runs normally while players decide). Seven consumers:  Consumer	Behavior while IsJumpActiveJunkService	CurrentState.IsSpawning = false; restored on return to Idle EventOrchestrator	SetJumpPaused(true) — odometer and channel ticking suspended, and any Active handler is force-finished TrainFuelManager	SetJumpFreeze(true) — drain rate pins to 0; ApplyFuelDamage early-returns TrainShieldManager	SetJumpFreeze(true) — ApplyDamage early-returns QuestSourcesLoader	Reports QuestConfig.Metrics.BiomeJumps progress once, on the IsJumpActive -> false edge (arrival, not vote-pass) ThreatTimerManager	Countdown paused; reset to a full Counting on the IsJumpActive -> false edge (arrival) — see Threat Timer RockService	Every rock in flight despawns (RockRemoved reason Despawn); no spawn rolls until arrival. The new CurrentBiome restarts the rock curve — see Rock Hazards  Why SetTrainStarted is not reused to halt junk spawning​  JunkService already gates spawning on Signals.SetTrainStarted, which looks like the obvious signal to reuse for a jump. It is not: EventOrchestrator.Initwires SetTrainStarted(true) to EventOrchestrator.Reset(). Re-firing it after a jump would silently zero the event odometer and desynchronize encounter pacing. OnJumpPhaseChanged is a dedicated signal precisely so the jump doesn't carry that invisible side effect.  Why jumping despawns an active encounter wave​  EventOrchestrator.SetJumpPaused(true) calls each channel's existingactiveFinish() — the same path the MaxActiveDistance watchdog and Reset()already use. PirateAttackEvent registers its spawned wave asctx.janitor:Add(wave, "Destroy"), so force-finishing it despawns any surviving pirates. This is deliberate, not a side effect: it's what makes "players are safe inside the wormhole" actually true — without it, a live wave would keep shooting people through the transition — and it doubles as a panic button, a balance lever the later chase-timer/pressure-loop spec should be aware of.

searchDocs.title: The biome seam​
searchDocs.content: -- inside JumpDriveManager local function prepareBiome(biomeId: string, done: () -> ()) workspace:SetAttribute(JumpDriveConfig.BIOME_ATTRIBUTE, biomeId) done() end   This local function — not a separate module — is the entire seam the future biome-content overhaul replaces. Today it writes the CurrentBiome attribute and calls done() immediately. The InWormhole hold already waits ondone() (floored by MinWormholeHold, capped by the MaxWormholeHoldwatchdog), so real scenery/weather/hazard load time is absorbed with no other change to this module — the overhaul only needs to replace prepareBiome's body.

searchDocs.title: Rewards on arrival​
searchDocs.content: Two separate call sites fire on arrival, not one:  JumpDriveManager.finishJump, on the Exit -> Idle transition, grantsCoinManager.AddCoins, XPManager.AddXP, and BattlePassManager.AddExp to every living player in ReviveState.LivingPlayers() — down players get nothing (each pcall-wrapped so one player's DataStore hiccup can't rob the rest of the party). Values live inJumpDriveConfig.ArrivalReward. JumpDriveManager never requiresQuestManager.  Rift Harvest (permanent party perk, id JumpBounty): finishJump pays ArrivalReward.Coins × (1 + JumpBountyBonus) coins and ArrivalReward.Xp × (1 + JumpBountyXP) XP, both floored. Battle Pass EXP is not changed.  Quest progress is a different module entirely: QuestSourcesLoader listens toSignals.OnJumpPhaseChanged itself and reportsQuestManager.ReportPartyProgress(QuestConfig.Metrics.BiomeJumps, 1) once, on the same IsJumpActive -> false arrival edge (see the cross-system table above). It lives there, not in JumpDriveManager, because of the convention documented on QuestConfig.Metrics itself: every quest metric gets its source wired in QuestSourcesLoader, so all quest sources stay discoverable in one file instead of being scattered across each feature that can grant progress.

searchDocs.title: Client presentation​
searchDocs.content: JumpTransitionController plays the show from the phase edges. It clonesReplicatedStorage.JumpDriveVfx.Wormhole (the Art Place black hole) and keeps the template's own scale:  Phase	What players seeEngulf	The train front fires a blue laser (LaserLength studs, three Beams) with a large shake kick. A small hole appears at the tip, grows to full scale while the laser fades, then glides in with MotionMaster PivotMove: slow start (RampUp), cruise, and a brake that starts once the whole train is inside the inner sphere. It stops centred on the full train. The speed lines (TeleportVFX, detached and fixed in front of the train) and the FOV build up from the first move. The shake builds up as the hole comes near. InWormhole	The train is inside. The server swaps the biome at once. The shake ramps up to its peak over Inside. Exit	The hole speeds past the train back and on for ExitPast studs, then shrinks. Speed lines, FOV and shake fade out.  The client solves the speeds from the phase times and the train length, so the motion always fills its phase. The train is the built platforms plus their ghosts in ReplicatedStorage.PlatformGhosts, so the hole centres on the full train even before every platform is built. A phase packet that arrives while the previous motion still runs (lag, or a player who joined mid-jump) snaps the hole to where the new phase starts, so the biome swap is never in view.  The controller owns one Janitor per jump plus one per phase. Ending the jump removes the hole, the speed lines and the camera offsets. The shake and FOV are offsets on top of whatever the camera scripts write: a render step afterEnum.RenderPriority.Camera treats any value it did not write as the new base, so the offsets never stack up with CameraController or the sprint FOV tween. Nothing in this system takes camera or movement control; the player keeps playing while the world changes around them.  Music and ambience wait for the exit. MusicDirector resolves the Jumpcontext through Exit, and BiomeController swaps the look on theCurrentBiome change (inside the hole) but holds the new ambience beds untilIsJumpActive turns false.  JumpDriveGuiController drives the panel and feeds the banner from the singleJumpStateSync payload, so they can never disagree. Pure text/state rules live in JumpDriveGuiRules (Studio self-check in the plan). Both ScreenGuis are authored in StarterGui (JumpDriveGui, PartyVoteGui; Enabled = false,ResetOnSpawn = false) and bound from PlayerGui. The code also setsResetOnSpawn = false: with true, a respawn replaces the copy and the bound references go stale. ReplicatedStorage.GuiAssets holds only templates that code clones onto parts (SurfaceGuis such as TrainShieldGui).  JumpButton: while Idle, hold it (MouseButton1/Touch) to charge — oneReqDepositJumpCharge per HOLD_TICK, a single success toast on release. While Ready, click it to open the vote; the press must begin in Ready, so releasing a hold that just filled the drive never opens a vote.Threat card ("UNKNOWN SIGNAL", never names the boss): readsThreatStateSync, hidden until the first one. Omen line, 12-segment meter and mm:ss clock come from JumpDriveGuiRules.threatView; omen texts areThreatConfig.CardOmens. The dot blink and the last-20 % border pulse are step toggles in the 0.1 s tick.Destination card: with ReplicatedStorage.ResearchUnlocked.Special_BiomeSelectorpresent, four biome buttons Biome1..4 (current biome left out) sendReqPickJumpDestination, locked once the vote opens; without it, "DESTINATION: ERROR" and "Biome Selector module broken". The card switches the moment the research finishes, even with the panel open.Vote: a VoteRow in the panel and the PartyVoteGui banner. The banner shows only while Voting, and not to the initiator or to anyone with the panel open, so nobody sees two sets. Y/N keys belong to the banner:PartyVoteGui binds them with ContextActionService only while the banner shows, so they do nothing for the vote opener or with the panel open (the panel's VoteRow shows no key hints). Key hints show only with a keyboard. The banner shows "n/m voted", not who agreed.

searchDocs.title: Config surface​
searchDocs.content: JumpDriveConfig — edit gameplay here, never in manager or controller code:  Section	FieldsStation / interaction	BENCH_TAG, JUMP_PROMPT_PART_NAME, PROXIMITY_TOLERANCE Transition	Transition: LaserLength, LaserDrop, LaserGrow, HoleDelay, Grow, StartScale, Approach, RampUp, Inside, Exit, ExitPast, Shrink, HoleOffset, InnerOrbName, SpeedLinesName, Shake (degrees per stage), FovAdd, Beams, LaserLight Charge	MAX_CHARGE, CHARGE_PER_POINT (charge per pool Energy point), HOLD_TICK, DEPOSIT_PER_TICK, MIN_DEPOSIT_INTERVAL, REQUEST_COOLDOWN (per-player floor on picks and ballot changes) Phases	Phase (string enum), IsJumpActive(phase), VoteDuration, EngulfDuration/MinWormholeHold/ExitDuration (built from Transition), MaxWormholeHold Biomes	BIOME_ATTRIBUTE (workspace attribute name), Biomes (destination list Normal, Volcano, Ice, Void, Storm; a jump never rolls the current biome; each id needs a SoundConfig.Music.BiomeFolders entry), START_BIOME (Normal), BIOME_SELECTOR_NODE Rewards	ArrivalReward — Coins/Xp/BPExp per player, flat for now VFX	VFX_FOLDER, WORMHOLE_MODEL  Perks: JumpSparkPerMinute (Jump Spark, Party shop, 1) — a 1 Hz clock in JumpDriveManager.Initialize counts travel seconds while Signals.SetTrainState says the train moves and the phase is Idle; each full minute adds JumpSparkPerMinute% of MAX_CHARGE and calls refreshReadiness (which broadcasts, and enters Ready at full). The vote still runs. JumpChargeBonus (Jump Engineer, Party) — each deposit gains CHARGE_PER_POINT ×(1+b) charge per Energy point. See Perks.

searchDocs.title: Not in scope​
searchDocs.content: These are deliberately deferred to their own future specs; each has a named seam so an implementer doesn't need to touch anything documented above:  Chase timer / pressure loop — built: see Threat Timer. It resets on the Exit -> Idle arrival edge. The Leviathan boss itself is still deferred (seam: Signals.OnThreatArrived).Biome content overhaul — per-biome scenery, skybox, lighting, weather, ambience, spawn tables, hazards. The seam is prepareBiome(biomeId, done)(see above).Reward scaling by biome tier or jump count — flat values belong with the content overhaul, which is what introduces tiers.EnemySpawner is not an OnJumpPhaseChanged consumer: it has no ambient spawn loop of its own, only SpawnAt/SpawnWave called from event handlers, so gating at EventOrchestrator is sufficient.
