searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/JunkController.client.luau	Client rendering: pool management, movement loop, retract animation, collection cleanup Server	src/ServerScriptService/JunkService.server.luau	Server authority: weighted spawn loop, pity system, odometer, claim/finalize handshake Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnHelper.luau	Volume-weighted random spawn position helper Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/GenericPoolInstance.luau	Instance pool used for junk visuals (vendored; RetrieveObject / InsertObject) Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luau	All tuning: spawn rates, speeds, tier weights, type chances, despawn distance Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/DebrisField.luau	Decorative debris: free-list pool, spawn roll, per-frame move Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/DebrisMath.luau	Pure debris rules: chance per biome, spawn point, train clearance Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/DebrisConfig.luau	Debris tuning: chance, cap, offsets, clearance, spin  Packets: SpawnJunk, SetJunkSpeed, JunkCollected, ReqJunkClaim, ReqJunkClaimBatch, ReqJunkFinalize, BeginJunkRetract, JunkBonus, DroneGrab — see Networking MapSignals: SetTrainState, SetTrainStarted, ApplyTierMultiplier, ApplyTypeMultiplier, TryClaimJunk, TryClaimJunkBatch, TryFinalizeJunk, OnJunkCollected — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Client rendering and pooling​
searchDocs.content: JunkController builds per-model GenericPoolInstance pools at startup, one per model name found in JunkAssets, with initial size 5, max 60, expand by 10. On SpawnJunk it checks the MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS = 250 cap, retrieves a model from the pool, sets Transparency = 0, parents it to workspace/JunksVisuals, and records it in activeJunks and junkMap. A PreSimulation loop advances the smoothstep speed ramp, moves each active junk by currentSpeed * dt along MOVE_DIRECTION, applies per-junk random rotation, and increments DistanceTraveled; junk despawns via RemoveJunkLocal when DistanceTraveled > DESPAWN_DISTANCE.  JunkController also bridges claim/finalize signals from GrabHook.client to Packets.ReqJunkClaim / Packets.ReqJunkFinalize via Signals.TryClaimJunk and Signals.TryFinalizeJunk, and exposes GetJunkIdFromPart(part) via BindableCore so GrabHook.client can resolve a junk ID from a raycast hit part.

searchDocs.title: Retraction and collection cleanup​
searchDocs.content: On BeginJunkRetract, the client removes the junk from simulation and moves it to retractingJunks. The local player's animation is driven by GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile; other players see an observer lerp on RenderStepped. An 8-second safety-net timeout returns the model to the pool if JunkCollected never arrives. On JunkCollected, the client cleans up rope attachments and beams on the model and returns it to the pool.

searchDocs.title: Server spawn loop​
searchDocs.content: JunkService performs weighted tier selection: each tier's weight is multiplied by GlobalModifiers.TierMultipliers[tier], and a random number selects the tier by accumulated weight. Type selection uses pity: if spawnsSinceLastEnergy >= ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD (8), an Energy-type junk is forced; otherwise a type is chosen weighted by SpawnChance * TypeMultiplier. The pity counter resets on every Energy spawn.

searchDocs.title: Special junk​
searchDocs.content: spawnSpecial(tier, count) and spawnCache(count) add junk outside the spawn roll: at SpawnHelper.GetRandomPoint(), ignoring MAX_SERVER_JUNKS and IsSpawning. The type is rolled by SpawnChance × TypeMultipliers without touching the pity counter. A Cache is a JunkConfig.Special entry (Tier = 0, Type = "Cache", model in JunkAssets.Special.Cache; the current one is a placeholder crate). Its grab credits the whole Yield table (50 Wood / 30 Metal / 20 Energy) to the pool at the player and gets no Lucky bonus. JunkToolManager skips the Special folder, so a Cache never becomes a Tool.  Perk travel clock. A 1 Hz loop counts travel seconds while the train has started, is running (SetTrainState) and is not in a jump (IsSpawning). Each perk keeps its own accumulator (SalvagePerkMath.tick) that only grows while the perk is live: Salvage Beacon (BeaconJackpots) spawns Tier 5 junk every SALVAGE_BEACON_SECONDS; Treasure Map (TreasureCaches) spawns a Cache every TREASURE_MAP_SECONDS. The EventOrchestrator odometer is not used: it does not run while EventConfig.Enabled = false. Beacon and Map spawns that fall due while the jump phase is Voting or JumpDriveConfig.IsJumpActive are held in pendingSpecial and spawn when the phase leaves that set (arrival, or a failed vote), because the jump removes junk spawned during the vote. Salvage Drone is not held: its grab goes straight to the player.  Salvage Drone (party, DroneGrabs): every SALVAGE_DRONE_SECONDS of travel, droneGrab picks the nearest tier junk within SALVAGE_DRONE_RANGE of the first TrainEngine-tagged instance that is not collected and not under a live reservation. It marks the junk Collected at once (a player claim of it then fails), fires DroneGrab(id, bench) to all clients with the nearest placed Workbench, and after DRONE_FLIGHT_SECONDS fires Signals.DroneJunkDelivered(bench, type, tier); ShredderServer turns it into pool materials and animates the bench. Fuel Line counts drone Energy grabs. No engine, junk or placed workbench: that grab is skipped. Clients fly the junk visual to the bench (MotionMaster.PivotMove) and return it to the pool; no JunkCollected follows.

searchDocs.title: Odometer and despawn​
searchDocs.content: The server records SpawnOdometer (the value of junkOdometer at spawn time) and SpawnPos for each active junk; the junk's current world position is reconstructed on claim as SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer). A distance-based despawn on Heartbeat removes any junk where (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer) > DESPAWN_DISTANCE, mirroring the client-side DistanceTraveled check. The junk counter wraps at 65535 (NumberU16 boundary) to keep IDs compact in the SpawnJunk packet.

searchDocs.title: Claim and finalize validation​
searchDocs.content: ReqJunkClaim reconstructs the junk's world position, checks distance against MaxDistance × (1 + HookRangeBonus) + 15 studs (latency slack), enforces a per-player cooldown, computes retract time, reserves the junk until fly-out + retract + RESERVATION_TIMEOUT (5 s slack), and fires BeginJunkRetract to all clients. ReqJunkFinalize checks reservation ownership and that the reservation has not expired, marks the junk collected, fires JunkCollected to all clients, then awards it: Energy junk credits its Yield as points to MaterialPool (origin = the player's character pivot); Wood/Metal junk gives the tool to the player's Backpack. SetTrainState(isMoving) and SetTrainStarted(started) are wired to Signals.SetTrainState and Signals.SetTrainStarted for external control.

searchDocs.title: Spawn volumes​
searchDocs.content: SpawnHelper:Init() caches all BasePart children of workspace/SpawnVolumes weighted by volume; SpawnHelper.GetRandomPoint() picks a random world position inside one of the spawn volumes using volume-weighted selection. SpawnHelper:Init() must be called before the spawn loop — JunkService calls it at startup; if no SpawnVolumes parts exist in workspace, GetRandomPoint always returns nil and no junk spawns.

searchDocs.title: Disabling spawn volumes​
searchDocs.content: Spawn volumes can be grouped and toggled at runtime without touching the workspace. Author an optional SpawnGroup string attribute on a BasePart under workspace/SpawnVolumes; every part sharing the same value forms a togglable group. Parts with no SpawnGroup attribute are ungrouped and always active — never affected by a toggle. SpawnHelper exposes three methods on top of Init / GetRandomPoint:  SpawnHelper:SetGroupEnabled(groupName: string, enabled: boolean) — enables or disables every volume in groupName. warns on an unrecognized group name (typo guard) but still records the state.SpawnHelper:IsGroupEnabled(groupName: string): boolean — true unless the group is currently disabled; unknown or ungrouped names always read true.SpawnHelper:GetGroups(): { string } — the distinct SpawnGroup values authored across the spawn volumes, for validation/debug.  The pirate-ship event uses this to disable the ship-facing group during the at-range cannon phase: junk stops spawning toward the ship, and any junk already floating there clears out via the normal distance-despawn instead of being force-removed, so the area is clean by the time players board. If every group with volumes ends up disabled, GetRandomPoint() returns nil and the spawn loop simply idles until a group is re-enabled — no junk spawns, but nothing errors.  JunkService disables the "Rocks" group (RockConfig.SPAWN_GROUP) once at startup. That volume (SpawnVolumes.Part3, in front of the train head) belongs to Rock Hazards; junk never spawns from it.

searchDocs.title: Decorative debris​
searchDocs.content: Space-wreck debris (hull pieces, fins, a ladder, glass shards, and so on) floats past with the junk to fill the space. It is purely visual and client-only: no packet, no server state, and each player sees their own debris. The 25 models live in ReplicatedStorage.DebrisAssets. Each model's solid parts are one union (GeometryService:UnionAsync, UsePartColor off so face colors stay, CollisionFidelity = Box); only Glass parts stay separate, because a union has one material and one transparency. That is 60 parts across all 25 models instead of 364. Every part has CanCollide, CanQuery, CanTouch and CastShadow off, so GrabHook and weapon raycasts pass straight through. The models use matte materials (Plaster, Fabric, Rubber; Glass only for windows and shards) and a painted palette with no gray metal, wood or glow, so they never read as junk or as rocks.  Spawn. After JunkController stores a new junk from SpawnJunk, it calls DebrisField.TrySpawn(startPos). That rolls DebrisMath.spawnChance(CurrentBiome): DebrisConfig.DEFAULT_SPAWN_CHANCE (0.25) or a SpawnChance override (Void 0.6). Debris therefore follows junk for free: none before the train starts, none during a jump, and junk dropped by MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS rolls nothing.Position. Each model's radius is DebrisMath.boundingRadius — measured from the model pivot, not the bounding-box centre, because debris is placed and spun about its pivot. DebrisMath.pickSpawnPoint offsets from the junk's startPos (X ±8, Y/Z ±20 studs), keeps radius + JUNK_GAP away from that junk, and rejects points whose path crosses the train corridor (the live TrainPlatforms bounding box, plus 4 studs beside, 14 above, 4 below). It retries 6 times, then skips. The client does not use SpawnHelper: with streaming on it may not have the volume parts, and the junk startPos already respects the server's SpawnGroup toggles.Move and despawn. JunkController's PreSimulation loop calls DebrisField.Step(moveAmount, dt) with the same ramped speed as junk. Debris spins slowly (ROT_SPEED), despawns past DESPAWN_DISTANCE, and is capped at MAX_CLIENT_DEBRIS (60) per client.Why not GenericPoolInstance. That pool moves only a model's root part, which would tear these multi-part anchored models apart, and welds do not help (a weld re-activated after its root moved outside the workspace locks in the wrong offset). DebrisField keeps a plain free list per model (retire = Parent = nil), caches each part's offset from the model pivot, and moves every live part with one workspace:BulkMoveTo(..., Enum.BulkMoveMode.FireCFrameChanged) per frame. Total copies (live + idle) never exceed MAX_CLIENT_DEBRIS. A spawn picks a random model and reuses its idle copy; under the cap, a new clone goes to the model with the fewest copies, so the capped set holds every model; at the cap, any idle copy is reused. A busy field therefore never clones or destroys (Studio check: 60 clones for ~1,680 Void spawns, all 25 models used).Missing assets never stall junk. JunkController requires DebrisField before it wires junk, so DebrisField waits at most ASSET_WAIT_SECONDS (10) for DebrisAssets, then warns and turns debris off. The folder lives only in the place file (not in git): a fresh rojo build or a new place has no debris until the models are copied in.Density is an upper bound. The chance is per junk spawn, but the 60 cap and clearance retries limit it; in the Void the cap binds first (about 60 debris per 70 s of travel). Tune in playtests.Adding a model. Union its solid parts (keep Glass separate), put the Model with a PrimaryPart in ReplicatedStorage.DebrisAssets, and set the part flags above. No code change.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Both sides integrate the same ramp — keep them in sync The server (junkOdometer) and client (DistanceTraveled) both use the identical smoothstep ramp over SPEED_RAMP_DURATION. If you change the ramp formula in one place, change it in the other. Drift causes the server's proximity check to reject valid claims.  Reservation timeout is 5 seconds If a client claims junk but never finalizes (e.g. disconnects mid-retract), the reservation expires 5 seconds (RESERVATION_TIMEOUT) after the expected reel-in ends (fly-out + retract, so Long Line and Wide Net pulls never expire mid-reel). Another player can then claim the same junk. The client has a safety net (RETRACT_RECLAIM_TIMEOUT = 8 s, added to the retract time) that returns the model to the pool if JunkCollected never arrives — it must exceed RESERVATION_TIMEOUT plus fly-out plus round-trip time.  Pool cleanup is mandatory. Every path that removes a junk from activeJunks or retractingJunks must call CleanupJunkModel then pool:InsertObject. Skipping cleanup leaks HookAttachment or Beam instances on the model, which will appear on the next retrieval.workspace/JunksVisuals folder must exist. JunkController uses WaitForChild to find it; the folder should be created in the place file or by a server startup script.Junk ID wraps at 65535. This is intentional for the NumberU16 wire type in SpawnJunk. Long-running servers are safe because entries are removed before the counter can collide.Tier 5 weight is 0. Items in Tier 5 will never spawn under default config. Set the weight above 0 to enable them.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Salvage Instinct (permanent, SalvageTierUpChance 0.04/level): FinalizeJunkForPlayer rolls first. On a hit, the grab uses tier + 1 (max Tier 5) and a random model of that tier, if that tier has the type (a Cache never tiers up). Gold Rush, Junk Collector and Lucky Charm then use the final tier. A tier-up fires the same JunkBonus toast as the bonus perks. Drone grabs do not roll.Scrap Pay (ScrapPayCoins 1): each finalized grab pays CoinManager.AddCoins(player, value, "ScrapPay"). A net pays per junk; a Cache grab pays too.Energy Tap (EnergyTapBonus 1): a player's Energy grab passes the bonus to creditEnergy, which adds it after the Energy Siphon rounding (a flat +1).Gold Rush (JunkCoinsT4, JunkCoinsT5): FinalizeJunkForPlayer pays that many coins for a tier 4 / tier 5 grab (the final tier, after Salvage Instinct; any type) through CoinManager.AddCoins.Golden Lure / Energy Forecast: PerkEffectsDispatcher sends the combined tier multipliers and the Energy type multiplier; ApplyTierMultiplier / ApplyTypeMultiplier overwrite, never multiply. See Perks — Shop perk layer.Scrap Shield (permanent, ScrapShieldHP 2/level): each finalized grab calls HealthManager.AddShield(player, "Scrap", value, PerkConfig.SCRAP_SHIELD_SECONDS, PerkConfig.SCRAP_SHIELD_MAX_STACKS) (20 s, at most 5 stacks). Wide Net finalizes per junk, so each junk in the net counts as one grab.Junk Collector (LuckyCoinCopies) / Lucky Charm (BonusJunkChance): after a Wood/Metal/Energy grab, grantLuckyBonuses gives extra junk through giveJunk (the same path as a grab: a Tool, or Energy points to the pool). Junk Collector counts grabs per player (session-only, only while live) and copies every LUCKY_COIN_EVERYth grab (same type and final tier; same model unless Salvage Instinct raised the tier). Lucky Charm rolls BonusJunkChance per grab; the bonus has the grabbed type and a tier from LUCKY_CHARM_TIER_WEIGHTS (SalvagePerkMath.rollTier). Each bonus fires JunkBonus(perkName, type, tier) to the player; JunkController shows a toast. A bonus is not a grab: no counter, quest, Fuel Line, Scrap Shield, Gold Rush, Scrap Pay or Energy Tap.Fuel Line (party, FuelPerEnergyJunk): each Energy grab calls TrainFuelManager.AddFuel(value).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant S as JunkService (server) participant C as JunkController (client) participant G as GrabHook (client) S->>S: selectRandomJunk() - weighted tier + pity type S->>S: assign id (U16), record SpawnOdometer + SpawnPos S->>C: SpawnJunk(id, modelName, startPos) C->>C: pool:RetrieveObject(startPos), add to activeJunks/junkMap S->>C: SetJunkSpeed(targetSpeed) Note over S,C: first receipt snaps currentSpeed; later receipts smoothstep-ramp Note over S,C: Shared speed ramp (identical smoothstep both sides)<br/>Server: junkOdometer += currentSpeed * dt<br/>Client: DistanceTraveled advances in PreSimulation<br/>Despawn when delta > DESPAWN_DISTANCE (both sides) G->>G: Player fires GrabHook -> Signals.TryClaimJunk(id, hitPos) G->>C: Signals.TryClaimJunk C->>S: ReqJunkClaim(id, hitPos) S->>S: proximity check vs junkOdometer, in-flight check, reserve junk S->>C: BeginJunkRetract(id, hitPos, retractTime, player) Note over C: local player -> GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile<br/>other players -> observer lerp on RenderStepped G->>C: Signals.TryFinalizeJunk(id) C->>S: ReqJunkFinalize(id) S->>S: verify reservation + timeout, mark Collected, award (Energy → MaterialPool, else Tool) S->>C: JunkCollected(id, player) C->>C: pool:InsertObject (returns model)

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: JunkConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luauPerks: JunkSpawnRateBonus (spawn interval ÷(1+b) — Dense Debris), EnergyYieldBonus (Energy credit ×(1+b), rounded — Energy Siphon), JunkTierRarityBonus (via ApplyTierMultiplier), plus the GrabHook claim keys (HookRangeBonus, ReelSpeedBonus, NetCapacityBonus — see GrabHook). See Perks.Playbook: Adjust Junk Flow  Field	Default	EffectMAX_SERVER_JUNKS	200	Hard cap on server-side active junk entries MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS	250	Client silently drops SpawnJunk events beyond this count MOVE_DIRECTION	Vector3.new(1,0,0)	World direction all junk travels DESPAWN_DISTANCE	700 studs	Odometer delta at which junk is removed (both sides) DEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE	0.5 s	Seconds between junk spawns when train is moving STOPPED_SPAWN_RATE	1.5 s	Seconds between spawns when train is stopped DEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED	10 studs/s	Junk movement speed when train is moving STOPPED_JUNK_SPEED	5 studs/s	Junk movement speed when train is stopped SPEED_RAMP_DURATION	1.5 s	Smoothstep ramp time on speed change ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD	8	Non-energy spawns before Energy is guaranteed BaseModifiers.GlobalSpawnRateMult	1.0	Global spawn rate multiplier (runtime-adjustable) Tiers[n].Weight	varies	Relative spawn weight for each tier (Tier 5 is 0 = disabled) Tiers[n].Types[t].SpawnChance	varies	Relative spawn chance for each type within a tier Tiers[n].Types[t].Yield	varies	Item count awarded on collection  Model lists (Tiers[n].Types[t].Models) are auto-populated from ReplicatedStorage/JunkAssets/TierN/TypeName folder contents at require time.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​

searchDocs.title: Data​
searchDocs.content: One OrderedDataStore per board, key = tostring(UserId), integer values. The ordered store is the record; no ProfileStore field holds these numbers.  Board	Store	Value	Write	Written whenlevel	LB_TotalXP_v1	total EXP (shown as LV n)	max	XP profile load + every XPManager.AddXP coins	LB_CoinsEarned_v1	coins actually added by CoinManager.AddCoins (not refunds, not the wallet)	add	every AddCoins run	LB_LongestRun_v1	best single-run played seconds	max	run payout (RunEndService, Leave or run end) kills	LB_Kills_v1	enemies killed, all runs	add	run payout (RunEndService)  Coins earned before the board shipped are not counted. Level backfills on the player's next join.

searchDocs.title: Writing (both places)​
searchDocs.content: LeaderboardWriter.Add / Max only touch an in-memory buffer keyed by UserId. Flush writes it: add → IncrementAsync, max → UpdateAsync that returns nil (no write) when the stored value is already as high. Flushes run every FLUSH_SECONDS (60), on PlayerRemoving and on the PersistenceRegistry flush. A failed write goes back into the buffer for the next flush. On BindToClose, Drain(20) flushes, waits up to 20 s for writes that other flushes already started (e.g. the last player's PlayerRemoving flush), then flushes once more to retry any that failed.  Studio never writes (WRITE_IN_STUDIO = false): the writer prints [LeaderboardWriter] Studio, not written: … instead, like the read-only ProfileStore sessions.

searchDocs.title: Reading (Lobby)​
searchDocs.content: Every REFRESH_SECONDS (120) LeaderboardService:  reads each board's top 100 (GetSortedAsync(false, 100)); a failed board keeps its last good list;names the top 10: players in the server by DisplayName, the rest with one UserService:GetUserInfosByUserIdsAsync call (cached until the server restarts);reads every Lobby player's own values, one BatchGetAsync per board;sends each ready player their payload. A joiner gets theirs from the "Leaderboard" JoinSync sender.  Rank: 1 + the number of top-100 entries above the player's own (fresh) value, so a score that landed after the last refresh still ranks right. Below a full top 100 it reads 100+ (ordered stores cannot look up one key's rank); no score, or a board that was never read, reads — (no score also shows PLAY A RUN).

searchDocs.title: Monitor (client)​
searchDocs.content: LeaderboardController connects LeaderboardSync, waits up to 30 s for workspace.Lobby_TV_Animation.Screen (missing → one warning, no monitor), clones ReplicatedStorage.GuiAssets.LeaderboardGui into PlayerGui with Adornee = Screen (per player, because the YOU row differs), and applies the art ids from LeaderboardConfig. Every CYCLE_SECONDS (10) it shows the next board and runs the progress bar with MotionMaster. Before the first payload it shows LOADING SCORES…; a payload with status = "offline" shows SCORES OFFLINE · RETRYING. Head shots come from Players:GetUserThumbnailAsync (cached).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Game Instance / Lobby Lobby CoinManager.AddCoins ─┐ XPManager.AddXP/load ─┼─► LeaderboardWriter ─► OrderedDataStores ─► LeaderboardService ─► LeaderboardSync ─► LeaderboardController RunEndService payout ─┘ (buffer, 60 s) (4 boards) (top 100, 120 s) (per player) (SurfaceGui)   LeaderboardSync payload:  { status = "ok" | "offline", boards = { [boardId] = { { userId, name, value } } }, -- ≤ 10, index = rank mine = { [boardId] = { rank, value } }, -- rank 0 none, 1..100, 101 = "100+" }

searchDocs.title: Studio setup (Lobby)​
searchDocs.content: Workspace.Lobby_TV_Animation (the floating TV Model, ModelStreamingMode = Persistent: the Lobby uses instance streaming, and a far monitor would not stream in; RootPart anchored, the other parts hang on it by Motor6D). Screen: an invisible Part (CanCollide/CanQuery/CanTouch off, Massless) laid flat on the glass of Lobby_TV_Monitor, front face out, 16:9, joined to the monitor by a WeldConstraint so it follows the TV animation. The glass is curved, so the GUI corners stand a little in front of it seen from the side. Move or scale the whole model freely.ReplicatedStorage.GuiAssets.LeaderboardGui: SurfaceGui template, FixedSize 1600×900. Text labels for names are called PlayerName (a child called Name would clash with Instance.Name).Art: the image ids are in LeaderboardConfig.ART and the board Icon fields. Edge/Fill are 9-slice images (SliceCenter 88,88,152,152, SliceScale 0.5), white, tinted in Studio. The source SVGs/PNGs were removed after upload; they are in git history (commit 0537bc3, roblox-gui-prototypes/assets/leaderboard/).

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: LeaderboardConfig: CYCLE_SECONDS 10, REFRESH_SECONDS 120, FLUSH_SECONDS 60, FETCH_COUNT 100 (page maximum), SHOW_COUNT 10 (the layout has 10 places), WRITE_IN_STUDIO false. Changing a Store name starts that board from empty.

searchDocs.title: What gets preloaded​
searchDocs.content: Instances under ReplicatedStorage, Workspace, Lighting, SoundService, StarterGui, StarterPack, and MaterialService whose class is in PRELOAD_CLASSES (Animation, Sound, Decal/Texture, MaterialVariant, SurfaceAppearance, ImageLabel, ImageButton, ParticleEmitter, Beam, Trail, Sky).MeshPart TextureIDs as plain content ids. The MeshPart itself is skipped, so its mesh still streams in during play.Every rbxassetid:// string in the Configs modules (except rbxassetid://0). This covers ids that exist only in code, such as SoundConfig SFX and TrainConfig.BRAKE_LEVER_ANIM_ID. ChronoConfig is skipped: it must only be required through the Chrono wrapper. PreloadAsync fails every bare id string, so each id goes in a carrier instance of its type: ids in SoundConfig go in a Sound, ids under a key that contains "anim" go in an Animation, and all other ids go in an ImageLabel. A new animation id in a config must have "anim" in its key name, or it is loaded as an image. MeshPart TextureID values go in an ImageLabel too. The BGM folder (ReplicatedStorage[SoundConfig.Music.BgmFolder], BGMs) is skipped: its full-length songs load on demand when a playlist starts.  A new asset in a config module or a replicated folder is picked up with no extra wiring. An id hardcoded inside a controller is not picked up; move it into a config.

searchDocs.title: Progress bar​
searchDocs.content: The bar first creeps toward JOIN_END while the place downloads (Roblox gives no progress for that). The preload then fills the rest, one step per batch. ASSET_TIMEOUT caps how long one stuck batch can hold the screen. Failed assets are warned, not fatal.  SoundManager.Pool.Warm also uses PreloadLib, to keep its parked pool Sounds loaded.

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleServer	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/MaterialPool.luau	Sole authority: Get, atomic Spend, SpendUpTo, Add, ArcPoints; broadcasts every change; "MaterialPool" JoinSync sender Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/MaterialPoolClient.luau	Client read model: Get (nil before first snapshot), Changed(gained, origin, landing), idempotent Init Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/MaterialHudController.client.luau	Code-built HUD, slide/toggle, fly-to-HUD effect Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/MaterialHudConfig.luau	HUD + effect tuning  Packets: MaterialPoolUpdate — see Networking Map

searchDocs.title: How it works​
searchDocs.content: Sources: shredder completion (ShredderServer) and research cancel refunds (ResearchService) call MaterialPool.Add(counts, MaterialPool.ArcPoints(station)). Energy junk grabs add at the player (Energy Tap adds a flat bonus to a player's own grab); Wreck Salvage (WreckSalvageService, hidden until enemy ships exist) adds Wood + Metal at a damaged EnemyShip.Sinks: workbench crafts (WorkbenchService) and research enqueues (ResearchService) call MaterialPool.Spend(cost); false means nothing was consumed.SpendUpTo(mat, missing, perPoint): the Energy spend path. Spends ceil(missing ÷ perPoint) points (at least 1), capped by the pool, and returns (pointsSpent, unitsAdded). Every Energy consumer calls it with its own *_PER_POINT rate, so a top-up never wastes points.Replication: every change fires MaterialPoolUpdate(wood, metal, energy, gainedWood, gainedMetal, gainedEnergy, origin, landing) to all clients. Spends and the join snapshot carry zero gain. The join snapshot is a broadcast, not FireClient, because the Packet library flushes broadcasts first each frame — a per-player snapshot could land after a same-frame gain and leave the joiner stale.Effect backstop: each fly effect destroys its Janitor after its time budget even if a piece thread errors, so undelivered value is always handed back to the counter.HUD: hidden by default. Slides down on any gain, on LeftControl, or on the touch-only pull tab; tapping the open panel or pressing the key again closes it; auto-hides after HIDE_DELAY.Rows: Wood, Metal, Energy (Energy colour 13FAFD). Panel sized for three rows: PANEL_HEIGHT_SCALE 0.165, PANEL_MIN_HEIGHT_PX 96, PANEL_ASPECT 1.6.Effect: if the gain's origin is on screen and within MAX_EFFECT_DISTANCE, up to MAX_FLY_PIECES local Handle clones arc out, rest for LAND_HOLD, then fly as 2D icons into their row; each carries a share of the gain. Pieces are split across materials in proportion to the gain; every material with a gain gets at least one. Energy has no CraftingMaterials template, so its pieces skip the 3D arc and fly as 2D icons from the grab point. Otherwise the counter rolls up over ROLL_DURATION.Counter rule: displayed = server total − value still in flight (clamped ≥ 0), so overlapping gains and mid-flight spends always settle on the exact total.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant SS as ShredderServer / ResearchService participant MP as MaterialPool (server) participant C as MaterialPoolClient (every client) participant H as MaterialHudController participant G as Workbench / TechTree GUIs SS->>MP: Add({Wood, Metal}, origin, landing) MP->>C: MaterialPoolUpdate(wood, metal, energy, gainedWood, gainedMetal, gainedEnergy, origin, landing) C->>H: Changed(gained, origin, landing) C->>G: Changed (repaint if open) H->>H: slide down, arc + fly-to-HUD, tick counters, hide after delay Note over MP: WorkbenchService / ResearchService call Spend (atomic)

searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/NotificationManager/init.luau	Full toast manager: layout, animation, audio, cleanup. Do not require this directly from feature code Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/NotificationController.client.luau	One-line bootstrap: calls NotificationManager.Init() Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/NotificationConfig.luau	Types, colors, images, SFX names, device sizing, animation timing, MaxConcurrent, ExecutedFunctionTimeout  Packets: none — notifications are client-onlySignals: RequestNotification, RequestClearNotifications (both consumed, fired by any controller) — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Firing a toast​
searchDocs.content: Any client script fires Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?). NotificationManager is the sole subscriber:  Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("success", "Item placed!") Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("warn", "Low fuel!", 5) Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("info", "Loading...", nil, function() task.wait(2) -- toast stays open until this returns end)   NotificationController.client.luau calls NotificationManager.Init() once; after that, NotificationManager subscribes to Signals.RequestNotification and Signals.RequestClearNotifications. No other setup is required. Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() closes every active toast immediately.

searchDocs.title: Toast lifecycle​
searchDocs.content: NotificationManager creates (lazily) a ScreenGui named NotificationGui (DisplayOrder 200, above every modal and its dim frame — e.g. WorkbenchGui at 130) with a UIListLayout container anchored top-center, offset by NotificationConfig.TopOffsetScale (a fraction of viewport height). New toasts insert at the top of the stack; LayoutOrder is a negated monotonic counter so newer toasts sort above older ones. Executed-function toasts sit above timed toasts in a reserved LayoutOrder band.  Font size and padding are viewport-responsive: scaled by math.min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) / BaseScreenMin, clamped to [0.7, 1.3]. Text width is measured via TextService:GetTextSize after accounting for icon width, time-bar width (timed toasts only), and padding gaps, so the label never clips.  Close animations run a MotionMaster tween that shrinks the frame to UDim2.fromOffset(0, 0); a per-entry Janitor destroys the frame when the tween completes. A debounced viewport resize handler (requestResize) re-measures and re-tweens all live toasts when the window size changes.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Use Signals — never require NotificationManager directly Feature controllers must fire Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?). Requiring NotificationManager directly and calling internal functions breaks the decoupled contract and will error if accidentally required server-side.  type must exactly match one of the five lowercase strings in NotificationConfig.Types. An unrecognized type is silently dropped (no toast, no error).duration overrides the device default (NotificationConfig.Device.Desktop.Duration or .Mobile.Duration). Pass nil to use the default.executedFunction makes the toast persist until the function returns (or ExecutedFunctionTimeout elapses). It runs in a pcall-protected task.spawn — errors are suppressed and the toast still closes. Keep the function short; it runs on the client main thread.When MaxConcurrent is reached, the oldest timed toast is force-closed. Executed-function toasts are never evicted by the cap — avoid queuing many long-running ones simultaneously.Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() closes all toasts regardless of type or remaining duration. Use it only for hard resets (e.g. character death, scene transitions).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Feature as Any client controller participant Manager as NotificationManager participant Sound as SoundManager Feature->>Manager: Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?) Manager->>Manager: validate type against NotificationConfig.Types Manager->>Manager: enforce MaxConcurrent (evict oldest non-executed toast if needed) Manager->>Manager: build toast Frame (icon, time-left bar, gradient-sweep text) Manager->>Sound: PlaySFX(NotificationConfig.SfxNames[type]) Manager->>Manager: intro animation (MotionMaster size expand + fade in) alt timed toast Manager->>Manager: task.delay(duration or device default, closeEntry) else executed-function toast Manager->>Manager: task.spawn(executedFunction) -> closeEntry on return end Feature->>Manager: Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() Manager->>Manager: closeEntry() on every active toast simultaneously

searchDocs.title: Room states​
searchDocs.content: Each Studio part tagged trigger becomes a Zone. A clone of ServerStorage.RoomTexts sits under it and shows the room state.  State	Entered when	Billboard showsEmpty	Server start, or 1 s after the room clears	0 / 5 Selecting	A player with no party enters an empty room. A party is created with that player as leader.	"choosing party size" Countdown	The leader picks a size in the GUI (SetRoomSize)	members / size, countdown m:ss, access mode (PUBLIC / FRIENDS ONLY / INVITE ONLY) Teleporting	The countdown reaches 0	"teleporting"

searchDocs.title: Flow​
searchDocs.content: Leader enters an empty room. The server creates a party, sets the room to Selecting, opens the GUI (ToggleRoomSizeGui) and locks the leader's controls (SetPlayerControl false). Leader picks a size (1–5) and who can join. SetRoomSize sets MaxMembers and the access mode, moves the room to Countdown and starts the 5-minute forced launch. The leader's controls unlock. The server ignores the packet unless the sender is the leader, the size is 1–5, the access mode is 0–2 and the room is still Selecting. During the countdown the leader can change the mode with SetRoomAccess; this never removes members. Other players enter during the countdown. PartyRoomRules.canJoin decides, in this order: the room must be in Countdown and not locked; a saved ban refuses; a full crew refuses; an invite lets them in; INVITE ONLY refuses; FRIENDS refuses a non-friend of the leader (IsFriendsWithAsync). A refused player gets a RoomNotice line ("This crew is full.", …) and EjectPlayer steps them 12 studs back. A player already in a crew who walks through another dock is ignored. A player leaves the room. A member leaves the party. If the leader leaves, leadership moves to another member. If the leader is alone, the party disbands, the countdown stops and the room resets. Countdown rules. Each second the server applies PartyRoomRules.nextEndsAt: when every member is ready (ReqSetReady), the end moves to now + 5 s (never later); while an invite waits, the end stays at least 10 s away. It writes EndsAt and InviteHold; clients compute the timer from workspace:GetServerTimeNow().2 s before the end (lock-in), every member's controls lock; ReqSetReady, SetRoomAccess and CancelRoom are ignored from then on. At 0, TeleportParty fulfils the Session Rejoin contract: TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync(GAMEPLAY_PLACE_ID) returns an access code and the PrivateServerId.SessionStore.WriteRoster writes the party's user ids under that PrivateServerId. If this fails, the party does not teleport.SessionStore.SeedPointer writes one session pointer per member. A failure here only disables mid-run rejoin.PersistenceRegistry.ReleaseForTeleport(members) saves and ends each member's coin, XP, perk and inventory sessions without a kick, so the Game Instance opens them without waiting on the session lock.party:TeleportMembers(GAMEPLAY_PLACE_ID, { ReservedServerCode = accessCode }) teleports the party. The room resets 5 s later. If any step fails (always in Studio, where teleports do not work), the server clears what it wrote, unlocks and ejects every member, disbands the party and resets the room. If the failure comes after the release (TeleportMembers errors, or TeleportService.TeleportInitFailed fires for one member), PersistenceRegistry.Reopen also gives those members their sessions back. In Studio ReserveServerAsync fails first, so no session is released and nothing reopens.  Cancel: the panel's LEAVE button sends CancelRoom. The server ejects the player. The playerExited handler then removes them (a leader with crew hands leadership to another member; a leader alone disbands the party).  Panel open / close: the server fires ToggleRoomSizeGui(true) to every player who joins a party (leader included) and false when they leave or the party disbands.  No client party remote. The vendored PartySystem used to create a PartyRemoteFunction that let any client create parties, accept invites, change the size, toggle invite-only or set an unfiltered party name. The Lobby no longer creates it: every party change goes through the room packets above, which PartyCreation validates.

searchDocs.title: Room attributes​
searchDocs.content: PartySystem already replicates ReplicatedStorage.PartySystem.PhysicalParties/<leader name> with one Members/<name> ObjectValue per member. The party room GUI reads only these attributes:  On	Attribute	Type	MeaningPhysicalParty	Dock	string	The trigger part's DockName attribute (Studio), else "Dock <n>" PhysicalParty	State	number	PartyRoomRules.State (1 Selecting, 2 Countdown, 3 Teleporting) PhysicalParty	Size	number	Chosen crew size (1 while Selecting) PhysicalParty	Access	number	PartyRoomRules.Access (0 public, 1 friends, 2 invite only) PhysicalParty	EndsAt	number	Launch time in workspace:GetServerTimeNow() seconds (0 while Selecting) PhysicalParty	InviteHold	boolean	An invite is waiting, so the end is held Member ObjectValue	Seat	number	1–5, join order; a leave frees the seat for the next joiner Member ObjectValue	Ready	boolean	Ready check; a new member joins not ready Member ObjectValue	Leader	boolean	Set by PartySystem (moves on leadership transfer) Member ObjectValue	Level	number	XPManager.GetLevel; refreshed on Signals.OnPlayerLevelUp Member ObjectValue	PartyPerks, PersonalPerks	string	Saved shop loadout (PerkInventoryManager.GetLoadout), comma-separated ids (PartyRoomRules.joinIds); refreshed on Signals.OnShopLoadoutChanged

searchDocs.title: Invites​
searchDocs.content: Leader only, during the countdown, before lock-in. Only friends in the same Lobby server (no cross-server invites).  ReqInvite(userId): the server checks the sender leads a room in Countdown, the crew is not full, the target is in this server, in no crew, not already invited, not on the leader's saved ban list, and a friend (IsFriendsWithAsync, checked again after the yield). One invite every 3 s per leader. Then party:InvitePlayer(target) (PartySystem's 20 s expiry), EndsAt on the Invites/<name> ObjectValue, and InviteOffer(partyId, inviterUserId, dock, endsAt) to the target.Invites do not hold seats. The leader can invite more friends than there are open seats; the first to accept takes the seat. When the crew fills, the other waiting invites are revoked and the leader gets "Crew is full. Your other invites were cancelled."Hold: while any invite waits, the countdown end stays at least 10 s away (InviteHold is true).ReqAnswerInvite(partyId, accept): no → the invite is revoked (the hold ends). Yes → canJoin with invited = true and the leader's saved bans; OK → the character is pivoted into the dock's trigger box, so the normal zone join adds them (no second join path). Refused → RoomNotice ("This crew is full.", …).

searchDocs.title: Saved bans​
searchDocs.content: Decided: a ban is saved for good on the leader's account and works in every Lobby server. It refuses the banned player from any crew that leader leads, until the leader unbans them. It acts only while its owner leads: as a member you can still share a crew led by someone else. Players already in a crew stay when leadership moves.  Store. ProfileStore PlayerBans, key UserId: { Bans = { [userIdString]: bannedAtUnix }, SchemaVersion = 1 }, max 100 entries (PartyRoomRules.MAX_BANS). Registered with PersistenceRegistry (save + teleport hand-off) and JoinSync like the other Lobby profiles.Ban. ReqBanCrew(userId): sender leads a room in Countdown, not locked; target is in the crew. BanStore.Add (refused when full: "Ban list is full. Unban someone first."), then party:BlacklistPlayer (removes the member; RoomChat drops their TextSource), EjectPlayer, and "You were removed from Dock N." to the target. The notice does not say the ban is saved.Join check. The zone join and the invite answer pass banned = BanStore.IsBanned(currentLeader, userId); a ban beats an invite.Unban. ReqUnbanCrew(userId) removes the entry and, when the sender leads a crew that blacklisted that player, calls party:UnblacklistPlayer. It does not pull anyone into the dock.Client. MyBansSync sends the owner's whole list on load and after each change; the panel's My bans manager reads it.

searchDocs.title: Party room panel​
searchDocs.content: PartyRoomGuiController opens the panel on ToggleRoomSizeGui(true) and finds the local player's PhysicalParty (it waits up to 5 s for it to replicate). It never asks the server for state: PartyView.Watch repaints on any attribute or child change (at most once per frame) and PartyView.Snapshot reads everything.  Layout. Wide is authored at 1920×1022: UIScale = min(W/1920, (H-58)/1022). Under 0.68 the compact layout is used (same instances, other sizes; authored at 844×332, scale clamped 0.75–1.5): CREW / CHAT tabs, 330-wide crew list without perk chips, chat full width. While the compact panel shows, ProximityPromptService.Enabled is false (it covers the thumbstick).Head. State chip: CHOOSE SIZE (amber) · LAUNCH IN m:ss (teal) · WAITING FOR INVITE (amber, InviteHold) · LOCKED IN m:ss (orange, last 2 s) · TELEPORTING (mint); the timer is EndsAt - workspace:GetServerTimeNow(). The leader gets AccessControl (SetRoomAccess); others see AccessTag. READY sends ReqSetReady; LEAVE sends CancelRoom and reads LOCKED once locked in. HIDE folds the panel into the pill.Size bar (leader while Selecting): crew size 1–5 and who can join, START sends SetRoomSize(size, access).Crew list. One row per seat up to the size: avatar in the seat color, LEADER / YOU tags, "@name · Lv N", up to 4 party perk chips, a ready mark. A party perk equipped by two players turns wine (COUNTS ONCE in the loadout box). An open seat shows "Walk into Dock N to join" / "Friends of <leader> only" / "Invite only", or "2 invites waiting · 0:14". Tapping a row shows that player's loadout; tapping a chip fills PerkInfo with the ShopPerkConfig description.Mute / ban. Tap a name in the chat (the NameHit button over the name at the start of a line) to open the ActionBar, or select a crew row to swap its perk chips for RowActions: MUTE / UNMUTE (ReqMuteCrew), BAN (leader only, hidden once locked in, BANS FULL at 100) → YES, BAN / NO → ReqBanCrew. The muter sees "Kai is muted for you. Tap the name to unmute."Invite picker (leader, open seat INVITE): friends in this server (Players:GetPlayers() filtered by a cached LocalPlayer:IsFriendsWithAsync). Button states: INVITE · SENT m:ss · IN DOCK N · IN YOUR CREW · BANNED · CREW FULL. The list stays open for more invites and closes at lock-in.My bans. MyBansBar (anyone with saved bans) → MANAGE opens BanManager: one row per ban, names of players who are not in the server from one batched UserService:GetUserInfosByUserIdsAsync per open, UNBAN → ReqUnbanCrew.Chat badge. Player lines that arrive while the chat is hidden (pill, or the compact CREW tab) count on the CHAT tab and pill badges.Invite prompt. InvitePromptController shows "Nova invites you to Dock 2", "3 / 4 crew · launch in 0:24 · invite ends in 0:20", JOIN / NO. It closes on an answer, when the invite ends or is revoked, and on a RoomNotice (shown in the Toast for 3 s).Update in place. Lists are rebuilt only when their content key changes; the 0.2 s timer only sets Text, so a button is never destroyed mid-press.

searchDocs.title: Room chat​
searchDocs.content: Roblox rule: every game with text chat must use TextChatService; a custom chat window is fine only when it sends through a TextChannel.  Server (RoomChat). The first member join opens TextChatService.Room_<PartyId>. Every join calls channel:AddUserAsync(userId) (in a pcall, on its own thread); it returns nil when the player's chat is off, and then nothing happens. Leave, eject and ban destroy that player's TextSource. Disband and a successful teleport destroy the channel.What the channel handles for us: the text filter per viewer, parental controls, age groups, blocked users, Roblox's flood limit, and abuse reports from the Roblox menu. Do not add a custom filter, a custom report button, or a user-made party name (it would need its own filter).Client. SEND calls channel:SendAsync(text) (cut to 200 characters). Lines are drawn only from channel.MessageReceived; TextChatMessage.Text is already filtered for this viewer, and it is RichText-escaped (PartyRoomRules.escapeRichText) before display. The raw TextBox text is never shown to anyone else. A player with chat off (TextChatService:CanUserChatAsync false) sees "Chat is off for your account." and no input. The channel's own OnIncomingMessage prefixes room lines with [Dock N] in the Roblox chat window and bubbles.Mute. ReqMuteCrew(userId, muted) fills a per-viewer set; the channel's ShouldDeliverCallback drops a muted sender's lines for that viewer only. Muting needs the target in the viewer's crew; unmute is always allowed. Session only (cleared on PlayerRemoving).

searchDocs.title: Packets​
searchDocs.content: These are in the Lobby's own registry, not in the Networking Map.  Packet	Direction	Payload	PurposeEjectPlayer	S->C	NumberU8 distance	Push the character back out of a room SetRoomSize	C->S	NumberU8 size, NumberU8 access	Leader picks the crew size and who can join; starts the countdown SetRoomAccess	C->S	NumberU8 access	Leader changes who can join during the countdown ReqSetReady	C->S	Boolean8	Sets the sender's Ready attribute (Countdown, not locked) RoomNotice	S->C	String	One notice line for the player (refused join, …) CancelRoom	C->S	none	LEAVE: the server ejects the sender (ignored once locked in) ReqMuteCrew	C->S	NumberF64 userId, Boolean8 muted	Mute / unmute a crew member's room chat for the sender only ReqInvite	C->S	NumberF64 userId	Leader invites a friend in this server InviteOffer	S->C	String partyId, NumberF64 inviter userId, String dock, NumberF64 invite end	Opens the invite prompt ReqAnswerInvite	C->S	String partyId, Boolean8 accept	JOIN / NO on the invite prompt ReqBanCrew	C->S	NumberF64 userId	Leader bans a crew member for good (save + kick) ReqUnbanCrew	C->S	NumberF64 userId	Remove a saved ban MyBansSync	S->C	Any { [userIdString]: bannedAtUnix }	The owner's saved ban list SetPlayerControl	S->C	Boolean8	Enable / disable movement controls ToggleRoomSizeGui	S->C	Boolean8	Show / hide the party room panel, for every member (wire name "EnableRoomSizeGui") LeaderboardSync	S->C	Any { status, boards, mine }	Every board's top 10 + the viewer's rank and value, after each refresh and on JoinSync. Defined in Packets/LobbyShared.luau (the Game Instance never sends it). See Leaderboard

PerkMenuGuiController binds MainContainer.TopContainer (tabs, level / points / coin chips, CloseButton), LoadoutPage (8 slot rows, filters, EmptyLabel, ExampleCard), UpgradePage (filters, ExampleCard with PipContainer and CostLabel, the detail panel with LevelList.ExampleLevelRow, UpgradeButton, RespecButton, RespecAllButton) and ShopPage (filters, ExampleCard, detail, BuyButton1–3). searchDocs.title: Known gaps​
searchDocs.content: Party room icons have no asset ids (hide, leave, send, chat, ready check, muted, open-seat plus); the ImageLabels are empty until they are uploaded (see TODO.md). Invite hold has no cap. Each waiting invite holds the launch at least 10 s away, for up to 20 s; a leader who keeps re-inviting a friend who never answers can push the 5-minute forced launch back. Cross-server invites are out of scope (decided): only friends in the same Lobby server. Volume sliders change nothing audible in the Lobby. The Lobby has no sound yet; the values save and apply in the Game Instance. The Danmaku row also only saves (NovaChat is Game Instance only). SprintFov applies in both places. Mid-run rejoin routing is not built. The Lobby seeds the session pointers, but it does not read a returning player's pointer and send them back to their live server (spec steps 1–5 of the rejoin flow). A returning player goes through the normal room flow.

searchDocs.title: Kinds​
searchDocs.content: Kind	Buy	Stock	ActiveConsumable	Price coins for one copy	Copies[id]	The whole run that used a copy, even at 0 copies left Expiring	One of Variants (Seconds, Price)	Banked[id] (clock stopped) or Expires[id] (clock running)	While Expires > now  Expiring clock. The first equip moves Banked into Expires = now + Banked. Time added while the clock runs (a purchase or a grant) extends Expires. Time added while it is stopped goes to Banked. Unequip never pauses the clock, and the clock also runs while the player is offline.

searchDocs.title: Loadout rules​
searchDocs.content: Slots: per pool and kind (ShopPerkConfig.Slots[pool][kind]). Personal: 3 consumable (+1 at Lv 10, 30, 60; max 6) and 1 expiring (+1 at Lv 25, 50; max 3). Party: 1 consumable (+1 at Lv 45; max 2) and 1 expiring (+1 at Lv 70; max 2). Saved data is one dense list per pool; canEquip counts the equipped entries of the perk's own kind. The Lobby has one Studio row per slot (<Pool><Kind>Slot<i>, up to Base + #ExtraAtLevels) and LoadoutPage waits for each one, so a new slot level also needs a new row in PerkMenuGui.Equip appends to the end of the pool. Unequip removes one slot and the later slots move up. The saved lists never have gaps.Equip checks, in this order: unknown → hidden → wrong pool → level → not owned → already equipped → exclusive → no slot of its kind.Same perk once: a pool holds each perk at most once. Perks of one Family stack: Overcharged Rounds (+10%) and Marksman Tonic (+20%) give +30% gun damage. Family is a label for the catalog and GUI.Exclusive groups: a pool holds at most one perk per ExclusiveGroup: XPBoost (XP Booster, XP Booster II), CoinBoost (Coin Booster, Coin Booster II), Crit (Lucky Shot, Star Shot), AutoCannon (Smart Cannon, Orbital Sentinel) and BuildCost (Scrap Discount Card, Builder's Grant). Equip returns EXCLUSIVE and the Lobby card reads Can't use with <name>. Both clocks still run while equipped. Family stays a label only.Level gate applies to buy and equip, not to Grant. A granted perk above the player's level waits in the inventory.Hidden perks (Hidden = true in ShopPerkConfig, built batch by batch in Perk Rework part 5) cannot be bought or equipped.Prune runs on every profile load and before each buy, equip and grant. It deletes ended clocks and removes each loadout entry that is unknown, hidden, in the wrong pool or no longer owned, and each later entry of an exclusive group (old saves; the first in slot order stays), and each entry past the most slots of its kind (old saves; the first in list order stays — the level count is checked at equip, because the XP profile can load after the inventory). Unequip does not prune, so the slot index the client sent still points at the perk it shows.

searchDocs.title: Box-only super rares​
searchDocs.content: The 16 super rare perks (BoxOnly = true, all Expiring, UnlockLevel = 1, one variant with Price = 0) come only from a perk box (0.1% roll, see Quests). The shop list (PerkGuiRules.shopIds) skips them and canBuy returns BOX_ONLY; the Loadout and inventory pages show and equip them like any expiring perk, in the normal Expiring slots of their pool.

searchDocs.title: Dev test path​
searchDocs.content: /perk <id> in chat (Studio only, place owner / group rank 250+) grants the perk and puts it in this run's ActiveRun with its clock running, so a super rare can be tested without a 0.1% roll or a Lobby trip. See ReqDevActivatePerk in the Networking Map.

searchDocs.title: Coin shop​
searchDocs.content: Buy(player, id, variantIndex) checks that both the inventory and coin profiles are loaded, then the level gate and price (PerkLoadoutState.canBuy), then calls CoinManager.DeductCoins. Only after a successful deduct does it add the stock. A failed deduct changes nothing.

searchDocs.title: Grant​
searchDocs.content: PerkInventoryManager.Grant(player, id, amount, reason) gives stock with no price and no level gate: amount is copies for a consumable and seconds for an expiring perk. Hidden perks can be granted. Drops and the Battle Pass (Perk Rework part 6) use it.

searchDocs.title: Run start​
searchDocs.content: The Game Instance passes a run id to PerkInventoryManager.Initialize: game.PrivateServerId (the reserved server), else game.JobId, else a fresh GUID (both are empty in Studio, so each Studio Play is a new run). On each profile load, the manager first asks SessionCoordinator.IsAuthorized(player) (it yields until the roster is read, and is always true under the Studio bypass). A player the party lock bounces back to the Lobby keeps every copy: no run starts for them. For an authorized player, BeginRun:  If ConsumedRun == runId, this is a rejoin: ActiveRun stays and nothing is used.Otherwise it prunes, copies Loadout into ActiveRun, uses one copy of each equipped consumable, sets ConsumedRun, and prunes again. The second prune unequips consumables that reached 0, so the next run's loadout is honest. An expiring perk whose clock ended is not in ActiveRun.Fires Signals.OnShopPerksChanged(player) and replicates.  The Game Instance binds no buy, equip or unequip handler, so ActiveRun cannot change during the run. GetActiveRun(player) is the list Perk Rework part 3 reads. It returns the saved ActiveRun only when ConsumedRun is this server's run id; otherwise (the Lobby, a bounced player, a profile whose last run was another server) it returns empty lists, so an old run's perks can never apply. PerkInventorySync sends the same filtered list, so a client never shows an old run's perks.  Effects: PerkEffectsDispatcher reads GetActiveRun and GetExpires (the expiring clock ends) and republishes on OnShopPerksChanged and at each expiry; see Perks — Shop perk layer.

searchDocs.title: Loadout GUI​
searchDocs.content: The Lobby PerkMenuGui (see Perks — Client) has two shop perk pages. Button states come from the pure PerkLoadoutState and PerkGuiRules; every command runs in task.spawn and ignores the reply (the next PerkInventorySync reconciles).  Loadout page. The slot column starts with PoolTabs (Personal / Party), which picks the pool for the whole page. Below it the column shows that pool's rows: <Pool>ConsumableHeader + <Pool>ConsumableSlot1–N, then <Pool>ExpiringHeader + <Pool>ExpiringSlot1–N (N = the most slots of that kind); each kind header shows its used/open count. The inventory's FilterContainer holds only the kind filter; a Divider line sits in the gap between the two columns. PerkGuiRules.slotRows maps row i of a kind to the i-th list entry of that kind, so UnequipButton sends that entry's dense-list index (PerkInventoryClient.Unequip(pool, index); packets unchanged). A row above the player's count reads Locked · reach Lv N; an open row reads Empty slot; a filled row shows the kind mark, the name, the foot text and UnequipButton — also when an old save fills a row above the count. The inventory lists every known, non-hidden id in Copies, Banked or Expires, filtered by pool and kind (All / Consumable / Expiring); an empty list shows EmptyLabel. Foot text: ×N copies, <h:mm:ss> left (live), Banked <duration> or Expired (red). Card verb: Unequip (equipped), Equip, or the canEquip block reason (Requires Lv N, No free slot, Expired); clicking equips or unequips.Shop page. Cards follow the visible list rule within the pool and kind (PerkGuiRules.shopIds: the next milestone is found inside the filtered list, so a kind filter never goes blank); status Lv N, Own ×N or Owned; price from 1,000 when there are several variants. The detail shows the kind, <Group> · <Pool> · Lv N, the description, You own (foot text) and the note (Works for one run. / A second copy adds time. The effect does not double., plus the "counts once" sentence for Party). BuyButton1–3 show one price each (BUY, BUY 30 MIN, or REQUIRES LV N / NEED COINS when canBuy blocks); unused buttons are hidden.  The client clock is Workspace:GetServerTimeNow(), the same clock as the server's os.time() Expires.

searchDocs.title: Teleport hand-off​
searchDocs.content: A profile that is still open in the Lobby delays the session start in the Game Instance. PartyCreation.TeleportParty therefore calls PersistenceRegistry.ReleaseForTeleport(members) right before party:TeleportMembers. Each manager's release marks the player released, saves and ends the session, and its OnSessionEnd handler skips the usual kick. If TeleportMembers errors, or TeleportService.TeleportInitFailed fires for one member, PersistenceRegistry.Reopen starts the sessions again and the client gets fresh snapshots. In Studio ReserveServerAsync fails first, so this path runs only in a published test.  sequenceDiagram participant C as Lobby client participant L as PerkInventoryManager (Lobby) participant S as PerkLoadoutState participant P as PartyCreation participant G as PerkInventoryManager (Game Instance) C->>L: ReqEquipShopPerk(id, pool) L->>S: prune, canEquip, equip L-->>C: (ok, code) + PerkInventorySync P->>L: ReleaseForTeleport(members) P->>P: TeleportMembers G->>G: StartSessionAsync (no lock wait) G->>S: beginRun(runId) G-->>G: Signals.OnShopPerksChanged G-->>C: PerkInventorySync

searchDocs.title: Saved data​
searchDocs.content: Store PlayerPerkInventory (key = UserId), separate from PlayerPerks:  { Copies = {}, -- { [shopPerkId]: number } Banked = {}, -- { [shopPerkId]: seconds }, clock not started Expires = {}, -- { [shopPerkId]: os.time() clock end } Loadout = { Personal = {}, Party = {} }, ConsumedRun = "", ActiveRun = { Personal = {}, Party = {} }, SchemaVersion = 1, }

searchDocs.title: Result codes​
searchDocs.content: Code	Name	Meaning0	OK	Done 1	NO_PROFILE	Inventory or coin profile not loaded 2	UNKNOWN	Unknown id, bad argument, or an empty slot 3	HIDDEN	Not built yet (part 5) 4	LEVEL_REQUIRED	Player level below UnlockLevel 5	NOT_ENOUGH_COINS	Balance below the price 6	NOT_OWNED	No copy or no time left 7	NO_SLOT	Every slot of the perk's kind in the pool is full 8	WRONG_POOL	Personal perk sent to Party, or the reverse 9	ALREADY_EQUIPPED	The pool already holds this perk 10	BAD_VARIANT	No duration at that variant index 11	EXCLUSIVE	The pool already holds a perk of the same ExclusiveGroup 12	BOX_ONLY	A super rare: only a perk box grants it, the shop never sells it

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Equipping changes no stat until Perk Rework part 3 adds the shop layer to PerkEffectsDispatcher.The client commands yield until the server answers. In the Game Instance there is no handler, so they return nil after the Packet's 10 s timeout.The run start lives in PerkSystemLoader, a gameplay script, so a future Tutorial place would also use consumables. Decide that when the Tutorial exists.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleShared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PlaceableActions.luau	Client bind/unbind helper + poof visual renderer; auto-connects poof broadcast on the client side Server	src/ServerScriptService/PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau	Server validation, atomic claim, Tool grant, BroadcastPlaceablePoof dispatch Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau	PlaceableActions sub-table with all tuning knobs  Packets: ReqStashPlaceable, ReqMovePlaceable, BroadcastPlaceablePoof — see Networking MapSignals: OnPlaceableStashed, OnPlaceableMoved — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Binding the GUI​
searchDocs.content: PlaceableActions.bind(model, gui) wires MoveButton and StashButton into the packet system and returns a Binding with a single Unbind() method. On success the module fires Signals.OnPlaceableMoved or Signals.OnPlaceableStashed so other systems can react without polling. Call binding:Unbind() when the GUI closes — failing to unbind leaves the Janitor alive and button listeners connected to a GUI that may already be gone.

searchDocs.title: Poof visual​
searchDocs.content: The poof handler is client-only and lives in PlaceableActions.luau. On receiving BroadcastPlaceablePoof it clones the matching model from ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableItems, strips scripts/collisions/shadows from the clone, parents it to workspace.PlaceablePoofs, then runs a parallel MotionMaster.Sequence that shrinks every BasePart to near-zero while fading it out. The clone self-destructs when the sequence completes.

searchDocs.title: Server validation and atomic claim​
searchDocs.content: PlaceableActionsServer owns the OnServerInvoke handlers for ReqStashPlaceable and ReqMovePlaceable. It runs, in order: a per-player cooldown check (os.clock), an ancestry check (model.Parent == workspace.PlacedObjects), an attribute check (PlaceableName attribute on the model), a tool template check (ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools/<Name>), and a proximity check (HRP distance <= MaxActionDistance). The atomic claim pattern (model.Parent = nil followed by a re-read) prevents two simultaneous requests from granting the same item twice. The handler returns boolean — false on any failed check, true on full success.

searchDocs.title: Move and the revert store​
searchDocs.content: On a successful Move, the handler also calls PlaceableRevertStore.Set(player, { cframe = cframe, placeableName = placeableName, tool = newTool }), recording the item's original CFrame under the granted tool instance. This lets the build-mode cancel (RequestPlacementRevert) revert the item to its original spot if the player presses X without re-placing. The entry is cleared when the player re-places via PlaceItem, when the revert fires and consumes it, or when the player leaves the server.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Three requirements must all be present A placeable supports Stash/Move only when all three of the following exist simultaneously: A Model in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name> (already required for placement).A Tool template in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> with a PlaceableName attribute set to the same name string.ImageButton instances named exactly MoveButton and StashButton somewhere inside the GUI that PlaceableActions.bind is called with. Every match is wired, so a multi-page GUI (e.g. the Workbench) may repeat them per page. Either the Tool or a button may be omitted, but the missing one will log a warning and that action will be silently unavailable to the player. If PlaceableTools/<Name> is missing, the server returns false and nothing is destroyed — no item is lost — but the player gets no feedback.  The server proximity check (MaxActionDistance) is a second guard independent of the ProximityPrompt range. Keep them in sync when tuning the in-world prompt.Stash/Move discards all per-instance state on the placed model. The granted Tool is always a fresh clone from the template. If per-instance state matters, snapshot attributes before the action reaches the server.Any nearby player can stash any placement — ownership is not tracked. Add per-instance owner attributes and an ownership check in handleAction if griefing becomes a concern.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as PlaceableActions (client) participant S as PlaceableActionsServer participant O as All clients P->>C: Press MoveButton / StashButton C->>S: ReqMovePlaceable / ReqStashPlaceable S->>S: Cooldown check (per-player, os.clock) S->>S: Ancestry check (model.Parent == PlacedObjects) S->>S: Attribute check (PlaceableName) S->>S: Tool template check (PlaceableTools/<Name>) S->>S: Proximity check (HRP distance <= MaxActionDistance) S->>S: Atomic claim (model.Parent = nil, race guard) S->>S: Clone Tool -> player.Backpack alt Move S->>S: humanoid:EquipTool(newTool) end S->>O: BroadcastPlaceablePoof(cframe, placeableName, isMove) S->>S: model:Destroy() + record cooldown timestamp O->>O: PlaceableActions plays shrink tween + SFX

searchDocs.title: Entering build mode​
searchDocs.content: On tool equip, PlacementClient creates one PlacementSystem instance (grid size 2, tag BuildArea), calls SetBuildMode(true) and SetGhostModel(template), and fires ClientToggleGhost. It also fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(false) to disable the aim camera. PlacementCameraController then takes over: it freezes the player, swings the camera over the player and zooms out into a straight-down CameraType.Scriptable view that move input pans, fades any PlacementOccluder-tagged geometry, and exits through a CoolTransitions checkerboard. See Camera.

searchDocs.title: Tracking the ghost​
searchDocs.content: A Heartbeat loop rate-limited to GhostUpdateHz (default 20 Hz) raycasts, calls UpdateGhostPosition, and fires ClientUpdateGhost with the resulting CFrame. Signals.OnBuildValidityChanged fires whenever validity changes so UI and audio can react. Grid/free toggle, rotation, confirm, cancel, and ghost-lock are all driven by signals wired to BuildModeGuiController. The client listens for ServerToggleGhost / ServerUpdateGhost and calls SetOtherGhost to render other players' ghost previews.

searchDocs.title: Mobile build GUI​
searchDocs.content: BuildModeGui is touch-only (BuildModeGuiController enables it on OnBuildModeChanged when UserInputService.TouchEnabled). It is authored for an 844×390 phone; each container has a UIScale = clamp(min(W/844, H/390), 0.75, 1.5), refreshed on ViewportSize change.  StatusBar (top centre): StateBox holds StateChip + HintText — READY (green, "Tap to move · stick pans"), BLOCKED (red, "Can't place here"), or LOCKED (amber, "Unlock to move it"; wins over the other two). CancelButton sits beside it, far from PLACE.ActionCluster (bottom-right thumb corner, 212×212): a 108 px PlaceButton and three 72 px circles on an arc around it — RotateButton (left), LockButton (up-left), GridButton (up). GRID/LOCK show their on state with an amber stroke and label (GRID/FREE, LOCK/LOCKED). PLACE turns dark with a red stroke and reads BLOCKED while the spot is invalid; it stays tappable and PlacementClient ignores it.Validity comes from OnBuildValidityChanged. PlacementSystem.ClearGhostModel resets IsValid to false without firing, so the controller also resets to BLOCKED on every build-mode entry until the first valid ghost update.While building on touch, MobileGeneralGui, TrainFuelGui and HealthStaminaGui are disabled, and each returns to its own pre-build Enabled on exit. The native jump button hides because PlacementCameraController disables the Humanoid Jumping state during the freeze.

searchDocs.title: Server relay and validation​
searchDocs.content: PlacementServer relays ClientToggleGhost to other players after confirming the item name exists in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems, and relays ClientUpdateGhost (CFrame type-checked) to other players. On PlaceItem it enforces a per-player cooldown (PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 s), character/tool guards, ray-origin distance (MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 55 studs), final-position distance (MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60 studs), and collision validity — all using an isolated PlacementSystem instance with a ServerStorage-parented ghost that is never replicated.

searchDocs.title: Finalizing a placement​
searchDocs.content: On success, the server clones the template, calls finalizeModel (makes CollisionBox invisible + non-collidable, visual parts opaque, and tags the CollisionBox with PlacementObstruction so future placements collide with it), parents it to workspace/PlacedObjects, destroys the player's tool, and broadcasts ghost-clear to all clients. Any player whose character overlaps the placed item — the placer or anyone else — is then teleported clear of it (see Players never block; safe push-out).

searchDocs.title: Shared PlacementSystem​
searchDocs.content: PlacementSystem handles ghost model lifecycle, grid-snap vs free-placement position calculation, collision-box derivation, obstruction validity check, and other-player ghost rendering. IS_CLIENT guards prevent Texture and TweenPlus calls from running on the server; SetBuildMode is client-only (it creates grid Texture instances on build area parts), while the server sets IsBuildMode = true directly. Each PlaceItem request creates an isolated PlacementSystem instance — this is intentional, so concurrent requests from different players cannot corrupt shared state. Never cache a server-side PlacementSystem across requests.

searchDocs.title: Cancelling build mode​
searchDocs.content: Pressing X (configurable via PlacementConfig.CancelKey) or the on-screen Cancel button (mobile) fires Signals.RequestPlacementCancel. Both paths reach the same cancelPlacement function in PlacementClient, which snaps build-mode visuals off and sends a RequestPlacementRevert RemoteFunction call to the server. Escape is intentionally not used — Roblox reserves it for the in-game menu.  The server checks PlaceableRevertStore to determine the outcome:  Session type	OutcomeFresh placement (item was never placed before)	Server returns false → client calls humanoid:UnequipTools() and the tool returns to the Backpack Move session, original spot is free	Server re-places the item at its original CFrame, destroys the tool, returns true → item reverts, no unequip needed Move session, original spot is occupied	Server returns false → client falls back to unequip  See Placeable Actions for how a Move session records the revert entry.

searchDocs.title: Players never block; safe push-out​
searchDocs.content: BuildObstructionFilter never includes player characters, so no player blocks the client ghost or the server check. NPCs, placed items, and PlacementObstruction fixtures still block. After the item is parented, pushPlayersClearOfBox in PlacementServer finds every character overlapping the item's collision box and teleports each one:  Nearest safe spot around the box (findSafeSpot): 8 directions, starting toward the player, each far enough out that a PUSH_CHARACTER_SIZE box clears the item along that direction (box half-extent + character half-extent + PUSH_ITEM_GAP). A spot is safe when it is inside the BuildArea footprint (shrunk by the clearance), a floor exists within PUSH_FLOOR_PROBE studs below, and a PUSH_CHARACTER_SIZE box there touches no PlacementObstruction part.Else beside the nearest living player who is not in the box (same search, zero-size box around them).Else spawn: player.RespawnLocation or the first SpawnLocation, 3 studs above it.Else the player stays and the server logs a warn.  The revert path uses the same function.  The platform it clamps into comes from PlacementSystem.LastBuildAreaPart, populated only by CalculatePlacement's raycast (the PlaceItem path). The revert path re-places at a stored CFrame and never calls CalculatePlacement, so LastBuildAreaPart is nil there; PlacementServer falls back to findBuildAreaBelow, a dedicated helper that raycasts straight down from the revert position (filtered to the BuildArea tag, the same idiom CalculatePlacement uses) to resolve the platform part.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit — do not relax the server thresholds MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 55 (sized to the top-down camera's reach, sqrt(PanRadius² + ZoomMax²)), MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60, and PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 in PlacementServer are the primary defences against remote placement exploits. Raising these values substantially would allow clients to place items anywhere in the world or spam unlimited items.  Model structure is required. Every entry in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems must have a CollisionBox (BasePart) child. Without it, PlacementSystem warns and falls back to bounding-box collision, which can cause floating or incorrect validity checks.Obstruction is tag-driven, not folder-driven. Build placement only avoids a volume if it is tagged PlacementObstruction. Placed items are tagged automatically on their CollisionBox by finalizeModel. Any static world model that placement must respect (e.g. TrainShieldGeneratorPlaceholder, ResearchBench) must have a CollisionBox BasePart tagged PlacementObstruction by hand. Tag the CollisionBox part only, never the whole model — sibling sub-models like TrajectoryPoints would otherwise become map-wide placement blockers.CollisionBox must not be named RootPart or tagged PlacementIgnore. Those names cause the part to be treated as invisible/non-collidable in the ghost.SetBuildMode must only be called on the client. Calling it on the server would create Texture instances in workspace and replicate them to all clients.Ghost relay is observer-only. The GhostModels folder and its contents exist only on the client; the server's validity check correctly skips that folder for this reason.Cutscene and combat gates (isInCutscene, isInCombat) in PlacementClient are not yet wired to any external system — they are TODO integration points.  Server-side security thresholds live in PlacementServer.server.luau as local constants (MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE, MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE, PLACE_COOLDOWN) — treat them as sensitive anti-exploit values.
