searchDocs.title: Point and coin economy​
searchDocs.content: Each level-up grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point.Available points = playerLevel - spent, computed by PerkState.available — points are never stored directly. spent = the pool's perk levels plus the UnlockPointCost of every unlocked perk in that pool.Points cannot go negative; the pool is floored at 0.Upgrade cost: level n of a perk costs 1 point + UpgradeCoinStep × n coins. PerkState.upgradeCost(perkId, n) is the single price source (server, PerkClient, GUI). UpgradeCoinStep is 100, 200 or 350 per perk (perk review part 5 moved unlock levels but kept the coin steps). Starters pay upgrade coins too.Respec costs nothing to start, returns all points in the chosen pool, re-locks non-starter perks, and refunds every coin paid on them (see Coin ledger).Points carry across places because PerkManager uses the same DataStore key (PlayerPerks) everywhere in the universe.  PerkConfig.Perks is the single tuning surface. Each perk has Category, DisplayName, Description, MaxLevel, display Order, a Buffs list, the unlock fields, UpgradeCoinStep, and an optional Hidden flag. Each BuffSpec is { Key, PerLevel, Format? }: the dispatcher publishes PerLevel * level under Key.  PerkState.effectText(perkId, level) builds the GUI text: every {i} in Description becomes the formatted value of Buffs[i]. Format picks the formatting: "percent" (default, 0.025 → 2.5%), "count" (whole number), "total" (1 + value — Wide Net shows the whole net size), "seconds" (1.5 s). Example: Field Medic at level 5 reads +50% regen, −1.5 s regen delay.

searchDocs.title: Unlock gate​
searchDocs.content: Every perk declares an UnlockLevel (player level) gate plus a one-time cost: UnlockCost (coins) and UnlockPointCost (points from the perk's own pool). A perk with all three at 0 is a free starter, auto-unlocked: Iron Constitution (Personal) and Scavenger's Eye (Party).  Unlock is permanent: it persists on the PlayerPerks profile as an Unlocked map ({ [perkId]: boolean }).  function PerkManager.UnlockPerk(player: Player, perkId: string): (boolean, number) function PerkManager.AllocatePoint(player: Player, perkId: string): (boolean, number)   UnlockPerk validates with PerkState.canUnlock (order: UNKNOWN_PERK → PERK_UNAVAILABLE → ALREADY_UNLOCKED → LEVEL_REQUIRED → NO_POINTS → NOT_ENOUGH_COINS), deducts UnlockCost via CoinManager.DeductCoins, records it in the ledger, marks the perk unlocked, and replicates. AllocatePoint validates with PerkState.canAllocate (order: UNKNOWN_PERK → PERK_UNAVAILABLE → PERK_LOCKED → AT_MAX_LEVEL → LEVEL_REQUIRED (upgrade gate) → NO_POINTS → NOT_ENOUGH_COINS), deducts the upgrade coins before it raises the level (a failed deduct changes nothing), records them in the ledger, fires OnPerkStateChanged, and replicates. The frozen enum (PerkResultCodes):  Code	Value	MeaningOK	0	Success NO_PROFILE	1	Profile not loaded UNKNOWN_PERK	2	Perk id not in PerkConfig AT_MAX_LEVEL	3	Already at MaxLevel NO_POINTS	4	Pool can't pay (upgrade: < 1; unlock: < UnlockPointCost) PERK_LOCKED	5	Perk not yet unlocked ALREADY_UNLOCKED	6	Unlock requested twice LEVEL_REQUIRED	7	Below UnlockLevel (unlock) or the upgrade gate (upgrade) NOT_ENOUGH_COINS	8	Below UnlockCost (unlock) or the upgrade price (upgrade) NOTHING_TO_RESET	9	Per-perk respec on a perk at level 0 that is locked or a starter PERK_UNAVAILABLE	10	Perk is Hidden (declared, mechanic not built yet)  Unlocking a perk changes no buffs (its level is still 0), so UnlockPerk does not fire Signals.OnPerkStateChanged.  Hidden perks. A perk whose mechanic is not built yet ships with Hidden = true. canUnlock/canAllocate return PERK_UNAVAILABLE, and PerkClient never lists or commands it. PerkState.spent still counts its levels, so un-hiding needs no migration. Wreck Salvage (Plunder) is hidden until enemy ships exist (perk review part 3). Levels carried over from Plunder stay and still use Party points; the Party pool "reset all" (PerkManager.Respec) refunds them, because a hidden perk has no card for the per-perk respec.

searchDocs.title: Upgrade gates​
searchDocs.content: Each perk level also needs a player level: PerkState.upgradeGate(perkId, n) = UnlockLevel + ceil((n − 1) × UPGRADE_GATE_SPAN / (MaxLevel − 1)), capped at XPConfig.MAX_LEVEL. Level 1 needs UnlockLevel; the max level needs UnlockLevel + 35 (PerkConfig.UPGRADE_GATE_SPAN). Example: Ricochet (unlock 65, max 5) → levels at player Lv 65 / 74 / 83 / 92 / 100. canAllocate refuses a level under its gate with LEVEL_REQUIRED. Levels a save already holds above the gate stay; only new levels are checked.  Unlock levels are spread over player levels 1–75 in power bands (Basic 1–20, Mid 20–45, Strong 45–75). Levels 76–100 open only upgrade gates (the last loadout slot opens at Lv 70). See Progression — what each level opens.

searchDocs.title: Coin ledger​
searchDocs.content: CoinsSpent: { [perkId]: number } on the profile records every coin paid per perk (unlock + each upgrade). Respec (PerkManager.Respec, a pool) and per-perk respec (PerkManager.RespecPerk) refund exactly CoinsSpent[perkId] through CoinManager.RefundCoins — un-inflated, not scaled by the Pocket Change CoinGainBonus — then clear the entry. Only the ledger decides a refund, never current prices, so a later re-tune of UnlockCost or UpgradeCoinStep never changes what a reset returns. If the coin profile is gone mid-respec, the perk is still reset and a warn names the lost amount.  Respec clears PerkLevels, re-locks non-starter perks, then re-seeds starters. Per-perk respec is validated by PerkState.canRespecPerk (UNKNOWN_PERK → NOTHING_TO_RESET). Both fire OnPerkStateChanged and replicate. The starter rule lives in one place, PerkState.isStarter.

searchDocs.title: Migration​
searchDocs.content: migrateAndSeed runs on every load; each step is version-guarded:  Schema 1 (PerkSchemaVersion < 1): one-time clean-slate wipe of PerkLevels/Unlocked.Schema 2 (PerkSchemaVersion < 2, the Perk Rework): the 12 old perks are gone. The v1 unlock prices of every old unlocked perk (frozen in LEGACY_V1_UNLOCK_COSTS inside PerkManager; starters add 0) are added to the persisted PendingLegacyRefund, then PerkLevels, Unlocked and CoinsSpent are wiped and the version is set to 2.Starters are re-seeded after the steps.  The wipe never waits. The payout waits for the coin profile: payLegacyRefund polls CoinManager.IsLoaded for up to 60 s, then refunds PendingLegacyRefund and sets it to 0. If the coin profile does not load in time (or the perk session ends first), the amount stays saved and is paid on a later join — never lost, never paid twice.

searchDocs.title: Where perk commands run​
searchDocs.content: PerkManager.Initialize() loads profiles, migrates, replicates and resends on level-up. The four request packets are bound only by PerkManager.WireCommandHandlers(), which only the Lobby's PerkLoadoutService calls: perk changes are Lobby-only. In the Game Instance the Perk menu's buttons get no answer (Studio logs OnServerInvoke not found) until Perk Rework part 4 makes that menu read-only.  PerkManager, CoinManager, XPManager and PerkInventoryManager each register a teleport hand-off with PersistenceRegistry: the Lobby ends their sessions without a kick right before a party teleport and reopens them if it fails. See Perk Inventory.  Shop perks (consumable and expiring, equipped in the Lobby) are a separate system: see Perk Inventory.

searchDocs.title: Party-max resolution​
searchDocs.content: Party perks apply to the entire server, but only the highest level held by any single player is active. If Player A has Fuel Saver 6 and Player B has Fuel Saver 3, the server resolves at 6. PerkEffectsDispatcher recomputes the max on every allocate, respec, player join, and player leave.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk layer​
searchDocs.content: Perk Rework part 3 adds shop perks on top of the permanent perks. PerkEffectsDispatcher stays the only writer; for every key:  Personal: permanent value + the sum of the player's live shop perks.Party: permanent party max + each live party shop perk, counted once. Two players with the same party perk do not stack; different perks of one family do. <ShopPerkId>HolderId names the first holder (0 = not active).Largest wins (ShopPerkEffects.MAX_KEYS): for AutoLoaderRate and BuildCostReduction the shop layer keeps the largest value instead of the sum, because a super rare replaces its shop twin (Orbital Sentinel, auto cannons 60%, over Smart Cannon, 30%; Builder's Grant, builds 35% cheaper, over Scrap Discount Card, 20%). Two players can hold one of each, so the loadout ExclusiveGroup alone is not enough. Permanent perks still add on top.  A shop perk is live when it is in this run's ActiveRun (read only through PerkInventoryManager.GetActiveRun), visible, and (expiring) its clock has not ended. Every shop key is written each publish (0 when nothing is live), so an ended perk clears its key. The math lives in the pure ShopPerkEffects module (Studio self-check at boot). A shop key with no reader logs one warn at boot.  Expiry: the clock is real time. The dispatcher keeps one task.delay to the earliest upcoming expiry among present players and republishes when it fires, so a perk can end mid-run.  Junk bridges: JunkService overwrites its multipliers, so the dispatcher sends one value per tier — tier 1 1 − TierOneShift, tier 2 1 + TierOneShift · w1 / w2 (Golden Lure keeps the tier 1+2 total), tiers 3–5 1 + JunkTierRarityBonus — and ApplyTypeMultiplier("Energy", 1 + EnergySpawnBonus) (Energy Forecast).

searchDocs.title: Buff contract​
searchDocs.content: PerkEffectsDispatcher is the sole writer of the buff folders — every other system reads, never writes. It listens to Signals.OnPerkStateChanged, Signals.OnShopPerksChanged, PlayerAdded, PlayerRemoving and the next shop perk expiry, then calls publishPersonal and publishParty. Both write every BuffSpec.Key of every perk in the pool, and every shop key of the pool. searchDocs.title: Armor damage mitigation​
searchDocs.content: Crafted armor (see Armor / ArmorConfig / ArmorManager) is the base of this mitigation, not the perk. HealthManager's damage sink calls ArmorManager.Absorb(player, amount, efficiency), passing the player's ArmorEfficiency perk bonus read fresh on every hit. The Plated perk does not reduce damage on its own; it's an efficiency multiplier on the equipped kind's BaseReduction, applied identically whether the worn kind is Ballistic or Energy:  reduction = clamp(kind.BaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, ArmorConfig.MaxReductionCap)   Absorb scales amount by (1 - reduction) as the final step before it reaches health, and drains the worn kind's pool by whatever was absorbed — mitigation and pool drain happen in the same call, because the two cannot be split without the pool going stale (see Armor — Mitigation). With nothing equipped, or an Energy kind at zero pool, the perk contributes nothing. Because the attacker's DamageBonus is already applied upstream in WeaponServer, attacker bonus and defender mitigation multiply independently: base * (1 + DamageBonus) * (1 - reduction). Coverage is every path routed through CombatService/HealthManager (Bullet/AOE and NPC hits); damage written directly to Humanoid.Health bypasses the sink and is not mitigated (see Health).

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: PerkClient.luau is the GUI-agnostic data layer (owns no GUI). It caches the authoritative PerkStateSync snapshot (perkLevels, unlocked, personalAvailable, partyAvailable, playerLevel, coinsSpent) and watches the replicated PartyPerkBuffs folder. A snapshot without coinsSpent (an older server during a live update) reads as {}. Queries return PerkView descriptors via GetPerks/GetActivePerks/GetAvailablePoints/GetPerk/GetPlayerLevel; hidden perks are skipped. Commands: optimistic-prediction Allocate/Respec/CanRespec, plus Unlock(perkId) (no optimistic coin prediction — the server owns the balance), and a Changed signal fired on every snapshot update.  "Active" is category-aware: a Personal perk is active at the player's Level > 0; a Party perk is active at its server-wide ActivePartyLevel > 0 (read from <PerkId>Level). PerkView carries Group, Summary, EffectText, NextEffectText (nil at max), UpgradeCost (coins for the next level, 0 at max), UpgradeGate (player level for the next level, 0 at max), CoinsSpent (what a reset refunds), CanRespec, the unlock fields, and for Party perks ActiveEffectText and ActivePartyHolder: Player? (from <PerkId>HolderId). PerkController.client.luau is the one-line bootstrap that calls PerkClient.Init() once on join.  Active Perks menu. ActivePerksGuiController.client.luau binds the Studio-authored StarterGui.ActivePerksGui, a read-only view and the Game Instance's only perk GUI. It opens from a TopbarPlus "Active Perks" icon (toggle key O; CloseButton deselects it). Personal / Party tabs (Bottom.LeftColumn.CategoryContainer, above the list) list PerkClient.GetActivePerks(tab) into LeftColumn.PerkContainer (clones of ExampleItem: icon, name, value), then the run's shop perks: Personal = ActiveRun.Personal minus ended clocks (PerkGuiRules.liveRunIds); Party = every party shop perk with PartyPerkBuffs.<Id>HolderId ~= 0, by Order. Each row is styled by its type (there is no rarity config): PERMANENT (permanent perk, line stroke), THIS RUN (Consumable, mint), TIMED (Expiring, orange) and SUPER RARE (BoxOnly, wins over Kind: amber stroke on a wine fill); the selected row gets a brighter fill and keeps its stroke. The row value is LV n (Party: the active server level), RUN or the time left. The detail panel (Bottom.InfoContainer) shows the icon, the name, a type tag and the Group tag, PerkConfig.CategoryBlurb (hidden on phones), a LevelBox (LEVEL n / max, LASTS THIS RUN, or TIME LEFT h:mm:ss — your own clock, ticking once a second while open; — for a Party perk only another player holds, since the client knows only its own clocks), an OwnerBox (HELD BY You / the Party holder, hidden when nil) and the effect line (shop perks: Description). It repaints on PerkClient.Changed (also PartyPerkBuffs changes) and PerkInventoryClient.Changed; an own clock that ends drops its row. A tab with nothing active shows EmptyNote. Size follows the screen through MainContainer.UIScale (wide = min(W / 1920, H / 1022); below 0.68 the compact phone layout, the WorkbenchGuiController pattern). It has no reset button: perk changes are Lobby-only.  Lobby Perk menu. PerkMenuGuiController/ (Lobby only) binds the Studio-authored StarterGui.PerkMenuGui: one window with three pages, a header and three TopbarPlus icons on the right of the topbar (align("Right"); the left side holds the Roblox chat and native buttons). "Perks" (key P) opens the Upgrade tab, "Loadout" (key L) the Loadout tab and "Shop" (key B) the Shop tab; pressing the icon of the open tab closes the menu, another icon switches tab (all icons have autoDeselect(false); the window is the one source of truth). Each page picks its pool with a PoolTabs bar (Personal / Party tab buttons in a dark rounded frame, the ActivePerksGui CategoryContainer pattern): on Upgrade and Shop it is the first item of FilterContainer, one card column wide; on Loadout it tops the slot column. CloseButton closes; a part tagged PerkKiosk with a ProximityPrompt opens the Loadout tab. MainContainer.UIScale = min(W / 1920, H / 1022) of the ScreenGui area. The header shows the level (PerkClient.GetPlayerLevel), the pool points (Upgrade tab only) and the coins (— until the first Signals.OnCoinsChanged; the controller connects it before its first yield). Every page repaints on PerkClient.Changed, PerkInventoryClient.Changed and OnCoinsChanged while open; countdowns tick once a second without rebuilding the lists. All text and list rules live in the pure PerkGuiRules; selected / unselected looks are read from the authored instances (LoadoutTab / UpgradeTab; the Loadout page's AllButton / ConsumableButton for the kind filters; the Upgrade page's PoolTabs.PersonalButton / PoolTabs.PartyButton for the pool tabs; Pip1 / Pip4).  Upgrade page. Cards follow the visible list rule (reachable perks plus the next milestone level, sorted by UnlockLevel then Order). Unlocked: n/max or MAX and pips. Locked: dimmed, Lv N / Unlock / Locked, and CostLabel (1 pt + 250 coins). The detail shows PERMANENT, <Group> · Lv n / max or <Group> · Unlock at Lv N, the Summary, Now / Next effects, and Show all levels (an unlock row plus one row per level, owned rows in 94D2BD). UpgradeButton follows PerkGuiRules.upgradeAction: Requires Lv N, Need points, Need coins, Unlock, Maxed, Needs Lv N (upgrade gate), Upgrade; only Unlock (PerkClient.Unlock) and Upgrade (PerkClient.Allocate) act. LeftContainer.FilterContainer.PoolTabs picks the pool (Personal at start).  RespecButton (gray) resets the selected perk → PerkClient.RespecPerk; enabled when view.CanRespec, and hidden while no perk is selected.RespecAllButton (red) resets the shown pool → PerkClient.Respec(pool); enabled when PerkClient.CanRespec(pool). Its Label reads HOLD TO RESET <POOL>.  Each SubLabel shows the refund: CoinsSpent and points (levels + unlock points). Switching the filter, the tab or closing the menu cancels both holds. The Loadout and Shop pages are described in Perk Inventory — Loadout GUI.  Hold-to-reset. HoldButton.luau drives every reset button. Each button holds a Studio-authored HoldFill (Frame; 9B2226 in the Lobby PerkMenuGui) with a UIGradient whose transparency has a hard edge at 0.5, and a Label. Pressing sweeps the gradient Offset from (-0.6, 0) to (0.5, 0) (start past -0.5 so no sliver shows at the left edge) over PerkConfig.RESPEC_PERK_HOLD_TIME (one perk) or PerkConfig.RESPEC_HOLD_TIME (a whole pool) (MotionMaster, linear). Releasing anywhere, closing the menu, or changing the selection / tab cancels and empties the fill. A disabled button dims its Label and ignores presses.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: New readers must use PerkBuffRead Read buff values through PerkBuffRead.Personal / PerkBuffRead.Party, and apply reductions with PerkBuffRead.Reduce / ReduceCost. Do not add new inline PerkBuffs folder lookups, and never let a reduction stack reach zero. PerkBuffRead and PerkState run Studio-only boot asserts on the shared math.  Points are derived, not stored Available points are never stored directly. Available points = level - spent. Never add a separate stored point counter — it will desync.  Refunds come from the ledger only A respec refunds CoinsSpent[perkId], never a price recomputed from the config. Any new coin charge on a perk must call recordPaid, or a reset will under-refund.  Party perk levels shown in the GUI are per-player, not the resolved active level A Party card's LV n/max and the detail panel's CURRENT LEVEL show how many levels this player bought. The Active Perks menu shows the server-resolved max.  PerkEffectsDispatcher must run before PerkManager on join PerkEffectsDispatcher seeds its folder at boot. PerkManager fires OnPerkStateChanged after profile load, which triggers a republish. The ordering is correct because both are ServerScriptService scripts and PerkManager.Initialize() is called from PerkSystemLoader, which yields on ProfileStore:StartSessionAsync before firing the signal.  HPBonus subscription attaches once at join HealthManager subscribes to the HPBonus attribute change in PlayerAdded, not CharacterAdded. If PerkBuffs/<UserId> does not exist at join time (the dispatcher hasn't seeded yet), the subscription is skipped for that session. In practice the dispatcher seeds synchronously at boot, so the folder exists before any player's PlayerAdded fires normally.

searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Client as PerkController (client) participant Manager as PerkManager (server) participant Coins as CoinManager (server) participant Dispatcher as PerkEffectsDispatcher (server) Note over Manager: JOIN Manager->>Manager: profile loaded (migrateAndSeed: schema steps + seedStarters) Manager->>Coins: payLegacyRefund (waits for IsLoaded, then RefundCoins) Manager->>Client: PerkStateSync(levels, unlocked, personalAvail, partyAvail, playerLevel, coinsSpent) Manager->>Dispatcher: publish personal buffs (0s); publishParty() Note over Client,Manager: UNLOCK Client->>Manager: ReqUnlockPerk(perkId) Manager->>Coins: DeductCoins(UnlockCost) Manager->>Manager: CoinsSpent[perkId] += UnlockCost; Unlocked[perkId] = true Manager->>Client: PerkStateSync (no OnPerkStateChanged — buffs unchanged) Note over Client,Manager: ALLOCATE (upgrade) Client->>Client: optimistic level++, avail--; repaint() Client->>Manager: ReqAllocatePerk(perkId) Manager->>Manager: canAllocate (points + coins) Manager->>Coins: DeductCoins(UpgradeCoinStep × nextLevel) Manager->>Manager: CoinsSpent[perkId] += cost; level++ Manager->>Dispatcher: Signals.OnPerkStateChanged:Fire(player) Manager->>Client: PerkStateSync(...) Dispatcher->>Dispatcher: publishPersonal(player); publishParty() Note over Client,Manager: RESPEC Client->>Manager: ReqRespecPerk(perkId) / ReqRespecPerks(pool) Manager->>Coins: RefundCoins(CoinsSpent[perkId]) Manager->>Manager: clear level + ledger; re-lock non-starters Manager->>Dispatcher: Signals.OnPerkStateChanged:Fire(player) Manager->>Client: PerkStateSync(...) searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: PerkConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luauPlaybooks: Tune Perks, Tune Perk Unlocks  Field	EffectPerks[id].Buffs	List of { Key, PerLevel, Format? }; each key publishes PerLevel * level. Perks[id].MaxLevel	Cap on levels in this perk. Perks[id].DisplayName	Shown in the perk panel header. Perks[id].Description	Effect text; {1}, {2} … become the formatted value of Buffs[1], Buffs[2] …. Perks[id].UnlockCost	One-time coin cost to unlock (0 = free starter). Perks[id].UnlockLevel	Minimum player XP level required to unlock (0 = none). Perks[id].UnlockPointCost	One-time point cost from the perk's own pool; counted as spent, returned by respec (0 = free). Perks[id].UpgradeCoinStep	Level n costs UpgradeCoinStep × n coins. Re-tuning never changes refunds (ledger). Perks[id].Hidden	true = declared but not listed or unlockable (part 5 flips it). UPGRADE_GATE_SPAN	Player levels from a perk's unlock to its max-level gate (35). MIN_REDUCTION_FACTOR	Lowest fraction of a base value any reduction can leave (default 0.1). NET_REEL_SLOWDOWN_PER_EXTRA	Wide Net: reel slows by this fraction per extra junk in one cast (default 0.10). RESPEC_HOLD_TIME	Seconds a reset-all (whole pool) button must be held before the respec fires (default 3). RESPEC_PERK_HOLD_TIME	Seconds a single-perk reset button must be held (default 0.75; shorter, as it undoes much less). CategoryBlurb	One-line pool explanation shown in both perk menus' detail panels. STORE_NAME	ProfileStore key — change this only if you intentionally want to wipe all saved perk + unlock data.

searchDocs.title: Data model and curve​
searchDocs.content: The profile stores a single value, TotalXP (lifetime cumulative). Level and progress are never stored — they're derived from it every time via XPCurve:  XPCurve.xpToNext(level: number): number -- round(CURVE_COEFF * level ^ CURVE_EXP) + CURVE_OFFSET, 0 at/above MAX_LEVEL XPCurve.levelFromTotal(totalXP: number): number XPCurve.progress(totalXP: number): (level: number, xpIntoLevel: number, xpForNextLevel: number)   Defaults: CURVE_COEFF = 5, CURVE_EXP = 1.5, CURVE_OFFSET = 45, MAX_LEVEL = 100. Total XP to reach level 100 is roughly 204,000. All constants live in XPConfig.

searchDocs.title: Earning (party-shared)​
searchDocs.content: XP is shared with the whole party; one party occupies one server, so every living player in the server receives the full award via XPManager.AddPartyXP. Down players (ReviveState, see Paid Revive) get no kill or party XP; XPManager requires ReviveState, so the Lobby maps it too (nobody is down there).  Source	Amount	TriggerDistance	DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK (1) every DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS (5s)	Train is in its "go" state (running, not braked/stalled) — driven off Signals.SetTrainState Run reward	(50 + 15/min) × time multiplier × short-run factor, via AddXP (personal, not party-shared)	RunEndService, once per player per run — see Run Results Kills	KILL_XP (10) × (1 + KillXPBonus + PartyKillRewardBonus) per player, via AddXP	Any EnemyNPC-tagged model's Humanoid.Died (attribution-agnostic). The same hook pays CoinConfig.KILL_COINS — see Economy  The train starts braked, so no distance XP accrues before the first un-brake.  Perk multiplier: AddXP scales every award by 1 + XPGainBonus + PartyXPBonus (XP Booster, XP Booster II, Veteran Voyager). TotalXP stays whole; the fraction carries to the player's next award (in memory only, dropped on leave).  function XPManager.AddXP(player: Player, amount: number): number -- whole XP added function XPManager.GainMultiplier(player: Player): number -- 1 + XPGainBonus + PartyXPBonus function XPManager.AddPartyXP(amount: number)   Both are no-ops (AddXP returns 0) if amount <= 0 or the profile isn't loaded. AddXP fires XPLevelUp (to all clients) and Signals.OnPlayerLevelUp when the level increases, then replicates XPStateSync.

searchDocs.title: Level-up VFX​
searchDocs.content: XPLevelUp(player, level) reaches every client. Each one clones ReplicatedStorage.<LEVELUP_VFX> at that player's feet (keeping the template's own rotation; the art part is turned 0,0,90 so its emitters point up), welds it to the HumanoidRootPart so it follows the player, and emits each emitter's EmitCount once (Bloom 1, Star 1, Ring 1, Sparks 40). The beam holds LEVELUP_VFX_BEAM_HOLD (1 s), then shrinks to 0 width over LEVELUP_VFX_BEAM_FADE (0.4 s) with MotionMaster; Debris removes the clone after 3 s. A character that is not streamed in, is dead, or a place without the template skips it silently. Only the owner's client raises the toast.

searchDocs.title: Cross-place sharing (lobby ↔ gameplay)​
searchDocs.content: DataStores are universe-wide: both places use the same STORE_NAME and key (tostring(UserId)), so XP/Level are shared automatically. The Lobby runs XPManager.Initialize() from places/Lobby/ServerScriptService/PerkLoadoutService.server.luau (perk points and level gates need the level) but not XPSystemLoader — there are no earners in the Lobby.  Teleport hand-off. XPManager registers a PersistenceRegistry.RegisterHandoff pair: right before a party teleport the Lobby ends the session without the usual kick, so the Game Instance opens it without waiting on the session lock, and reopens it if the teleport fails. See Perk Inventory — Teleport hand-off.  Leaderboard. XPManager offers the player's TotalXP to the HIGHEST LEVEL board (LeaderboardWriter.Max) on profile load and after every AddXP, so players from before the board appear on their next join. See Leaderboard.  XPManager.IsLoaded(player) reports whether the XP profile is loaded. GetLevel returns 1 until then, so PerkManager waits for IsLoaded (up to 30 s) before its first perk snapshot, or the snapshot would show level-1 points.

searchDocs.title: Not yet built​
searchDocs.content: An XP bar HUD (would consume OnXPChanged), level rewards (hook: XPLevelUp), per-killer attribution, and additional XP sources are all unbuilt.

searchDocs.title: What each level opens​
searchDocs.content: Perks and loadout slots unlock over player levels 1–75 (perk review part 5). Levels 76–100 open only permanent-perk upgrade gates (the last loadout slot opens at Lv 70).  Levels	Opens1–20	Basic perks (both pools, all kinds). Personal consumable slot 4 at Lv 10. 20–50	Mid perks; the full Basic and Mid sets by Lv 50. Personal expiring slot 2 at Lv 25, consumable slot 5 at Lv 30, Party consumable slot 2 at Lv 45, Personal expiring slot 3 at Lv 50. 50–75	Strong perks: Wide Net, Ricochet, Gun Crew, Emergency Generator, Gold Rush, XP / Coin Booster II, Smart Cannon, Energy Recycler, Cannon Drill, Golden Lure (Lv 75). Personal consumable slot 6 at Lv 60, Party expiring slot 2 at Lv 70. 76–100	Upgrade gates only: the max level of a perk needs UnlockLevel + 35.  Tuning lives in PerkConfig / ShopPerkConfig (UnlockLevel, UPGRADE_GATE_SPAN, Slots); see Perks and Perk Inventory.

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ProximityPickupController.client.luau	PickupItemReady hover/spin, PickupItemClaimed float-to-hand animation and SFX Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ProximityPickupServer.luau	RegisterItem, Claim, zone creation, shared-loot zone.Touched handler, _TryMerge, player-disconnect cleanup Server	src/ServerScriptService/DroppedToolService.server.luau	DroppableSurface tag wiring, DescendantAdded drop detection, DropLandingHelper integration Shared	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/CollisionGroups.luau	Centralized registrar for every collision group + its collidability matrix Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ProximityPickupConfig.luau	Radius, float duration, hover/spin parameters, merge settings, landing poll constants  Packets: PickupItemClaimed, PickupItemReady — see Networking MapSignals: none — this system communicates only via Packets and Roblox-native events (AncestryChanged, CollectionService, zone.Touched)

searchDocs.title: Drop path​
searchDocs.content: Pressing Backspace drops the equipped Tool as a direct child of workspace. A workspace.DescendantAdded listener in DroppedToolService catches craft-material Tools parented directly to workspace (the Roblox default Backspace drop path). The handle's CollisionGroup is set to "DroppedMaterial", CanCollide = true, Anchored = false. DropLandingHelper.waitForLanding(handle) then polls every DROP_POLL_INTERVAL (0.1 s) for DroppableSurface contact and a velocity below SETTLED_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD (0.5 studs/s). On landing, the handle is re-anchored with rotation reset to identity, and ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem(tool, metadata, callback, keepModel=true) is called.  DroppedToolService also bootstraps two PhysicsService collision groups: DroppedMaterial (Tools that leave the player's hand) and DroppableSurface (tagged geometry). DroppedMaterial is non-collidable with Default and collidable with DroppableSurface, so dropped items fall through characters and walls but land on tagged floors.

searchDocs.title: Registration and claim​
searchDocs.content: ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem(part, metadata, callback, keepModel?) is the sole public registration entry. It generates a GUID itemId, sets PickupItemId on the part as an attribute, tags the part "PickupItem", spawns an invisible anchored sphere zone (DEFAULT_RADIUS = 6 studs) in workspace.PickupZones, and fires PickupItemReady to all clients. zone.Touched is the primary claim trigger — any player, shared-loot semantics. Claim(part, player) is the programmatic claim path (no current caller). Both paths call the same executeClaimAsync, which transitions the record to "Claimed", destroys the zone, broadcasts PickupItemClaimed, then after FLOAT_DURATION (0.25 s) calls the callback and cleans up.  _TryMerge runs MERGE_DELAY (1 s) after registration and absorbs a newly registered handle into a nearby same-type unclaimed survivor within MERGE_RADIUS (2 studs), accumulating Quantity on the survivor. It skips keepModel items — merging would destroy one of the actual inventory objects, so only non-keepModel handles are eligible.

searchDocs.title: Client hover and claim animation​
searchDocs.content: ProximityPickupController listens to two packets only; it creates no UI and does no proximity math. PickupItemReady applies a HoverEffect (bob + Y-spin) to the handle via a Janitor-managed cleanup handle, and wires AncestryChanged so the effect stops cleanly when the part is destroyed. PickupItemClaimed stops the hover effect, then for the local claimer plays a pickup SFX (via SoundManager.PlaySFXAt using CharacterAnchor to resolve the player's position) and tweens the handle toward the camera using MotionMaster.Play; for all other clients it destroys the handle immediately.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Shared loot — not owner-only Any player who steps into the pickup sphere claims the item, regardless of who dropped it. If owner-only pickup is ever needed, the RegisterItem signature must be extended with an owner: Player? parameter and the zone.Touched handler must gate on it (see audit comment PP6 in ProximityPickupServer).  DroppableSurface tagging — no code change needed. Any BasePart tagged "DroppableSurface" in CollectionService is automatically assigned the DroppableSurface collision group at runtime via GetInstanceAddedSignal. To make a new floor or shelf surface catchable, tag it in Studio only.Collision groups are registered in one place. CollisionGroups.luau (ServerStorage/SharedModules) is the sole registrar and owns the full collidability matrix. Besides DroppedMaterial/DroppableSurface, it defines Character (every character BasePart, assigned by CharacterCollisionService) and WeaponProjectile (thrown charges, assigned by ServerProjectile). Because characters now live in their own group rather than Default, dropped materials and projectiles both pass through players while still colliding with world geometry. Any system that needs a new group or a new pair rule should edit CollisionGroups.luau, not call PhysicsService directly.keepModel semantics. When keepModel = true (the DroppedToolService path), the registered part is the actual Tool that will go into the player's Backpack — RegisterItem will not destroy it, and the callback sets tool.Parent = player.Backpack. When keepModel = false, the caller registers a stand-in handle and the callback grants the real item; the floor handle is destroyed after claim.Zone placement. Pickup zones are parented to workspace.PickupZones (not to the item part). This prevents "trying to set locked parent!" physics warnings when the zone is destroyed at claim time while the item is still mid-float.Late-joining players. ProximityPickupServer registers a JoinSync sender ("ProximityPickups") that replays all currently "Unclaimed" PickupItemReady events once the joining client announces readiness, so items already on the floor will show their hover effect for late joiners. It no longer connects Players.PlayerAdded directly — see Join-Sync Snapshot Handshake for why a PlayerAdded push is unreliable.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant DTS as DroppedToolService participant PPS as ProximityPickupServer participant C as ProximityPickupController (client) P->>DTS: Press Backspace (Tool -> workspace) DTS->>DTS: DropLandingHelper.waitForLanding (poll 0.1s) DTS->>PPS: RegisterItem(tool, metadata, callback, keepModel=true) PPS->>PPS: generate itemId, tag PickupItem, spawn sphere zone PPS->>C: PickupItemReady(part, itemId) C->>C: HoverEffect.Apply (bob + spin) P->>PPS: zone.Touched -> executeClaimAsync PPS->>PPS: record.State = Claimed, destroy Zone PPS->>C: PickupItemClaimed(itemId, claimer) C->>C: cleanup hover; if claimer == LocalPlayer, play SFX + float to hand; else destroy PPS->>PPS: after FLOAT_DURATION, callback(player, metadata) -> Backpack

searchDocs.title: Board​
searchDocs.content: Each period (Daily, Weekly) × category (Personal, Party) has its own box in profile.Data.Board[scope][category]:  Field	MeaningOffer	Offered quests { Id, Used }. OFFER_SIZE (5) at each reset. Used = refreshes spent on that offered slot Active	Accepted quests { Id, P, Claimed, Used, Mult }. P = progress, Mult = Contract Bonus locked at completion Temp	Temporary slots bought this period  Each scope also stores Period, Pts (mileage points, 0–5) and Got (claimed checkpoints). The profile root holds RefreshCredits, Boxes and Purchases (the last PURCHASE_HISTORY processed receipt ids).  Eligible quests. QuestBoardState.eligible(scope, category) lists the pool quests whose Metric is a key of QuestConfig.Metrics. Quests with a metric that has no source yet are never offered. A Personal quest also needs its metric in QuestConfig.PersonalMetrics (reported with an actor through ReportProgress); ownerless metrics such as BiomeJumps advance Party quests only, so a Personal quest on them stays off the board. A small pool gives fewer than 5 offers.Slots. BASE_SLOTS (3) + owned slot passes of that period + Temp. Passes + temporary slots are capped at MAX_EXTRA (3). A claimed quest keeps its slot until the reset. When slots shrink below the active count, the actives stay and accept returns SLOTS_FULL.Accept moves an offered quest into a free slot. Cancel is allowed only while P == 0 and the quest is not claimed; the quest returns to the offered list with its Used count.Refresh replaces one offered quest with another eligible quest that is not offered or active. Each offered slot has FREE_REFRESHES (1) free refresh; the replacement inherits the count. After that, a refresh spends a paid RefreshCredit; with none, the server shows the refresh product prompt (NEEDS_PURCHASE). No other eligible quest → NO_REPLACEMENT, and the free refresh is not spent.Claim (Lobby) pays the period × category reward from QuestBoardConfig.Rewards, multiplied by the locked Mult, and adds 1 mileage point. Daily/Weekly quests pay coins + EXP only, no battle pass EXP.Mileage. Checkpoint k needs k points. Each checkpoint pays coins + EXP once; checkpoint 5 also adds perk boxes (Daily 1, Weekly 5).Perk box. OpenBox picks uniformly from every non-hidden Consumable/Expiring perk in ShopPerkConfig (except the box-only super rares, so the odds list shows each perk once) and grants it through PerkInventoryManager.Grant (no level gate): a consumable gives ConsumableCopies; an expiring perk banks one of its own lengths (Variants[i].Seconds), picked by PerkBox.LengthWeights — 1 length 100%, 2 lengths 70/30, 3 lengths 60/30/10, shortest first (QuestBoardState.rollLength). A running clock gets the seconds added, never reset. A SuperRareChance (0.1%) roll picks one of the 16 BoxOnly perks (QuestBoardState.superRareIds). The box is spent only when the grant succeeds. The GUI shows the odds from QuestBoardState.boxOdds (the same pool and config as the roll): a tier line on the box screen (QuestGuiRules.oddsLine) and every perk in the ODDS panel, 2 decimals. Each expiring name carries its length odds, e.g. XP Booster (1 h 60% · 12 h 30% · 1 d 10%) or Scrap Pay (1 d), so every chance a player can roll shows before they open or pay (Roblox paid random items rule). The opening result reads 12 H OF USE.

searchDocs.title: Reset​
searchDocs.content: On join, QuestManager registers the player only after CoinManager and XPManager report their profiles loaded, because both drop grants before that. Until then every quest request returns NO_PROFILE.  ensureCurrent runs on join, before every request and progress report, and on the ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS tick. When a scope's Period differs from the current index, QuestBoardState.sweep pays the old period's finished-but-unclaimed quests and reached-but-unclaimed checkpoints exactly once (boxes included). Then the scope is rebuilt with fresh offers, empty slots, Pts = 0 and Temp = 0.

searchDocs.title: Purchases (Lobby only)​
searchDocs.content: Temporary slot: 4 Developer Products (period × category). ReqBuyQuestSlot → the server shows the prompt; the receipt adds Temp += 1.Perk boxes: 2 Developer Products, Products.PerkBox.Single (3718951532, "Perk Mystery Box 1x", R$49) and .Bundle (3718951579, "Perk Mystery Box x5", R$199, PerkBoxBundleSize = 5). ReqBuyPerkBox(bundle) → the server shows the prompt; the receipt adds the boxes to Boxes. A bought box is the same box as a free one: same pool, same 0.1% super rare roll, same length odds. Lobby only.Paid random item policy: when PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync says ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted (or the call fails), the client hides GET BOXES (the Open button says NO BOXES at 0) and BuyBox returns NOT_FOR_SALE. Free mileage boxes still open.Refresh: 1 Developer Product. The receipt adds a RefreshCredit and spends it on the pending refresh target if it is still valid.Slot passes: 6 game passes (Daily I–III, Weekly I–III). Each owned pass gives +1 Personal and +1 Party slot of that period. Ownership is read with UserOwnsGamePassAsync at join and updated on PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished; it is not saved. Passes can be bought in any order (also from the website), so QuestStateSync sends the first configured pass the player does not own (QuestBoardState.nextPass) and the PERMANENT button offers that one.ReceiptRouter owns the place's single ProcessReceipt (Roblox allows one per server). It runs in the Lobby only; a receipt that reaches a Game Instance server has no handler there and returns NotProcessedYet, so Roblox retries it later. Unknown products, absent players and handler errors also return NotProcessedYet.QuestManager.settle(player, info, apply) makes each receipt grant once: (1) no profile → NotProcessedYet; (2) PurchaseId already in LastSavedData.Purchases → PurchaseGranted; (3) not in Data.Purchases → run apply and record the id (QuestBoardState.recordPurchase, last PURCHASE_HISTORY ids); (4) profile:Save() and wait up to 20 s for LastSavedData to hold the id → PurchaseGranted, else NotProcessedYet.Product and pass ids are 0 until they exist; 0 = not on sale (the server refuses with NOT_FOR_SALE, the GUI hides the button).Teleport hand-off. QuestManager registers PersistenceRegistry.RegisterHandoff: the Lobby ends the quest session without a kick right before a party teleport, so the Game Instance opens it at once, and reopens it if the teleport fails.

searchDocs.title: Period math​
searchDocs.content: Period indices come from os.time() (UTC), never client input:  Function	FormulaQuestState.dayIndex(now)	floor((now - DailyResetOffset) / 86400) QuestState.weekIndex(now)	floor((now - WeeklyResetOffset) / 604800) QuestState.dailyExpiresAt(now)	Unix timestamp the current daily period ends QuestState.weeklyExpiresAt(now)	Unix timestamp the current weekly period ends  Daily rolls at 00:00 local (QuestConfig.DailyResetOffset); Weekly rolls Monday 00:00 local (QuestConfig.WeeklyResetOffset, a 4-day base offset — the Unix epoch was a Thursday, so shifting 4 days aligns week starts to Mondays). Both offsets are derived from QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset — a fixed seconds-from-UTC offset defining the timezone "midnight" is measured in (pre-launch default US Eastern, -5 * 3600). It's fixed, so it does not track daylight saving; set it to 0 for pure UTC resets (DailyResetOffset = -ResetTimezoneOffset; WeeklyResetOffset = 345600 - ResetTimezoneOffset). The expiry functions are sent to the client so it can drive a live countdown with no client-side period math.

searchDocs.title: Season quests​
searchDocs.content: Scope = "Season" quests stay in QuestConfig.Quests and are not on the board. QuestState.seasonQuests() returns the whole curated set (Personal ids then Party ids, each sorted), active for the whole month. The period index is BattlePassState.seasonIndex(now), so Season quests reset with the battle pass. The Season rollover runs only where options.rollSeason is true (the Game Instance, where BattlePassManager runs).  A Season quest pays on completion: advancePlayer sets SeasonClaimed before the grant, pays Reward.Coins/Reward.Exp and fires Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted(player, quest.Reward), so BattlePassManager adds Reward.BPExp in the same season. The shipped pool pays Coins = 0, Exp = 0 and BPExp = 3000. The rollover still sweeps any finished, unpaid Season quest.

searchDocs.title: Attribution​
searchDocs.content: Two entry points on QuestManager mirror XPManager.AddXP/AddPartyXP:  function QuestManager.ReportProgress(actor: Player, metricKey: string, amount: number) function QuestManager.ReportPartyProgress(metricKey: string, amount: number)   Function	Has an actor	AdvancesReportProgress	Yes (e.g. junk collection)	Bumps the actor's own Lifetime metric, advances the actor's Personal quests, and fans the same amount out to every living online player's Party quests for that metric (down players get nothing, see Paid Revive) ReportPartyProgress	No (e.g. enemy died, train distance)	Advances every living online player's Party quests and bumps each one's Lifetime metric total (down players get nothing)  Either path calls ensureCurrent first (rolls any elapsed period before applying progress) and only replicates (QuestStateSync) to players whose progress actually changed.

searchDocs.title: Contract Bonus​
searchDocs.content: The Contract Bonus perk (QuestRewardBonus, id QuestTracker) is locked when a quest completes during a run. In the Game Instance, options.bonusFor(player) reads PerkBuffRead.Personal(player, "QuestRewardBonus"); QuestBoardState.advance stores 1 + bonus in Active.Mult on the below-target → at-target step. The Lobby claim pays floor(reward × Mult). A quest completed without the perk keeps Mult = 1.

searchDocs.title: Sources​
searchDocs.content: QuestSourcesLoader (gameplay-only — safe to run in the lobby place, where these events simply never fire) wires the QuestConfig.Metrics to their gameplay triggers:  Metric	Category	TriggerEnemyKills	Party	Humanoid.Died on any CollectionService-tagged ENEMY_TAG ("EnemyNPC") model — one Janitor per tracked enemy DistanceTravelled	Party	A recurring task.wait(DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS) loop credits DISTANCE_PER_TICK while Signals.SetTrainState reports the train running JunkCollected	Personal	Signals.OnJunkCollected — fired by JunkService once per successful finalized junk grab (collector, junkId)  A pool quest that uses one of these Metric keys is offered with no code change. A pool quest with any other metric stays off the board until its key is added to QuestConfig.Metrics and wired here. Wiring a brand-new metric needs one new source hookup in QuestSourcesLoader (see Tune Quests).

searchDocs.title: Perk seam​
searchDocs.content: profile.Data.Lifetime is a { [key]: number } table that is never reset by rollover — distinct from the per-period board. advancePlayer bumps Lifetime["QuestsCompleted"] by 1 on every below-target → at-target transition, and both report functions bump Lifetime["metric:"..metricKey] by the raw reported amount.  function QuestManager.GetLifetimeStat(player: Player, key: string): number   This is a deliberate seam for a future PerkConfig unlock criterion (e.g. "unlock this perk after QuestsCompleted >= 25") — not wired to any perk this cycle.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: QuestClient is a GUI-agnostic read-model, the same shape as PerkClient. It caches the QuestStateSync snapshot (board, passes, refresh credits, boxes, expiry timestamps, Season progress, lifetime stats), exposes getters for the GUIs and yielding request wrappers (accept, cancel, refresh, claim, claim mileage, buy slot, open box) that return the server's result code. A Changed signal fires on every snapshot. QuestGuiRules holds the shared display rules (number and clock text, slot kinds, cancel eligibility, tracker rows). The Lobby quest board (QuestBoardGui) and the Game Instance tracker (QuestTrackerGui) consume both. searchDocs.title: Lobby quest board GUI​

An offered row shows the reward and a refresh button: FREE while the slot has a free refresh, PAID while refresh credits remain, else the Robux price (hidden when the refresh product id is 0). ACCEPT reads SLOTS FULL when no slot is free. An active row shows progress, a slot chip (PASS, or TODAY / THIS WEEK for a temporary slot), CANCEL only at 0 progress, then CLAIM and CLAIMED.Extra slot row. The glow colour hints the tier (an Expiring perk sometimes shows teal first; super rare goes amber, then a hue loop and an overload beat). The 3rd hit waits for the answer (10 s cap). Then: flash, the box splits into its 3 faces, rays and confetti, the perk card flips in, the tier tag lands and the name types in (MaxVisibleGraphemes). SKIP jumps to the end; closing stops it. A failure goes back to the closed box with a toast. searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved quest data QuestConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerQuests") is the ProfileStore key for progress, claimed flags, and the never-reset Lifetime table. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile — all prior quest progress and lifetime stats are orphaned (not deleted, just unreachable). It must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places for the cross-place session handoff to share the same record.  Personal progress from ReportProgress also advances Party quests ReportProgress(actor, metricKey, amount) is not Personal-only — it fans the same amount out to every online player's Party quests for that metric, then additionally advances the actor's Personal quests. A Party pool quest that uses a Personal-sourced metric (JunkCollected) is live with no new source wiring.  Only live metrics are offered QuestPool holds all 100 quests, but QuestBoardState.eligible offers only quests whose Metric is a key of QuestConfig.Metrics. A bucket with few live quests shows fewer offers, and refresh returns NO_REPLACEMENT when nothing else is eligible.

No Studio work and no new packets.

searchDocs.title: Core loop​
searchDocs.content: Enqueue — player spends materials immediately (pay-on-enqueue, not pay-on-complete) to queue an eligible node. If nothing is active, the job just enqueued starts immediately. The server also checks the node's Gamepass (if any) before accepting — see Gamepass gating.Advance — a server tick burns bench fuel and advances the active job's elapsed time. Progress pauses whenever fuel hits 0; it resumes the instant fuel is added back. Nothing burns or advances while a player holds REFUEL (state.frozen).Complete — when elapsed >= duration, the node's level is recorded, Signals.OnResearchLevelUp fires, and the next queued job (if any) becomes active.Refuel — a player holds the REFUEL button in the tech tree GUI. The press sends ReqResearchHold(true) and the server freezes the bench. While held, the client only previews the fuel (nothing is spent). On release, TechTreeGuiController sends ReqResearchHold(false) and one ReqResearchRefuel(points); the server spends pool Energy via MaterialPool.SpendUpTo (bench fuel has no cap). There is no refuel ProximityPrompt — see Studio setup.Cancel — a player cancels a node's job (queued or active); see Cascade-cancel.  Because there is one shared queue and one shared fuel pool for the whole server, this is explicitly a co-op system: any player at the bench can enqueue, cancel, or refuel, and progress benefits everyone.

searchDocs.title: Buff nodes vs. unlock-flag nodes​
searchDocs.content: Every entry in ResearchConfig.Nodes is a Node with MaxLevel = 1 and a single Levels[1] entry (Cost, Duration). The levelling machinery (MaxLevel, Levels keyed by number) is still generic — it costs nothing to keep and a future node could ship with MaxLevel > 1 — but every node shipped today researches once. Two shapes exist:  Buff nodes declare an Effects list (not a single Effect) — e.g. { { Type = "StatBuff", Key = "MaxHP", PerLevel = 50 } }. A list is required because two nodes need more than one key at once: Shield_Efficiency/Shield_EfficiencyPlus each grant ShieldEfficiency and ShieldStrength, and Shield_Delta grants MaxHP and ShieldAutoRegen. ResearchEffectsDispatcher sums every entry across every researched node sharing a Key into ReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs (see Buff/unlock folders).Unlock-flag nodes have Effects = nil. Completing them writes only a ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> BoolValue; there is no buff to compute. This is every node outside the Train Shield branch — Ranged/Armor weapon and armor nodes gate Workbench recipes, and Train Weapon/Train Utility/Special nodes gate systems that do not exist yet (see Honest status of Effects). The one recipe gate actually wired in WorkbenchConfig — CraftSMG's RequiresNode = "Ranged_SMG" — points at a Ranged branch node, confirming any node id can gate a recipe. See Workbench Crafting for the consumer side.

searchDocs.title: Prerequisites are AND-lists​
searchDocs.content: Prereqs: { string }? is a list, not a single id — every listed prereq must be at level ≥ 1 (ResearchState.isEligible loops the list) — there is no OR, and no separate minimum-level field now that every node is MaxLevel = 1. Three nodes actually need more than one prerequisite, which is the reason the field is a list at all:  Ranged_EnergyFirearms — Ranged_SniperRifle and Ranged_ExplosivesShield_Delta — Shield_Gamma and Shield_EfficiencyPlusTrainWep_Sturmlanze — TrainWep_MissileLauncher and TrainWep_BurstCannon  ResearchConfig.validate() walks every Prereqs edge at Studio-boot time and warns on an unknown prereq id or a prereq cycle — see Verification.

searchDocs.title: Cascade-cancel​
searchDocs.content: Cancelling is keyed by (nodeId, fromLevel). ResearchState.cancel removes every queued job of the same node with targetLevel >= fromLevel (full refund), and if the active job belongs to the same node and active.targetLevel >= fromLevel, cancels it too at ResearchConfig.ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION (0.5) — the same mechanism the old multi-level Tech Tree used.  With every node now MaxLevel = 1, a node can only ever have one job outstanding at a time (queued or active, never both, and never two queued levels stacked behind each other) — ResearchState.validateEnqueue rejects a second enqueue for the same node with AT_MAX_LEVEL. So in practice cascade-cancel today always resolves to cancelling that single job: fromLevel is always 1, and there is nothing behind it to cascade into. The generic multi-level mechanism is kept as-is (smaller diff than removing it) in case a future node ships with MaxLevel > 1.  If neither the queue nor the active job matches, ReqResearchCancel returns NOTHING_QUEUED and nothing is refunded. Refunds are credited to the server-wide Material Pool with the bench's TrajectoryPoints as the effect origin (pivot fallback); every client animates them into the Materials HUD.

searchDocs.title: Fuel and pause behavior​
searchDocs.content: Fuel is a single server-wide reserve with no cap.While a job is active, fuel burns at ResearchConfig.FUEL_BURN_RATE (1.0/sec) — an idle bench (no active job) never burns fuel.ResearchState.advance clamps effectiveDt = min(dt, fuel / burnRate) so a job's elapsed only ever grows in step with fuel actually spent — the moment fuel reaches 0, elapsed stops advancing (the job pauses, it does not fail or lose progress). Refueling resumes it on the next tick.Refueling spends shared pool Energy: ReqResearchRefuel(points) calls MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", points × FUEL_PER_POINT, FUEL_PER_POINT) — the same path the Train Fuel, Train Shield, Jump Drive and Energy armor use — so a pool short of points pays what it has. An empty pool returns NO_FUEL_ITEM. One hold pays at most MAX_HOLD_POINTS (255) Energy, the NumberU8 limit; the client pays by itself at that point or after as long as that takes (25.5 s at the defaults, Rules.holdDone), even when a small pool stopped the charge first, so a real hold always ends before HOLD_TIMEOUT.Freeze while held. ResearchService keeps holds: { [Player]: deadline }. ReqResearchHold(true) (live bench, isNearBench) adds the player with a deadline HOLD_TIMEOUT (30 s) away (a repeat press keeps the first deadline); false or leaving removes them. While the set is not empty, state.frozen = true and ResearchState.advance changes nothing, so the fuel and the job timer stop for every player (shared bench, shared freeze). Each tick ResearchState.pruneHolds drops expired holders, so a lost release freezes the bench for 30 s at most. The handler only records the hold; the next tick (TICK_INTERVAL, 0.1 s) applies it and broadcasts when frozen changes, so toggling the free packet cannot send more than one broadcast per tick. frozen is serialized. The trigger is the GUI's hold-to-refuel button (pay on release, one request per hold) rather than a second ProximityPrompt — see Studio setup.  Fuel and queue are shared, not per-player There is exactly one fuel value and one queue for the entire server. Any player at the bench can enqueue against the shared queue, refuel the shared reserve, or cancel any job — including jobs another player paid for. This is intentional (co-op resource pooling) but means griefing-by-cancel is possible; there is no per-player ownership check.

searchDocs.title: Buff/unlock folders​
searchDocs.content: ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau is the sole writer of two ReplicatedStorage folders, both recomputed from scratch (not delta-accumulated) on every Signals.OnResearchLevelUp, iterating every node's Effects list:  Folder	Shape	Written by	Read byReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs	Attributes on the folder itself: one numeric attribute per StatBuff.Key (summed PerLevel * level across all nodes with that key), plus FuelEfficiency (product of DrainPerLevel ^ level across all FuelEfficiency-effect nodes; 1 = no effect)	ResearchEffectsDispatcher	TrainShieldManager (MaxHP), TrainFuelManager (FuelEfficiency), TrainShieldGuiController readout (ShieldStrength/ShieldEfficiency/ShieldAutoRegen — display only, see below) ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked	One BoolValue (named by nodeId, Value = true) per node at level ≥ 1	ResearchEffectsDispatcher	WorkbenchService (server gate), WorkbenchGuiController (client greying)  Recompute-from-levels means totals are always correct with no drift risk, at the cost of iterating every node in ResearchConfig.Nodes on every level-up (cheap — 31 nodes). ResearchEffectsDispatcher also seeds both folders once at server boot (before any player joins) so WaitForChild consumers never race an empty folder.  Honest status of Effects​  Only two of the five buff keys published by the Train Shield branch feed real gameplay math today — the other three are read by the shield monitor's readout and rendered, but nothing changes behavior based on them. Every other branch's nodes are unlock-flag-only; the systems they gate (energy weapons, collectors, recycler, shared storage, train weapons) do not exist yet.  Buff key	Consumer	Real effect day one?MaxHP	TrainShieldManager.computeMax	Yes FuelEfficiency	TrainFuelManager drain	Yes ShieldStrength	TrainShieldGuiController readout only	No — display only ShieldEfficiency	TrainShieldGuiController readout only	No — display only ShieldAutoRegen	TrainShieldManager regen loop (Shield δ)	Yes — 0.5% of max every 10 s; the Shield Capacitor perk doubles it  Util_EngineBooster (Train Utility branch) deliberately ships with no Effects at all: it is "+speed, burns more fuel", FuelEfficiency exists and works, but there is no train speed buff key yet — publishing only the fuel-cost half would make researching it a strict downgrade. It stays unlock-flag-only until a speed key exists.

searchDocs.title: Card states & palette​
searchDocs.content: TechTreeGuiController paints every card into one of five states, sourced from ResearchConfig.NodeStateColors — the single source of truth for the palette (Background, Stroke, NameText, StatusText, StatusIcon, Line):  State	MeaningLocked	Prereqs not yet met Available	Eligible, not queued/active/researched Queued	Waiting behind the active job InProgress	The active job — its stroke pulses between InProgress.Stroke and IN_PROGRESS_PULSE (a per-frame lerp in the controller's RenderStepped loop, never TweenService) Unlocked	Researched — mint (#94d2bd)  There is no Unaffordable state. A node you can reach but cannot pay for still renders Available — only the cost numbers (on the card and in the detail panel's UnlockCostContainer) turn red and the action button disables. One less state to build and to learn, and the affordance sits where the player is already looking when deciding to buy.  Connector lines are built from Prereqs by TechTreeGuiRules.connectors: for each prereq (left to right), three axis-aligned 4 px Frames — down from the prereq to a bus line halfway up the gap above the node, across to the entry point, and down into the node. Two prereqs enter 56 px apart. A segment takes the Line colour of the prereq that owns it (Locked dark, Available/Queued/InProgress grey, Unlocked green), so a path lights when its prereq completes. A line from a prereq more than one row up drops straight down that prereq's column; ResearchConfig.validate() warns if a card sits in that path.

searchDocs.title: Gamepass gating​
searchDocs.content: ResearchState stays pure and knows only about Prereqs — ownership is a separate gate layered on top by ResearchService:  Server checks MarketplaceService:UserOwnsGamePassAsync at enqueue time (ReqResearchEnqueue), caching the result per (player, passId); a PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished hook clears a cached denial so a mid-session purchase is picked up immediately. A gated node the player doesn't own is rejected with the new GAMEPASS_REQUIRED (11) result code.Client (TechTreeGuiController) checks UserOwnsGamePassAsync once per pass at load (and marks it owned on PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished) to show the detail panel's "Game pass" or "Game pass owned" chip. Display only — the card is still Available and the server still decides. A pass card has a gold rail and a ticket before its name.Owning the pass makes a node eligible; it is still queued with materials and duration like any other node.  Today exactly one node uses this: Special_BiomeSelector, gated on ResearchConfig.BIOME_SELECTOR_GAMEPASS_ID = 1982397425. Note that passesGamepassGate treats only a missing Gamepass field as "no gate" — a node carrying Gamepass = 0 is refused with GAMEPASS_REQUIRED, because 0 is not a pass anyone can own. So blanking the id locks the node rather than freeing it.

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared responsibilities​
searchDocs.content: Shared — ResearchState.luau is a pure, stateless module with no Roblox service calls: newState, levelOf, pendingLevel, isEligible (loops Prereqs, AND semantics), validateEnqueue, enqueue, cancel (cascade logic), advance (tick), refuel, serialize. Both the server (authority) and the client GUI (asState() cast over the cached snapshot, for greying/afford checks) call the same pure helpers, so the rules can never drift between sides. validateEnqueue deliberately does not check materials or gamepass ownership — those checks are server-only and layered on top by ResearchService.  Server — ResearchService.luau is the authoritative owner of ResearchState.State. It is a ModuleScript, not a .server.luau Script — see ModuleScript + loader split below. Initialize() (idempotent, guarded by a boot flag) wires all four packet handlers plus the RunService.Heartbeat tick loop, the gamepass ownership cache, and its PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished/PlayerRemoving hooks. GetLevels() exposes the live levels table for ResearchEffectsDispatcher to read.  Server — ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau is a one-line boot script: require(...ResearchService) then ResearchService.Initialize(). Mirrors PerkManager.luau / PerkSystemLoader.server.luau.  Server — ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau connects Signals.OnResearchLevelUp and republishes both buff/unlock folders from scratch, looping every node's Effects list. See Buff/unlock folders.  Client — TechTreeGuiController.client.luau drives StarterGui.TechTreeGui, which holds the panel plus a Templates folder (TabTemplate, CardTemplate, LineTemplate, TierTemplate, SelectionRing, EffectRowTemplate, ChipTemplate). It opens from the bench's TechPromptPart ProximityPrompt. Tabs are cloned once from ResearchConfig.Branches into the BranchTabs ScrollingFrame; a tab click rebuilds the tree for that branch only (one Janitor), and state updates only repaint. Selecting a card moves the SelectionRing and fills the detail panel: UNLOCKS rows (Unlocks) or EFFECT rows (Effects through EffectLabels), REQUIRES chips, the Metal/Wood/Time cost chips and the action button. When the node has a non-zero Gamepass the player does not own (and is not researched), the action button turns gold and shows BuyContent (ticket + BUY PASS + the Robux price from GetProductInfoAsync, … until it answers); a click opens PromptGamePassPurchase, and PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished marks the pass owned and repaints. The bottom row is the active job (click = cancel at 50%, or full with Lab Insurance), three queue slot cards (click = cancel, full refund) and the fuel stack: the BENCH FUEL header with the hint (m:ss OF RESEARCH, RESEARCH PAUSED in red, or PAUSED WHILE REFUELING in teal), the FuelRow (FuelAmount + FUEL, then EnergyLeft) and the REFUEL button. Pressing REFUEL sends ReqResearchHold(true) and stops the local clock; holding grows a client-only charge: FuelAmount counts up in pale teal, ← ⚡ n ENERGY LEFT and the header Energy count down. Release (anywhere), close or focus loss sends ReqResearchHold(false) and one ReqResearchRefuel(points); a hold pays by itself at MAX_HOLD_POINTS or after 25.5 s. A release within 0.3 s toasts Hold REFUEL to add more. With an empty pool the button greys out and reads NO ENERGY. While a hold freezes the bench the job box reads REFUELING; with no fuel and no hold the running card shows the Pause icon and PAUSED in red with a grey bar and no pulse, the detail pill reads PAUSED, and the job box reads PAUSED. Icon images come from ResearchConfig.Icons: every icon ImageLabel names its key in an Icon attribute. Icons, TabTemplate, CardTemplate, SelectionRing, TierTemplate and LineTemplate each hold a UIAspectRatioConstraint so they keep their shape; the controller sets each cloned line's ratio from its segment size. Move/Stash wiring is one call — PlaceableActions.bind(benchModel, screen), which finds the Move/Stash buttons of both layouts — see The bench is a placeable for when the buttons show. Between ResearchStateUpdate broadcasts, interpolated() fast-forwards the active job and the fuel locally with the known burn rate and the synced server clock.  Compact layout. TechTreeGui holds two panels built from the same templates: MainContainer (authored 1800×940, UIScale = min(W/1920, H/1022)) and CompactContainer (authored 1240×520). When the full scale drops below TechTreeGuiRules.COMPACT_BELOW (0.6, phones and 4:3 tablets), the controller shows CompactContainer instead, scaled by s = min(W/1240, H/520) and grown to min(W/s, 1400) × min(H/s, 860) (Rules.compactSize). The controller binds both panels into one View (bindView) and paints whichever fit() picks; crossing the threshold while REFUEL is held pays the hold first. The compact panel keeps the same names wherever the role is the same and drops: the TECH TREE title, the Metal/Wood header chips (the cost chips already read have/need), the RESEARCHED total, the detail icon, sub line, section labels and REQUIRES chips (a locked node's button reads NEEDS <PREREQ> / NEEDS <PREREQ> +n instead), the queue hint and slot times, and the BENCH FUEL header (FuelHint sits at the end of FuelRow and hides while ENERGY LEFT shows). Branch tabs are Templates.CompactTabTemplate clones in a horizontal BranchStrip.BranchTabs ScrollingFrame (AutomaticCanvasSize X, each tab Size = UDim2.new(0, 68, 1, 0) with a UIAspectRatioConstraint, DominantAxis = Height, inside it) beside the branch name and n / m RESEARCHED. AutomaticCanvasSize does not grow past items that hold an aspect-ratio constraint, so the controller also sets CanvasSize from the list's AbsoluteContentSize, and sizes the strip to its tabs while leaving the name 260 px. The tree sits in a vertical TechContainer ScrollingFrame with rows Rules.COMPACT_ROW_GAP (32 px) apart; its canvas height is Rules.treeHeight + 40.

searchDocs.title: ModuleScript + loader split (caution)​
searchDocs.content: ResearchService is a ModuleScript, booted by a separate loader ResearchService.luau lives under ServerStorage/SharedModules/ as a ModuleScript, not ServerScriptService/ResearchService.server.luau. This is deliberate: Roblox's require() only accepts ModuleScript instances — a *.server.luau file compiles to a plain Script, which can never be required by another script. Because ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau needs to call ResearchService.GetLevels(), ResearchService has to be a ModuleScript. The split mirrors the existing PerkManager.luau (ModuleScript, state + Initialize()) / PerkSystemLoader.server.luau (thin boot Script) pattern: ResearchService.luau defines state + an idempotent Initialize() that wires packets and the tick loop, but does nothing until Initialize() is called.ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau is the only script that calls ResearchService.Initialize(), exactly once per server. If you ever see require() fail on a *.server.luau/*.client.luau path in this codebase, this is the fix: split the requirable state into a ModuleScript and add a thin loader Script that calls its Initialize().

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Manual, one-time Studio work — none of this is created automatically by code:  Bench Model. The ResearchBench tag on ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableItems.ResearchBench, with PrimaryPart set; placed clones live under workspace.PlacedObjects and inherit the tag. Lookup is by tag, never by name — see The bench is a placeable.Refund-arc trajectory. A child Model named TrajectoryPoints (tagged PlacementIgnore, per the Placement "tag the CollisionBox only" rule) holding two BasePart children: SpawnPoint (arc start, the bench's output mouth) and LandingPoint (arc end, the floor drop zone). If missing, MaterialPool.ArcPoints falls back to the bench pivot; the refund is still credited.Research prompt. A child BasePart named TechPromptPart holding a ProximityPrompt — opens the GUI. MaxActivationDistance is set to ResearchConfig.INTERACT_DISTANCE by the client controller at runtime.No refuel prompt. Refueling is the hold-to-refuel button inside the opened GUI (FuelStack.RefuelButton), one ReqResearchRefuel(points) per release, see Core loop. There is no second ProximityPrompt and no REFUEL_PROMPT_PART_NAME constant.Material templates. ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials holds Wood and Metal Tool templates whose Handle the clients clone for the cosmetic refund effect — shared with the Shredder, no duplication needed.StarterGui.TechTreeGui. Built once through the Studio MCP (plan docs/_superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-tech-tree-gui.md, Task 3): the panel plus the Templates folder. Cards and lines are not authored by hand; they come from config. Icon ids go in ResearchConfig.Icons.  The bench is a placeable​  The bench is authored the same way as the Workbench: the ResearchBench tag lives on the template at ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableItems.ResearchBench, so every clone PlacementServer places inherits it. ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools.ResearchBench is the matching Tool (attribute PlaceableName = "ResearchBench", with a Handle).  The tag is not identity CollectionService:GetTagged(BENCH_TAG) matches three different things, in no guaranteed order: the placed bench, the ReplicatedStorage template, and other players' build-mode ghosts — PlacementSystem strips tags from the local ghost but not from the other-player ghosts it parents under workspace.GhostModels, prompts included. This is the trap CannonConfig documents when it says placed cannons are found by attribute and "NOT a CollectionService tag — that would also match client build-mode ghosts." Both lookups (ResearchService.findBench, the client's isLiveBench) therefore require Parent == workspace.PlacedObjects, the same condition PlaceableActionsServer enforces. A workspace-descendant check is not enough: ghosts live in workspace too, and an unfiltered lookup either measures isNearBench against a template in ReplicatedStorage — failing every enqueue with TOO_FAR — or hands out a working tech tree prompt on someone else's floating preview.  BenchInteractionContainer's MoveButton/StashButton go through PlaceableActions.bind, but PlaceableActionsServer.handleAction additionally requires a non-empty PlaceableName attribute on the placed Model. That attribute is never authored in Studio — PlacementServer stamps it at runtime on the line after it parents the clone (PlacementServer.server.luau, both the place and restore paths), which is why the PlaceableItems templates have no such attribute while the PlaceableTools Tools do (theirs is hand-authored and read at place-time). A bench dragged into workspace.PlacedObjects by hand therefore lacks it. open() checks it into stashable and hides the container when it fails, so the buttons are never visible-but-dead.  The ResearchBench Tool has no source today: it is not in StarterPack and CraftWorkbench is the only Kind = "Placeable" recipe. Stashing the world bench is currently the only way to hold it, so a player who stashes and then loses the Tool loses the bench. Add a Workbench recipe with Output = { Kind = "Placeable", PlaceableName = "ResearchBench" } if that matters.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Server re-checks proximity on every request The client's ProximityPrompt distance is never trusted. ReqResearchEnqueue, ReqResearchCancel, ReqResearchRefuel and a ReqResearchHold(true) press all re-run isNearBench on the server using INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE. A player invoking from range receives TOO_FAR.  Validate-then-consume ordering on enqueue ReqResearchEnqueue pays with one atomic MaterialPool.Spend(cost): it checks every cost entry against the server-wide pool before subtracting any. If the pool is short on any single material, nothing is consumed — there is no partial-payment state. The gamepass check runs after prereq/queue validation but before the materials check.  Cost is paid on enqueue, not on completion Materials are deducted the instant a level is successfully enqueued — the queue holds already-paid-for jobs. Cancelling is therefore the only way to get materials back, and only at the refund fractions described in Cascade-cancel.  Gamepass ownership is cached per (player, passId), including denials UserOwnsGamePassAsync is a yielding web call. ResearchService caches both grants and denials so it isn't re-queried on every enqueue attempt; a purchase completing mid-session clears the cached denial via PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished. A failed web call denies without caching, so the next attempt retries rather than sticking a player with a false negative.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as TechTreeGuiController participant S as ResearchService participant D as ResearchEffectsDispatcher P->>C: Walk within INTERACT_DISTANCE, trigger TechPromptPart C->>S: ReqResearchSnapshot() S->>C: { levels, active, queue, fuel } C->>C: cache populated; cards/detail/queue/fuel repainted P->>C: Click a card, then RESEARCH in the detail panel C->>S: ReqResearchEnqueue(nodeId) S->>S: re-check bench + proximity S->>S: ResearchState.validateEnqueue (unknown/prereq/max level/queue full) S->>S: passesGamepassGate(player, nodeId) - GAMEPASS_REQUIRED if ungated node not owned S->>S: MaterialPool.Spend(cost) - NOT_ENOUGH_MATERIALS if the pool is short S->>S: ResearchState.enqueue(...) - starts immediately if idle S->>C: (success, reasonCode) S->>C: ResearchStateUpdate(state, serverTime) loop every TICK_INTERVAL S->>S: ResearchState.advance(state, dt, FUEL_BURN_RATE) Note over S: effectiveDt = min(dt, fuel/burnRate) - progress pauses at fuel==0 alt elapsed >= duration S->>D: Signals.OnResearchLevelUp(nodeId, level) S->>S: startNext() - pop next queued job end S->>C: broadcast() on completion, or at most every HEARTBEAT_BROADCAST_INTERVAL end C->>C: interpolate elapsed/fuel locally between broadcasts (synced server clock) C->>C: repaint() - card/line states + detail panel + queue slots D->>D: republish(): recompute ResearchBuffs from every node's Effects list D->>D: publish ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> if level >= 1 P->>C: Click a queue slot or the in-progress panel C->>S: ReqResearchCancel(nodeId, fromLevel) S->>S: ResearchState.cancel -> (activeRefund?, queuedRefund) S->>S: eject queuedRefund @ 1.0, activeRefund @ ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION S->>C: (success, reasonCode) + broadcast() P->>C: Press REFUEL C->>S: ReqResearchHold(true) S->>S: holds[player] = now + HOLD_TIMEOUT; state.frozen = true + broadcast() P->>C: Release (client-only preview until now) C->>S: ReqResearchHold(false) C->>S: ReqResearchRefuel(points) S->>S: MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", points × FUEL_PER_POINT, FUEL_PER_POINT) S->>S: ResearchState.refuel(state, value) S->>C: (success, reasonCode) + broadcast()

searchDocs.title: Verification​
searchDocs.content: Two checks, split by what each can actually see at runtime — there is no automated test suite for this project.  ResearchConfig.validate() — pure data, no DataModel access, runs under RunService:IsStudio() at the bottom of the module so it warns on every Studio session. Asserts every Prereqs entry names a real node in the same branch and a higher row, the prereq graph is acyclic, every node has Levels[1], a known Branch, a whole-number Tier from 1 to MAX_TIER (5, the rows the tree canvas fits), a Column of 0/0.5/1, a free card slot, and Unlocks or Effects; a centred node is alone in its row; no line runs through a card; every Effects entry has a handler in the dispatcher and every StatBuff key has an EffectLabels entry; every branch icon is a key of Icons; and NodeStateColors defines all six fields for all five states. It also warns once while icon ids are blank.  TechTreeGuiRules is pure, so the layout maths and every number-driven string have a Studio self-check (plan docs/_superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-tech-tree-gui.md, Task 1 Step 4).  Everything else is Studio verification, per project convention.
