Also mapped into the Lobby (XPManager / QuestManager require it; nobody is down there) Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ReviveCredits.luau	Saved revive credits (PlayerRevive ProfileStore): receipt idempotency, Grant, TakeOne Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ReviveService.luau	Spawn, death, revive, purchase prompt, rewarded ad, receipts, crew countdown Server	src/ServerScriptService/ReviveSystemLoader.server.luau	ReviveCredits.Initialize(), ReviveService.Initialize(), then ReceiptRouter.Start() (the Game Instance's one ProcessReceipt)  Packets: ReqReviveBuy, ReqReviveAd, ReviveStateSync — see Networking MapSignals: OnPlayerDownChanged — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: How it works​
searchDocs.content: ReviveService.Initialize sets Players.CharacterAutoLoads = false and spawns each joining player with LoadCharacter. On a character's Humanoid.Died it:  captures the player's Tools (SessionState.CaptureTools),sets the status to Down and ReviveState.SetDown(player, true),sends ReviveStateSync,spends a saved credit at once if the player has one (status UsingCredit).  A revive shows Reviving / UsingCredit for REVIVE_DELAY_SECONDS (1 s), then calls LoadCharacter (normal spawn, full health from HealthManager's CharacterAdded reset) and puts the captured Tools back with SessionState.RestoreTools.

searchDocs.title: Every receipt becomes a saved credit first​
searchDocs.content: A Robux purchase and a rewarded ad grant the same "Revive" product. Its ProcessReceipt handler is ReviveCredits.Grant: +1 credit once per PurchaseId, PurchaseGranted only after a save that contains the id (the QuestManager.settle pattern). Only then does ReviveService spend the credit on the down player. If the player is not down any more, or the run is over, the credit stays saved and revives them on their next death, in any run.  The grant comes only from the receipt, never from ShowRewardedVideoAdAsync's result or PromptProductPurchaseFinished. An ad receipt is recognised by receipt.ProductPurchaseChannel == Enum.ProductPurchaseChannel.AdReward and marks the run's ad as used.  sequenceDiagram participant C as Client participant S as ReviveService participant M as MarketplaceService participant P as ReviveCredits S->>C: ReviveStateSync(Down) C->>S: ReqReviveBuy S->>C: ReviveStateSync(Buying) S->>M: PromptProductPurchase M-->>S: ProcessReceipt (ReceiptRouter) S->>P: Grant: +1 credit, save P-->>S: saved → onGranted S->>P: TakeOne S->>C: ReviveStateSync(Reviving) Note over S: 1 s, then LoadCharacter + RestoreTools S->>C: ReviveStateSync(Alive)   A down player never keeps a saved credit: besides the death, the rejoin and the receipt, a 1 s heartbeat spends one for any present Down player. That catches a receipt whose save took longer than 20 s (Roblox retries it, and the retry only answers PurchaseGranted) and a credits profile that loaded after the death.  The ad flow is the same with ReqReviveAd → AdPlaying → AdService:ShowRewardedVideoAdAsync(player, CreateAdRewardFromDevProductId(PRODUCT_ID)). A finished prompt or ad whose receipt has not landed keeps the status (and the countdown hold) for up to 30 s, then returns to Down.

searchDocs.title: Rejoin while down​
searchDocs.content: State is keyed by UserId and lives for the server's life. A player who leaves during the 1 s "REVIVING…" step already paid, so the revive finishes when they rejoin. A down player who disconnects and rejoins is not spawned: they come back Down on the menu, with the same "ad used" flag and the Tools captured at death. The rejoin grace health provider skips a health of 0, so a later revive is never killed by a restored 0.

searchDocs.title: Studio stand-ins​
searchDocs.content: While ReviveConfig.PRODUCT_ID == 0 there is no product. In Studio ReqReviveBuy revives at once and ReqReviveAd marks the ad used and revives at once, each with a warning. Outside Studio both do nothing.

searchDocs.title: All-down countdown​
searchDocs.content: ReviveService re-checks the crew on every status change, on every leave, and once a second:  present = players in the server; down = present players whose status is not Alive;graceAlive = players seen this run who are disconnected, still in rejoin grace (SessionState.HasGrace) and were alive.  When ReviveRules.allDown(present, down, graceAlive) turns true, crewEndsAt = now + ALL_DOWN_SECONDS (20 s, server time) and every client gets it in ReviveStateSync. A revive (or a living player joining) clears it.  Each second ReviveRules.countdownPhase moves the countdown on:  Phase	WhenRunning	before crewEndsAt Hold	at 0 while a purchase prompt, ad or revive is in flight, for at most HOLD_MAX_SECONDS (30 s). holdBy names the first such player End	otherwise  At End the run is over: every status becomes RunOver (ReviveService.MarkRunOver, idempotent), then TrainGameOver.Trigger(TrainGameOverReason.ALL_DOWN). RunEndService owns the rest: payout, the results screen, and SessionCoordinator.EndRunToLobby() after RunRewardConfig.RESULTS_SECONDS (see Run Results). A hull breach or Leviathan strike calls MarkRunOver first and then kills every living player; their deaths see RunOver and start nothing. ReviveService also counts each down and each revive into RunStats. After the end nothing revives; a receipt that still lands becomes a saved credit for the next run, and a credit taken for a revive that had not loaded yet is given back (ReviveCredits.GiveBack). If the lobby teleport fails, the player is kicked with a message instead of waiting on "GOING TO THE LOBBY…" (not in Studio, where teleports always fail). A player who rejoins after the end gets no character; RunEndService pays them and shows the results inside the results window, or bounces only that player after it.  Only the all-down end works this way. A hull breach or a Leviathan strike does not change who is down.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: ReviveGuiController (StarterPlayerScripts/ReviveGuiController/) binds three Studio-built ScreenGuis (all ResetOnSpawn = false, Enabled = false in StarterGui) and draws only what ReviveStateSync says:  ScreenGui	DisplayOrder	HoldsReviveDimGui	-2 (below NovaChat's -1)	Dim — menu only, so the chat stays readable over it ReviveGui	20	RevivePanel (menu) and SpectateBar CrewDownGui	21	CountdownBanner — shown while the crew countdown runs or holds  Only the revive GUIs while down. HudBlackout (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules, shared with the results screen: Set(owner, hide), hidden while any owner hides) records every other enabled PlayerGui ScreenGui, turns it off (and off again if anything turns it on or a new one appears), and turns exactly those back on at revive. Satchel's hotbar and the TopbarPlus icons use their own switches. NovaChat and the Roblox topbar stay (NovaChat follows TopbarEnabled). The cursor is freed with Signals.RequestMouseIcon(true, "Revive").Run over. At RunOver the controller treats the player as not down: every revive GUI turns off, spectating stops, and it releases its HudBlackout owner and cursor request. The Run Results screen takes over (there is no "RUN OVER" copy).Reset Character is off (SetCore("ResetButtonCallback", false), retried until the CoreGui accepts it): a free death would skip the paid revive.Ad button shows only when the run's ad is unused and AdService:GetAdAvailabilityNowAsync(RewardedVideo) returned IsAvailable when the menu opened. An ad that did not finish (status back from AdPlaying to Down) triggers a new check, because IsAvailable is good for one ad play only. Any other result shows Robux only. The visible ad button is registered with RegisterAdOpportunityAsync.Price comes from MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo(PRODUCT_ID, Product).PriceInRobux, written after the Robux glyph utf8.char(0xE002) (as in TechTree and QuestBoard). No price shows while PRODUCT_ID is 0, the call fails, or the product is not on sale. With regional pricing on, the price is the viewer's regional price (99 R$ is the default).Lobby asks first: the first tap swaps in "LEAVE THE RUN?" + YES / NO; NO or LOBBY_CONFIRM_SECONDS (5 s) goes back; YES fires Signals.LeaveToLobbyRequested.Spectate (Spectate.luau) cycles the other living players (Prev / Next, Q / E, gamepad L1 / R1) and fires Signals.RequestSpectateTarget; with nobody up the camera watches the train core (TrainConfig.CORE_TAG). The bar shows the target's head shot, name, "WATCHING · n OF m UP" and a health bar (orange under 30%).Timer is computed every frame from crewEndsAt - workspace:GetServerTimeNow(), not sent each second.Scale. UIScale = min(W/1920, H/1022); under 0.68 the compact layout (authored at 844×332, scale clamped to 0.75–1.5) is applied: the panel turns into a 780×252 row anchored to the bottom, the banner drops its second line and the bar shrinks to 68 high (LOBBY becomes icon-only).Rejoin while down. StarterGui is copied into PlayerGui only on spawn, and a down player is not spawned, so the controller clones the three GUIs itself after 5 s and destroys the duplicate the next spawn brings.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: One ProcessReceipt per server. The Game Instance now starts ReceiptRouter in ReviveSystemLoader, with only the Revive product registered. Every other product still returns NotProcessedYet here, so Roblox retries it in the Lobby. A Revive receipt that reaches the Lobby is retried in the next run.Characters do not respawn by themselves. Anything that expects an automatic respawn after death must go through ReviveService.

searchDocs.title: Motion​
searchDocs.content: A front rock moves in a straight line at constant speed: RockMath.positionAt(spawnPos, velocity, spawnTime, t) (eruption rocks add gravity, see Eruptions). The server sends those values once in RockSpawn; every client moves its own pooled copy with the same formula, so there is no per-frame network traffic. Braking does not slow rocks. The spin is cosmetic.

searchDocs.title: Spawning​
searchDocs.content: Every ROLL_INTERVAL the server rolls RockMath.spawnChance(t, …) when the train has started, no jump is active, the game is not over, workspace.CurrentBiome is in RockConfig.Biomes, and fewer than MAX_ACTIVE rocks are live. t is the time in the current biome; a CurrentBiome change resets it. A rock spawns at a random point in the SpawnGroup = "Rocks" volume (SpawnVolumes.Part3) and aims at a random point in the dome's rim plane, so every rock meets the dome. Model, size multiplier (SCALE_MIN..SCALE_MAX on the model's own scale) and spin axis are random; the biome sets material, color and transparency.  p(t) = 0 t < GRACE (60 s) p(t) = P_START + (P_PEAK − P_START) · s(x) GRACE ≤ t < PEAK_AT (720 s) x = (t − GRACE) / (PEAK_AT − GRACE), s(x) = 3x² − 2x³ p(t) = P_PEAK t ≥ PEAK_AT   Time in biome	Ice / Storm rocks/min	Volcano / Void rocks/min0:00–1:00	0	0 1:00	3.0	3.6 5:00	5.7	7.0 9:00	10.4	12.9 12:00 → boss	12.0	15.0  Storm front rocks use the Ice rates in a dark wet Slate look; Void front rocks use the Volcano rates (the last, hardest biome) in dark Basalt. RockConfig.BiomeOrder is { "Ice", "Volcano", "Storm", "Void" }: its index is on the wire, so new biomes are appended, never reordered.

searchDocs.title: Shooting​
searchDocs.content: Rocks have no server parts. Weapons test them with sphere math through RockService: hitscan at the lag-compensated time, rocket and cannon shells per flight step, and every player explosion through ApplyAOE. HP = HP_PER_SCALE × mult. See Weapons and Cannon.

searchDocs.title: Impact​
searchDocs.content: At spawn the server computes when the rock reaches the dome sphere (dome radius + rock radius). At that time:  shield above 0 → TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(DAMAGE_PER_SCALE × mult, "Rock", { Position = dome surface point, Severity }), the rock breaks on the dome (ShieldHit). Severity maps the size multiplier onto SHIELD_HIT_SEVERITY (0.3–0.6), so a bigger rock makes a bigger flash; damage never sets the visuals;shield at 0 → the rock flies on to the nose plane, then calls ApplyDamage (with the nose point as Position), which bleeds to fuel and then the hull (HullHit). See Train Shield.  A jump or game over despawns every rock. Delayed callbacks check rock identity, so a removed rock never lands.

searchDocs.title: The dome​
searchDocs.content: ReplicatedStorage.ShieldDome (the dome template; the client clones it for the front and rear domes) is a half sphere of 8 Beams (2 rings × 4 quarter circles, the same beam as the ShieldTubeSegment tube) with a Radius attribute. Its PrimaryPart position and Radius are the server's collision sphere, so moving or resizing it in Studio moves the collision too. Rings, not slices: narrow slices repeat the texture and look striped. Its look (hidden by default, hit flash, reveals, break / reboot) belongs to the shield — see Train Shield — Dome. RockController does not read the shield: because the dome is hidden most of the time, a rock is not held at its surface (it would freeze in mid-air). It flies on for one network delay (~1.5–3 studs at SPEED 15) until RockRemoved arrives.

searchDocs.title: Eruptions​
searchDocs.content: In a biome with a RockConfig.Eruptions rule, a source appears from time to time in a band around the train and throws rocks at the whole train: front, middle and rear. This is a second rock kind (RockConfig.Kind.Eruption) in the same RockService registry, so weapons hit eruption rocks with no weapon changes. The front rocks above are unchanged and keep their own cap.  Biome	Source	RocksVolcano	A fire pillar rises out of the haze (y −70)	6–10 small lava rocks Ice	A frozen-cloud chunk cracks high above (y 250)	3–5 big ice shards that drift out and fall Storm	A waterspout rises out of the sea fog (y −70)	4–7 medium wreck debris pieces Void	A mini rift (small black hole) opens beside the train at deck height (y 20)	4–7 medium void rocks in floaty arcs  The rule is read per event: RockService looks up Eruptions[CurrentBiome] at each roll and uses that rule for the whole event.  Spawn band. The train line is the segment from the front dome center to the rear dome center (TrainPlatforms.RearX − TrainConfig.SHIELD_REAR_INSET), read at each event, so a longer train moves the band too. A source spawns at PILLAR_Y where the XZ distance to that line is between INNER and OUTER: a rounded box around the train (RockMath.eruptionPoint).  Timeline. The server fires EruptionStart(position, eruptTime) with eruptTime = now + WARNING: clients show the warning. At eruptTime, if no jump started, the game is not over and the current biome still maps to the same rule, the server spawns ROCKS_MIN–ROCKS_MAX rocks while under the rule's MAX_ACTIVE.  Motion. Each rock aims at a random deck point (X between the dome centers, Z within DECK_HALF_WIDTH of the line, Y = DECK_Y) with a flight time of FLIGHT_MIN–FLIGHT_MAX. RockMath.launchVelocity solves the launch velocity; positionAt adds ½·GRAVITY·dt². RockSpawn carries kind and biomeIndex, so clients find the same rule and add the same gravity. Ice uses a low gravity (−20): from 250 studs up, −60 would launch the shards upward first. Void uses −30: from deck height, −20 brings far rocks in low from the side, under the shield's upper half; −30 is the weakest gravity whose arcs meet it from every spot in the band.  Impact. The shield is the upper half of a capsule around the train line with the dome radius (RockMath.timeToHalfCapsule, rock radius added).  The arc meets it while the shield is above 0 → ApplyDamage(DAMAGE, DAMAGE_SOURCE, { Position = shell point, Severity = SEVERITY }), removed as ShieldHit.Shield at 0 → the rock flies on to its deck point at the end of its flight → ApplyDamage(DAMAGE, DAMAGE_SOURCE, …) (bleeds to fuel, then hull). One event spends at most one hull hit: once a rock of that event lands on the hull, its other rocks pass spareHull = true (see Train Shield), so an event on an empty train counts like one front rock. Also, every living player within PLAYER_RADIUS of the impact takes PLAYER_DAMAGE as "AOE" / "Explosion" through HealthManager.ApplyDamage. Removed as HullHit (shatter burst).  Knob	Volcano	Ice	Storm	VoidINNER / OUTER	60 / 350	60 / 350	60 / 350	60 / 350 PILLAR_Y	−70	250	−70	20 WARNING	2 s	2 s	2 s	2 s ROCKS_MIN / ROCKS_MAX	6 / 10	3 / 5	4 / 7	4 / 7 FLIGHT_MIN / FLIGHT_MAX	4 / 6 s	4 / 5.5 s	4 / 6 s	4 / 6 s GRAVITY	(0, −60, 0)	(0, −20, 0)	(0, −60, 0)	(0, −30, 0) SCALE_MIN / SCALE_MAX	0.35 / 0.65 (~3–6 studs)	0.65 / 1.1 (~6–10 studs)	0.45 / 0.78 (~4–7 studs)	0.45 / 0.78 (~4–7 studs) HP / DAMAGE / SEVERITY	15 / 8 / 0.15	40 / 12 / 0.25	25 / 10 / 0.2	25 / 10 / 0.2 PLAYER_DAMAGE / PLAYER_RADIUS	20 / 6	20 / 6	20 / 6	20 / 6 P_START / P_PEAK (same GRACE / PEAK_AT curve)	0.05 / 0.133 (1 per 40 s → 1 per 15 s)	0.044 / 0.1 (1 per 45 s → 1 per 20 s)	0.044 / 0.1	0.044 / 0.1 MAX_ACTIVE	40	20	28	28 Look	bright CrackedLava	pale blue Ice	wet wreck WoodPlanks	dark Basalt DAMAGE_SOURCE / PILLAR_TEMPLATE / SFX	Eruption / EruptionPillar / Eruption	IceFall / IceFall / IceFall	Waterspout / Waterspout / Waterspout	VoidRift / VoidRift / VoidRift PILLAR_LIFETIME	4 s	3 s	4 s	4 s  Client. On EruptionStart, RockController takes the rule of CurrentBiome (eruptions never start during a jump, and the biome only changes inside one) and clones ReplicatedStorage.<PILLAR_TEMPLATE> at the position. Its enabled emitters and light are the warning. At eruptTime it bursts every emitter that has an EmitCount attribute, enables the rest, and plays the rule's SFX at the source. PILLAR_LIFETIME later every emitter, light and beam switches off, every visible part of the source (Transparency < 1; only the Void rift orb has any) shrinks to nothing over 1 s with MotionMaster, and Debris removes the source once the particles die. Eruption rocks use their rule's Material / Color / Transparency and gravity. Rock pools hold MAX_ACTIVE + the largest rule MAX_ACTIVE per model.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: ReplicatedStorage.RockAssets — rock Models (each with a PrimaryPart; parts anchored, CanCollide/CanTouch off). Any model works in any biome.ReplicatedStorage.RockShatterVFX — a part with ParticleEmitters; an EmitCount attribute sets the burst size. The shield-hit burst is ReplicatedStorage.ShieldHitVFX, owned by Train Shield.ReplicatedStorage.ShieldDome (name and attribute in TrainConfig.DOME_NAME / DOME_RADIUS_ATTRIBUTE; Radius attribute; authored at the front-dome spot — the server reads its PrimaryPart as the collision center), Workspace.RockVisuals (folder).ReplicatedStorage.EruptionPillar (Volcano PILLAR_TEMPLATE) — a Model whose Base part (anchored, CanCollide/CanQuery/CanTouch off, invisible) holds Smoke (enabled), Fire (disabled), Embers (disabled, EmitCount 60) and a PointLight.ReplicatedStorage.IceFall (Ice PILLAR_TEMPLATE) — same layout: Frost mist (enabled), Crack falling ice dust (disabled), Shards (disabled, EmitCount 30) and a dim cold PointLight.ReplicatedStorage.Waterspout (Storm PILLAR_TEMPLATE) — Swirl mist (enabled), Column rising water (disabled), and Burst water spray (disabled, EmitCount 40) on a Top attachment 110 studs up, so it shows above the fog. No light.ReplicatedStorage.VoidRift (Void PILLAR_TEMPLATE) — Base plus BlackHoleModel, a copy of the Art Place black hole scaled to a ~40-stud rim: dark Neon BlackOrb core, grey Neon GlowOrb rim, two beams (all parts anchored, CanCollide/CanQuery/CanTouch off). SpaceSmokeEmitter ×3 and DistortionEmitter (the dark red twirl, spinning 360°/s) are enabled; FXPartSmoke.SmokeEmitter turns on at the eruption; Teleport1/2/3 sparks are bursts (EmitCount 60 / 30 / 15). GlowOrb.Twirl (a disabled BillboardGui) is for the far rift scenery only, see Biomes — Void. No light.A missing template → one warning per name; rocks still fly. The Eruption, IceFall, Waterspout and VoidRift SFX in SoundConfig are silent until ids are set.A SpawnVolumes part with SpawnGroup = "Rocks". Junk disables this group. Part3 sits ~50 studs from the nose for testing; move it ~250–400 studs ahead for play.

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: RockConfig. Key fields: Biomes[b] (Material, Color, Transparency, P_START, P_PEAK), SCALE_MIN/SCALE_MAX, SPEED, SPIN_SPEED, AIM_SPREAD, HP_PER_SCALE, DAMAGE_PER_SCALE, SHIELD_HIT_SEVERITY, ROLL_INTERVAL, GRACE, PEAK_AT, MAX_ACTIVE; eruptions in Eruptions[b] (see Eruptions). See Config Map.

searchDocs.title: Not in scope​
searchDocs.content: Late joiners do not see rocks already in flight; no reward for a destroyed rock; Shield Nova and enemy explosions do not affect rocks.

searchDocs.title: Payout formula​
searchDocs.content: Per player, at their payout moment:  minutes = floor(seconds / 60) timeMult = 1 + (MULT_MAX - 1) * clamp((seconds/60 - MULT_START_MIN) / (MULT_FULL_MIN - MULT_START_MIN), 0, 1) shortFactor = SHORT_RUN_FACTOR if seconds < SHORT_RUN_MIN * 60 else 1 coins = CoinManager.AddCoins(player, (BASE_COINS + COINS_PER_MIN * minutes) * timeMult * shortFactor, "RunReward") exp = XPManager.AddXP(player, (BASE_EXP + EXP_PER_MIN * minutes) * timeMult * shortFactor)   With the defaults: 1× up to 5 min, linear to 2.5× at 30 min, capped. Under 5 min the payout is 10 % (anti-farm: "start, leave, repeat" must not beat staying). Perk bonuses multiply on top inside AddCoins / AddXP, which return the amount really added, so the screen shows the real numbers.  seconds is the time this player was in this server for this run. The clock pauses while the player is disconnected and continues on a rejoin (RunStats rows live for the server's life, keyed by UserId).

searchDocs.title: When a player is paid​
searchDocs.content: Moment	Who	ThenRun end	every player in the server	results screen Leave button during the run (ReqLeaveToLobby)	that player, for their own time	the normal Lobby teleport (no results screen); crew page shows them LEFT EARLY Rejoin inside the results window	that player, once their profiles load	results screen with the same auto-return time Rejoin after the window	nobody	only that player is bounced to the Lobby  Each player is paid at most once per run. A payout waits up to 30 s for the coin and XP profiles; a second caller (ClientReady, the Leave hook) waits for the first one's result, so nobody sees a 0/0 screen. A payout that cannot land (profiles never loaded, player gone) claims nothing, so a later rejoin inside the window is paid. A player who is not on the run's roster (SessionCoordinator.IsAuthorized false, being bounced) is never paid and is dropped from the crew list (RunStats.Remove). The leave payout runs in the SessionCoordinator.SetLeaveHook hook, before JoinGuard.BounceToLobby, so profiles are still loaded. After the run end the hook pays nothing new: BACK TO LOBBY waits for (or finishes) the run-end payout, then leaves.

searchDocs.title: Run end​
searchDocs.content: Signals.OnTrainGameOver (any reason: all down, hull breach, Leviathan strike) is the single trigger:  sequenceDiagram participant TGO as TrainGameOver participant RES as RunEndService participant REV as ReviveService participant STA as RunStats participant C as Clients TGO->>RES: OnTrainGameOver(reason) RES->>REV: MarkRunOver() (no countdown, prompts, credits, respawn) RES->>STA: Freeze() (clocks and counts stop) RES->>RES: kill every living player (HealthManager.SetHealth 0) RES->>C: pay + RunResults to each player Note over RES: RESULTS_SECONDS (180 s) RES->>RES: SessionCoordinator.EndRunToLobby()   MarkRunOver runs before the kill, so the deaths see RunOver and start nothing. Players stay down for the whole window (CharacterAutoLoads is off). The world freezes: EventOrchestrator stops rolling events, VoidEnemyService removes every void enemy and spawns no more, and rocks and the threat timer already stop on game over.

searchDocs.title: Stats​
searchDocs.content: Stat	SourceTime	join → run end (or the Leave button), paused while disconnected Kills	Signals.PlayerKilledEnemy (the player whose hit was lethal) Junk	Signals.OnJunkCollected, 1 per junk Damage	CombatService.ApplyToModel: health actually removed by a player's hit Downs	ReviveService death → Down Revives	ReviveService revive → LoadCharacter  The payout (Leave or run end, once per player) also sends the run's kills (RunStats.Kills) to the MOST KILLS board and the played seconds to the LONGEST RUN board. See Leaderboard.

searchDocs.title: Results screen (client)​
searchDocs.content: RunResultsController binds the Studio-built StarterGui.RunResultsGui (Enabled = false, ResetOnSpawn = false, IgnoreGuiInset = false, DisplayOrder −2 so NovaChat draws above it). A rejoiner after the run end is never spawned, so the controller clones the GUI itself after 5 s; it connects RunResults before that, so an early packet waits. Built from the approved prototype roblox-gui-prototypes/2026-10-26-run-results-gui-prototype.html.  On open: HudBlackout.Set("RunResults", true) hides every other ScreenGui (NovaChat stays; Satchel and TopbarPlus use their own switches). Nothing is restored: the player teleports out. The revive GUIs step aside at RunOver (see Paid Revive). The cursor is freed with Signals.RequestMouseIcon(true, "RunResults").Page 1 — YOUR REWARDS: time survived, time bonus bar (5 → 30 min) and multiplier (×2.50 MAX in mint at the cap), then the Coin and EXP cards. Chips: BASE n, then ×m TIME (or ×0.10 UNDER 5 MIN in muted text for a short run), then ×p PERKS only when the perk multiplier is above 1.001.Count-up (RewardAnimation, MotionMaster only, ~4.5 s): panel spring 90 % → 100 % (UIPanel preset on the viewport UIScale); at 0.4 s the time counts up over 1.4 s with the bar and multiplier; at 1.8 s the multiplier pops with a ring; the coin card starts at 2.0 s and the EXP card at 2.3 s — each chip pops in while the number rolls to that step (0.6 / 0.7 / 0.6 s), then a burst of 12 icons, a ring and the card outline lights. A tap on page 1 cleans the animation Janitor and snaps to the final values. SFX: RunRewardTick (throttled 0.06 s), RunRewardStamp, RunRewardBurst.Page 2 — CREW STATS: one row per crew member (head shot, name, YOU / LEFT EARLY tag, time, kills, junk, damage, downs, revives) and a RUN m:ss pill. No reward columns.Footer: page button, AUTO RETURN IN m:ss (from endsAt − workspace:GetServerTimeNow()), BACK TO LOBBY (Signals.LeaveToLobbyRequested → ReqLeaveToLobby, no second payout).Scale: UIScale = min(W/1920, H/1022); under 0.68 the compact layout (authored at 844×332, scale clamped 0.75–1.5) applies the prototype's phone overrides from a table in the controller; the 1920 values are read back from the Studio instances.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: RunResults payload (S→C, one player):  { mine = { seconds, timeMult, shortFactor, baseCoins, coinsPaid, coinPerkMult, baseExp, expPaid, expPerkMult }, endsAt = <workspace:GetServerTimeNow() of the Lobby teleport>, crew = { { userId, displayName, seconds, kills, junk, damage, downs, revives, leftEarly } }, }   coinPerkMult = coins paid ÷ (base × timeMult × shortFactor), 1 when nothing was paid. expPerkMult = XPManager.GainMultiplier(player): AddXP's whole number can include an earlier award's carried fraction, which would show a false PERKS chip. Late joiners get it through JoinSync ("RunResults").

searchDocs.title: Threat model​
searchDocs.content: A reserved server (created by the lobby via TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync) already blocks the normal server-list join and rejects follow-a-friend joins. Two vectors remain: launching the gameplay placeId directly and landing in a non-reserved public server (game.PrivateServerId == ""), or a non-roster user reaching a reserved server with a stale access code or expired session.  JoinGuard closes both by validating every joiner against an authoritative roster keyed off the engine-set game.PrivateServerId, which cannot be spoofed from the client — so authorization can never be forged.

searchDocs.title: Cross-place contract​
searchDocs.content: Coordination between the lobby and gameplay places goes through two MemoryStore hash maps (fast, TTL-native, built for ephemeral cross-server state — unlike DataStore, which is slower, rate-limited, and has no native expiry). SessionStore is the only module that touches them.  Roster — keyed by privateServerId:  { partyId, authorizedUserIds: {number}, leaderUserId, createdAt }   The lobby writes this immediately before TeleportAsync, so it exists by the time the gameplay server boots. SessionStore.GetRoster reads it on boot with a short retry loop (GET_RETRIES × GET_RETRY_WAIT) to cover the boot/write race. SessionCoordinator mutates it via RemoveFromRoster when a grace window expires, and clears it entirely via ClearRoster on run end.  Session pointer — keyed by userId:  { placeId, accessCode, privateServerId, jobId, status, heartbeatAt }   This lets the lobby route a rejoiner back to the exact live server. The lobby seeds placeId/accessCode/privateServerId at teleport time, obtaining accessCode + privateServerId from the server-only TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync(gameplayPlaceId). Gameplay fills jobId and heartbeats the entry via SessionStore.RefreshPointer(userId, jobId), which uses UpdateAsync to stamp only jobId/status/heartbeatAt onto the already-seeded entry — it returns without creating a pointer if the lobby never seeded one, since gameplay never learns the raw accessCode and must not fabricate it.  jobId is informational/liveness only — it is not used to route the rejoin. On the lobby side, rejoin must set opts.ReservedServerAccessCode = accessCode alone; the engine API forbids combining ReservedServerAccessCode with ServerInstanceId or ShouldReserveServer on the same TeleportOptions. The access code alone resolves to the one reserved server it was issued for. TeleportData may additionally carry { partyId, rosterVersion } for diagnostics/logging — never trusted for authorization.

searchDocs.title: Components​
searchDocs.content: JoinGuard — IsReservedServer() is true only for a non-empty PrivateServerId with PrivateServerOwnerId == 0 (rejects both a directly-launched public server and a VIP server). IsAuthorized(roster, userId) checks roster.authorizedUserIds. BounceToLobby(player) retry-teleports to DisruptionConfig.LOBBY_PLACE_ID, reusing that config and its TELEPORT_RETRIES count from the Disruption system.SessionCoordinator.IsAuthorized(player) — whether the player may play this run: false when every player is bounced (not a reserved server, or no roster), otherwise the Studio bypass or the roster check. It yields until Initialize has read the roster. PerkSystemLoader passes it to PerkInventoryManager.Initialize, so a bounced player never uses a shop perk consumable (see Perk Inventory).SessionState — RegisterProvider(name, capture, restore) lets other managers plug into the grace/restore flow (see below). Capture(player) must run synchronously from PlayerRemoving, before any deferred teardown clears state. HoldForGrace/HasGrace/TakeBundle/Discard manage the grace window via a Janitor per held entry. CaptureTools(player) / RestoreTools(player, folder) are public so ReviveService can keep a player's Tools across a death (see Paid Revive); the caller of CaptureTools owns the folder until RestoreTools destroys it.SessionCoordinator.EndRunToLobby() — marks every player as a clean leaver (no grace hold) and bounces them all to the lobby; a player whose teleport fails is kicked with a message (outside Studio), so nobody waits on a finished run. RunEndService calls it when the results window ends (see Run Results). A rejoin inside the results window is paid and shown the results; a rejoin after it bounces only that player.SessionCoordinator.SetLeaveHook(fn) — one hook run (and awaited) on ReqLeaveToLobby before the teleport; RunEndService uses it to pay a mid-run leaver while their profiles are still loaded.SessionSystemLoader — registers AmmoManager.Snapshot/RestorePool and HealthManager.GetHealth/SetHealth as SessionState providers (under the keys "ammo" and "health"), then calls SessionCoordinator.Initialize(). The health capture returns nil when health is 0 or less: a dead player rejoins on the revive menu (ReviveService keeps them down by UserId), and restoring a 0 would kill the revived character.

searchDocs.title: Grace and restore flow​
searchDocs.content: On an unexpected PlayerRemoving (no prior ReqLeaveToLobby), SessionCoordinator.handleLeave synchronously calls SessionState.Capture(player) — which clones every Tool from the player's Backpack and Character into a per-user folder under ServerStorage.SessionToolCache, then runs every registered provider's capture (ammo pool snapshot, current health) — and holds the bundle via SessionState.HoldForGrace(userId, bundle, SessionConfig.GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS, onExpire). The player stays on the roster while held.  Scenario	What happensRejoin within the grace window	JoinGuard re-admits the player (still authorized). SessionCoordinator.handleJoin sees SessionState.HasGrace(userId) and calls scheduleRestore, which waits for CharacterAdded (or applies immediately if a character already exists) and, deferred one frame so HealthManager's full-health CharacterAdded reset runs first, calls SessionState.Restore(player, bundle) — reattaching cached Tools to the fresh Backpack and running every provider's restore. The player respawns at the normal train/party spawn; character position is never captured or restored. Grace window expires without a rejoin	The task.delay in HoldForGrace fires onExpire, which clears the session pointer and removes the user from the roster so they can no longer rejoin; the bundle's Janitor destroys the cached Tools folder. Clean leave (ReqLeaveToLobby)	SessionCoordinator marks the userId in cleanLeaving before bouncing, so the ensuing PlayerRemoving calls SessionState.Discard (no grace hold) and clears the pointer + roster entry immediately. Run end	When PlayerRemoving leaves the server empty (#Players:GetPlayers() <= 1, checked before removal completes) or on game:BindToClose, runEnded clears the roster and every remaining pointer for this privateServerId. No live-server rejoin is possible once the run has ended — a later rejoin attempt lands in the normal lobby flow.  SessionState's tools-folder cleanup uses an explicit Janitor index (Janitor:Add(toolsFolder, "Destroy", TOOLS_JANITOR_INDEX)), not the implicit form, specifically so TakeBundle can detach the folder without destroying it: it calls Janitor:RemoveNoClean(TOOLS_JANITOR_INDEX) (clears the index with no side effect) rather than Janitor:Remove (which would run the cleanup method immediately and destroy the very folder the caller is about to restore Tools from).  A SESSION_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS loop in SessionCoordinator periodically refreshes the roster TTL (SessionStore.RefreshRosterTTL) and every present, authorized player's pointer TTL (SessionStore.RefreshPointer), so a live run never expires while a dead run (crashed process, no clean shutdown) self-expires after ENTRY_TTL_SECONDS.

searchDocs.title: Non-goals​
searchDocs.content: Live-server rejoin only — rejoin works only while the reserved server stays alive (≥ 1 member keeps it running). If the server empties, the run ends and rejoiners return to the lobby fresh; there is no shared-world snapshot or run resurrection.No character-position restore — a rejoining player always respawns at the normal train/party spawn.No DataStore for ephemeral state — health/ammo/Tools grace-window state lives only in server memory (SessionState) and is lost if the server itself dies during the grace window; this is a deliberate scope cut, not an oversight.The lobby implementation (reserve, roster write, rejoin UI) is a separate project; only the cross-place contract above is specified here.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: BYPASS_GUARD_IN_STUDIO still exercises grace/restore In Studio, SessionConfig.BYPASS_GUARD_IN_STUDIO (default true) makes SessionCoordinator authorize everyone unconditionally, since no reserved server or lobby exists locally. It does not disable the grace/restore code paths — a Studio playtest still exercises Capture/HoldForGrace/Restore normally.

searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Player participant Coordinator as SessionCoordinator participant State as SessionState participant Guard as JoinGuard participant Store as SessionStore (MemoryStore) Note over Player,Coordinator: UNEXPECTED DROP Player--xCoordinator: PlayerRemoving (no prior ReqLeaveToLobby) Coordinator->>State: Capture(player) — Tools + ammo + health Coordinator->>State: HoldForGrace(userId, bundle, GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS, onExpire) alt Rejoin within GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS Player->>Coordinator: PlayerAdded (still on roster) Coordinator->>Guard: IsAuthorized(roster, userId) Guard-->>Coordinator: true Coordinator->>State: HasGrace(userId) == true Coordinator->>State: scheduleRestore -> TakeBundle + Restore (on CharacterAdded) State-->>Player: Tools reattached; ammo + health restored at train spawn else Grace window expires State->>State: onExpire fires Coordinator->>Store: ClearPointer(userId); RemoveFromRoster(privateServerId, userId) Note over Player: A later join is now unauthorized -> Guard.BounceToLobby ejects them end

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: SessionConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SessionConfig.luau  Its names and GAMEPLAY_PLACE_ID/map-name values are the contract with the lobby. The lobby lives in this repo and requires the same module (see Multiple Places). SESSION_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS	How often (30s) the live gameplay server refreshes the roster + session-pointer TTLs in MemoryStore. searchDocs.title: Config & schema​
searchDocs.content: SettingsConfig is pure data with no client dependencies, so the server can require it directly. SettingsConfig.Definitions is the single registry — one entry per setting key, typed as:  export type Definition = { type: "number" | "boolean" | "enum", default: any, category: string, label: string, order: number, min: number?, max: number?, step: number?, options: { string }?, }   SettingsConfig.GetDefaults() returns a fresh { [string]: any } map of every key to its default — this seeds both a brand-new ProfileStore profile and profile:Reconcile() for existing ones. SettingsConfig.VolumeBusByKey maps the four volume setting keys to their SoundConfig/Groups bus name (Master, BGM, SFX, Ambience) — the one place that mapping is declared, reused by both the migration step and SettingsAppliers. SettingsConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerSettings") is the ProfileStore name and must not change without a migration plan, since it is also where the legacy Volumes table is read from.  SettingsSchema is the single validator, called identically by server and client so the two sides can never disagree on what's valid. SettingsSchema.Validate(key, value): (boolean, any) looks key up in Definitions (unknown key is rejected, acting as an allowlist); for "number" it rejects non-numbers/NaN then clamps to [min, max]; for "boolean" it requires an exact boolean; for "enum" it requires membership in options. SettingsSchema.Sanitize(map) builds a complete settings map from GetDefaults() overlaid with every entry in map that passes Validate — anything invalid or no longer in the registry is silently dropped.

searchDocs.title: Server authority​
searchDocs.content: SettingsManager owns one ProfileStore session per player (PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync(tostring(player.UserId), ...)), following the same lifecycle pattern as CoinManager/XPManager: it kicks the player if the session fails to start, ends the session and re-kicks on OnSessionEnd, and ends the session on PlayerRemoving.  On join, before profile:Reconcile() runs, migrateLegacyVolumes(profile) does a one-time, idempotent copy: for every key in VolumeBusByKey, if Settings[key] is unset and the legacy profile.Data.Volumes[bus] is a valid number, it's validated and copied into Settings[key]. Once a key exists in Settings it is never overwritten from Volumes again, so this is safe to leave running indefinitely. The legacy Volumes table itself is left in place (not cleared) after migration.  After Reconcile and Sanitize, resetStaleAudioDefaults(profile) compares profile.Data.AudioDefaultsVersion (missing = 0) with SettingsConfig.AUDIO_DEFAULTS_VERSION. A profile below that version gets the current default for every key in VolumeBusByKey, then is stamped with the version. Bump AUDIO_DEFAULTS_VERSION after changing a SoundConfig.GroupVolumes default, because Reconcile only fills missing keys and saved profiles otherwise keep the old values. The bump also overwrites volumes a player chose. AudioDefaultsVersion is deliberately not in PROFILE_TEMPLATE: Reconcile would stamp it on old profiles and skip the reset.  SettingsManager.Initialize() — called once per server by SettingsSystemLoader.server.luau — wires Packets.SaveSetting.OnServerEvent: it looks up the player's profile (drops the message if none), checks key is a string, re-validates (key, value) through SettingsSchema.Validate, and on success writes profile.Data.Settings[key] = coerced. There is no explicit save call — ProfileStore autosaves the profile. Any invalid or unknown-key message is silently dropped.

searchDocs.title: Client API​
searchDocs.content: SettingsClient — initialized once via SettingsController.client.luau calling SettingsClient.Init() at startup — is the only module the settings GUI talks to. It holds a local cache of every setting's current value and exposes Get(key), Set(key, value): boolean, GetAll(), GetDefinition(key), and GetByCategory() (every definition grouped by category and sorted by order; today: "Audio" with 5 entries, "Controls" with 1, CameraSensitivity, "Gameplay" with 3 toggles).  Internally, applyAndNotify(key, value) is the shared path for both the join-sync handler and Set: it writes the cache, calls SettingsAppliers.Apply(key, value), then fires Signals.OnSettingChanged:Fire(key, value). The join-sync path calls only applyAndNotify (never scheduleSave), which is what prevents applying the server's own synced values from looping back into another save. scheduleSave(key, value) debounces persistence per key: the latest value is stashed in a pending table, and a single task.delay(0.25, ...) per key sends the trailing value via Packets.SaveSetting:Fire(key, value) — rapid changes (e.g. dragging a volume slider) collapse into one network send 0.25s after the drag settles.

searchDocs.title: Client appliers​
searchDocs.content: SettingsAppliers is a client-only key -> (value) -> () registry, kept deliberately separate from SettingsConfig so the shared config module stays free of client-only dependencies (Groups, UserSettings()) that the server must never require. The four volume keys are wired generically by iterating VolumeBusByKey and calling Groups.SetVolume(bus, value) — see Sound for the underlying SoundManager.SetVolume/GetVolume primitives; persistence lives here, not in SoundManager. Apply(key, value) looks up and calls the applier for key, or no-ops silently if the key has no client-side effect — CameraSensitivity is a deliberate example of the no-entry-needed case: it has no applier because CameraController reads it directly via SettingsClient.Get("CameraSensitivity") at startup and stays live via Signals.OnSettingChanged (see Camera).

searchDocs.title: Settings GUI​
searchDocs.content: SettingsGuiController binds StarterGui.SettingsGui (authored in Studio, not in src/). A right-aligned TopbarPlus icon "Settings" opens it; K toggles it (bindToggleKey, ignored while typing; not P, which the Lobby Perks menu owns); CloseButton deselects the icon. On PC it holds Signals.RequestMouseIcon key "SettingsGui" while open. The GAMEPLAY / VOLUMES tabs (CategoryContainer, its own row under the title) show GameplaySettingGroup / VolumeSettingGroup inside the SettingsContainer ScrollingFrame; the selected tab is teal with deep text.  The tree follows the Ocean Sunset house style (prototype roblox-gui-prototypes/2026-10-27-settings-gui-prototype.html): MainContainer 1000 wide, AutomaticSize Y, DisplayOrder 130, IgnoreGuiInset false, no ResponsiveScale tag. Size follows the screen through MainContainer.UIScale: wide = min(W/1920, H/1022); below 0.68 the controller swaps in the compact sizes (authored at 844×332, scale clamped to [0.75, 1.5]), the same mechanism as ActivePerksGuiController. Each row is OptionName · ValueContainer · OptionText (the value: 65%, 1.00, ON/OFF).  A ROWS table maps each authored row name to a setting key. The definition type picks the widget: "number" → slider, "boolean" → toggle.  Row	Key	EffectMasterVolumeOption / SoundEffectVolumeOption / AmbienceVolumeOption / BGMVolumeOption / UISoundVolumeOption	MasterVolume / SFXVolume / AmbienceVolume / MusicVolume / UIVolume	bus volume, 0..1 (shown as %) MouseSensitivityOption	CameraSensitivity	CameraController (0.1..3, linear) DanmakuOption	Danmaku	NovaChat DanmakuService.SetEnabled (the NovaChat handler listens) DamageNumbersOption	DamageNumbers	DamageNumbers.SetEnabled (applier) SprintFovOption	SprintFov	SprintController (Game Instance and Lobby) keeps the base FOV when off  Slider: LineContainer holds a teal Fill (width = value) and the 44×44 SliderHead hit frame. Its UIDragDetector is set to CustomScale at bind, so the script places the head. The value comes from the pointer X over LineContainer (drag or click), snapped to step. The head's Dot turns teal with an ink ring while dragged.Toggle: a click on ValueContainer.Value flips it. On = teal pill, deep knob at X 0.73; off = deep pill with line stroke, muted knob at X 0.27 (MotionMaster). OptionText reads ON (ink) / OFF (muted).Rows repaint on Signals.OnSettingChanged, so the join-sync can land after the GUI binds.New row: clone a row of the same kind in Studio, then add one ROWS entry.

searchDocs.title: Adding a new setting​
searchDocs.content: Two steps, at most:  Add one entry to SettingsConfig.Definitions — a unique key, a type ("number" | "boolean" | "enum"), a default, a category + label for the GUI, an order within that category, and the relevant bounds (min/max/step for "number", options for "enum"). That's enough for the setting to round-trip end to end: it seeds into new profiles, syncs on join, validates, and persists.If the setting has a direct client-side effect, add a matching entry to SettingsAppliers's appliers table — a one-argument function that applies value. Skip this step for settings with no client effect.  No packet, schema, or ProfileStore change is needed for a new setting — SettingsSchema.Validate and SettingsManager are fully generic over the Definitions table.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Never call SettingsAppliers or SettingsManager's internals directly GUI code should only ever call SettingsClient.Get/Set/GetAll/GetDefinition/GetByCategory and listen to Signals.OnSettingChanged. Calling SettingsAppliers.Apply directly skips validation, caching, and persistence — the value will apply visually but never save and will be wiped out by the next join-sync. SettingsManager is server-only and cannot be called from client code; firing Packets.SaveSetting directly skips client-side validation and the cache, desyncing SettingsClient.Get from what the server actually has.  The join-sync path never re-saves. SettingsClient.Init()'s SyncSettings handler calls applyAndNotify directly, not Set — applying the server's own synced values must never re-fire a save back to the server in a feedback loop.SettingsManager.Initialize() re-validates every SaveSetting message. A modified or out-of-date client can fire any (key, value) pair; the server drops anything that fails SettingsSchema.Validate rather than trusting the client's own clamping.Legacy Volumes data is migrated, not deleted. migrateLegacyVolumes copies old per-bus volumes into the generic Settings map once, but the old Volumes table is left on the profile afterward. Don't write new code that reads profile.Data.Volumes.Removing a Definitions entry doesn't delete saved data, but does stop syncing it. SettingsSchema.Sanitize drops any key no longer present in Definitions, so a removed setting simply disappears from SyncSettings/GetAll going forward — it does not actively scrub the old key from the ProfileStore document.CameraSensitivity scales GetMouseDelta(), not an engine property. UserGameSettings.MouseSensitivity is gated behind the RobloxScript capability (CoreScript-only) and throws if a game LocalScript writes it. UserInputService.MouseDeltaSensitivity is settable but only scales GetMouseDelta() consumers — it would have had no effect on the old default Roblox camera, which didn't consume GetMouseDelta() for look/rotation at all. That constraint is why CameraController is a fully script-owned Scriptable camera that reads raw GetMouseDelta() and scales it by CameraConfig.MouseLookBaseSpeed * sensitivity itself. See Camera.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Player participant SM as SettingsManager participant SC as SettingsClient participant Appliers as SettingsAppliers Note over SM: Join Player->>SM: onPlayerAdded SM->>SM: PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync ("PlayerSettings") SM->>SM: migrateLegacyVolumes(profile) - idempotent Volumes -> Settings copy SM->>SM: profile:Reconcile() - fill missing keys from GetDefaults() SM->>SM: SettingsSchema.Sanitize(profile.Data.Settings) SM->>SC: Packets.SyncSettings(settings) SC->>SC: for each key: SettingsSchema.Validate -> applyAndNotify SC->>Appliers: SettingsAppliers.Apply(key, value) SC-->>SC: Signals.OnSettingChanged(key, value) - no re-save Note over SC: Manual change (GUI calls SettingsClient.Set) Player->>SC: SettingsClient.Set(key, value) SC->>SC: SettingsSchema.Validate(key, value) SC->>Appliers: SettingsAppliers.Apply(key, coerced) - immediate local effect SC-->>SC: Signals.OnSettingChanged(key, coerced) SC->>SC: scheduleSave(key, coerced) - debounced 0.25s SC->>SM: Packets.SaveSetting(key, coerced) SM->>SM: SettingsSchema.Validate(key, value) - server re-validates, never trusts client SM->>SM: profile.Data.Settings[key] = coerced - ProfileStore autosaves

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ShredderClient.client.luau	Prompt registration, nonce-guarded two-step handshake, junk-count-reactive HoldDuration updates Server	src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau	Session management, anti-exploit validation, junk consumption, yield credited to MaterialPool Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShredderMath.luau	Shared ComputeHoldDuration helper (linear interpolation) Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShredderResultCodes.luau	Frozen result-code enum (9 codes) shared between client and server Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ShredderConfig.luau	All tunable constants for interaction, hold duration, anti-exploit, client arc animation, and asset names  Packets: ReqShredderStart, ReqShredderComplete, ShredderHoldEnded — see Networking MapSignals: none — the shredder is a self-contained two-step RemoteFunction handshake

searchDocs.title: Client: prompt and handshake​
searchDocs.content: ShredderClient watches CollectionService for Workbench-tagged models. On each workbench it finds a ProximityPrompts/ShredPromptPart/ProximityPrompt, sets ActionText, HoldDuration, and MaxActivationDistance from config, and wires three connections: PromptButtonHoldBegan (fires ReqShredderStart), PromptButtonHoldEnded (fires ShredderHoldEnded and bumps the nonce to cancel), and Triggered (fires ReqShredderComplete only when the nonce matches the armed value). A Backpack and Character Janitor pair keeps HoldDuration in sync whenever junk is added or removed. If the player holds the prompt with zero Wood/Metal junk, an "info" notification fires and the prompt is briefly disabled.

searchDocs.title: Server: two-step session​
searchDocs.content: ReqShredderStart validates the workbench tag, proximity (INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE), per-player cooldown, and junk availability. It stores a session record (workbench, start time, computed duration, junk snapshot). ReqShredderComplete re-checks all constraints plus timing (elapsed >= duration - HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE), re-validates junk still belongs to the player from the snapshot, computes the Wood/Metal yield, and destroys all junk Tools.

searchDocs.title: Processing animation​
searchDocs.content: Each placed workbench plays ShredderConfig.PROCESS_ANIMATION_ID (looped) on its AnimationController.Animator while any hold is on. The server plays it, so it replicates to every client. Holds: a player from a successful ReqShredderStart until ReqShredderComplete, ShredderHoldEnded, a new start, leaving, or a safety timeout (duration + HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE + 1 s); and each Salvage Drone junk for ShopPerkConfig.DRONE_PROCESS_SECONDS. ShredderHoldEnded only releases the animation hold; it never ends the session, because it can arrive after ReqShredderComplete. A bench with no Animator warns once and processes without the animation. The game creator must own the animation asset.

searchDocs.title: Output​
searchDocs.content: On a valid completion the server calls MaterialPool.Add({ Wood, Metal }, MaterialPool.ArcPoints(bench)). The pool is server-wide — no material Tools are created, nothing lands on the floor, and the workbench is never locked (WORKBENCH_BUSY is no longer returned). Every client animates the gain locally: Handle clones arc out of TrajectoryPoints and fly into the Materials HUD. See Material Pool.

searchDocs.title: Shared math and result codes​
searchDocs.content: ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration linearly interpolates hold time between MIN_HOLD_DURATION (1 item) and MAX_HOLD_DURATION (MAX_JUNK_COUNT items). Both client and server call it so the prompt ring and the server timing check always agree. ShredderResultCodes is a frozen enum used by both sides for unambiguous rejection reasons.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit thresholds are sensitive INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE, HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE, and PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN are the primary barriers against timing exploits and teleport-shredding. Increasing tolerances too far removes protection; tightening them too far breaks legit high-latency players.  Studio asset requirements:  Each workbench Model must be tagged "Workbench" with a PrimaryPart set.Each workbench should contain a child Model named "TrajectoryPoints" (tag it PlacementIgnore) with two invisible, anchored, non-collidable BasePart children: "SpawnPoint" (at the shredder output mouth) and "LandingPoint" (floor landing target). If it is missing, the pool is still credited and the effect starts at the workbench pivot.In ReplicatedStorage, a Folder named "CraftingMaterials" should contain Tool templates named "Wood" and "Metal", each with a BasePart child named "Handle". Clients clone the Handle for the cosmetic arc; without it the effect skips straight to the 2D fly.  Nonce guard. The client uses a per-workbench nonce pair (holdNonce, armedNonce) to drop stale ReqShredderComplete calls when the player releases early or changes workbenches mid-hold. Modifying the hold flow must preserve this guard or the server's NO_SESSION rejection will fire spuriously.  Junk snapshot. The server snapshots junk at ReqShredderStart time. ReqShredderComplete re-filters that snapshot to tools still in the player's possession — it does not re-scan the Backpack. This prevents inflation from picking up new junk during the hold.  Wood/Metal only. Only Metal and Wood junk types are consumed and yield output: KNOWN_JUNK_TYPES on both sides lists just those two. Energy junk never becomes a Tool — it is credited to the Material Pool on grab.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Energy Recycler (PartyPerkBuffs.ShredEnergyPerJunk): each shredded junk also credits that much Energy in the same MaterialPool.Add.Overclock Core (PartyPerkBuffs.OverclockBonus): one server-wide counter counts each Wood/Metal junk processed at a workbench (player shred or drone) while the perk is live. Every ShopPerkConfig.OVERCLOCK_EVERYth junk yields ×(1 + bonus) (computeYield per junk).Salvage Drone delivery (Signals.DroneJunkDelivered(bench, type, tier) from JunkService): Wood/Metal is processed like one shredded junk (Overclock, Efficient Shredding, Energy Recycler); Energy credits its Yield × (1 + EnergyYieldBonus). The pool gain arcs from the bench TrajectoryPoints, and the bench animates.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant C as ShredderClient participant S as ShredderServer C->>C: PromptButtonHoldBegan - countJunks() > 0 C->>S: ReqShredderStart(bench) S->>S: validate tag, proximity, cooldown, junk count S->>S: ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration() S->>S: record session + StartTime S->>C: (isValid, duration, code) C->>C: prompt.HoldDuration = duration C->>C: PromptButtonHoldEnded -> nonce bump (cancels armed session) C->>C: Prompt.Triggered (hold complete), armedNonce check passes C->>S: ReqShredderComplete(bench) S->>S: re-validate session, workbench match, elapsed >= duration - TOLERANCE S->>S: re-verify junk still owned, computeYield(junks) S->>S: destroy junk Tools, record cooldown S->>S: MaterialPool.Add({Wood, Metal}, ArcPoints(bench)) Note over S: MaterialPoolUpdate to all clients<br/>(each plays arc + fly-to-HUD) S->>C: (success, woodCount, metalCount, code)

searchDocs.title: At a glance​
searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SprintController.client.luau	Input binding, WalkSpeed/FOV prediction, intent signalling, sync consumption Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/StaminaManager.luau	Drain/regen simulation, sync dispatch Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SprintValidation.luau	Shared sprint gate conditions (humanoid state checks) Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/StaminaConfig.luau	Speed, FOV, drain/regen, validation thresholds  Packets: StaminaSprintIntent, StaminaStateSync — see Networking MapSignals: OnStaminaValueChanged, OnSprintToggled, MobileSprintToggled — see Signals Map

searchDocs.title: Client prediction​
searchDocs.content: SprintController binds sprint to LeftShift and ButtonB (gamepad) via ContextActionService; a separate MobileSprintToggled signal handles the mobile toggle button. On each RenderStepped tick it calls canSprintNow() (wraps SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint) and calls setSprinting accordingly, which sets humanoid.WalkSpeed, tweens FieldOfView via TweenPlus, and fires Signals.OnSprintToggled. Sprint intent resets on CharacterRemoving and on WindowFocusReleased.  On StaminaStateSync the client clamps the received stamina, forces sprint off if the server says so, and fires Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged for the HUD (HealthStaminaGuiController: 10 stamina cells; at 0 stamina the value reads "TIRED").

searchDocs.title: Server authority​
searchDocs.content: StaminaManager maintains a StaminaRecord per player (Stamina, IsSprinting, SprintIntent, LastSprintTime, LastSyncTime). On the StaminaSprintIntent packet it immediately updates sprint state and calls syncPlayer. Its Heartbeat loop clamps dt to MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s to prevent large delta spikes, drains stamina at StaminaDrain * dt while sprinting (perks: SprintDrainReduction, FreeSprint, FreeSprintAlways), and regenerates at StaminaRegen * dt (perk: StaminaRegenBonus) after RegenDelay seconds of not sprinting.  It syncs to the client when sprint state changes, stamina hits 0 (forced stop), stamina refills to max, or the periodic sync interval (STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s) elapses while stamina is changing. StaminaManager.RestoreStamina(player, amount) is available for pickup items but has no caller yet. StaminaManager.Initialize() must be called exactly once — it is called by StaminaSystemLoader.server.luau.

searchDocs.title: Shared validation gate​
searchDocs.content: SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint(humanoid, rules) returns false if health is 0, MoveDirection magnitude is below MinMoveDirection, the character is moving backward beyond MaxBackwardComponent, or horizontal speed is below MinHorizontalSpeed. It is called identically on the client (canSprintNow) and the server (canPlayerSprint) so the gate condition can never desync between the two sides.

searchDocs.title: Lobby sprint​
searchDocs.content: The Lobby has its own places/Lobby/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SprintController.client.luau. It reads the same StaminaConfig keys, speeds and FOV, runs the same SprintValidation gate, honours the SprintFov setting, and listens to MobileSprintToggled from the mapped MobileGeneralGuiController. It has no stamina: no drain, no StaminaManager, no packets, so the player sprints for as long as they hold the key. It tweens FOV with MotionMaster (TweenPlus is not mapped in the Lobby). Perk speed bonuses, build mode and cannons do not exist there.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Sprint logic must be mirrored on both sides SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint is the shared gate. If you add a new sprint-blocking condition (e.g. stun), add it to SprintValidation and verify it is called by both SprintController (client) and StaminaManager (server). A condition added only to one side will cause desyncs.  WalkSpeed is client-only. The server does not validate movement speed (see audit note S3 in SprintController's source); a cheating client can move at any speed. If movement integrity becomes necessary, add a server-side speed sanity check.STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s (10 Hz). The server only sends a sync when stamina is actively changing — if stamina is full and the player is standing still, no sync is sent, which is intentional.MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s clamp. The server caps the Heartbeat delta so a lag spike cannot drain or regen an unrealistic amount of stamina in one tick. Do not remove this clamp.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Quick Breath (StaminaRegenBonus): StaminaManager regen × (1 + bonus); server only (the client shows the synced value).Sprint Boots (MoveSpeedBonus): SprintController scales walk and sprint speed, and re-applies it on cannon dismount, respawn and buff change. There is no server speed cap.Free Runner (FreeSprint): StaminaManager skips sprint drain while the replicated workspace attribute PirateAttackActive is not true (set by PirateAttackEvent). The client needs no change: it shows the server's synced stamina.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​

searchDocs.title: Facade and playback​
searchDocs.content: SoundController.client.luau calls SoundManager.Init() once at startup. Init creates the bus graph and listener (Groups.Ensure), starts measuring every known asset in the background (Normalizer.Prime), warms the positional sound pool (Pool.Ensure plus per-asset pre-warm), connects the replication receiver (SFX.ConnectReplication), and autostarts any ambience beds listed in SoundConfig.Ambience.Autostart. Asset preloading happens earlier, in ReplicatedFirst/LoadingScreen.client.luau: it preloads every rbxassetid:// string in the Configs modules plus every Sound in the replicated services through PreloadLib.  After Init, any client script or tool may require(SharedModules.SoundManager) and call the facade (PlaySFX, PlaySFXAt, PlayLooped, PlayMusic, SetAmbience, SetVolume). The submodules (Groups, Normalizer, AudioMath, Pool, SFX, Music, Ambience) are internal and should not be required directly.

searchDocs.title: Signal chain​
searchDocs.content: flowchart LR P2D["AudioPlayer (2D SFX, loops, BGM, ambience)"] --> BA P3D["AudioPlayer (positional)"] --> SH[AudioPitchShifter] --> EM[AudioEmitter on a pooled part] EM -. "InteractionGroup SoundManager" .-> L[AudioListener on CurrentCamera] L --> BA BA["Bus fader A (SFX / BGM / Ambience / UI)"] --> BB[Bus fader B] BB --> M["Master fader pair"] --> LIM["AudioLimiter (MaxLevel -1 dB)"] --> OUT[AudioDeviceOutput]   The listener feeds the SFX bus. The bus instances live in SoundService.SoundManagerBuses (client-created). Each sound's AudioPlayer.Volume = clamp(gain × mix × fade, 0, 10):  gain comes from the normalizer and is fixed for the whole play.mix is the config Volume (or opts.Volume), default 1.0.fade is the MotionMaster fade in / out / crossfade.  Bus and Master faders are set only by SetVolume (the Settings system).

searchDocs.title: Loudness normalizer​
searchDocs.content: Normalizer loads each asset in an unwired, never-played AudioPlayer, waits for IsReady (gives up after 10 s), and reads GetWaveformAsync(0..TimeLength, Samples). AudioMath.LoudnessDb splits the samples into ~400 ms windows, drops windows below GateDb (silent intros and tails), and takes the RMS of the rest. The gain is 10^((TargetDb − measured) / 20), clamped to MinGain..MaxGain; an asset with no window above the gate gets 1.0 (never boosted). One gain per asset id per session; two requests for the same id share one measurement.  Init primes every id in SoundConfig (beds and playlist tracks first, then SFX) one at a time in the background. When a sound plays before its gain is known:  One-shots (PlaySFX, PlaySFXAt, replicated sounds) play at once at gain 1.0; the next play uses the real gain.Loops and beds wait up to 0.5 s for the gain, then start at 1.0. PlayLooped still returns its handle at once. Music tracks wait up to 5 s (GAIN_WAIT in Music.luau): BGMs tracks are measured only when their playlist starts, and a first measurement takes about 1–2 s.  The normalizer reads only the raw asset, never a bus. Raising a bus raises every sound on it by exactly that factor. SoundConfig.Normalize.Enabled = false makes every gain 1.0 (A/B listening switch). Self-check from the Studio command bar:  loadstring(game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.SoundManager.AudioMath.Source)().SelfCheck()

searchDocs.title: Positional replication​
searchDocs.content: The server does not play audio itself — ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau acts only as a validated relay for Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation:  Per-player rate limit (MIN_INTERVAL = 0.05s) rejects bursts.Payload shape is validated (data.SoundConfig.Id must be a string).The sound ID must be in ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS, built at startup from SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() — any SFX entry with Replicate = true is included automatically.The original payload is passed to every other connected player via FireClient.  The receiving client's SFX.ConnectReplication handler acquires a pooled voice at the given position and plays it, the same path PlaySFXAt uses locally. The payload carries the sender's mix volume, never its gain; the receiver applies its own gain.

searchDocs.title: BGM contexts​
searchDocs.content: SoundConfig.Music.Playlists defines six named playlists — one per BGM context (Normal, Combat, LowFuel, Jump, Pursuit, Boss). There is no generic/default playlist; Music.Play falls back to "Normal" only when called with no argument.  Context	Trigger	Gap behaviorNormal	Default; nothing else active	Gapped — random silence between tracks Combat	Server calls MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat")	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence LowFuel	Automatic, client-derived from fuel level	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence Jump	Automatic, from Packets.JumpStateSync while JumpDriveConfig.IsJumpActive(phase)	Continuous; Shuffle = false Pursuit	Automatic: train stalled (Signals.OnTrainStateChanged), or the Threat Timer phase is Imminent (Packets.ThreatStateSync)	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence Boss	Automatic: the Threat Timer phase is Arrived (Packets.ThreatStateSync); outranks Combat so enemy waves do not cut it	Continuous — overlapping crossfade, no silence

searchDocs.title: BGM tracks (BGMs folder)​
searchDocs.content: Track ids do not live in SoundConfig. BgmTracks.Get(playlist, biome) reads them from ReplicatedStorage.BGMs each time a playlist starts, so the artist adds or removes tracks in Studio with no code edit:  Normal and Combat are per-biome (PerBiome = true). They read the folder SoundConfig.Music.BiomeFolders[CurrentBiome] (NormalArea, VolcanoArea, IceArea, Void, StormArea).LowFuel, Jump, Pursuit and Boss read the shared folder BGMs.Shared.The lowercase Sound name gives the role: the role word (normal, battle, lowfuel, jump, pursuit, boss), optionally followed by digits (normal2) or by the artist's "maybe" marker (normal(?), normal(?2)). A track that still has its library name (Blizzard Approaching) is skipped. Only SoundId is read.No folder, no biome entry, or no matching track → the playlist's config Tracks (empty today → silence).  MusicDirector passes the CurrentBiome workspace attribute to PlayMusic. When the biome changes while a per-biome context plays, the music crossfades to the new biome's tracks. During Jump (or any shared context) the change waits until a per-biome context comes back. Music.Play primes the normalizer with the resolved ids, because Init only measures ids that are in SoundConfig.  Priority when more than one condition is true: Jump > Boss > Combat > Pursuit > LowFuel > Normal. MusicDirector.client.luau holds five local inputs — jumpActive (from JumpStateSync), combatContext (set by the server), stalledActive and lowFuelActive (both derived locally from Signals.OnTrainStateChanged), and threatPhase (from ThreatStateSync) — and recomputes the resolved context on every change to any of them, calling SoundManager.PlayMusic(context) only when the resolved context actually changes. A low-fuel state during combat is suppressed without losing track position when combat ends.  Driving combat from server gameplay code (an event or outpost zone):  local MusicService = require(game.ServerStorage.SharedModules.MusicService) MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat") -- on event/outpost enter MusicService.SetContext(player, "Normal") -- on event/outpost leave   MusicService.SetContext is stateless — it only fires Packets.SetMusicContext to the targeted player. Passing "Normal" clears the combat override; the client then falls back to LowFuel or Normal based on its own fuel state. Low fuel itself needs no gameplay code: MusicDirector watches Signals.OnTrainStateChanged and activates LowFuel whenever fuel / TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL drops below SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct (default 0.25).

searchDocs.title: Volume persistence​
searchDocs.content: The five buses (Master, SFX, BGM, Ambience, UI) persist across sessions as part of the generic Settings system, not inside SoundManager itself. SoundManager.SetVolume(group, volume) / GetVolume(group) remain the immediate-apply primitives — they set the Groups fader pairs directly and do nothing else. AudioFader.Volume tops out at 3, so each bus is two faders in series: v splits as a = min(v, 3), b = v / a, which covers 0..9. Settings above 9 cap at 9. GetVolume returns the player's number, not the fader product.  UI code that needs the change saved calls SettingsClient.Set("MasterVolume" | "MusicVolume" | "SFXVolume" | "AmbienceVolume" | "UIVolume", value) instead. SettingsClient.Set validates via SettingsSchema, applies it (SettingsAppliers maps the key to a bus via SettingsConfig.VolumeBusByKey and calls Groups.SetVolume), fires Signals.OnSettingChanged(key, value), and schedules a debounced save (Packets.SaveSetting) that coalesces rapid changes (e.g. a slider drag) into one trailing send. On join, SettingsManager delivers the saved settings map via Packets.SyncSettings; SettingsClient applies each entry the same way but never re-saves a synced value, so no feedback loop results. See Settings for the full validate/apply/persist flow.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Never create ad-hoc Sound or AudioPlayer instances All audio must go through SoundManager. A hand-made Sound or AudioPlayer skips the buses (volume settings have no effect), skips the normalizer, skips the positional pool (memory churn), and may leak across character reloads.  Emitters need the interaction group SoundService.DefaultListenerLocation creates a default AudioListener with an empty interaction group, wired straight to the device output. An AudioEmitter with an empty group is heard by that listener and skips the buses. Every emitter SoundManager creates, and its own listener, use SoundConfig.InteractionGroup ("SoundManager").  SoundManager.Init() must be called before any Play* call. It is called once by SoundController.client.luau; do not call it again elsewhere.PlaySFXAt parents a pooled BasePart at the given Vector3 in the workspace; the pool releases it after TimeLength + 0.05 seconds. An asset that is not ready within 2 s is skipped. Do not hold references to the part or player after the call.PlayLooped returns a LoopHandle. The caller must call handle:Stop() or handle:Destroy() when done — an abandoned handle leaks a live AudioPlayer under SoundService. The handle's Player field is the AudioPlayer; FadeTo(volume) sets the mix, the gain stays applied.A sound entry with Replicate = true and an empty Id ("") is excluded from the allowlist automatically by GetReplicatedIds(); the pool warm step also skips empty IDs.The BGM and Ambience buses default below 1.0, so music and ambience sit under SFX at the same mix value.The AudioLimiter after Master is a safety net only. At very high settings it may hold peaks down instead of distorting.

searchDocs.title: Phases​
searchDocs.content: stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Counting Counting --> Imminent: remaining reaches 0 Imminent --> Arrived: SPAWN_DELAY elapsed (OnThreatArrived fires) Counting --> Counting: jump arrival (reset to ARRIVAL_SECONDS) Imminent --> Counting: jump arrival Arrived --> Counting: jump arrival   Phase	MeaningCounting	The countdown runs from ARRIVAL_SECONDS (900 s) Imminent	The countdown hit 0. The omen toast shows, and SPAWN_DELAY (30 s) runs in real time Arrived	Signals.OnThreatArrived fired once. Holds until the next jump arrival

searchDocs.title: Speed​
searchDocs.content: The countdown speed is a pure function of the current state (speedFor):  Condition (first match wins)	SpeedTrain not started yet, a jump is active, game over, or phase Arrived	0 (paused) Phase Imminent	1 Train stalled (OnTrainFuelStateChanged stalled = true)	STALLED_SPEED (4) × Bait Buoy Otherwise	1 × Bait Buoy  Imminent ignores fuel on purpose: the 30 s is the party's last warning, and refuelling during it neither shortens nor lengthens it. An Emergency Generator coast does not speed up the countdown — the signal reports a coast as empty = true, stalled = false, and the timer reads only stalled. The client shows a "running on fumes" toast instead (see Client).  Bait Buoy (party shop perk, PartyPerkBuffs.ThreatSlowdown 0.10): the Counting speed is PerkBuffRead.Reduce(speed, ThreatSlowdown) (× 0.9, never below 10%). Imminent stays real time. A change of the attribute calls commit, so remaining is snapshot under the old speed. Clients read the replicated speed from ThreatStateSync, so the clocks need no change.  Braking does not pause the countdown. A braked train burns no fuel (Train Fuel); the Leviathan clock is the cost of waiting.

searchDocs.title: Algebraic model​
searchDocs.content: Like TrainFuelManager, there is no per-frame loop. Every input (train start, fuel state, jump phase, game over) calls commit(), which:  snapshots remaining -= speed * (now - lastEventTime) under the old speed,picks the new speed with speedFor,bumps a nonce and, if the speed is above 0, schedules task.delay(remaining / speed) to advance the phase — a stale callback whose nonce no longer matches does nothing,broadcasts ThreatStateSync(phase, remaining, speed, serverTime).  Entering a new phase (enterPhase) moves lastEventTime to now before committing, so the new phase's budget is not reduced by time spent in the old one. Time lost while stalled stays lost: refuelling only returns the speed to 1.  Clients compute the live countdown as max(0, remaining - speed * (GetServerTimeNow() - serverTime)), the same extrapolation TrainStateSync uses.

searchDocs.title: Jump reset​
searchDocs.content: OnJumpPhaseChanged pauses the countdown while JumpDriveConfig.IsJumpActive(phase) is true. On the arrival edge (active → inactive) it resets to a full Counting, whatever the phase was. If the train is still stalled on arrival, the new cycle starts at STALLED_SPEED.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: TrainClient shows two fuel toasts from TrainStateSync edges: FUMES_MESSAGE (warn) when coastEndsAt goes from 0 to a value above 0, and FUEL_OUT_MESSAGE (alert) when isStalled goes from false to true. They follow the stall flag, not the countdown speed, so the fuel-out toast also shows during Imminent.ThreatController shows OMEN_MESSAGE (alert) once when the phase becomes Imminent.MusicDirector plays Pursuit while the train is stalled or the phase is Imminent, and Boss while the phase is Arrived (priority Jump > Boss > Combat > Pursuit > LowFuel > Normal). The Pursuit and Boss playlists have no tracks until asset ids are added to SoundConfig.  A player who joins while one of these states is already active gets that toast once, from the join snapshot. This is intentional: they need to know.

searchDocs.title: Seams​
searchDocs.content: Leviathan boss. Signals.OnThreatArrived is where the future boss spec spawns the boss. The boss must leave on the OnJumpPhaseChanged arrival edge, matching the reset above. It hits the train with TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(amount, ThreatConfig.BOSS_DAMAGE_SOURCE, { Position = <dome surface point>, Severity = 1 }); see Train Shield — Hull.Void enemies. Separate from the boss: void enemy swarms hit the train through TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage on the orchestrator's Void channel — see Void Enemies.Game-over cutscene. Reads the TrainGameOverReason from Signals.OnTrainGameOver.

searchDocs.content: ThreatConfig timer fields: ARRIVAL_SECONDS (900), STALLED_SPEED (4), SPAWN_DELAY (30), Phase. Toasts: NOTIF_TYPE, FUMES_NOTIF_TYPE, NOTIF_DURATION, FUMES_MESSAGE, FUEL_OUT_MESSAGE, OMEN_MESSAGE. Hull fields are documented under Train Shield — Hull.
