searchDocs.title: How it works​
searchDocs.content: Order: at boot the server numbers every Model under Workspace.TrainPlatforms: FrontPlatform (FRONT_PLATFORM_NAME) is 1, the rest by distance from it. It writes the number to a PlatformIndex attribute. No Studio setup is needed; adding or removing a platform Model in Studio changes the count (add a Costs entry for each new locked index).Starting count: STARTING_PLATFORMS platforms start built. The server raises any value below 2 to 2 (with a warn); a value above the platform count means all start built.Boot: platforms above the starting count move to ServerStorage/LockedPlatforms. A copy with every CollectionService tag removed goes to ReplicatedStorage/PlatformGhosts/<index> (tags must go: GetTagged also returns ReplicatedStorage instances, so a tagged copy would count as a BuildArea). Each locked platform gets Seam and SeamAxis attributes.State: attributes on TrainPlatforms — BuiltCount, DepositedWood, DepositedMetal (progress of platform BuiltCount + 1), and RearX (largest X of the built platforms, written at boot and after each build; the Train Shield length follows it). Attributes replicate to late joiners, so there is no JoinSync sender.Deposit: the handler moves min(cost − deposited, pool) of each material via MaterialPool.Spend, with no yield between reading and writing. A second request in the same frame sees the new totals; a request for an already-finished platform returns STALE. Material is never spent past the cost.Build: when both materials are full, the locked platform is parented back into TrainPlatforms. Placement and drop code find its BuildArea / DroppableSurface tags at run time — no placement change.Client: the ghost and billboard show only while the prompt is shown (PromptShown / PromptHidden). The prompt is disabled in build mode, where F toggles grid mode.Reveal: on ChildAdded of a platform not present at load, the client hides the real platform (LocalTransparencyModifier) in the same callback, extrudes a visual copy behind a neon wall (SWEEP_DURATION), then shows the real one. Collision is live the whole time.  sequenceDiagram participant P as PlatformExtendController participant S as PlatformExtendService participant MP as MaterialPool participant TP as TrainPlatforms (attributes) P->>S: ReqPlatformDeposit(index) S->>MP: Spend({ Wood, Metal }) S->>TP: DepositedWood / DepositedMetal alt both full S->>TP: parent platform, BuiltCount += 1 TP-->>P: ChildAdded → hide, sweep, show end S-->>P: (code, woodAdded, metalAdded)

searchDocs.title: Dev command​
searchDocs.content: /expand (alias /platform) in chat builds the next platform at once, free, and plays the normal reveal. It sends ReqDevExpandPlatform; DevCommandsService gates it on place owner / group rank 250+ and calls PlatformExtendService.DevBuildNext(). Any Wood/Metal already deposited toward that platform is cleared (it was spent from the pool).  Fallback reveal If the scan sweep is rejected after playtesting, replace only the body of playReveal with a dust-cloud burst that shows the platform while it is hidden.

Sound ids: SoundConfig keys PlatformDeposit, PlatformBuilt.  Perks: BuildCostReduction (Thrifty Builder, Party) — each platform cost goes through PerkBuffRead.ReduceCost (×max(0.1, 1−b), rounded up) in both PlatformExtendService (charged) and PlatformExtendController (shown). See Perks.

searchDocs.content: No persistence (platforms reset with the server, like the pool), no out-of-order building, no refunds or demolition.

searchDocs.title: Algebraic fuel model​
searchDocs.content: getFuel() is computed as fuelAtLastEvent - currentRate * elapsed rather than ticked every frame. commitEvent snapshots fuel under the old rate before switching to the new one, so every transition (brake, refuel, stall) is seamless. A scheduleNonce guards task.delay callbacks: any subsequent commitEvent increments the nonce, and a stale callback no-ops if its captured nonce no longer matches. Do not call reschedule directly — always go through commitEvent.  While hasStarted = false (before the first brake release), the drain rate is forced to 0 and no task.delay stall timer is scheduled — fuel is frozen pre-game.

searchDocs.title: Brake toggle​
searchDocs.content: Triggering a TrainBrakeLever-tagged prompt sends ReqToggleBrake(lever). The server flips isBraked; on the first-ever un-brake it also sets hasStarted = true and fires Signals.SetTrainStarted(true). Either way it calls commitEvent(), which reschedules the stall task.delay under the new rate and broadcasts TrainStateSync. The client updates the lever's ActionText ("Stop Train" / "Resume Train") from the returned isBraked. A braked train has rate 0, so no stall is scheduled (the same path as the pre-start and jump freezes).

searchDocs.title: Lever animation​
searchDocs.content: Purely cosmetic and entirely client-side — the server never knows the lever's physical pose. TrainClient swings the pivot by BRAKE_LEVER_SWING_DEG about the pivot's own Z axis between the two brake states, using MotionMaster (never TweenService), and plays BRAKE_LEVER_ANIM_ID once on the model's Animator as a button-press flourish plus the TrainBrakeLever SFX.  Which end means "braked" is a property of how the model was posed, not of the brake logic, so it lives in config: BRAKE_LEVER_REST_IS_BRAKED says whether the authored pose is the braked one. If the lever reads backwards in-game, flip that boolean — don't negate BRAKE_LEVER_SWING_DEG, which only changes which way it rotates.  Three rules keep it honest:  Only a flip animates. TrainStateSync also arrives on refuel and stall events, so the handler compares isBraked against the previous value — otherwise the lever would re-swing every time someone tops up the tank.Joining snaps. The first snapshot after joining, and any lever that registers late (tag added at runtime, streaming), poses instantly with no swing.Reversal is continuous. The in-flight tween lives in the lever's Janitor under the "leverTween" index; adding a new one there destroys the old, which pauses it in place rather than resetting it, so a mid-swing toggle starts from wherever the lever actually is.  Every client animates from the same replicated isBraked, so no extra network traffic is needed to keep the levers agreeing.

searchDocs.title: Refuel​
searchDocs.content: Triggering a TrainEngine-tagged prompt sends ReqRefuelTrain(engine). The server validates the tag, proximity, and that the tank isn't already full, spends pool Energy via MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", maxFuel − fuel, FUEL_PER_POINT) (only the points needed; 0 spent → NO_ENERGY), clears a stall if fuel becomes > 0, then calls commitEvent(newFuel). A boolean isRefueling mutex serializes concurrent requests — it is not a queue, so a second request while one is in flight returns NO_ENERGY even if the pool has Energy; the player can retry immediately after.  The engine is the PowerCore model, which is also the Jump Drive bench (it carries both tags). Its refuel prompt has a 1.5 s HoldDuration so the refuel animation has time to read.  Refuel animation​  Cosmetic, and every player sees it. Roblox replicates ProximityPrompt.PromptButtonHoldBegan/Ended to the server, but it runs no distance check on them, so TrainFuelManager validates each hold (proximity, pool Energy > 0, fuel < max). Then it writes the holder's UserId to the engine attribute TrainConfig.REFUEL_ATTR ("RefuelingBy", 0 = nobody). A watchdog drops a hold after HoldDuration + REFUEL_HOLD_GRACE if its end event never arrives. PlayerRemoving also drops it. With two holders, the attribute shows one of them until both release. No packet is involved: the attribute replicates, and late joiners see it at once.  TrainRefuelFxController animates off the attribute. While it is non-zero, the controller sends an Energy_Tier1 clone from the holder's chest to ChuteAttachment every REFUEL_FX.CellInterval (MotionMaster.SplineMove + shrink). The model does a squash-and-stretch about its bottom center: it stretches up, leans left, leans right, and settles. Each lean hinges on a bottom edge, so the base stays grounded. When the bounce blends out, every part is written back to its exact rest CFrame/Size from a snapshot, so drift cannot accumulate. Tuning is in TrainConfig.REFUEL_FX. The attribute never gates the refuel itself.

searchDocs.title: Fuel out​
searchDocs.content: Running out of fuel no longer ends the round. A stall lasts until fuel is added: the drain rate is 0, the brake cannot be toggled, and nothing is scheduled. While the train is stalled, the Threat Timer runs at ThreatConfig.STALLED_SPEED, so the Leviathan arrives sooner. Round endings now come from the train hull (see Train Shield — Hull).  Every commitEvent compares two flags against the last values it sent — empty (fuelAtLastEvent <= 0) and isStalled — and fires Signals.OnTrainFuelStateChanged(empty, stalled) when either flips. Fuel can only reach 0 at a commit (onEmpty, onStall, ApplyFuelDamage), so the edge is exact. An Emergency Generator coast is empty = true, stalled = false: the hull counts hits, but the threat timer does not speed up. ThreatTimerManager reads stalled; TrainShieldManager reads empty.  TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage(amount: number, source: any?): boolean is the combat fuel-damage sink. amount is fuel units already converted by TrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR — the only caller today is TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage, once the shield is at 0. It returns true when fuel absorbed the hit and false when fuel was already 0 (stalled or coasting), in which case the caller counts a hull hit. Before the round is live, during a jump, after game over, or for an amount that is not > 0 (or is NaN), it is a no-op that returns true. A hit that leaves fuel above 0 commits the lower level. A hit that drives fuel to 0 sets isStalled before commitEvent(0), so the train stalls at once — there is no Emergency Generator coast on this path, and the round does not end.  TrainFuelManager.AddFuel(amount: number) is the perk fuel source (Fuel Line, from JunkService on each Energy grab). It caps at max fuel, clears a stall or a coast like a refuel (any gain), and is a no-op after game over, on a full tank, or for an amount that is not a positive finite number.

searchDocs.title: Client HUD prediction​
searchDocs.content: TrainFuelGuiController reads the authored StarterGui.TrainFuelGui (never creates UI). It holds no snapshot of its own — every RenderStepped frame it asks TrainStateCache.PredictedFuel() for the extrapolated fuel level (fuel - rate * (now - serverTime), clamped to [0, maxFuel]) and smooths displayedFuel toward it with frame-rate-independent exponential smoothing (k = 8). The HUD is a plate in the same style as HealthStaminaGui: a train icon + FUEL label, a well of 10 cells (cell i fills clamp(pct * 10 - (i - 1), 0, 1), pct = fuel ÷ the snapshot's maxFuel) and a Value text. Cells are mint while running and amber while braked (isBraked). Coast and stall both happen at 0 fuel, so the well stroke and deco frames carry them: an Emergency Generator coast turns them orange and the value reads COAST 23s (counts down to coastEndsAt); a stall (isStalled) pulses them red/rust and the value reads STALLED. Phone-sized screens use a compact layout; the controller applies both layouts and the UIScale.  Before the server has sent a snapshot, PredictedFuel() returns nil — the controller never invents a starting value (it used to seed one from TrainConfig.INITIAL_FUEL/MAX_FUEL plus a client-read workspace:GetServerTimeNow(), which is what produced the reported 0% flash; see Join-Sync Snapshot Handshake). While nil, the HUD renders a placeholder ("—", muted label and value, empty cells) instead. The first non-nil value is applied directly rather than eased into, so there is no visible sweep from a guessed number.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Each TrainEngine-tagged and TrainBrakeLever-tagged root (a Model or BasePart) must contain a BasePart named TrainConfig.PROMPT_PART_NAME ("ProxPromptPart") with a child ProximityPrompt. Both client and server resolve the prompt part recursively via PromptResolver, so it may be nested at any depth. The prompt's MaxActivationDistance and the engine's ActionText are authored in Studio; only the lever's ActionText is set by script.  The engine model (PowerCore) also needs ModelStreamingMode = Atomic (Workspace streams, and the refuel animation snapshots every part on stream-in) and an Attachment named TrainConfig.CHUTE_ATTACHMENT_NAME ("ChuteAttachment") at any depth, where the Energy cells fly to. Without the attachment, refuel still works and the animation is skipped with a warning.  A brake lever model additionally needs, for the animation:  A PrimaryPart acting as the pivot, anchored, with all moving geometry WeldConstrainted (or Motor6Ded) to it. An assembly containing an anchored part is rigid, so writing PrimaryPart.CFrame carries the whole lever on every client with no physics ownership involved. Without a PrimaryPart the prompt still works and the animation is skipped with a warning.The lever saved in a known pose, with TrainConfig.BRAKE_LEVER_REST_IS_BRAKED set to say which state that pose represents. The current rig follows the usual convention — lever pulled toward the player means braked — and is authored that way, hence BRAKE_LEVER_REST_IS_BRAKED = true.Optionally an AnimationController/Animator for the button press. No Animator simply means no press flourish.  Do not leave a Script inside the model driving the lever itself — the pose is owned by TrainClient and a second writer will fight it.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: A stall never ends the round on its own There is no grace timer any more. A stalled train only speeds up the Threat Timer; the round ends through the hull in TrainShieldManager, whose TrainGameOver.Trigger is still a placeholder (log + Signals.OnTrainGameOver, no cutscene or round reset yet).  Algebraic drift note: commitEvent captures now() once and uses it for both lastEventTime and the serverTime field broadcast in TrainStateSync. Any task.wait or async work inserted between the snapshot and the broadcast would drift the client's extrapolation baseline — keep commitEvent synchronous.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Spare Tank (PartyPerkBuffs.MaxFuelBonus, 20): max fuel = MAX_FUEL + MaxFuelBonus. maxFuel() replaces every MAX_FUEL read in the manager and travels in TrainStateSync, so the HUD and music use the real cap. A change of the attribute commits (clamps fuel when the perk ends); it is skipped while stalled (fuel is 0, so there is nothing to re-clamp).Emergency Generator (permanent party perk, LastGaspSeconds 15/level): when drain empties the tank, onEmpty starts a coast instead of a stall: coastEndsAt = now + LastGaspSeconds, rate 0, fuel 0, and the train still counts as running (junk keeps moving). reschedule arms the coast end → onStall. Any fuel gain ends the coast (commitEvent clears coastEndsAt when fuel > 0 or stalled). Fuel damage to 0 skips the coast and stalls at once. A coast does not speed up the Threat Timer; the client shows a "running on fumes" toast. The coast clock does not pause for a jump.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Sv as TrainFuelManager participant Cl as TrainClient participant Cache as TrainStateCache participant Gui as TrainFuelGuiController Note over Sv,Cl: JOIN - via JoinSync on ClientReady, not PlayerAdded Sv->>Cl: TrainStateSync(fuel, rate, isBraked, isStalled, serverTime, maxFuel, coastEndsAt) Cl->>Cache: SetFuel(snapshot) Cl->>Cl: Signals.OnTrainStateChanged(snap) - MusicDirector, lever ActionText Note over Cl,Sv: BRAKE TOGGLE Cl->>Sv: ReqToggleBrake(lever) Sv->>Sv: validate lever tag + proximity, flip isBraked (first un-brake: hasStarted=true) Sv->>Sv: commitEvent() - snapshot fuel, switch rate, scheduleNonce++, reschedule() Sv-->>Cl: (success, isBraked, code) Sv->>Cl: TrainStateSync(...) Note over Cl,Sv: REFUEL Cl->>Sv: ReqRefuelTrain(engine) Sv->>Sv: validate proximity + not full, spend pool Energy (SpendUpTo) Sv->>Sv: commitEvent(newFuel) Sv-->>Cl: (success, fuelAdded, code) Note over Sv: NATURAL STALL Sv->>Sv: task.delay(timeToEmpty) fires -> onStall(): isStalled=true, commitEvent(0) Sv->>Sv: commitEvent fires OnTrainFuelStateChanged(empty, stalled) - ThreatTimerManager speeds up Note over Sv: COMBAT FUEL HIT Sv->>Sv: TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage while shield==0 -> ApplyFuelDamage(amount*FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR) Sv->>Sv: newFuel<=0: isStalled=true, commitEvent(0) - returns true (absorbed) Sv->>Sv: fuel already 0: returns false - TrainShieldManager counts a hull hit Note over Gui: CLIENT HUD LOOP (RenderStepped) Gui->>Cache: PredictedFuel() - nil until first snapshot -> render placeholder Gui->>Gui: predicted = snap.fuel - snap.rate*(now-snap.serverTime); smooth k=8 Gui->>Gui: cell fills + state colors (mint/amber, coast/stall stroke)

searchDocs.title: Bodies and looks​
searchDocs.content: A body (ServerStorage.EnemyAssets.<Id>, ModelStreamingMode = Atomic so a streaming client gets the root and the look together) is an invisible anchored HumanoidRootPart, a Humanoid (BreakJointsOnDeath and RequiresNeck off, display off) and 1–2 invisible hitboxes welded to the root (CanQuery on, so hitscan and AOE find them). VoidEnemyService.Spawn clones it, sets HP from config, tags it EnemyNPC, sets attribute Visual = <Id>, parents it to workspace.ActiveEnemies, and calls EnemyChrono.Track (player hitscan gets lag compensation).  A look (ReplicatedStorage.EnemyModels.<Id>) is the full part model. VoidEnemyController clones it for every body with a Visual attribute, eases it toward the body root (1 - exp(-LookEase·dt)) and poses it every frame within LookNear, every 3rd frame within LookFar, else every 10th. A missing look warns once per Id; the body still works.  Only the body root replicates its movement. The server sets it every Heartbeat along the current MoveTo; behaviors decide at 10 Hz.

searchDocs.title: Look rig format​
searchDocs.content: Editing a look in Studio needs no code as long as it keeps this format:  Root — invisible PrimaryPart at the model pivot; the name tag hangs on it.Joints/J_<name> — invisible pivot parts. Attributes: Parent (another joint's name, or empty = the root), Kind, and the numbers that kind reads.Every other part — attribute Joint = <name> follows that joint; no attribute = static.A Parent loop (A → B → A) warns once and hangs the joint where the loop closes off the root.  Each frame: pose(joint) = pose(parent) * restOffset(joint) * wiggle(Kind, t). Rest offsets come from the saved model, so moving, resizing, recoloring, adding or deleting parts and joints just works. A new ray is a copy of an old ray's joints and parts.  Kind	Motion	AttributesSpin	Turns around its Y axis	Rate (rad/s) Wave	Per axis A·sin(t·F + P)	AX FX PX, AY FY PY, AZ FZ PZ Sway	Eel body segment: side sway, turned along the body, vertical bob	K, D, Len, A0, A, F, Lag, Bob, BobF Snap	Jaw snap around X: A·max(0, sin(t·F))³	A, F  Parts the client reads by name: Void Cyst Core and Tip, Drifter Nozzle, Ogler Eye (with its PointLight) and Pupil, Sirenspine Tip1..Tip8. Keep these names.

searchDocs.title: The shield rule​
searchDocs.content: VoidEnemyService.Impact(origin, target, attack, attacker) is the only way an enemy deals damage:  jump: nothing (a glob still in the air when the jump starts) shield > 0: point = VoidEnemyMath.clipToShield(origin, target, front, rear, radius) or target TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(Damage, Source, { Position = point, Severity }) -- players and deck take nothing, even when the attack was aimed at a player shield == 0: TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(Damage, Source, nil, spareHull) -- fuel, then hull CombatService.ApplyAOE(target, Radius, PlayerDamage, "AOE", attacker, { attacker })   The shield shape is the upper half-capsule around the front and rear dome centers (VoidEnemyMath.shieldLine, same shape RockService uses). Curved paths (bile arc, a diving Shatterbeak) test each short step. EndPoint(origin, target) gives the same point without damage, so rushes and dives aim at the shield surface. The client clips its visuals with the same math while TrainStateCache.ShieldFraction() > 0.  Every shield hit shows the forcefield for a random 0.5–1.25 s — see Train Shield — Dome.

It removes itself (no kill credit)	One Impact at the end of the rush Drifter	1–2, beside the train	Flies in (3 s), hovers bobbing, lobs bile every LobEvery from the stinger at a player on the train (PlayerAimChance) or a deck point	Lob visual at once; the hit lands LobTime later through After, even if the Drifter died Shatterbeak	flock of 3–5, 40 studs above the nose line	Wanders; the next free bird dives every DiveEvery (a busy bird gives its turn to the next): wind-up (DiveWindup), dive, hit (Ram), bounce, rejoin	One Impact when the dive meets the shield, reaches the target or its height (it never goes into the deck), or times out Ogler	1, at a post above the train	Flies in, stares. One sweep spends at most one hull hit (spareHull after the first), like one eruption Sirenspine	1 + escort (2 Drifters, 4 Shatterbeaks)	Holds a post ahead of and above the nose; pulses every PulseEvery (Pulse)	No attack. Buff (below)  All cooldowns divide by the enemy's AttackRateMult attribute (VoidEnemyService.Rate); for the Ogler, the charge and the cooldown (the beam time stays the same).  PickTarget aims only at players who stand on the train (OnDeck: over the TrainPlatforms box, at most 15 studs above it), never at a player who fell off.

searchDocs.title: Sirenspine buff​
searchDocs.content: Each pulse sets DamageTakenMult, AttackRateMult and Buffed on every other void enemy within BuffRadius, and clears them on enemies that left the radius. When the Sirenspine dies or is removed, OnGone clears all three at once. CombatService.ApplyToModel multiplies NPC damage by DamageTakenMult (see Enemy Combat). The client draws a gold highlight and three tethers to the nearest Sirenspine's closest pipe tips while Buffed is set.

searchDocs.title: Spawning​
searchDocs.content: The Void channel in Events Orchestrator rolls every 600 odometer studs (~21 s at cruise). VoidSwarmEvent.CanTrigger blocks every roll until the crew has finished any weapon research (a RangedWeapon or TrainWeapon node at level 1 or more) or the train has made its first jump to a new biome (VoidSwarmEvent.unlocked). After that it blocks rolls during a jump and passes with the current biome's Chance. Both conditions are for this run only (research is session-only). Start picks a pack by the biome's Weights, spawns it into an EnemyWave, and finishes when the wave clears, on a jump, or after MaxActiveSeconds. The wave is on the event's Janitor, so every end path despawns survivors. searchDocs.content: Layer	File	RoleClient	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TrainShieldController.client.luau	Energy-recharge prompt registration, ReqRechargeShield calls; on TrainShieldSync writes TrainStateCache then fires Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TrainShieldGuiController.client.luau	Every copy of the shield readout — the diegetic SurfaceGui per TrainShieldMonitor-tagged part and the full-screen zoom ScreenGui — plus the zoom prompt. Renders a placeholder until the first snapshot arrives Client	src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TrainShieldDomeController.client.luau	Sole owner of the whole shield look (front dome, tube, rear dome) and every shield-hit effect: hit burst + flash on TrainShieldHit, random reveals, break / reboot flicker — see Dome Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ShieldDomeMath.luau	Pure dome math: key sampling, reveal / flash envelopes, beam transparency and particle size scaling, severity mapping Shared	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/TrainStateCache.luau	Client-side cache of the last authoritative shield (and fuel) snapshot; the sole source the monitor reads from — see Join-Sync Snapshot Handshake Server	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainShieldManager.luau	Authoritative shield state, recharge handler, damage sink (ApplyDamage), buff-driven max recompute Server	src/ServerScriptService/TrainShieldSystemLoader.server.luau	Bootstrap — calls TrainShieldManager.Initialize() once per server Shared	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/MaterialPool.luau	Energy points, spent via SpendUpTo (shared with Train Fuel) Shared	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ProximityValidation.luau	Console/engine proximity checks, shared with Train Fuel Shared	src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainGameOver.luau	Idempotent game-over gate, shared with Train Fuel Config	src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/TrainConfig.luau	Shield knobs alongside the fuel knobs  Packets: TrainShieldSync, ReqRechargeShield, TrainShieldHit — see Networking MapSignals: OnTrainShieldChanged — fired by TrainShieldController, consumed by TrainShieldGuiController to refresh the capacity readout and by TrainShieldDomeController for the break / reboot edges — see Signals MapJoin-time delivery: via JoinSync on ClientReady, not Players.PlayerAdded — see Join-Sync Snapshot Handshake

searchDocs.title: Recharge​
searchDocs.content: Triggering a ShieldConsole-tagged prompt sends ReqRechargeShield(console). The server validates the tag and proximity, and spends pool Energy via MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", maxShield − currentShield, SHIELD_PER_POINT) (only the points needed, never over-filled). An isRecharging boolean mutex serializes concurrent requests — like the fuel system's isRefueling, it is not a queue: a second request in flight returns SHIELD_FULL or NO_ENERGY rather than a queued success. On success the client plays SoundManager.PlaySFX("ShieldRecharge").

searchDocs.title: Damage / fuel bleed-through​
searchDocs.content: TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(amount, source?, hit?, spareHull?) → boolean is the single damage entry point for the train — all incoming attack/hazard damage, whether it lands on the shield or bleeds through to fuel, routes through this call. Rock Hazards is the first caller: an unshot rock calls ApplyDamage(damage, "Rock", { Position, Severity }) when it reaches the shield dome, or the nose when the shield is 0. It returns true when the hit landed on the hull. spareHull = true drops a hit that would land on the hull; eruptions use it so one eruption spends at most one hull hit. Guards (all must pass or the call is a no-op): hasStarted must be true, TrainGameOver.HasFired() must be false, amount must be > 0 and not NaN.  Shield > 0 (absorbs): currentShield = max(0, currentShield - amount); broadcast() -- a hit that drives it exactly to 0 discards its excess; this does NOT end the round Shield == 0, fuel > 0: TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage(amount * TrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR, source) -- a hit that zeroes fuel stalls the train; it does NOT end the round Shield == 0, fuel == 0: ApplyFuelDamage returns false -> hull hit (see Hull)   hit = { Position: Vector3, Severity: number } is optional and only drives visuals: when the shield absorbs the hit, the server fires TrainShieldHit so every client draws it on the dome — see Dome. A malformed hit (not a table, a missing or non-finite Position, a non-number or NaN Severity — see ShieldDomeMath.validHit) is dropped silently; the damage still applies. The packet goes out after the snapshot and Shield Nova, so a bad hit can never block them.  This replaced the old behavior where the shield reaching 0 called TrainGameOver.Trigger directly — shield depletion by itself no longer ends the round, it just removes the train's damage buffer. TrainConfig.CORE_TAG ("TrainCore") marks the train's structural model; Shield Nova centers its burst on it (falling back to the engine).

searchDocs.title: Hull​
searchDocs.content: With the shield at 0 and fuel at 0, the train has a hull of ThreatConfig.HULL_HITS (3) hits. ApplyDamage learns that fuel is empty when TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage returns false, and then calls hitHull(source):  A hit whose source is ThreatConfig.BOSS_DAMAGE_SOURCE ("Leviathan") ends the round at once: TrainGameOver.Trigger(LEVIATHAN_STRIKE).Any other hit adds 1 to hullHits. The HULL_HITS-th hit ends the round: TrainGameOver.Trigger(HULL_BREACHED).  The round can also end with ALL_DOWN (5): every player down and the revive countdown over. ReviveService triggers it, not the hull (see Paid Revive).  An Emergency Generator coast counts as empty fuel, so hull hits count during a coast too (the train keeps coasting; a hit does not stall it).  Restore. The hull returns to full only after the train is safe — shield above 0 or fuel above 0 — for ThreatConfig.HULL_RESTORE_DELAY (60 s) without a break. updateHull() runs from broadcast() (every shield change) and from Signals.OnTrainFuelStateChanged (every fuel-empty edge), and acts only on the safe/unsafe edge: the safe edge starts the delay, the unsafe edge cancels it with a nonce. Topping up while safe never restarts the delay. This stops players from resetting the hull by feeding 1 Energy and letting it drop back to 0.  Rocks and void enemies reach the hull once shield and fuel are both 0; the Leviathan boss is separate future work; see Threat Timer.

searchDocs.title: Max formula (buffs)​
searchDocs.content: maxShield = (BASE_SHIELD + ResearchBuffs.MaxHP) * (1 + PartyPerkBuffs.TrainShieldBonus)   Research Bench additive: each completed Train Shield node accumulates onto ResearchBuffs.MaxHP — Shield_Alpha +50, Shield_Beta +100, Shield_Gamma +150, Shield_Delta +200 (each MaxLevel = 1, up to +500 total) — added before the perk multiplier. See Research Bench.Party perk multiplicative: TrainShieldBonus = 0.05 * maxLevel across all players (server-max resolution), applied on top of the base + Research sum.Ratio-preserving recompute: when either buff changes, recomputeMax preserves the current fill ratio (currentShield / oldMax) and rounds to the nearest integer — a player at 60% shield stays at ~60% after an upgrade.  subscribeBuffs attaches GetAttributeChangedSignal listeners to both buff folders via WaitForChild, then calls recomputeMax once after attach to catch any missed signals during the wait. See Research Bench and Perks for the upstream buff systems.

searchDocs.title: Dome​
searchDocs.content: The force field wraps the whole train in three parts, and TrainShieldDomeController is the only owner of all of them. Damage sources never draw shield effects; they pass a hit to ApplyDamage.  Part	What it isFront dome	A client clone of ReplicatedStorage.ShieldDome (the dome template, authored at the front-dome spot): a half sphere of 8 Beams on an invisible DomeAnchor, with a Radius attribute. Also the rock collision sphere — see Rock Hazards — The dome. Tube	Client clones of ReplicatedStorage.ShieldTubeSegment (one segment = 2 half-arch beams) from the front dome center to the rear dome center. ShieldDomeMath.tubeLayout picks N = max(1, round(L / SHIELD_TUBE_SEGMENT)) segments, each exactly L / N wide, so there are no gaps. With no length (L ≤ 0) there is no tube and no rear dome. Rear dome	A second client clone of the ShieldDome template, turned 180°, centered SHIELD_REAR_INSET (3.8 studs) inside the rear end. No collision.  Length. PlatformExtendService writes TrainPlatforms.RearX (the largest X of the built platforms; the train faces −X) at boot and after every build. On each change the controller destroys the old tube and rear dome (one Janitor) and lays them out again, then gives the new beams the current visibility at once. Clients never measure platforms, because Workspace streams. Until RearX arrives only the front dome exists. The tube and rear dome live in a client-created Workspace.ShieldVisuals folder.  Hit path. ApplyDamage(amount, source, { Position, Severity }) → if the shield absorbs it, the server fires TrainShieldHit(position, severity) → every client plays a burst of ShieldHitVFX at the position, flashes the whole shield and plays ShieldHit. The hit that breaks the shield is sent at severity 1.  Severity contract. Severity is 0–1, set by each damage source in its own config, and never derived from damage — so rebalancing damage never changes visuals. Rocks map their size multiplier onto RockConfig.SHIELD_HIT_SEVERITY (0.3–0.6). The Leviathan passes 1. A new source picks its own value. Severity scales the particle size (SHIELD_HIT_SIZE_SCALE), the particle count (SHIELD_HIT_COUNT_SCALE × the emitter's EmitCount attribute), the SFX volume (SHIELD_HIT_VOLUME_SCALE) and the flash peak (SHIELD_FLASH_LEVEL).  Visibility. One value v (0–1) per frame scales the authored transparency of every shield beam — front dome, tube and rear dome alike: t' = 1 − (1 − t)·v. v = 1 is the authored look; the beams switch off below 0.01.  State	vDefault	0 (hidden) Hit flash	lerp(SHIELD_FLASH_LEVEL, severity), held for a random SHIELD_HIT_HOLD (0.5–1.25 s, picked per hit), then linear to 0 over SHIELD_HIT_FADE (0.25 s). Every shield hit uses it: rocks and void enemies Random reveal	every 60–120 s: fade in to 0.7–0.9 over 1 s, hold 10 s, fade out — client-local, never while the shield is 0 Break (shield → 0)	SHIELD_BREAK_KEYS: flash full, flicker 3–4 times, dark; ShieldBreak SFX Reboot (0 → above 0)	SHIELD_REBOOT_KEYS: flicker in to 0.9, hold ~1.5 s, fade; ShieldReboot SFX Shield 0	0  Flash and reveal combine by max. A break or reboot sequence overrides both while it runs; a hit during one still plays its burst. The first snapshot after joining is neither a break nor a reboot.  The dome must never block rays or projectiles The grabhook, hitscan rays and projectiles pass through the shield because it is only Beams on parts with CanCollide, CanQuery and CanTouch all off — DomeAnchor, the ShieldTubeSegment emitters and ShieldHitVFX. Any part added to the dome, the tube template or ShieldHitVFX later must keep all three off. Rock collision is sphere math on the server, not parts, so it does not depend on them.

searchDocs.title: Shield monitor​
searchDocs.content: The shield HUD is diegetic first: TrainShieldGuiController clones the ReplicatedStorage.GuiAssets.TrainShieldGui SurfaceGui template onto every BasePart tagged TrainConfig.SHIELD_MONITOR_TAG ("TrainShieldMonitor"), discovered via CollectionService:GetTagged plus live add/remove signals. The clone is created client-side, so each player drives their own independent copy on the same shared surface — no server/replication involvement in the GUI itself. Each registered monitor owns a Janitor that destroys the clone when the tag is removed.  A second ProximityPrompt on the console opens PlayerGui.TrainShieldGui, a full-screen copy of the same layout, for players who want to read the console without standing at the right angle to the glass. Both assets share one element tree under MainContainer (Header, Hero, Gauge, Stats, Warning), so one resolveView and one render path serve both — see The zoom view below.  Readouts​  All five readouts are wired to real sources today. SHIELD HEALTH and CAPACITY also drive real gameplay math (current/max shield). STRENGTH, EFFICIENCY, and AUTO-REGEN read the Shield_Efficiency/Shield_EfficiencyPlus/Shield_Delta buff keys and display them accurately — but nothing in the codebase changes damage or refuel math based on those three yet, so researching them changes the readout, not the shield's actual behavior. See Research Bench — Honest status of Effects.  Readout	Source	BehaviourShield % / 10-cell bar / ONLINE-CRITICAL / SHIELD HEALTH	TrainStateCache.ShieldFraction()	Eased per frame, then banded (below) CAPACITY	TrainStateCache.ShieldMax() ÷ BASE_SHIELD	100% at stock; rises as ResearchBuffs.MaxHP and the party perk raise max STRENGTH	ResearchBuffs[SHIELD_STRENGTH_BUFF_KEY]	B → A → S per ShieldStrengthRatings; B when unset EFFICIENCY	ResearchBuffs[SHIELD_EFFICIENCY_BUFF_KEY]	Percentage added to an Energy insert; 0% when unset AUTO-REGEN	ResearchBuffs[SHIELD_AUTOREGEN_BUFF_KEY]	FUNCTIONAL (mint) once > 0, else BROKEN (rust)  The shield fraction is bucketed into one of TrainConfig.ShieldBands, healthiest first:  Band	Shield	Text (Color)	Readout	Fill (Tint)	GlossHEALTHY	above 60%	#94d2bd	#0a9396	#0a9396	#94d2bd WARNING	30–60%	#ee9b00	#ee9b00	#ee9b00	#e9d8a6 DANGER	30% or below	#bb3e03	#bb3e03	#ae2012	#ca6702  Each band carries four colours. Color paints the SHIELD HEALTH text and the lit zone label under the bar. Readout paints the big number, the %, and the status pill's text and stroke. Tint paints the white Shield icon (through ImageColor3), the lit bar cells and the lit zone rail. Gloss is the thin highlight line on each lit cell. Text red is rust and fill red is red (the Ocean Sunset role map), so DANGER text stays readable on the dark screen; a healthy shield reads teal on the icon and mint on SHIELD HEALTH, which is deliberate. DANGER is also where the Shield ImageLabel swaps to its cracked asset and the status flips to CRITICAL.  The bar has 10 cells of 10% each. Cell i fills clamp(fraction × 10 − (i − 1), 0, 1) of its width (Fill frame Size X), so 45% reads as four full cells and a half one; a cell under 35% full hides its Gloss line. Under the bar, a three-part rail (RailDanger/RailWarning/RailHealthy, grow ratios 3/3/4 so they line up with cells 1–3, 4–6, 7–10) and its labels light the current band and leave the others in the line colour. Moving up a band costs an extra SHIELD_BAND_HYSTERESIS (0.03), so a value resting on a boundary can't strobe between two colours every frame.  The percentage is always out of the current max, so a capacity upgrade raises what 100% is worth without the number ever reading above 100 — SHIELD CAPACITY is where a 2000-point shield shows up as 200%, not the shield readout.  What updates when​  Only the eased shield number needs RenderStepped; one global loop drives every view. The other four stats change rarely, so they run event-driven off Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged (capacity moves only when the server recomputes max, which is the same event that carries a snapshot) and ResearchBuffs.AttributeChanged. ResearchBuffs is a plain attribute folder in ReplicatedStorage, so the Tech Tree's totals replicate to the client for free — no packet, no server change. The controller waits up to 30s for the folder, since a server script creates it, then reconciles once after attaching.  TrainStateCache.ShieldFraction() returns nil until the server has actually sent a snapshot. The monitor does not invent a starting value — it used to seed displayedShieldPct = 1, asserting "Online 100%" before the server had spoken at all; see Join-Sync Snapshot Handshake. While nil it renders a placeholder ("—", neutral grey, % hidden, every cell dark, status NO SIGNAL) and snaps directly to the first real value with no eased sweep.  TrainShieldController writes TrainStateCache before firing Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged, so the monitor sees the same snapshot whether it reads the cache at init or the signal fires while it's already running.  The zoom view​  StarterGui.TrainShieldGui is a ScreenGui with ResetOnSpawn = false, so the PlayerGui copy survives respawns and is resolved exactly once at startup. The controller forces Enabled = false at init regardless of how the asset was saved.  It holds a full-screen Dim frame and the same 1554×1000 MainContainer as the monitor, fitted to the screen by MainContainer.UIScale (min(W × 0.94 / 1554, H × 0.92 / 1000), recomputed on AbsoluteSize change); it is not tagged ResponsiveScale. The TrainConfig.SHIELD_ZOOM_PROMPT_PART_NAME prompt on each ShieldConsole opens it; its MainContainer.Header.CloseButton (zoom copy only) closes it. While the panel is up every zoom prompt is disabled, so the Close button is the only exit and a held key can't retrigger the prompt sitting underneath the panel. The render loop skips the zoom view entirely while it is hidden, and stats are re-applied on open so a panel opened after a buff change is never stale.  Opening fires Signals.RequestMouseIcon(true) on PC (UserInputService.MouseEnabled and KeyboardEnabled), which is what makes the Close button clickable — the third-person camera otherwise holds MouseBehavior = LockCenter with the icon hidden. CameraController is the sole owner of those properties; this controller never writes them directly, so shift-lock and aim mode stay the single arbiter and aim mode still outranks the request. See Camera — Modes and the Signals Map.  The panel is modal, so setHudHidden clears the rest of the HUD under it. That takes three switches, because no single one covers everything:  Switch	HidesStarterGui:SetCore("TopbarEnabled", false)	Roblox's topbar and every CoreGui it owns — chat, leaderboard, menu button Satchel:SetBackpackEnabled(false)	The hotbar and inventory TopbarPlus.setTopbarEnabled(false)	Satchel's inventory icon  The middle one is the easy mistake: SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.Backpack, false) does nothing here, because Satchel already called it at boot and draws its own hotbar. Satchel re-applies its own flag every Heartbeat, so the hotbar cannot flip back on while the panel is up. Disabling it also unbinds the number-key hotbar actions, so tools can't be swapped through the panel. The third is needed because TopbarPlus icons live in developer ScreenGuis that TopbarEnabled never reaches.  Satchel and TopbarPlus are required inside the zoom setup task after the Close button is wired, not at the top of the file — requiring Satchel boots the entire backpack UI and can yield, and neither the diegetic monitor nor the panel's exit should wait on that. SetCore is pcall'd because it errors if the CoreGui has not registered the callback yet.  One caveat from the engine: with TopbarEnabled false, the strip the topbar occupied still captures mouse events, so a button placed in the top 36 px of the panel will not respond to clicks. Keep interactive elements clear of it.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Each ShieldConsole-tagged root (Model or BasePart) carries two prompt parts, each a BasePart with a child ProximityPrompt, resolved recursively via PromptResolver:  Config field	Part name	Prompt doesSHIELD_PROMPT_PART_NAME	InsertFuelPromptPart	Spend pool Energy to recharge (TrainShieldController → ReqRechargeShield) SHIELD_ZOOM_PROMPT_PART_NAME	OpenMonitorGuiPart	Open the full-screen readout (TrainShieldGuiController)  Give the two prompts distinct ActionText — both shipped as Interact / Shield Generator, which is indistinguishable in game. Multiple consoles are supported, each registered independently.  Tag every BasePart that should display a monitor with TrainConfig.SHIELD_MONITOR_TAG. Element names in both assets — ReplicatedStorage.GuiAssets.TrainShieldGui (the SurfaceGui template) and StarterGui.TrainShieldGui (the zoom ScreenGui) — are load-bearing and must match each other: TrainShieldGuiController resolves one shared path set with WaitForChild and will hang on startup if either asset renames or re-nests anything under MainContainer. The only differences between the two trees are the zoom copy's Header.CloseButton, UIScale, UICorner + UIStroke and sibling Dim frame. Tag the train's structural model with TrainConfig.CORE_TAG ("TrainCore") — Shield Nova's burst center; until it exists the TrainEngine model is used.  Never tag a MeshPart as the monitor. A SurfaceGui adorns its part's bounding box face, not the mesh geometry, and its orientation is the part's CFrame — so a screen that is inset, curved, or tilted inside its bounding box will have the GUI floating in front of it at the wrong angle, with no way to correct it short of rotating the visible mesh. Instead add an invisible flat Part (Transparency = 1, CanCollide/CanQuery/CanTouch off, ~0.05 thick) aligned to the real glass plane and nudged ~0.02 studs out to avoid z-fighting, then tag that. Workspace.Monitor is the reference case: Monitor_Screen's glass is a flat slab leaning back ~31.6°, so the tag lives on a sibling ScreenSurface part instead — 7.5877 × 4.8854 studs, aspect ~1.553 (SizingMode = FixedSize, CanvasSize 1554 × 1000), sat exactly 0.02 studs proud of the glass along its own normal to avoid z-fighting.  That height is not the glass's bounding-box height. The glass leans back ~31.6°, so its extent along its own plane is 4.1067 / cos(31.6°) ≈ 4.82 studs — a surface matched to the bounding box would cover only 85% of the visible glass. The current size covers the full slab. Note it deliberately covers more than the unoccluded aperture: raycasting a grid at the glass with every opaque part of the model as a target shows the bezel opening is rounded, not rectangular, so the extreme corners of this rectangle sit over the CRT bulge. Keep GUI content inside the middle ~90% rather than shrinking the surface — a strictly inscribed rectangle covers only 44% of the glass and reads as far too small.  The layout is authored in fixed pixels on the 1554 × 1000 canvas. If the surface ratio changes, change CanvasSize to match (and ZOOM_CANVAS in the controller), or the canvas stretches to the new ratio.  The shield needs ReplicatedStorage.ShieldDome (the dome template at the front-dome spot; PrimaryPart = DomeAnchor, Radius attribute, beams Enabled = false), ReplicatedStorage.ShieldTubeSegment (a Model of 2 half-arch BeamEmitter parts whose pivot lies on the dome's axis; beam width runs along the train) and ReplicatedStorage.ShieldHitVFX (a Part with ParticleEmitters; an EmitCount attribute sets the base burst size). Leave the beams' authored look at full strength — the controller only ever fades it down. Sound ids for ShieldHit, ShieldBreak, ShieldReboot live in SoundConfig.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: TextSize stops at 100 Roblox caps TextSize (and TextScaled) at 100. The big shield number is 220 px on the canvas, so Hero.Readout.ShieldValue is authored at TextSize 100 with a child UIScale of 2.2. The layout reads the scaled AbsoluteSize, so the % beside it still lines up. Any later label above 100 px needs the same trick. All labels use a fixed TextSize on the fixed canvas (no TextScaled): Unica One for display text, Montserrat SemiBold for labels, Roboto Mono Bold for numbers. Do not reach for AlwaysOnTop to sharpen text: it renders over 3D geometry, so the GUI would draw straight through the monitor bezel.  LightInfluence must stay at 0 The monitor has to stay readable across every biome, including night and interior ones. SurfaceGui.LightInfluence is 0 on the template, meaning environmental lighting has no effect and the CRT renders its authored colours everywhere. Any value above 0 tints the screen toward ambient and makes it dim exactly where visibility matters most. Brightness (emissive scaling, only active while LightInfluence is 0) is left at 1; raising it washes out the dark panel colours. This applies only to the SurfaceGui — the zoom ScreenGui is drawn in screen space and is unaffected by world lighting either way.  The template's Adornee is cleared on every clone A SurfaceGui with a non-nil Adornee renders on that instance and ignores its parent, so an Adornee saved into GuiAssets.TrainShieldGui propagates to every clone and the monitor renders nowhere — silently, with no error. This bit the project once already, when the template kept a reference to the deleted placeholder generator. TrainShieldGuiController now sets gui.Adornee = nil after cloning, so the asset can be re-authored on any part without breaking the monitor.  Two upgrade stats are displayed but not yet enforced STRENGTH and EFFICIENCY render from ResearchBuffs attributes the Tech Tree writes, but the server does not read them: ApplyDamage applies full damage and handleRecharge adds a flat SHIELD_PER_POINT per point. AUTO-REGEN is enforced: see Passive regen and perks. Wiring one up is therefore two edits, and both are required or the monitor will advertise a buff the server never applies: A ResearchConfig node with Effect = { Type = "StatBuff", Key = <the matching TrainConfig key>, PerLevel = … } — ResearchEffectsDispatcher accumulates any StatBuff key, so no dispatcher change is needed. This alone moves the readout.The corresponding read in TrainShieldManager — scale the hit in ApplyDamage, scale value in handleRecharge, or implement the regen loop. The controller and TrainConfig need no change either way; that is the point of routing the display through named buff keys instead of hardcoding the stock strings.  Recharge mutex is not a queue isRecharging is a boolean, not a queue. A second recharge request while one is in-flight returns SHIELD_FULL or NO_ENERGY — not a queued success. The player can try again immediately after.  Pre-game freeze hasStarted is false until Signals.SetTrainStarted fires (the first brake release on the fuel side). ApplyDamage is a no-op until then.

searchDocs.title: Passive regen and perks​
searchDocs.content: Passive regen (research Shield δ, ResearchBuffs.ShieldAutoRegen > 0): every SHIELD_AUTOREGEN_INTERVAL (10 s) a loop in TrainShieldManager adds max × SHIELD_AUTOREGEN_PCT (0.5%, at least 1) while the round is live, the game is not over and the shield is below max. A broken (0) shield regens too.Shield Capacitor (party shop perk, ShieldRegenBonus 1): the regen is × (1 + ShieldRegenBonus). It does nothing without the research.Shield Nova (permanent party perk, ShieldNovaDamage 40/level): the ApplyDamage hit that takes the shield to 0 calls tryNova. If the 180 s cooldown (SHIELD_NOVA_COOLDOWN) is ready, it deals CombatService.ApplyAOE damage in SHIELD_NOVA_RADIUS (30) around the first TrainCore-tagged instance (else the TrainEngine model), pushes enemies away with one server impulse (SHIELD_NOVA_KNOCKBACK), and fires ExplosionAt(center, radius, "ShieldNova"). Every player character is in the ignore list, because an AOE with no attacker would hit players. A rock that empties the shield triggers it.  Shield depletion is no longer a game over The shield can sit at 0 indefinitely, and so can fuel (a stall only speeds up the Threat Timer). Only the hull ends the round.  typeof guard on OnServerInvoke ReqRechargeShield.OnServerInvoke receives (player, console) where console is client-supplied. A typeof(console) == "Instance" guard runs before acquiring the isRecharging lock, so a malformed invocation (nil or non-Instance) is rejected cleanly without erroring.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Hardened Shield (PartyPerkBuffs.ShieldDamageReduction): ApplyDamage reduces hits the shield absorbs; the fuel bleed after the shield is down is unchanged.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Sv as TrainShieldManager participant Cl as TrainShieldController participant Cache as TrainStateCache participant Gui as TrainShieldGuiController Note over Sv,Cl: JOIN - via JoinSync on ClientReady, not PlayerAdded Sv->>Cl: TrainShieldSync(currentShield, maxShield) Cl->>Cache: SetShield(current, max) Cl->>Cl: Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged(current, max) Gui->>Cache: ShieldFraction() every RenderStepped; ShieldMax() on the signal Note over Cl,Sv: RECHARGE Cl->>Sv: ReqRechargeShield(console) Sv->>Sv: isRecharging mutex, validate tag + proximity Sv->>Sv: MaterialPool.SpendUpTo("Energy", missing, SHIELD_PER_POINT) Sv-->>Cl: (success, shieldAdded, code) Sv->>Cl: TrainShieldSync(...) Note over Sv: DAMAGE (rocks today; enemies / Leviathan later) Sv->>Sv: ApplyDamage(amount, source, hit?) - guard hasStarted, not HasFired, amount>0 alt currentShield > 0 Sv->>Sv: currentShield = max(0, currentShield - amount) Sv->>Cl: TrainShieldHit(position, severity x 255) - only if hit is valid Sv->>Sv: broadcast() else currentShield == 0 Sv->>Sv: TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage(amount * FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR, source) end Note over Sv: BUFF CHANGE Sv->>Sv: ResearchBuffs.MaxHP or PartyPerkBuffs.TrainShieldBonus changes Sv->>Sv: recomputeMax() - ratio-preserving rescale, broadcast() Note over Gui: SHIELD READOUT (RenderStepped, every view) Gui->>Cache: ShieldFraction() - nil until first snapshot -> placeholder Gui->>Gui: displayedShieldPct eased; pickBand() -> colour, HEALTHY/WARNING/DANGER, image swap Note over Gui: UPGRADE STATS (event driven, not per frame) Gui->>Cache: ShieldMax() / BASE_SHIELD -> SHIELD CAPACITY Gui->>Gui: ResearchBuffs.AttributeChanged -> strength / efficiency / auto-regen

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: TrainConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/TrainConfig.luau (shield fields below; for fuel knobs see Train Fuel)Perks: TrainShieldBonus (max shield ×(1+b)), ShieldPerEnergyBonus (recharge shield per Energy point = SHIELD_PER_POINT ×(1+b)). Both are Party keys read through PerkBuffRead.Party. See Perks. searchDocs.title: Client: controller and handlers​
searchDocs.content: WeaponController.client.luau is the bootstrap that watches the local character for Tool equip/unequip events. It looks up WeaponConfig[tool.Name].Category and dispatches to the matching category handler (GunHandler or ThrowableHandler). It creates one Janitor per equipped Tool (and one per character) so all connections clean up correctly on unequip, death, or weapon switch. It fires Signals.WeaponEquipped/Signals.WeaponUnequipped for the HUD, and Signals.RequestShootingCamera on equip/unequip to toggle the aim camera mode. It binds R to OnReload and G to OnDetonate for handlers that declare those callbacks.  GunHandler — hitscan + rocket cosmetic + ammo prediction. On activate, it gates on a client-local fire-rate check and predicted magazine count (via AmmoApi), then fires ReqFireWeapon(origin, dir, renderTime). It draws the shooter's own tracer (hitscan only; rocket has no local projectile) and supports semi and automatic fire. OnReload fires ReqReloadWeapon and predicts the ammo transition after the server-confirmed reload window. Authoritative ammo is reconciled via WeaponMagSync → Signals.WeaponMagChanged and AmmoPoolSync → Signals.AmmoPoolChanged.  ThrowableHandler — grenade and C4. On activate, it gates on the throw cooldown, plays throw sound, and fires ReqThrowProjectile(origin, dir). There is no local projectile cosmetic — the server-spawned instance replicates to all clients. For C4 (Detonation == "Manual"), OnDetonate fires ReqDetonate. Grenade ignores G.  TrajectoryPreview — a client-local green-neon ballistic arc shown while any throwable is equipped, using a fixed pool of reused BasePart segments updated every RenderStepped. Origin offset (SPAWN_OFFSET = 2.5) and upward aim bias match ServerProjectile/ThrowableHandler exactly so the preview arc matches the real projectile path. Purely cosmetic — no packets sent.  WeaponEffectsController — consumes replicated combat FX packets. WeaponFired is ignored for the local shooter (who already drew its own tracer) and renders tracer + impact spark for other players' shots. ExplosionAt renders an expanding neon sphere + sound for rocket, grenade, and C4 detonations, for everyone including the shooter.

searchDocs.title: Shared validation (WeaponValidation)​
searchDocs.content: Pure math run on both client (prediction) and server (authority):  canFire(lastFireTime, cooldown, now) — fire-rate gate.resolveHumanoidModel(part) — resolves a hit part to its Humanoid-bearing Model.applySpread(direction, spreadDegrees) — applies a random spread cone to an aim direction (cosmetic on client; server does its own authoritative ray).isWithinRange(origin, hitPos, maxDistance) — range cap check.ammoAfterShot(mag) / ammoReloadFromPool(mag, pool, magazineSize) — pure ammo transitions. ammoReloadFromPool returns (newMag, taken) where taken is the pool amount consumed.aoeFalloff(center, hitPos, radius, maxDamage) — linear AOE falloff.queryAOEModels(center, radius, ignore) — sphere overlap returning { model, humanoid, distance } for AOE application.

searchDocs.title: Server: packet handling​
searchDocs.content: WeaponServer.server.luau receives all weapon packets and runs per-category validation (fire-rate, ammo, origin tolerance, direction validity) before any damage or projectile spawn. It manages gun ammo initialisation on equip via WeaponState.EnsureAmmo + WeaponMagSync. On reload, it waits ReloadTime, calls ammoReloadFromPool, consumes the drawn ammo from AmmoManager, then fires WeaponMagSync + AmmoPoolSync (the latter emitted by AmmoManager.ConsumeAmmo). On a successful throwable throw, the server destroys the player's matching Tool (onThrowProjectile — 1 Tool = 1 throw). It drives the FastCast2 rocket caster (rocketServerCaster) — its LengthChanged callback steps the cosmetic part, its Hit callback calls CombatService.ApplyAOE and broadcasts ExplosionAt. It also handles throwable throw (onThrowProjectile) and detonate (onDetonate).

searchDocs.title: Lag compensation​
searchDocs.content: Hitscan hits on NPCs are rewound to what the shooter saw. The client sends Chrono.EnemyRenderTime() with ReqFireWeapon; the server clamps it with LagCompensation.ResolveRewindTime (in the past, at most min(1, ping×2 + 0.6) s; bad values → no rewind, the request is never dropped) and runs LagCompensation.Raycast. Each live NPC's snapshot at that time gives delta = current * past:Inverse(); the ray is shifted by delta and tested against that NPC alone, while world geometry and dead NPCs are tested unrewound. The shooter's own position is never rewound. Rockets and throwables have travel time and are not compensated. See Chrono Replication.

searchDocs.title: Server: damage routing (CombatService)​
searchDocs.content: CombatService is the single damage router with two primary entry points:  ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, amount, attackType, attacker, aoeVariant?) — applies damage to a resolved Model. Players route through HealthManager.ApplyDamage (keeping the HUD-tracked record correct — see Health); faction-tagged NPCs ("EnemyNPC"/"FriendlyNPC") take direct humanoid:TakeDamage. Anything without a recognized faction is ignored. Friendly-fire is enforced via Factions.canDamage: only Player↔Enemy damage lands; players never hurt players or friendly NPCs. A nil attacker is treated as environmental and bypasses the faction gate. Self-damage from one's own AOE is exempt.ApplyAOE(center, radius, maxDamage, attackType, attacker, ignore) — calls queryAOEModels, applies aoeFalloff to each target, and routes through ApplyToModel with aoeVariant = "Explosion".  Also available: ApplyToPart(part, amount, attackType, attacker, aoeVariant?) — resolves a hit part to its Humanoid-bearing Model then calls ApplyToModel. EnemyWeapon calls the same entry points for enemy fire — see Enemy Combat.  ApplyToModel and ApplyToPart return (routed: boolean, dealt: number): dealt is the NPC health actually removed (an overkill hit counts only what was left; 0 for a player target or a miss). Vampire Rounds lifesteal runs here on dealt, so every player weapon gets it — see Combat perks.  Rock Hazards. Rocks have no server parts, so every player weapon also tests them through RockService: hitscan calls RockService.RaycastHit at the shooter's view time (RockMath.shooterViewTime: server time minus half of GetNetworkPing(), at most 1 s — rocks are drawn at the client's server time, not through the NPC interpolation buffer, so rewindTo does not apply) and a nearer rock takes the shot (scaledDamage + crit, no headshot or finisher); the rocket caster tests each flight step with RockService.SegmentHit and explodes on a rock (data.done stops a second explosion); rocket, grenade and C4 blasts also call RockService.ApplyAOE.

searchDocs.title: Combat perks (Perk Rework part 5)​
searchDocs.content: Vampire Rounds (Lifesteal 0.03, shop): after a player's hit removes NPC health, CombatService heals the attacker by dealt × Lifesteal through HealthManager.HealPlayer, capped at ShopPerkConfig.LIFESTEAL_MAX_PER_SECOND (2 HP/s, 100-HP scale) by a per-player bucket (CombatPerkMath.lifestealTake). Any weapon counts: guns, explosives, cannons.Weak Spot (WeakSpotBonus 0.15, shop): when the owner's hitscan bullet removes enemy health and the enemy survives (a killing hit does not mark, so no glow stays on the body), WeaponServer calls CombatService.Mark(model, WEAK_SPOT_SECONDS, bonus) and fires EnemyMarked. ApplyToModel multiplies any player damage to a marked enemy by 1 + bonus (guns, AOE, cannons — the whole party; enemy fire and the environment do not get it). A re-hit refreshes the mark; it never stacks. Before Weak Spot, an NPC's DamageTakenMult attribute (the Sirenspine buff, see Void Enemies) scales all damage to it. Clients show a red AlwaysOnTop Highlight (WeaponEffectsController).Finishing Touch (FinisherBonus 0.25, shop): at the hitscan hit site, CombatPerkMath.finisherExtra passes the bonus as scaledDamage's extra when the enemy is below ShopPerkConfig.FINISHER_HEALTH_FRACTION (25%) of its max health. Guns only; rockets, throwables and cannons do not get it.Ricochet (RicochetChance 5%/level, permanent): after a hitscan hit removes enemy health, a server roll bounces PerkConfig.RICOCHET_DAMAGE_FRACTION (35%) of the shot's full damage (before overkill, so a kill shot bounces as hard as any hit) to the nearest other live EnemyNPC within RICOCHET_RADIUS (12 studs) that the hit point can see. It runs once per hit and never for the bounce, so it cannot chain. The tracer is a WeaponFired with the first enemy as shooter, so every client (the shooter too) draws it. Rockets and throwables never ricochet.Last Stand (LastStandBonus 0.20, shop): scaledDamage adds the bonus while the attacker's HealthManager.GetHealth / GetMaxHealth is below ShopPerkConfig.LAST_STAND_HEALTH_FRACTION (0.25). Every weapon that uses scaledDamage gets it, explosives too.Rally Banner (RallyDamageBonus 0.05 + RallyRegenBonus 0.20, party): PerkBuffRead.Rally(player, key, RALLY_RADIUS) returns the party value while another live player is within ShopPerkConfig.RALLY_RADIUS (20 studs), else 0. scaledDamage adds the damage part; HealthManager regen adds the regen part. No tick or flag: each reader checks distance when it asks. RallyAuraController (client) checks the same rule once a second and fades a thin gold CylinderHandleAdornment ring in at the local character's feet.

searchDocs.title: Server: per-player state (WeaponState)​
searchDocs.content: Per-player authoritative state. Fields per player record:  lastFire: { [weaponName]: number } — os.clock() of last shot/throw per weapon; gates fire-rate.ammo: { [weaponName]: { mag, reloadEndsAt } } — magazine count and reload window (reloadEndsAt is the os.clock() timestamp when a reload finishes; 0 means not reloading). Reserve is no longer stored here — pool ammo is owned by AmmoManager.active: { ActiveCharge } — active manual throwables (C4) awaiting detonation.  Key functions: EnsureAmmo (seeds magazine from config), GetMag/SetMag, GetLastFire/SetLastFire, IsReloading, SetReloadEnd, GetActiveCount, AddActive, TakeAllActive. Clear destroys all active charges and removes the player's record on PlayerRemoving.

searchDocs.title: Server: projectiles (ServerProjectile)​
searchDocs.content: Spawns and owns server-authoritative, replicated projectile instances cloned from ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets into workspace/ServerProjectiles. Two spawn paths:  spawnRocket(templateName, cframe) — anchored, non-collidable cosmetic part; the caller (WeaponServer) steps its CFrame along the FastCast2 cast.spawnThrowable(templateName, origin, direction, speed, rest, ignore) — server-owned physics rigid body. prepareAssembly un-anchors all parts, sets the WeaponProjectile collision group (passes through characters), and applies per-mode elasticity: "Stick" (C4) elasticity = 0 (lands dead); "Bounce" (Grenade) elasticity = 0.15 (one small hop). installSettle polls until the charge has contacted a world surface and come to rest, then anchors it flat. Network ownership is kept server-side via root:SetNetworkOwner(nil).

searchDocs.title: HUD integration contract​
searchDocs.content: This system ships no UI. A HUD widget that wants to display ammo or combat feedback must consume:  Packets (server → owning client, handled by AmmoApi): WeaponMagSync(weaponName, mag) — authoritative magazine count sent on equip, after each shot, and after reload completion.AmmoPoolSync(ammoType, amount) — authoritative pool count for a given ammo type sent whenever the pool changes (shot, reload, craft). AmmoApi read surface (preferred over raw packets): AmmoApi.GetMag(weaponName) → (mag, magSize) — current magazine and max size.AmmoApi.GetPool(ammoType) → (amount, capacity) — current pool and capacity cap.AmmoApi.GetEquippedAmmo() → (mag, magSize, pool, cap)? — combined ammo for the equipped gun; nil for non-guns.AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount(toolName) → count — counts matching Tools in the Backpack + equipped slot. Signals (client-side): WeaponEquipped(toolName, category) — fired on equip.WeaponUnequipped(toolName) — fired on unequip.WeaponMagChanged(weaponName, mag) — fired by AmmoApi on predicted mag update and on WeaponMagSync reconciliation.AmmoPoolChanged(ammoType, amount) — fired by AmmoApi on AmmoPoolSync or local prediction.ThrowableCountChanged(toolName, count) — fired by AmmoApi when the backpack throwable count changes.WeaponReloadStarted(weaponName, reloadTime) — fired when a reload request is sent.WeaponReloadComplete(weaponName) — fired when the reload window elapses or reload is rejected.WeaponLocalHit(model) — fired on a predicted hitscan hit for hitmarker display.  Ammo HUD. AmmoHudController (client) drives the authored AmmoGui (bottom-right ScreenGui). The count is split across two labels either side of a divider — MainContainer.AmmoCount and MainContainer.ReserveAmmoCount — laid out horizontally by a UIListLayout. For guns that is the loaded magazine beside the reserve pool; for throwables the carried count goes in AmmoCount and ReserveAmmoCount shows an em-dash, so the widget keeps its shape across weapon swaps. The GUI has no weapon-name label, so the equipped weapon's DisplayName is not shown. It is hidden when nothing is equipped. All data comes from AmmoApi + the weapon/ammo Signals; the HUD never talks to the server.  The label names are load-bearing AmmoHudController resolves AmmoCount and ReserveAmmoCount by name with an untimed WaitForChild. Renaming either in Studio stalls the controller at load (Roblox's "Infinite yield possible" warning names the missing instance). Divider is layout-only and is never touched by code.

searchDocs.title: Ammo economy​
searchDocs.content: Pool and magazine model​  Ammo is split into two distinct layers:  Magazine (WeaponState, server) — per-gun in-memory count representing what is currently loaded. The magazine is seeded to MagazineSize rounds on the gun's first equip (EnsureAmmo) and then persists across deaths within the session (it is not refilled on every equip or on respawn). On each shot the magazine decrements by one. On reload, the magazine refills from the pool. The magazine is the only ammo state WeaponState owns; there is no longer a reserve field per gun.Pool (AmmoManager, server) — per-player, per-type in-memory count of unloaded ammo. Entirely session-only — nothing is persisted to a DataStore. The pool is seeded to each type's Starting value on the player's first spawn only; it then persists across deaths for the rest of the session (dying never refills reserve ammo). Every type's Starting is 0: players are never given free reserve ammo — all reserve ammo is crafted (see Crafting ammo). AmmoManager.EnsureStarting re-syncs the current pool to the owning client on each respawn so the HUD shows the correct value after the character and Backpack rebuild. The pool is shared across all guns of the same ammo type.  A freshly crafted weapon still spawns with one full magazine (the magazine is seeded to MagazineSize on first equip), so it can fire immediately. But once that magazine is emptied the gun cannot be reloaded until the player crafts ammo into the reserve pool.  Ammo types (AmmoConfig)​  Ammo type	Display name	Capacity	Starting (first spawn)Light	Light Rounds	300	0 Heavy	Heavy Rounds	60	0 Rocket	Rockets	12	0  Gun → ammo type mapping:  Gun	Ammo typePistol, SMG, AR	Light SR	Heavy RocketLauncher	Rocket  Reload flow​  Client fires ReqReloadWeapon.Server checks mag < magSize and pool > 0; rejects otherwise (returns 0 reload time).Server waits ReloadTime, then calls ammoReloadFromPool(mag, pool, magSize) (in WeaponValidation), which returns (newMag, taken).AmmoManager.ConsumeAmmo(player, ammoType, taken) is called atomically; it clamps, deducts, and fires AmmoPoolSync to the owning client.Server sets the new magazine via WeaponState.SetMag and fires WeaponMagSync to the owning client.  Throwables​  Throwables are physical Roblox Tools in the player's Backpack. Each throw consumes exactly one Tool: WeaponServer.onThrowProjectile destroys the equipped throwable Tool server-side on a successful throw. There is no numeric reserve or CarryCount in WeaponState — count is inferred by AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount by scanning the Backpack and equipped slot.  C4 detonation is intentionally decoupled from holding the Tool: ThrowableDetonateController.client.luau listens for the global G keybind and fires ReqDetonate regardless of what is currently equipped. The server no-ops if the player has no active charges. This design handles the edge case where the last C4 was thrown (destroying its Tool) but live charges are still stuck to surfaces awaiting detonation.  Crafting ammo​  See Workbench Crafting for the full crafting flow; the recipe values below are illustrative — WorkbenchConfig.Recipes is canonical.  Ammo can be replenished at a Workbench. Crafting recipes in the "ammo" category call AmmoManager.AddAmmo (which clamps to Capacity). Available ammo recipes:  Recipe	OutputCraftLightAmmo	+60 Light Rounds CraftHeavyAmmo	+12 Heavy Rounds CraftRocketAmmo	+2 Rockets CraftGrenade	3 Grenade Tools CraftC4	1 C4 Tool  Weapon Tool recipes clone the template from ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates directly into the player's Backpack.  Client read surface (AmmoApi)​  AmmoApi is the single client-side cache and read surface for all ammo data. HUD widgets and handlers should call AmmoApi rather than listening to raw packets.  Method	Returns	NotesGetMag(weaponName)	(mag, magSize)	Current magazine count and magazine capacity. GetPool(ammoType)	(amount, capacity)	Current pool count and pool capacity cap. GetEquippedAmmo()	(mag, magSize, pool, cap)?	Combined view for the equipped gun; nil for non-guns or unarmed. GetThrowableCount(toolName)	count	Counts matching Tool instances in Backpack + equipped slot.  AmmoApi listens to WeaponMagSync and AmmoPoolSync packets, updates its cache, and fires the corresponding Signals. It also watches the player's Backpack for tool additions/removals (rebinding per-character via Janitor) to keep GetThrowableCount accurate. Bootstrapped once by AmmoController.client.luau.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Fire-rate enforcement Guns enforce 60/RPM intervals and throwables enforce CooldownTime via WeaponState.GetLastFire. Requests that arrive too early are silently dropped.  Server-authoritative ammo and reload Magazine counts and reload timing are owned by WeaponState on the server; pool ammo is owned by AmmoManager. Firing at an empty magazine is rejected. Firing while a reload window is active (reloadEndsAt > now) is rejected. Reloading with an empty pool is rejected. Neither the magazine count, pool count, nor the reload timer is read from the client.  Origin, spread, and distance validation The claimed muzzle origin for guns and throw origin for throwables must be within 14 studs of the server-side HumanoidRootPart position and must be a finite (non-NaN) vector. Claimed directions with zero or non-finite magnitude are rejected before normalization. The server caps hitscan range at MaxDistance on its authoritative ray; applySpread is applied client-side for feel only — the server recasts from the validated origin and does not verify the spread angle.  Friendly-fire prevention Enforced in CombatService.ApplyToModel via Factions.canDamage. Only Player↔Enemy damage lands. Players never damage other players or friendly NPCs; enemies never damage other enemies or friendly NPCs. Self-damage from one's own AOE is exempt — the self-check bypasses the faction gate so a player's own rocket can still hurt them if they walk into the blast.  NPC pass-through via CollectionService tag: the "EnemyNPC"/"FriendlyNPC" CollectionService tag is the dual-purpose NPC marker. It gates damage routing in CombatService (only tagged NPCs with a Humanoid take weapon damage) and, via NpcCollisionService, places NPC parts in the Character collision group so thrown charges physically pass through them (see Enemy Spawner → Collision and combat wiring). A Model without a recognized faction tag receives no damage and does not block thrown projectiles — tag it or it is invisible to the weapon system.  HealthManager routing via CombatService: HealthManager writes record.Health → humanoid.Health but never reads back from the Humanoid. Any external write that bypasses HealthManager.ApplyDamage (via CombatService) will leave the HUD showing a stale record value. Never write to humanoid.Health directly for player damage. See Health.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Extended Mags (MagazineBonus): magazine size via WeaponValidation.magazineSize (rounds down, min 1) on the server (WeaponServer equip + reload) and the client (AmmoApi.GetMag).Battle Rations (PartyDamageBonus): adds to DamageBonus inside scaledDamage.Lucky Shot (CritChance): server roll on hitscan hits; a crit doubles the hit.Blast Kit (ExplosiveDamageBonus): adds to grenade, rocket and C4 damage.Grenadier (BlastRadiusBonus): scales the blast radius for both ApplyAOE and the ExplosionAt visual.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Config module: WeaponConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/WeaponConfig.luau. Edit stats here — never in handler or server code.Config module: AmmoConfig — src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/AmmoConfig.luau.Perks: SpreadReduction (GunHandler spread ×max(0.1, 1−b), client only — the server trusts the fire direction), ReloadSpeedBonus (WeaponServer reload timer ÷(1+b); GunHandler predicts the same value), HeadshotBonus (WeaponServer headshot multiplier ×(1+b)), DamageBonus (scaledDamage). See Perks.  Common fields (all weapons): Category ("Gun"|"Throwable"), DisplayName, ToolName (must match the in-game Tool's Name exactly), Damage (base per-bullet; 0 for throwables, AOE only), DamageType ("Bullet"|"AOE"), HeadshotMultiplier? (gun only, applied on a ray hit against a part named "Head").  Gun fields: FireMode ("Hitscan"|"Projectile"), RPM (fire interval = 60/RPM), Automatic (hold-to-fire vs. semi), MagazineSize (reserve pool lives in AmmoManager, keyed by AmmoType), AmmoType ("Light"|"Heavy"|"Rocket"), ReloadTime, Spread (max cone half-angle, degrees), MaxDistance, FireSound/ReloadSound/DrySound/ImpactSound. Projectile-only additions: ProjectileSpeed, Gravity (Vector3), AOERadius, AOEDamage (center damage, linear falloff to 0 at radius), CosmeticTemplate (name in ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets).  Throwable fields: Detonation ("Fuse" auto after FuseTime | "Manual" all charges on ReqDetonate), Rest ("Bounce"|"Stick"), ThrowSpeed, FuseTime (Fuse only), MaxActive (Manual only, max simultaneous charges per player), AOERadius/AOEDamage, CooldownTime, CosmeticTemplate, ThrowSound/ExplodeSound.  Note: CarryCount has been removed. How many throwables a player carries is determined by how many matching Tool instances are in their Backpack (crafted or spawned); AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount reads this count at runtime.
