searchDocs.title: Opening the bench​
searchDocs.content: The GUI is the Ocean Sunset rebuild of 2026-10-27 (prototype: roblox-gui-prototypes/2026-10-27-workbench-gui-prototype.html, whose build notes list every instance). WorkbenchGui (DisplayOrder 130, above the Satchel hotbar) holds a full-screen Dim and a solid MainContainer (1440×820 offset, surface fill, 18 px corner, 3 px line stroke). It has two pages under MainContainer.Bottom's UIPageLayout: WorkbenchContainer (recipe crafting) and ArmoryContainer (the armor tab). The Top.CategoryContainer tabs Personal (CRAFT) and Recharge jump between them; a touch swipe also flips pages, and the active tab (teal fill, deep text) follows UIPageLayout.CurrentPage either way. Each page repeats its own StashButton/MoveButton in a Footer; PlaceableActions.bind wires every match.  Hovering a MoveButton / StashButton eases its BackgroundColor3 to the line color via MotionMaster and back on mouse leave. This is purely cosmetic, wired in WorkbenchGuiController.client.luau (not PlaceableActions), and only on devices with a mouse — a tap fires MouseEnter without MouseLeave, which would leave the hover look stuck.  Scaling. Sizes are authored in offset at the 1920×1080 reference and scaled by MainContainer.UIScale (wide = min(W/1920, H/1022)). Below 0.68 the controller applies a compact layout authored at 844×332 (scale clamped to [0.75, 1.5]): the WIDE values are captured from Studio at start-up, the COMPACT overrides live in the controller, and live clones (chips, recipe cards) are re-synced from their templates. Compact hides the description. Same pattern as the Health/Stamina HUD.  On the first open of a session, the detail pane auto-selects the first recipe in the grid's sort order (Category, then DisplayName — the same order shown under the "All" filter) so it never shows the unselected Studio placeholder. This is a one-time default: once any recipe is selected (by this default or by a player click), the selection persists across closes/reopens like any manual pick.

searchDocs.title: Client — recipe grid and gating​
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchGuiController opens via the bench CraftPromptPart ProximityPrompt. It builds the recipe grid from WorkbenchConfig.Recipes: each card shows the recipe's Icon (the item thumbnail the artist renders) and DisplayName. A recipe whose RequiresNode is not present in ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked gets a darkened thumbnail, a muted name and an amber LockBadge; the selected card has an amber stroke. CategoryChips holds one chip per WorkbenchConfig.Categories entry (label = uppercased CategoryLabels); a chip fires Signals.RequestWorkbenchCategory to re-filter the grid, and the active chip is amber. The detail pane shows the thumbnail, uppercased name, a category tag, the description and the Wood/Metal rows (have / need, mint when enough, rust when short). AcceptButton reads CRAFT (teal) and fires ReqCraft; when it can't, it is disabled (sunk fill, amber text, lock icon) and its label gives the reason: LOCKED — RESEARCH FIRST, NOT ENOUGH WOOD, NOT ENOUGH METAL or NOT ENOUGH MATERIALS. Signals.OnItemCrafted fires on a confirmed success. The CloseButton closes the GUI. Uses a Janitor per GUI open/close lifecycle.

searchDocs.title: Server — authoritative craft handler​
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchService is the sole owner of the authoritative ReqCraft handler. On ReqCraft(bench, recipeId) it validates, in order:  Look up the recipe in WorkbenchConfig (else UNKNOWN_RECIPE).Verify the bench is a tagged Workbench Model (else INVALID_TARGET).Re-check proximity, INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE (else TOO_FAR).CRAFT_COOLDOWN gate, per-player timestamp (else COOLDOWN).Check the RequiresNode gate in ResearchUnlocked (else LOCKED).CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(player, recipe.Output) — verify the output slot is usable before consuming any materials (else OUTPUT_FAILED).Atomically spend the cost from the server-wide Material Pool with MaterialPool.Spend(cost) (false → INSUFFICIENT_MATERIALS, nothing consumed).  On pass: call CraftOutputDispatcher.grant(player, recipe.Output) and record the cooldown timestamp. The handler returns (success: Boolean8, code: NumberU8).

searchDocs.title: Output dispatch​
searchDocs.content: CraftOutputDispatcher handles the four output kinds:  Kind == "Weapon" — clones the named Tool from ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates into the player's Backpack.Kind == "Armor" — calls ArmorManager.Grant(player, output.ArmorKind), which awards the kind at full pool or refills it if already owned, and auto-equips if nothing is worn. See Armor — Crafting.Kind == "Placeable" — grants the named Tool from ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> into the player's Backpack.Kind == "Ammo" — adds to the player's session-only ammo pool via AmmoManager.AddAmmo.  isFeasible(player, output) verifies the target output slot is usable (e.g. the template exists, the armor kind is known and not already at full pool) before materials are consumed. A misconfigured recipe never costs the player materials.

searchDocs.title: Recipe schema​
searchDocs.content: Recipes are declared in WorkbenchConfig.Recipes as a { [string]: Recipe } table keyed by a string recipe ID:  export type Output = { Kind: "Weapon", ToolName: string, Count: number? } | { Kind: "Armor", ArmorKind: string } | { Kind: "Placeable", PlaceableName: string } | { Kind: "Ammo", AmmoType: string, Amount: number } export type Recipe = { Category: string, -- one of RecipeCategories ("weapons"|"ammo"|"armor"|"workstation") DisplayName: string, Description: string, Tier: number, -- 1..5 flavor/quality badge only; NOT a prerequisite ladder Icon: string, -- rbxassetid:// string for the grid tile and detail panel Cost: { Wood: number?, Metal: number? }, RequiresNode: string?, -- Research Bench nodeId gate or nil = always available Output: Output, }   Tier is data only: the GUI no longer shows it (removed in the 2026-10-27 rebuild). It has no prerequisite chain and imposes no unlock order — any recipe with RequiresNode = nil is available to craft at any time regardless of Tier. The only unlock gate is RequiresNode. The Cost table is limited to Wood and Metal because the GUI renders exactly two material rows; adding a third material requires a GUI layout change and a matching config key.  The Recipes table is the live catalog. The shipped placeholder entries:  Recipe ID	Category	Cost	RequiresNode	OutputCraftPistol	weapons	Metal 10	nil	Weapon "Pistol" CraftArmorLight	armor	Metal 15	"Armor_Light"	Armor "Light" CraftWorkbench	workstation	Wood 5	nil	Placeable "Workbench" CraftSMG	weapons	Metal 25	"Ranged_SMG"	Weapon "SMG"  The other four armor recipes (CraftArmorMedBallistic, CraftArmorMedEnergy, CraftArmorHeavyBallistic, CraftArmorHeavyEnergy) follow the same shape, one per ArmorConfig.Kinds entry — see Armor — The catalog for the full table.  The workstation category currently contains only CraftWorkbench — it exists as its own dropdown filter rather than folding the Workbench into weapons or armor because future placeable stations (e.g. a second crafting structure) are expected to land in the same category.

searchDocs.title: Research gate seam​
searchDocs.content: ResearchEffectsDispatcher publishes leveled-up node IDs into a ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked folder (a BoolValue per node at level ≥ 1, named by nodeId) in parallel to the ResearchBuffs folder. This folder is written by the server whenever a node reaches level 1 and is read by:  WorkbenchService (server): authoritative gate check. A craft request whose recipe has a non-nil RequiresNode is rejected with LOCKED if the corresponding BoolValue is absent or false. Because the folder is written by the server, clients cannot forge an unlock.WorkbenchGuiController (client): greying. Recipes with a locked RequiresNode are rendered as unavailable in the grid so players know they need to research the gating node first. The client reads this folder but never writes it.  Unlike the old Tech Tree (where a node auto-unlocked the instant its pooled material cost was met), a gating Research Bench node now also costs time: the player pays materials on enqueue, then the node's level advances in real time (gated by bench fuel) before ResearchUnlocked is written. Recipes behind a RequiresNode are therefore no longer available the moment materials are gathered — see Research Bench for the full enqueue/advance/complete flow and the ResearchBuffs/ResearchUnlocked folder contract.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Tag the Workbench Model. In ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/Workbench, tag the root Model with the CollectionService tag Workbench (the same tag the Shredder scans for — one Model serves as both crafting station and shredder). Give it a BasePart named CraftPromptPart (anywhere under the Model — PromptResolver finds it recursively) containing a ProximityPrompt. Set the Model's PrimaryPart. The shredder half uses a sibling ShredPromptPart.Create ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates. Add a folder named WeaponTemplates inside ServerStorage. Place craftable weapon Tools here (e.g. clones of Pistol and SMG from StarterPack). These are separate from the StarterPack copies — the Workbench clones from here into the player's Backpack, so stat changes or visual differences can live here independently.Ensure craftable placeables exist. Each recipe with Output.Kind == "Placeable" needs a Tool at ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<PlaceableName>. The Workbench itself already follows this convention as a grid-placeable item.Material templates are shared. ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials already holds Wood and Metal Tool templates (shared with the Shredder and Research Bench systems). No duplication is needed.Wire ResearchUnlocked. ResearchEffectsDispatcher creates and writes this folder automatically at runtime. No manual Studio setup is required for the gate to function. If testing in isolation (without a running ResearchService/ResearchEffectsDispatcher), create a Folder named ResearchUnlocked in ReplicatedStorage and add BoolValue children named after whichever node IDs you want to treat as unlocked.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Server re-checks proximity on every craft The client proximity prompt is never trusted. WorkbenchService re-runs the distance check using INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE on every ReqCraft call. A player exploiting from range receives TOO_FAR.  Feasibility is checked before materials are consumed CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(player, recipe.Output) runs (and must succeed) before any material is spent from the pool. A recipe that references a missing weapon template or an unknown/already-full armor kind therefore fails without costing the player anything. Misconfigured recipes are safe to ship; they only result in a visible craft failure.  Research gate is read from server-written state The ResearchUnlocked folder is written exclusively by ResearchEffectsDispatcher on the server. A client cannot create or modify entries in that folder. The server re-reads the folder on every ReqCraft call, so a client that somehow fakes the UI greying cannot bypass the gate.  Cost is limited to Wood and Metal The GUI renders exactly two material rows. Cost may only specify Wood and/or Metal. Adding a third material type (e.g. Energy) requires a GUI layout change alongside the config key — otherwise the cost is silently unchecked on the client (though the server will still validate it).  Tier is a flavor badge, not a prerequisite ladder Tier (1–5) is not shown or read anywhere. There is no inter-recipe prerequisite chain derived from Tier values. The sole unlock gate is RequiresNode. Do not attempt to use Tier as a crafting order enforcer — it will not work without code changes.  Known edge case: respawn mid-craft (v1) If a player's Backpack disappears between the feasibility check passing and CraftOutputDispatcher.grant executing (e.g. the player respawns during that narrow window), materials may be spent from the pool but the grant returns OUTPUT_FAILED. The client receives a failure response and the pool loses the materials. This is an accepted v1 limitation — the window is sub-frame in practice. A future refund path or a pre-grant Backpack re-check is the recommended fix.

searchDocs.title: Shop perk effects​
searchDocs.content: Ammunition Specialist (PartyPerkBuffs.CraftedAmmoBonus, 0.2): CraftOutputDispatcher adds floor(Amount × (1 + bonus)) rounds for an Ammo output (still capped by AmmoConfig Capacity). Ammo types in ShopPerkConfig.CRAFTED_AMMO_EXCLUDED (Rocket) get no bonus. Grenades and C4 craft as weapons, so the perk never touches them.Scrap Recycler (PartyPerkBuffs.CraftRefund): after a successful craft, WorkbenchService gives back floor(spent × refund) Wood and Metal through MaterialPool.Add (arcs from the bench).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant P as Player participant C as WorkbenchGuiController participant S as WorkbenchService P->>C: Walk within INTERACT_DISTANCE C->>C: ProximityPrompt fires (CraftPromptPart) C->>C: GUI opens; grid from WorkbenchConfig.Recipes C->>C: Grey recipes whose RequiresNode is not in ResearchUnlocked P->>C: Click a recipe tile C->>C: Show DisplayName, Description, category tag, Cost rows, disabled reason P->>C: Click Craft button C->>S: ReqCraft(bench, recipeId) S->>S: look up recipe (else UNKNOWN_RECIPE) S->>S: verify tagged Workbench Model (else INVALID_TARGET) S->>S: re-check proximity (else TOO_FAR) S->>S: CRAFT_COOLDOWN gate (else COOLDOWN) S->>S: check RequiresNode in ResearchUnlocked (else LOCKED) S->>S: CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(Output) (else OUTPUT_FAILED) S->>S: verify materials held (else INSUFFICIENT_MATERIALS) S->>S: consume materials, CraftOutputDispatcher.grant(...) S->>S: record cooldown timestamp S->>C: (success, code) alt success C->>C: Signals.OnItemCrafted:Fire(recipeId) C->>C: success FX / SoundManager.PlaySFX(CraftSuccess) else failure C->>C: failure toast / SoundManager.PlaySFX(CraftFail) end
